to cause to go astray; metaph., of leading into error: Mk 13:22; pass., to be led astray: I Ti 6:10.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868 (ἀφίστημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό (< ἀφίστημι), [in LXX; De 24:1, 3, Je 3:8, Is 50:1 (כְּרִיתֻת, כְּרִיתוּת)*;]
1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.).
2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mt 19:7, Mk 10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, s.v.), Mt 5:31 (for other late exx., v. MM, s.v.; Kennedy, Sources, 121).†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4721 (στέγη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀπο-στεγάζω (< στέγη), [in Sm.: Je 49:10 (29:11)*;]
to unroof: Mk 2:4.†

strong.kjv: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ (< στερέω, to rob), [in LXX: Ex 21:10 (גּרע), De 24:14 (עשׁק), Ma 3:5, Si 4:1 29:6, 7 31 (34):21, 22*;]
to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, s.v.): absol., Mk 10:19, I Co 6:8; c. acc. pers., I Co 7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: I Co 6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but v. Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: I Ti 6:5.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι);
strong.def: ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal)
strong.kjv: damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 ἀπώλεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀπόλλυμι), [in LXX (Cremer, 797) for אבד, אֵיד, etc.;]
destruction, waste, loss, perishing (in π., of money, v. MM, s.v.): Mt 26:8, Mk 14:4, Ac 8:20, Ro 9:22, I Ti 6:9, II Pe 2:1; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, perdition, the antithesis of σωτηρία: Mt 7:13, Jo 17:12, Phl 1:28 3:19, II Th 2:3, He 10:39, II Pe 2:3 3:7, 16, Re 17:8, 11 (DB, iii, 744).†

strong.derivation: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of exciting emotion);
strong.def: to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 ἀρέσκω, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): c. dat. pers., Mt 14:6, Mk 6:22, Ro 8:8 15:2, I Th 2:15 4:1, I Co 7:32, 33, 34, Ga 1:10, II Ti 2:4; seq. ἐνώπιον (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 6:5.
2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (v. M, Th., ICC, I Co., 7:32, 33, 34; Cremer, 640 f.); Ro 15:1, 3, I Co 10:33, I Th 2:4.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517 (ῥώννυμι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἄρρωστος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: III Ki 14:5Α, Ma 1:8 (חלה), Si 7:35*;]
feeble, sickly: Mt 14:14, Mk 6:5, 13 16:[18], I Co 11:30.†

strong.def: to be first (in political rank or power)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
89 ἄρχω, [in LXX for חלל, משׁל, etc.;]
1. to begin.
2. to rule (v. DCG, ii, 538b.): c. gen., Mk 10:42, Ro 15:12. Mid., to begin: seq. ἀπό, Mt 16:21 20:8, Lk 14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jo 8:9, Ac 1:22 8:35 10:37, I Pe 4:17; c. inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mk 1:45 2:23 5:17, Lk 3:8, al. (v. M, Pr., 14 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, s.v.).

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ** ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀσελγής, licentious; v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Wi 14:26, III Mac 2:26*;]
licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Mk 7:22, Ro 13:13, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19 (Lft., in l.), Eph 4:19, I Pe 4:3, II Pe 2:2, 7, 18, Ju 4.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι);
strong.def: a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;]
a star: Mt 2:2, 7, 9, 10, Mk 13:25, I Co 15:41, Re 6:13 8:10, 11, 12 9:1 12:1, 4; metaph., ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός Re 2:28 22:16; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, Re 1:16, 20 2:1 3:1 (cf. ἄστρον, and v. DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4908 (συνετός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀ-σύνετος, -ον [in LXX: De 32:21 (נָבָל), Jb 13:2 (נפל), Ps 91 (92):6 (כְּסִיל), Ps 75 (76):5, Wi2, Si6*;]
without understanding or discernment: Mt 15:16, Mk 7:18 (Swete, in l.), Ro 1:21, 31 10:19 (for an ex. of its use in the moral sense, v. MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἀσφαλῶς, adv., [in LXX: Ge 34:25 (בֶּטַח), To 6:4, Wi 18:6, Ba 5:7, I Mac 6:40, III Mac 7:6*;]
(a). safely: Mk 14:44, Ac 16:23;
(b). assuredly: Ac 2:36.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5092 (τιμή);
strong.kjv: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄτιμος, -ον (< τιμή), [in LXX: Is 3:5 (קלה ni.), Is 53:3 (בּזה), Jb 30:4, 8 (בְּלִי־שֵׁם), Wi5, Si1*;]
without honour, dishonoured, despised: Mt 13:57, Mk 6:4, I Co 4:10; comp., I Co 12:23.†

strong.derivation: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G3155 (μάτην);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 αὐτόματος, -ον, and -η, -ον (etym. doubtful; v. Boisacq, Prellwitz, s.v.), [in LXX, Le 25:5, 11, IV Ki 19:29 (סָפִיחַ), Jos 6:5, Jb 24:24, Wi 17:6*;]
1. of persons, acting of one's own will.
2. Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord: γῆ, Mk 4:28 (MM, s.v.); πύλη, Ac 12:10.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);
strong.def: a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀφεδρών, -ῶνος, ὁ (cf. ἄφεδρος, Le 12:5) = cl. ἄφοδος (MM, s.v.),
a privy, drain: Mt 15:17, Mk 7:19 (ὀχετόν, WH, mg.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351 (φθείρω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ἄ-φθαρτος, -ον (< φθείρω), [in LXX: Wi 12:1 18:4*;]
imperishable, immortal;
(a). of things: I Co 9:25, I Pe 1:4, 23 3:4;
(b). of persons: of men, I Co 15:52; of God, Ro 1:23, I Ti 1:17 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀφρίζω (< ἀφρός),
to foam at the mouth: Mk 9:18, 20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ἄφρων), [in LXX for אִוֶּלֶת, נְבָלָה, etc.;]
foolishness: Mk 7:22, II Co 11:1, 17, 21.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5499 (χειροποίητος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ἀ-χειρο-ποίητος, -ον (< χειροποίητος),
not made by hands: Mk 14:58, II Co 5:1; metaph., περιτομή ἀ. (i.e. spiritual), Col 2:11 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† βαπτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< βαπτίζω) , prop., the act of which βάπτισμα is the result;
1. a dipping, washing, lustration: Mk 7:4; of Jewish ceremonial, He 9:10; in He 6:2, βαπτισμῶν διδαχήν (-ῆς), "the pl. and the peculiar form seem to be used to include Christian baptism with other lustral rites" (Westc, in l.).
2. baptism: FlJ, Ant., 18, 5, 2 (of John's baptism), and some Fathers (v. Soph., s.v.). Not so in NT, unless ἐν τ. βαπτισμῷ, in the act of baptism, Col 2:12, be read with Tr. (Rec., WH, R, -ματι).†

strong.def: son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, v. DB, iv, p. 762),
Bartimæus: Mk 10:46.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 βεβαιόω, -ῶ (< βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41):12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119):28 (קוּם pi.), III Mac 5:42*;]
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Ro 15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): I Co 1:8, II Co 1:21. Pass., I Co 1:6, Col 2:7, He 2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; v. next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†

strong.def: to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 βλαστάνω, [in LXX for צמח, etc.;]
1. to sprout: Mt 13:26, Mk 4:27, He 9:4.
2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: c. acc., Ja 5:18.†

strong.def: sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, v. Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.c.; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mk 3:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 βοηθέω, -ῶ (< βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Ac 21:28; c dat., Mt 15:25, Mk 9:22, 24 Ac 16:9, II Co 6:2 (LXX), He 2:18, Re 12:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 βροντή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX for רַעַם ;]
thunder: Mk 3:17, Jo 12:29, Re 4:5 6:1 8:5 10:3, 4 11:19 14:2 16:18 19:6.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (compare H01660 and H08081);
strong.def: oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γεθσημασεί (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, oil-press),
Gethsemane: called in Jo 18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Mt 26:36, Mk 14:32.†

strong.derivation: neuter plural of a derivative of G1078 (γένεσις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (< γένεσις);
1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead.
2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., v. MM, Exp., x; cf. also Rutherford, NPhr., 184): Mt 14:6, Mk 6:21.†

strong.def: "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective)
strong.kjv: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 γένος, -ους, τό (< γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc.;]
1. family: Ac 4:6 7:13 13:26.
2. offspring: Ac 17:28, 29, Re 22:16.
3. race, nation; Mk 7:28, Ac 4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, II Co 11:26, Phl 3:5, Ga 1:14, I Pe 2:9.
4. kind, sort, class: Mt 13:47 17:21, Rec., Mk 9:29, I Co 12:10, 28 14:10.†

strong.derivation: by variation for a derivative from (to tease cloth);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (< κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, IV Ki 18:17, Is 7:3 36:2*;]
a fuller, cloth-dresser: Mk 9:3.†

strong.def: the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.c., Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, Jg 9:53, II Ki 9:35); indecl. (exc. Mk 15:22, -άν),
Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: Mt 27:33, Mk 15:22, Jo 19:17.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1119 (γόνυ) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† γονυπετέω, -ῶ (< γόνυ, πίπτω);
1. to fall on the knees: seq. ἔμπροσθεν, Mt 27:29.
2. to fall down before one: c. acc., Mt 17:14, Mk 1:40, R, txt., 10:17.†

strong.def: nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 γυμνός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX chiefly for עָרוֹם ;]
naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as freq. in cl.) scantily or poorly clad (Is 20:2ff., To 1:16, II Mac 11:12): Mt 25:36, 38 43, 44, Mk 14:52, Jo 21:7, Ac 19:16, Ja 2:15, Re 3:17 16:15, 17:16; as subst., to γ., the naked body, Mk 14:51. Metaph., of things exposed, He 4:13; of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., c., 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293), II Co 5:3; of seed, bare, I Co 15:37 (Cremer, 168).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δαλμανουθά, ἡ
indecl.,
Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: Mk 8:10 (cf. Μαγαδάν).†

strong.derivation: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δαμάζω [in LXX: Da 2:40 (חֲשַׁל) * ;]
to tame, subdue: Mk 5:4, Ja 3:7; metaph., τ. γλῶσσαν, Ja 3:8 (Field, Notes, 237 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δειλός, -ή, όν (< δέος), [in LXX for רַךְ, etc. ;]
cowardly, fearful: Mt 8:26, Mk 4:40, Re 21:8.†

strong.def: the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δεκά-πολις, -εως, ὴ
Decapolis, a region east of the Jordan con­taining ten cities: Mt 4:25, Mk 5:20 7:31.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δερμάτινος, -η, -ον (< δέρμα), [in LXX for עוֹר ;]
of skin, leathern: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6 (cf. IV Ki 1:8).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 δέσμιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; < δεσμός), [in LXX for אסר;]
1. binding.
2. bound, captive; ὁ δ., as subst., a prisoner: Mt 27:15, 16, Mk 15:6, Ac 16:25, 27 23:18 25:14, 27 28:16 (Rec.) 17, He 10:34 13:3; ὁ δ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ, Eph 3:1, II Ti 1:8, Phm 1, 9; ὁ δ. ἐν κυρίῳ, Eph 4:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1204 (δεῦρο) and an imperative form of (to go);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 δεῦτε adv., as pl. of δεῦρο, 1. (b), q.v., [in LXX chiefly for לְכוּ ;]
come on! come here! come!: c. imperat., Mt 25:34 28:6, Jo 4:29 21:12, Re 19:17; c. subjc., Mt 21:38, Mk 12:7; seq. ὀπίσω, Mt 4:19, Mk 1:17; πρός, Mt 11:28; εἰς, Mt 22:4, Mk 6:31.†

strong.kjv: X after, be past, be spent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** δια-γίνομαι (Ion. and late Gk. for διαγίγν-), [in LXX, II Mac 11:26 * ;]
1. to go through, to pass, e.g. τ. νύκτα; absol., to live.
2. Of time, to intervene, elapse: ptcp., c. ἡμερῶν τινῶν, Ac 25:13; ἱκανοῦ χρόνου, ib. 27:9; τ. σαβάτου, Mk 16:1.†

strong.derivation: probably from an obsolete (to run on errands; compare G1377 (διώκω));
strong.def: an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 διάκονος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ (derivation unknown), [in LXX for נַעַר, שָׁרַת pi.: Es 6:3, 5, א B Es 1:10 2:2, Pr 10:4, 4 Mac 9:17 * ;]
1. in general, a servant, attendant, minister: Mt 20:26 22:13 23:11, Mk 9:35 10:43, Jo 2:5, 9, I Co 3:5, Ga 2:17, Eph 6:21, Col 4:7; δ. θεοῦ, Ro 13:4, II Co 6:4, I Th 3:2; δ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 11:23, Col 1:7, I Ti 4:6; cf. ὁ δ. ὁ ἐμός, Jo 12:26; δ. περιτομῆς, Ro 15:8; δ. καινῆς διαθήκης, II Co 3:6; δ. δικαιοσύνης, II Co 11:15; δ. [εὐαγγελίου], Eph 3:7, Col 1:23; δ. [ἐκκλησίας], Col 1:25.
2. As technical term for Church officer (so in pre-Christian times, v. M, Th., I, 32), a deacon: Phl 1:1, I Ti 3:8, 12; fem. (cf. Eccl. διακονίσσα), Ro 16:1 (cf. I Ti 3:11, and CGT, in l., also M, Th., l.c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 διακόσιοι, -αι, -α
two hundred: Mk 6:37, et al.

strong.def: to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or (reflexively) hesitate
strong.kjv: contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 δια-κρίνω [in LXX for שׁפט, דִּין, etc. ;]
1. to separate, hence, to distinguish, discriminate, discern: μηδὲν δ., Ac 11:12; οὐδὲν δ. μεταξύ, Ac 15:9; σε, I Co 4:7; τὸ σῶμα, I Co 11:29.
2. to settle, decide, judge, arbitrate: Mt 16:3, I Co 6:5 11:29 (ICC, in l.), ib. 31 14:29. Mid, and pass.;
1. to get a decision, contend, dispute: seq. πρός, Ac 11:2; c. dat. (but v. ICC, in l.), Ju 9; absol., Ju 22 (R, mg.).
2. Hellenistic (NT and Eccl., but not LXX), to be divided in one's mind, to hesitate, doubt: Mt 21:21 Ro 14:23, Ja 1:6; ἐν ἐαυτῷ, Ja 2:4; ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Mk 11:23; μηδὲν δ., Ac 10:20; δ. τ. ἀπιστίᾳ, Ro 4:20, Ju 22 (R, txt.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G3004 (λέγω);
strong.def: to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in argument or exhortation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 δια-λέγομαι (mid. of διαλέγω, to pick out, distinguish, as depon.), [in LXX: Ex 6:27, Is 63:1 (דּבר pi.), Jg 8:1 (ריב), I Es 8:46, Es 5:2, Si 14:20, II Mac 11:20 * ;]
to converse with, discourse (v. Cl. Rev., i, 45), discuss, argue: Ac 18:4 19:8, 9 20:9; c. dat. pers., Ac 17:17 18:19 20:7, He 12:5; seq. πρός, Mk 9:34, Ac 17:17 24:12; περί Ac 24:25, Ju 9; ἀπὸ τ. γραφῶν, Ac 17:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δι-αρπάζω [in LXX for בּזז, גּול, שׁסס, etc. ;]
to plunder: Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27.†

strong.def: to draw apart, i.e. sever or dismember

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-σπάω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נתק, as Jg 16:9 ;]
to break or tear asunder: pass., ἁλύσεις, Mk 5:4; Παῦλος, Ac 23:10.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G4724 (στέλλω);
strong.def: to set (oneself) apart (figuratively, distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 δια-στέλλω [in LXX for בּדל hi. (De 10:8, al.), זהר hi. (Ez 3:18, 19, al.), and 19 other words]
1. to divide, distinguish, define.
2. to command, charge expressly: pass., τὸ διαστελλόμενον, He 12:20. Mid., in late Gk. with same sense (so Ez, l.c.; et al. in LXX; MM, s.v.); a. dat. pers., Mk 8:15, Ac 15:24; seq. ἵνα, Mt 16:20, Mk 5:43 7:36 9:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5345 (φήμη);
strong.kjv: blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† δια-φημίζω
in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= הַדָּבָר, the matter), Mk 1:45, Mt 28:15; c. acc pers., to spread abroad one's fame: Mt 9:31.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 διδασκαλία, -ας, ἡ (< διδάσκω), [in LXX: Pr 2:17 (אַלּוּף), Is 29:13 (למד pu.), Si 24:33 39:8 * ;]
teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most freq. the latter: Ro 12:7 15:4, Eph 4:14, I Ti 4:6, 13, 16 5:17 6:1, 3, II Ti 3:10, 16, Tit 2:7, 10; ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., I Ti 1:10, II Ti 4:3, Tit 1:9 2:1; pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Col 2:22; δ. δαιμονίων, I Ti 4:1, δ. διδάσκειν, Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7 (LXX) (Cremer, 182).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δισ-χίλιοι, -αι, -α
two thousand: Mk 5:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 διωγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< διώκω), [in LXX: Pr 11:19 (רדף pi.), La 3:19 (מָרוּד), II Mac 12:23 * ;]
persecution: Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17 10:30 Ac 8:1 13:50, Ro 8:35, II Co 12:10, II Th 1:4, II Ti 3:11.†

strong.derivation: from an obsolete primary verb, (probably meaning to decoy;
strong.def: compare G1185 (δελεάζω)); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 δόλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מִרְמָה;]
1. in Hom., a bait.
2. a snare.
3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: Mt 26:4, Mk 7:22 14:1, Jo 1:47, Ac 13:10, Ro 1:29, II Co 12:16, I Th 2:3, I Pe 2:1, 22 3:10 (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 δρέπανον, -ου, τό (later form of Attic δρεπάνη, < δρέπω, to pluck), [in LXX for מַזְמֵרָה, חֶרְמֵשׁ, etc. ;]
a sickle, pruning-hook; Mk 4:29, Re 14:14-19.†

strong.def: properly, fastidious about eating (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δύσκολος, -ον (< κόλον, food), [in LXX for אֵיד, Je 29:9 (Je 49:8) (of. δυσκολία, Jb 34:30; εὔκολος, II Ki 15:3) * ;]
1. properly, of persons, hard to satisfy with food, hence, generally, hard to please (Eur., Plat.).
2. Of things, difficult, hard (Arist.): Mk 10:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δωρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ge 30:20 (זבד), Es 8:1, Pr 4:2 (נתן), Le 7:5 (15) (קׇרְבָּן), I Es 1:7 8:14, 55, Si 7:25 * ;]
to present, bestow. As depon. (with same sense), -έομαι, -οῦμαι: Mk 15:45, II Pe 1:3, 4.†

strong.def: to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐγ-κατα-λείπω, [in LXX chiefly for עזב ;]
1. to leave behind: ἡμῖν σπέρμα, Ro 9:29 (LXX).
2. to abandon, desert, forsake: c. acc. pers., Mt 27:46 (LXX), Mk 15:34 (ib.), Ac 2:27 (LXX) (WH, ἐνκ-), II Ti 4:10, 16 He 13:5 (LXX); τ. ἐπισυναγωγήν (cf. MM, Exp., xi), He 10:25. Pass., Ac 2:31 (WH, ἐνκ-), II Co 4:9.†

strong.kjv: be at (have, live in) peace, live peaceably

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 εἰρηνεύω (< εἰρήνη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁלם, שׁקט ;]
1. to bring to peace, reconcile (so I Mac 6:60).
2. to keep peace, be at peace: Mk 9:50, Ro 12:18, II Co 13:11, I Th 5:13 (cf. Si 28:9; Cremer, 246).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† ἐκ-θαμβέω, -ῶ (< ἔκθαμβος), [in LXX: Si 30:9 * ;]
1. to be amazed.
2. to amaze, terrify (Si 30:9). Pass., to be amazed, terrified: Mk 9:15 14:33 16:5, 6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐκ-λύω [in LXX for רָפָה, etc. ;]
1. to loose, release.
2. to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:3; of mental weariness, Ga 6:9, He 12:3, 5 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐκ-τινάσσω [in LXX for נָעַר ni., pi., etc. ;]
to shake off: κονιορτόν, Mt 10:14; χοῦν, Mk 6:11. Mid.: κονιορτόν, Ac 13:51; ἱμάτια, Ac 18:6 (cf. MM, Exp., iii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἔκφοβος, -ον [in LXX: ἔ. εἶναι for יָגֹר, De 9:19; also I Mac 13:2 * ;]
affrighted, terrified: Mk 9:16, He 12:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐκ-φύω [in OT (Sm.) Ps 104:14; (Al.) Is 61:11 * ;]
to cause to grow out, put forth (leaves): Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἑλληνίς [in LXX: II Mac 6:8 A * ;]
a Greek (i.e. Gentile) woman: Mk 7:26, Ac 17:12.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldean origin (H0426 with pronominal suffix) my God

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐλωί (-ΐ Rec.; ἑλωΐ LT; Aram. אֱלָהּ),
Eloi: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 (LXX).†

strong.def: to whelm on, i.e. wet (a part of the person, etc.) by contact with a fluid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἐμ-βάπτω
to dip in: τ. χεῖρα ἐν τ. τρυβλίῳ, Mt 26:23; mid., seq. εἰς, Mk 14:20.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to snort with anger);
strong.def: to have indignation on, i.e. (transitively) to blame, (intransitively) to sigh with chagrin, (specially) to sternly enjoin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐμ-βριμάομαι (T, -έομαι; Bl., § 22, 1), -ῶμαι (< βρίμη, strength, bulk, whence βριμάομαι, to snort with anger), depon., with aor. mid. and pass., [in LXX (Hatch, Essays, 25): Da LXX 11:30 (also Aq., Ps 7:12; Sm., Is 17:13) * ;]
to snort in (of horses, Æsch.), hence, to speak or act with deep feeling (DCG, i, 62b);
(a). to be moved with anger (cf. ἐμβρίμημα, La 2:6): c. dat., Mk 14:5, Jo 11:33; ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Jo 11:38;
(b). to admonish sternly: c. dat., Mt 9:30, Mk 1:43.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G43 (ἀγκάλη);
strong.def: to take in one's arms, i.e. embrace

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐν-αγκαλίζομαι (< ἀγκάλη), [in LXX for חִבֻּק pi., Pr 6:10 24:33 * ;]
to take into one's arms: Mk 9:36 10:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἐν-αντίος, -α, -ον (< ἀντίος, set against), [in LXX: ἐξ ἐναντίας, for נֶגֶד, etc.; ἐναντίον, for לִפְנֵי etc. ;]
over against, opposite, contrary: ἄνεμος, Mt 14:24, Mk 6:48, Ac 27:4; ἐξ ἐναντίας (ellipse obscure, v. Bl., § 44,1; Mozley, Ps 42:1-11), c. gen., Mk 15:39. Metaph., opposed, hostile: I Th 2:15, Ac 26:9 28:17; ὁ ἐξ ἐ., Tit 2:8. Neuter., -ίον, adv., as prep. c. gen., before, in the presence of: Lk 1:6 20:26 24:19 Ac 7:10 (ἔναντι, T), Ac 8:32 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1772 (ἔννομος) and the base of G1507 (εἱλίσσω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐν-ειλέω, -ῶ [in LXX I Ki 21:9 לוּט * ;]
to roll in, wind in: c. acc pers. et dat. rei, Mk 15:46.†

strong.kjv: do, (be) effectual (fervent), be mighty in, shew forth self, work (effectually in)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 ἐνεργέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Nu 8:24 B (עֲבֹדָה צְבׄא צָבָא ), Is 41:4, Pr 21:6 (פָּעַל), Pr 31:12 (גָּמַל), I Es 2:20, Wi 15:11 16:17 * ;] (for full lexical treatment, v. AR, Eph., 243 ff.);
1. intrans., to be at work or in action, to operate (opp. to ἀργέω): seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Mt 14:2, Mk 6:14, Eph 2:2; c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς (Lft., in l), Ga 2:8.
2. Trans., to work, effect, do: c. acc rei, I Co 12:11, Eph 1:11; id, seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., I Co 12:6, Ga 3:5, Phl 2:13; ἐ. ἐνέργειαν, Eph 1:19, 20 Pass. (taken as mid. by Lft., Ga., 204 f.; but v. AR, Eph., l.c.; Milligan, Th., 28 f.; Mayor, Ja., 177 ff.), in NT, "always used of some principle or power at work" (Meyer), to be actuated, set in operation: II Th 2:7; seq. ἐν, Ro 7:5, II Co 1:6 4:12, Eph 3:20, Col 1:29, I Th 2:13; seq. διά, c. gen. rei, Ga 5:6; ἐνεργουμένη (M, Pr., 156), Ja 5:16 (Cremer, 262).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3571 (νύξ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ἔννυχος, -ον (< νύξ), [in LXX: III Mac 5:5 * ;] (in cl. poët.; prose in late Gk. only)
nightly. Neut., adverbially, ἔννυχα (Rec. -χον), by night: Mk 1:35.†

strong.def: liable to (a condition, penalty or imputation)
strong.kjv: in danger of, guilty of, subject to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἔνοχος, -ον (= ἐνεχόμενος), (in LXX for רָשַׁע hi., etc. ;]
1. held in, bound by: c. gen. (cl. c. dat.), δουλείας, He 2:15.
2. In law-phrases
(a). liable to a charge or action (cl. c. dat., of crime): c. dat., of the tribunal (MM, Exp., xiii), Mt 5:21, 22; seq. εἰς (Field, Notes, 4 f.), Mt 5:22
(b). c. gen., of the punishment (Ge 26:11): θανάτου, Mt 26:66, Mk 14:64;
(c). c. gen. (cl. c. dat„ rarely c. prep.; MM, Exp., xiii), of the crime (II Mac 13:6): Mk 3:29;
(d). c. gen., of the thing injured, guilty (absol., in cl.): I Co 11:27, Ja 2:10 (cf. Is 54:17; DB, ii, 268a).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἔνταλμα, -τος, τό (< ἐντέλλω), [in LXX: Jb 23:11 (אָשֻׁר) Jb 23:12, Is 29:13 (מִצְוָה), Is 55:11 (aliter in Heb.)* ;]
a precept: pl., Mt 15:9 (LXX), Mk 7:7, Col 2:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐνταφιασμός, -οῦ (< ἐνταφιάζω),
preparation for burial: Mk 14:8, Jo 12:7.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-αγγέλλω [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi. ;]
to tell out, proclaim: I Pe 2:9 [Mk 16:1-20, "shorter conclusion"] (Cremer, 29).†

strong.def: to start up out of the ground, i.e. germinate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-ανα-τέλλω [in LXX: Ge 2:9, Ps 103(104):14 Ps 131(132):17 Ps 146(147):8 (צָמַח hi.); Ps 111(112):4 (זָרַח) * ;]
1. trans., to cause to spring up (LXX).
2. Intrans. (as ἀνατέλλω, Ge 3:18), to spring up: Mt 13:5, Mk 4:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the same as G160 (αἰφνίδιος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξάπινα = ἐξαπίνης, ἐξαίφνης (q.v.), [in LXX for פִּתְאוֹם, etc. ;]
suddenly: Mk 9:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the genitive case singular feminine of G846 (αὐτός) (G5610 (ὥρα) being understood);
strong.kjv: by and by, immediately, presently, straightway

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * ἐξ-αυτῆς (a κοινή word, = ἐξ αὐτῆς τ. ὥρας)
at once, forthwith: Mk 6:25, Ac 10:33 11:11 21:32 23:30, Phl 2:23.†

strong.def: to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-ορύσσω [in LXX: Pr 29:22; ὀφθαλμόν (-ούς), Jg 16:21, I Ki 11:2 (נָקַר)* ;]
to dig out, dig up: στέγην, Mk 2:4; metaph., ὀφθαλμούς (cf. LXX, ll c.; Herod., viii, 116), Ga 4:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the neuter of G3762 (οὐδείς);
strong.def: to make utterly nothing of, i.e. despise

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξ-ουδενέω (Rec. -όω; T, -θενόω), -ῶ, [in LXX (with vv. ll. -όω, -θενέω, -θενόω) for בּוּז, בָּזָה, מָאַס, בּוּס, etc. ;]
to despise, set at nought: Mk 9:12 (cf. ἐξουθενέω).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
strong.def: to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ἐπ-αγγέλλω [in LXX: Es 4:8 (אָמַר), Pr 13:12, Wi 2:13, al. ;]
1. to announce, proclaim.
2.
(a). to promise;
(b). to profess. Mid., also freq. in both these senses;
(c). to promise: c. dat. pers., He 6:13; c. acc rei, Ro 4:21, Tit 1:2; c. dat pers. et acc rei, Ja 1:12 2:5, II Pe 2:19; ἐπαγγελίαν, I Jo 2:25; c. inf., Mk 14:11, Ac 7:5; seq. λέγων, He 12:26; ptcp., He 10:23 11:11;
(d). to profess: θεοσέβειαν, I Ti 2:10; γνῶσιν, I Ti 6:21. Pass., Ga 3:19 (cf. προ-επαγγέλλω; and v. Cremer, 26).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐπ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX (chiefly metaph.) for אָחַר, הָלַךְ, etc. ;]
to follow after; in NT metaph.; absol.: Mk 16:20 (illustrated by use in verifying accounts; v. MM, Exp., xiv; Milligan; NTD, 78); c. dat. pers., of sins, I Ti 5:24 (cf. Ellic. and CGT, in l); τ. ἴχνεσιν, I Pe 2:21; ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ, I Ti 5:10.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G450 (ἀνίστημι);
strong.def: to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπ-αν-ίστημι [in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;]
to raise up against; mid., to rise up against: seq. ἐπί, c. acc pers., Mt 10:21, Mk 13:12.†

strong.def: occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (G2250 (ἡμέρα) being implied) to-morrow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 † ἐπ-αύριον, adv. [in LXX for מָחָר, Ge 30:33, elsewhere, Ex 9:6, al., for מׇחֳרָת ;]
on the morrow: in NT, ἡ ἐ. (sc. ἡμέρα), Mt 27:62, Mk 11:12, Jo 1:29, Ac 10:9, al

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐπι-γράφω [in LXX for כָּתַב, Nu 17:2 (17); fig., Je 38(31):33, al. ;]
to write upon, inscribe: Mk 15:26, Ac 17:23, Re 21:12; fig., He 8:10 (LXX) He 10:16 (ib).†

strong.def: to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐπι-λύω [in Aq.: Ge 40:8 41:8, 12; Th.: Ho 3:4 * ;]
1. to loose, release.
2. to solve, settle, explain: Mk 4:34, Ac 19:39.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G4476 (ῥαφίς);
strong.def: to stitch upon, i.e. fasten with the needle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ἐπι-ράπτω (Rec. -ρράπτω),
to sew upon: seq. ἐπί, c. acc, Mk 2:21.†

strong.derivation: apparently a middle voice of G2186 (ἐφίστημι) (with G3563 (νοῦς) implied);
strong.def: to put the mind upon, i.e. comprehend, or be acquainted with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἐπίσταμαι (prob. an old mid, of ἐφίστημι, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for יָדַע ;]
to know, know of, understand: c. acc pers., Ac 19:15; c. ptcp., ib. 24:10; c. acc rei, Mk 14:68, Ac 18:25, I Ti 6:4, Ja 4:14, Ju 10; seq. περί, Ac 26:26; ὅτι, ib. 15:7 19:25 22:19; ὡς, ib. 10:28; πῶς, ib. 20:18; ποῦ, He 11:8.†
SYN: γινώσκω (q.v.), οἶδα

strong.def: to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐπι-συν-τρέχω
to run together again: Mk 9:25 (v. Swete, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐρημία, -ας, ἡ (< ἔρημος), [in LXX: Is 60:20, Ez 35:4 (חָרֵב, חׇרְבָּה), ib. 35:9 (שִׁמֲמָה), Wi 17:17, Si 47:17, Ba 4:33, IV Mac 18:8 * ;]
a solitude, wilderness: Mt 15:33, Mk 8:4, II Co 11:26, He 11:38.†

strong.def: finally, i.e. (with G2192 (ἔχω)) at the extremity of life

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐσχάτως adv.,
extremely, utterly; ἐ. ἔχειν (= Lat. in extremis esse), only in late writers (cf. ἐν ἐσχάτοις εἶναι, FlJ, Ant., ix, 8, 6), to be at the point of death: Mk 5:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἔσω, Ion. and old Att.. form of εἴσω (< εἰς), adv., [in LXX for פְנִימָה etc. ;]
1. prop., after verbs of motion (to) within, into: Mt 26:58, Mk 14:54; c. gen., Mk 15:16.
2. As freq. in cl. (= cl. ἔνδον), after verbs of rest, within: Jo 20:26, Ac 5:23; οἱ ἔ. (opp. to οἱ ἔξω), I Co 5:12; ὁ ἔ. ἄνθρωπος, Ro 7:22, II Co 4:16, Eph 3:16.†

strong.def: a good message, i.e. the gospel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
76 εὐαγγέλιον, -ου, τό [in LXX for בְּשׂוֹרָה, בְּשׂרָה, II Ki 4:10 18:22 18:25 * ;]
1. in cl.,
(a). בְּשׂוֹרָה, a reward for good tidings (Hom.; pl., LXX, II Ki 4:10);
(b). in pl., εὐ. θύειν, to make a thank-offering for good tidings (Xen., al.).
2. Later (Luc., Plut., al.), good tidings, good news; in NT of the good tidings of the kingdom of God and of salvation through Christ, the gospel: Mk 1:15, Ac 15:7, Ro 1:16, Ga 2:2, I Th 2:4, al.; c. gen. obj., τ. βασιλείας, Mt 4:23; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ro 15:19, al.; τ. κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ, II Th 1:8; τ. υἱοῦ τ. θεοῦ, Ro 1:9; τ. δόξης τ. μακαρίου θεοῦ, I Ti 1:11; τ. δόξης τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 4:4; of the author, τ. θεοῦ, Ro 15:16, al.; of the teacher, ἡμῶν, Ro 2:16, II Co 4:3, I Th 1:5, II Ti 2:8; of the taught, τ. περιτομῆς, τ. ἀκροβυστίας, Ga 2:7; ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐ., Ga 2:5, 14 Col 1:5; ἡ ἐλπὶς (πίστις) τοῦ εὐ., Col 1:23, Phl 1:27 (v. Cremer, 31 ff.; and on the later eccl. use of the word„ M, Th., 143 f.)

strong.def: to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† εὐκαιρέω, -ῶ (= cl., εὖ σχολῆς ἔχειν; used by Polyb. and Philo; cf. Rutherford, NPhr. 205; MM, Exp., xiv),
to have leisure or opportunity I Co 16:12; c. inf., Mk 6:31; seq. εἰς, to devote one's leisure to, Ac 17:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 εὔ-καιρος, -ον [in LXX: Ps 103 (104):27 (עֵת), II Mac 14:29 15:20, 21, III Mac 4:11 5:44 * ;]
timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, Mk 6:21 (or empty, as in Byz. and MGr.; v. MM, Exp., xiv); βοήθεια, He 4:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** εὐκαίρως adv., [in LXX: Si 18:22 * ;]
seasonably, in season: Mk 14:11; opp. to ἀκ- (Kühner3, iv, 346 d), II Ti 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 εὐσχήμων, -ον (εὖ, σχῆμα), [in LXX: Pr 11:25 * ;]
1. elegant, graceful, comely (Eur., Plat., al.): τὰ εὐ. ἡμῶν (opp. to τὰ ἀσχ- ἡμ-), I Co 12:24; in moral sense, seemly, becoming, I Co 7:35.
2. Also in late Gk. (v. Swete, Mk., l.c.; MM, Exp., xiv), wealthy, influential (RV, of honourable estate): Mk 15:43, Ac 13:50 17:12.†

strong.def: properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 εὐώνυμος, -ον (εὖ, ὄνομα), [in LXX chiefly for שְׂמאׄל ;]
1. of good name or omen
2. Euphemistic for ἀριστερός, left: Ac 21:3, Re 10:2; ἐξ εὐωνύμων, on the left: Mt 20:21, 23 25:33, 41 27:38, Mk 10:40 15:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐφφαθά (Aram. אֶתְפְּתח, v. Abbott, Essays, 142 ff.; DCG, i, 522)
ephphatha, be opened: Mk 7:34.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to the base of G2218 (ζυγός);
strong.def: a belt; by implication, a pocket

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ζώνη, -ης, ἡ (ζώννυμι) [in LXX for אַבְנֵט, חֲגוֹרָה, etc.;]
a belt, girdle: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6, Ac 21:11, Re 1:13 15:6; as a receptacle for money, Mt 10:9, Mk 6:8.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἡδέως adv. (< ἡδύς, sweet), [in LXX: Pr 3:24 (ערב), etc.;]
gladly, with pleasure: Mk 6:20 12:37, II Co 11:19; superlat., ἥδιστα, very gladly (Bl., § 11, 3), II Co 12:9, 15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2456 εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
I. As substantive verb.
1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Ac 17:28, Jo 1:1 8:58 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Re 1:4, 8 4:8 11:17 16:5 (v. Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Ro 4:17, I Co 1:28.
2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mt 24:3, Mk 14:2 15:42, Lk 21:23, Jo 4:6, 23 5:10, al.
3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mt 2:13, 15, Mk 1:45 5:21 15:40, Lk 1:80 5:29, Jo 7:30, al.; seq. εἰς, Mk 2:1; seq. ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mt 1:20 21:25, Mk 11:30, Jo 3:31, al.
4. Impers., ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
(a). there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mt 16:28, Lk 16:19, Jo 3:1 5:2, Ro 3:10, al.; c. dat. (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mt 16:22, Lk 1:7, Jo 18.10, Ro 9:2, al.; ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mt 16:28 19:2, Mk 9:1, al.;
(b). c. inf., = ἔξεστιν (q.v.), it is possible: He 9:5, I Co 11:20, RV (but v. ICC, in l.).
II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mt 5:13 14:15, Lk 1:18, 19, Jo 1:1 4:19, Re 3:9, al. mult.
2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mt 13:19, I Co 9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Ga 4:24, Re 17:15, al.; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν, Mt 27:46, Mk 7:2, Ro 7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mk 3:17, Col 1:24, He 7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mt 26:26-28, Mk 14:22, 24, Lk 22:19, I Co 11:24 (v. ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. c.; DB, iii, 148 f.).
3. C. gen.: qual., etc., Mk 5:42, Lk 3:23, I Co 14:33, He 12:11, al.; part., I Ti 1:20, II Ti 1:15; poss., Mt 5:3, 10, Mk 12:7, Lk 4:7; of service or partisanship, Ro 8:9, I Co 1:12, II Co 10:7, II Ti 2:19.
4. C. dat. (BL, §37, 3): Ac 1:8 9:15, Ro 4:12, I Co 1:18 2:14, Re 21:7, al.
5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
(a). c. ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mt 10:30, Lk 9:32, Jo 3:24, Ac 21:35, I Co 15:19, al;
(b). c. ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mt 7:29, Mk 1:22, Lk 4:31 14:1, Ac 1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Ro 12:9, 10, He 13:5, al.;
(c). c. ptcp. aor. (cl), Lk 23:9.
6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mt 19:5, Mk 10:8, He 8:10, al.
7. C. adv.: Mt 19:20, Mk 4:26, Lk 18:11, al.
8. Ellipses;
(a). of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mt 8:29 24:32, Jo 21:22, 23, He 6:4, al.;
(b). of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mt 14:27, Mk 6:50, al.; absol. (cf. De 32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mk 13:6, Jo 4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).

strong.derivation: plural of a derivative of G2264 (Ἡρώδης);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἡρῳδιανοί (Rec. Ἡρω-), -ῶν, οἱ,
Herodians, partisans of Herod (cf. τὸυς τὰ Ἡρῴδου φρονοῦντας, FlJ, Ant., xiv, 15, 10): Mt 22:16, Mk 3:6 12:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Θαδδαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. תַּדִאַי, תַּדַּי),
Thaddæus: Mt 10:3, Mk 3:18 (WH, mg., Λεββαῖος, q.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 θαμβέω, -ῶ (θάμβος), [in LXX for בּעת ni., pi., etc.;]
1. to be amazed.
2. In late Gk., to astonish, terrify (II Ki 22:5): pass., Mk 1:27 10:32; seq. ἐπί, c. dat. rei, Mk 10:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * θανάσιμος, -ον (< θάνατος),
deadly: Mk 16:[18].†

strong.kjv: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 θαρρέω, -ῶ (later form of θαρσέω), [in LXX: Pr 1:21, Ba 4:21, 27, Da LXX 6:16 (17), IV Mac 13:11 17:4*;]
to be of good cheer or courage, to be confident: II Co 5:6, 8, He 13:6; τ. πεποιθήσει, II Co 10:2; seq. εἰς, II Co 10:1; ἐν, II Co 7:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 θαρσέω, -ῶ (v.s. θαρρέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, c. neg.;]
to be of good courage: imperat., θάραει, -εῖτε, Mt 9:2, 22 14:27, Mk 6:50 10:49, Jo 16:33, Ac 23:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 θαυμαστός, -ή, -όν (< θαυμάζω), [in LXX for פֶּלֶא and cogn. forms (Ps 117(118):22, 23 118(119):129, Is 25:1, al.), יָרֵא ni. (Ex 15:11, Ps 64(65):5, al.), אַדִּיר (Ps 8:1, 9 92(93):4), etc.;]
wonderful, marvellous: Mt 21:42(LXX), Mk 12:11(LXX), Jo 9:30, I Pe 2:9, Re 15:1, 3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 θερμαίνω (< θερμός), [in LXX chiefly for חמם;]
to warm, heat; mid., to warm oneself: Mk 14:54, 67, Jo 18:18, 25, Ja 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 θῆλυς, -εια, -υ, [in LXX chiefly for נְקֵבָה;]
female: as subst., ἡ θ., a female, a woman: Ro 1:26, 27; τὸ θ., Mt 19:4, Mk 10:6, Ga 3:28.†

strong.derivation: diminutive from the same as G2339 (θήρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
46 θηρίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of θήρ), [in LXX chiefly for חַיָּה;]
a wild beast, beast: Mk 1:13, Ac 11:6 28:4, 5, Tit 1:12, He 12:20, Ja 3:7, Re 6:8; of Antichrist, Re 11:7, 13-20.†

strong.derivation: akin to the base of G5147 (τρίβος);
strong.kjv: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 θλίβω, [in LXX chiefly (ὁ θλίβων) for צוּר;]
to press: c. acc. pers., Mk 3:9; ὁδὸς τεθλιμμένη, a narrow (compressed) way, Mt 7:14. Metaph. (as freq. in LXX), to oppress, afflict, distress: c. acc. pers., II Th 1:6; pass. (Vg., tribulor, tribulationem patior), II Co 1:6 4:8 7:5, I Th 3:4, II Th 1:7, I Ti 5:10, He 11:37 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-θλίβω).†

strong.kjv: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
45 θλίψις (LTr., θλῖψις), -εως, ἡ (< θλίβω), [in LXX for צָרָה, etc.;]
pressure (Arist.). In LXX and NT metaph., tribulation, affliction, distress: Mt 24:9, 21, 29, Mk 13:19, 24, Jo 16:21, Ac 7:11 11:19, Ro 12:12, II Co 1:4, 8 4:17 6:4 7:4 8:2, 13, Phl 4:14, II Th 1:6, Ja 1:27, Re 1:9 2:9, 22 7:14; c. ἀνάγκη (q.v.), I Th 3:7; στενοχωρία (which from the order of the words would appear to be the stronger term), Ro 2:9 8:35; διωγμός, Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17, II Th 1:4; θ. ἔχω, Jo 16:33, I Co 7:28, Re 2:10; ἔρχεσθαι ἐπί, Ac 7:11; ἐν θλίψει, I Th 1:6; pl., Ac 7:10 14:22 20:23, Ro 5:3, Eph 3:13, I Th 3:3, He 10:33; τ. Χριστοῦ, Col 1:24; θ. τῆς καρδίας, II Co 2:4; θ. ἐγείρειν, Phl 1:17.†

strong.def: to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor
strong.kjv: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 θορυβέω, -ῶ (< θόρυβος), [in LXX: Na 2:3(4) (רעל ho.), Da LXX 8:17 (בּעת ni.), Jg 3:26, Wi 18:19, Si 40:6*;]
1. to make a noise or uproar: mid., of loud and ostentatious lamentation, Mt 9:23, Mk 5:39, Ac 20:10.
2. Trans., to trouble, throw into confusion: τ. πόλιν, Ac 17:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 θόρυβος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for הָמוֹן, etc.;]
a noise, uproar, tumult, as of an excited mob: Mt 26:5 27:24, Mk 14:2, Ac 20:1 21:34 24:18; of mourners, = ὄχλος θορυβούμενος, Mk 5:38.†

strong.def: to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 θροέω, -ῶ (< θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: Ca 5:4 [המה*;]
1. to cry aloud, make an outcry.
2. to utter aloud.
3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: Mt 24:6, Mk 13:7, Lk 24:37 (WH, mg.), II Th 2:2 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 126).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * θυγάτριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of θυγάτηρ),
a little daughter, a term of endearment used in late Gk. (cf. B1., § 27, 4): Mk 5:23 7:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 θυρωρός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ (< θύρα, + οὖρος, a guardian), [in LXX: IV Ki 7:11 (שׁוֹעֵר), Ez 44:11 (פְּקֻדָּה), II Ki 4:6, I Es 7*;]
a door-keeper, porter: ὁ, Mk 13:34, Jo 10:3; ἡ, Jo 18:16, 17.†

strong.derivation: second person singular imperative active of G1492 (εἴδω);
strong.def: used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 ἴδε (Attic ἰδέ; the "later" accentuation is also found in Hom.; Veitch, 215)
1. prop., 2 aor. imperat. of ὁράω, q.v.
2. As interjection, apart from the construction of the sentence, and used where one or many are addressed, see! behold! lo!: Mt 25:20, 22, 25, Mk 2:24 3:34 11:21 13:1, 21 15:4, 35 16:6, Jo 1:29, 36, 48 3:26 5:14 7:26 11:3, 36 12:19 16:29 18:21 19:4, 14, 26, 27, Ga 5:2.†

strong.def: Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰδουμαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. אֱדוֹם), [in LXX: II Ki 8:14, a1.; elsewhere, as Ge 25:30, Ἐδώμ;]
Idumæa: Mk 3:8.†

strong.def: a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἱεροσολυμεῖτης (WH, Ἰερ-; Rec. -μίτης), -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Si 50:27(29) II Mac 4:22, 39 (V* -μήτης) 18:5*;]
an inhabitant of Jerusalem: Mk 1:5, Jo 7:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἰχθύδιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ἰχθύς),
a little fish: Mt 15:34, Mk 8:7.†

strong.def: Joses, the name of two Israelites

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἰωσῆς, -ῆ (Rec. -ή, Lk 3:29; AV, Jose; v.s. Ἰησοῦς, 3), and -ῆτος (Mk 6:3 15:40, 47), ὁ,
Joses;
1. brother of our Lord: Mk 6:3, Mt 13:55 (Rec., v.s. Ἰωσήφ).
2. Son of Mary: Mt 27:56 (-σήφ, WH, txt), Mk 15:40, 47.
3. v.s. Βαρνάβας.†

strong.derivation: from G2596 (κατά) and the same as G1476 (ἑδραῖος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 καθ-έδρα, -ας, ἡ (< κατά, + ἔδρα, a seat), [in LXX for מוֹשָׁב and cogn. forms;]
a chair, seat: Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15; of teachers, Mt 23:2.†

strong.def: Cæsaria, the name of two places in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 Καισαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ,
Cæsarea;
1. Cæsarea Philippi, at the foot of Lebanon: Mt 16:13, Mk 8:27.
2. Cæsarea of Palestine, on the sea-coast: Ac 8:40 9:30 10:1, 24 11:11 12:19 18:22 21:8, 16 23:23, 33 25:1, 4, 6, 13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 κἀκεῖ (by crasis for καὶ ἐκεῖ, and so sometimes written, v. infr.),
and there, there also: Mt 5:23 (κ. ἐ., Tr., mg.) 10:11 28:10 (κ. ἐ., T), Mk 1:35 (κ. ἐ., L) 38 (κ. ἐ., WH) 14:15 (κ. ἐ., WH), Jo 11:54, Ac 14:7 17:13 22:10 25:20 27:6.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2556 (κακός) and G3056 (λόγος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κακολογέω, -ῶ (< κακολόγος, slanderous), [in LXX: Ex 21:16 22:28, I Ki 3:13, Pr 20:20, Ez 22:7 (קלל pi., hi.), II Mac 4:1*;]
to speak ill of, revile, abuse: c. acc. pers., Mt 15:4, Mk 7:10(LXX) 9:39; c. acc. rei, Ac 19:9.†

strong.kjv: Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from G5477 (Χαναάν))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) Καναναῖος, -ου, ὁ (late Heb. קַנְאָנָא),
a Cananæan or Zealot (cf. ζηλωτής): Mt 10:4, Mk 3:18 (Rec. -νίτης).†

strong.def: to hunt down, i.e. search for

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατα-διώκω, [in LXX chiefly for רדף;]
"perfective" compound (M, Pr., 116), to pursue closely, follow up;
(a). with hostile intent (Thuc., i, 49, Ge 31:36 al.);
(b). with kindly intention (Ps 22 (23):6, I Ki 30:22, cf. Si 27:17): Mk 1:36.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-κόπτω , [in LXX for נכה hi., כּתת pi., etc.;]
to cut up, cut in pieces (cf. Is 27:9, Je 21:7, II Ch 34:7): ἑαυτὸν λίθοις, Mk 5:5.†

strong.def: to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate
strong.kjv: exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κατα-κυριεύω, [in LXX: Ge 1:28 (כּבשׁ), Ps 109 (110):2 (רדה) Si 17:4, al.;]
to gain or exercise dominion (over);
(a). absol. (Arist.);
(b). c. gen. (Arist., al.): Mt 20:25, Mk 10:42, Ac 19:16, I Pe 5:3.†

strong.def: to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 κατα-λαμβάνω, [in LXX for נשׂג hi., לכד, etc.;]
1. to lay hold of, seize, appropriate: Mk 9:18; c. acc. rei, I Co 9:24, Phl 3:12, 13.
2. to overtake: as carrel. of διώκω (Field, Notes, 158 f.), Ro 9:30; ἡ ἡμέρα, I Th 5:4; of evils, Jo 1:5 12:35 (cf. 6:17 T); hence, to surprise, discover: Jo 8:[3, 4],
3. Of mental action, to apprehend, comprehend; so mid., in NT (M, Pr., 158): Eph 3:18; seq. ὅτι, Ac 4:13 10:34; c. acc. et inf., Ac 25:25 (MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κατα-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Jb 15:6, Pr 25:18 (ענה), al.;]
to bear witness againt: c. acc. rei et gen. pers., Mt 26:62 27:13, Mk 14:60.†

strong.def: to turn upside down, i.e. upset

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-στρέφω, [in LXX for הפךְ, etc., Ge 19:21, Je 20:16, al.;]
1. to turn down, turn over; as, the soil.
2. to overturn, overthrow: Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15; pass. pf. ptcp., Ac 15:16(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κατα-χέω, [in LXX for יצק, נטה, עטה hi.;]
to pour down upon: c. gen. (cl.), Mk 14:3; seq. ἐπί, c. gen., Mt 26:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * κατ-εξουσιάζω,
to exercise authority over: c. gen. pers., Mt 20:25, Mk 10:42.†

strong.def: residence (properly, the act; but by implication, concretely, the mansion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κατ-οίκησις, -εως, ἡ (< κατοικέω), [in LXX for ישׁב, Ge 10:30, al.;]
dwelling: Mk 5:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† καυματίζω (< καῦμα),
to burn or scorch up: c. acc. seq. ἐν πυρί, Re 16:8. Pass., Mt 13:14, Mk 4:6; seq. καῦμα μέγα, Re 16:9.†

strong.def: a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† κεντυρίων, -ωνος, ὁ (Lat. centurio);
a centurion: Mk 15:39, 44, 45 (Mt, Lk, use ἑκατόνταρχος (-ης), q.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** κεφαλιόω (Rec. -αιόω, [so in LXX: Si 35 (32):8*]), -ῶ (< κεφάλιον, dimin. of κεφαλή, in late writers);
1. (-αιόω) to sum up (Thuc., al.).
2. (In NT, only) to wound on the head: Mk 12:4.†

strong.def: properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† κῆνσος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. census),
a poll-tax: Mt 17:25 22:17, Mk 12:14 (WH, mg., ἐπικεφάλαιον); τ. νόμισμα τοῦ κ., Mt 22:19 (v. MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 κινέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for נוּעַ hi., רמשׂ, etc.;]
1. to set in motion, move: Mt 23:4; τ. κεφαλήν (Ps 21 (22):8, al.), Mt 27:39, Mk 15:29; pass. (cf. Ge 7:21), Ac 17:28.
2. to remove: Re 2:5 6:14.
3. to excite, stir up: Ac 24:5; pass., 21:30 (cf. μετα-, συν-κινέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † κλοπή, -ῆν, ἡ (< κλέπτω), [in LXX for גּנב;]
theft: pl., Mt 15:19, Mk 7:22.†

strong.def: a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† κοδράντης, -ου, ὁ (Lat. quadrans, the fourth part of an as),
a quadrans (AV, farthing): Mt 5:26, Mk 12:42.†

strong.def: common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 κοινός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Pr 1:14 (אֶחָד) 21:9 25:24 (חֶבֶר), Wi 7:3, al.;]
1. common (general; = Lat. communis): Ac 2:44 4:32; κ. πίστις, Tit 1:4; σωτηρία, Ju 3.
2. common (ordinary; = vulgaris); hence in LXX (I Mac 1:47, al.) and NT, unhallowed, unclean (cl., βέβηλος, q.v.): Mk 7:2, 5, Ac 10:14, 28 11:8, Ro 14:14, He 10:29, Re 21:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 κοινόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: IV Mac 7:6 אR*;]
1. in cl., to make common.
2. In LXX, IV Mac 7:6, and NT (as κοινός, 2), to make ceremonially unclean, to profane (= cl., βεληλόω): Mt 15:11, 18, 20, Mk 7:15, 18, 20, 23, Ac 21:28; pass., He 9:13.
3. to count unclean (cf. δικαιόω): Ac 10:15 11:9.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G2849 (κολάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 *† κολαφίζω (< κόλαφος = Att., κόνδυλοι, the knuckles, the closed fist),
to strike with the fist, to buffet: Mt 26:67, Mk 14:65, II Co 12:7; pass., I Co 4:11, I Pe 2:20.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of (a small coin;
strong.def: probably akin to G2854 (κολλούριον)); a coin-dealer

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† κολλυβιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< κόλλυβος, a small coin, a rate of exchange),
a money-changer: Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15, Jo 2:15 (cf. κερματιοτής).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G2849 (κολάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κολοβόω, -ῶ (< κολοβός, docked), [in LXX: II Ki 4:12 (קצץ pi.)*;]
to cut off, amputate (LXX), hence, to curtail, shorten: Mt 24:22, Mk 13:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κοπάζω (< κόπος), [in LXX: Ge 8:1, Es 2:1 7:10 (שׁכךְ), Ru 1:18, al. (חדל), Jh 1:11, 12 (שׁתק), al.;]
to grow weary; of the wind (Hdt., Jh 1:11, 12), to abate, cease raging: Mt 14:32, Mk 4:39 6:51.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a maiden);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 κοράσιον, -ου, τό, (dimin. of κόρη), [in LXX chiefly for נַעֲרָה, Ru 2:8, al.; in Jl 3 (4):3, Za 8:5 for יַלְדָּה;]
a colloquial word which survives in MGr. (Kennedy, Sourcs, 154), girl, maiden: Mt 9:24, 25 14:11, Mk 5:41, 42 6:22, 28.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (H07133);
strong.def: a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κορβάν (Rec., T, -βᾶν), indecl. (Heb. קׇרְבָּן),
an offering, a gift offered to God: Mk 7:11 (cf. κορβανᾶς).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κούμ (Tr., txt., κοῦμ, Rec. κοῦμι) (Heb. imperat. masc., used as an interjection, קוּם),
koum (arise): Mk 5:41.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 (KJV) **† κράβαττος (Rec. κράββατος), ου, ὁ (a Macedonian word, = Lat. grabatus, cl. σκίμπους), [in Aq.: Am 3:12*;]
a camp bed, pallet: Mk 2:4, 9, 11, 12 6:55, Jo 5:8-11, Ac 5:15 9:33 (v. Swete, Mk., 2:4, and cf. κλίνη).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 κτῆμα, -τος, τό (< κτάομαι), [in LXX for כֶּרֶם, etc.;]
a possession, property: Mt 19:22, Mk 10:22, Ac 2:45 5:1.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G2932 (κτάομαι) (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 κτίζω, [in LXX chiefly for בּרא, Ps 50 (51):10, al.; also for קנה, Ge 14:19, Pr 8:22; יצר, Is 22:11 46:11, Wi 2:23, Si 1:4, 9 (and freq.), I Es 4:53, a1.;]
1. in cl., to people or found a region or city (I Es 4:53).
2. In LXX and NT, of God, to create: Mk 13:19, I Co 11:9, Col 1:16 3:10, Eph 3:9, I Ti 4:3, Re 4:11 10:6; ὁ κτίσας, Mt 19:4 (WH, R, mg.), Ro 1:25; of the divine operation on the soul, Eph 2:10, 15 4:24 (cf. Ps 51:10).†

strong.def: original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 κτίσις, -εως, ἡ (< κτίζω), [in LXX: Ps 103 (104):24 (קִנְיָן), Pr 1:13 A (הוֹן), To 8:5, Wi 2:6, Si 16:17, III Mac 2:2, al.;]
1. a founding, settling, foundation (cl.).
2. In LXX and NT,
(a). the act of creating, creation: Mk 10:6 (Swete, in l.), Mk 13:19, Ro 1:20, II Pe 3:4;
(b). that which has been created, creation: Ro 1:25 8:39, He 4:13; καινὴ κ., II Co 5:17, Ga 6:15; πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κ. (Hort., in l.), I Pe 2:13; collectively, of the sum of created things (Wi 19:6, Jth 16:14), Mk 16:[15], Col 1:15, 23, He 9:11, Re 3:14; of the irrational creation, Ro 8:19-22.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G2949 (κῦμα) (through the idea of circularity;
strong.def: compare G2945 (κύκλῳ), G1507 (εἱλίσσω)); to roll about

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κυλίω late form of κυλίνδω, [in LXX: Jos 10:18, I Ki 14:33, al. (גּלל), IV Ki 9:33 (שׁמט), al.;]
to roll, roll along. Pass., to be rolled; of persons (in Hom, as sign of grief), to roll or wallow: Mk 9:20.†

strong.def: rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * κυλλός, -ή, -όν,
1. crooked, crippled: Mt 15:30, 31 (WH, txt. om.);
2. maimed: Mt 18:8, Mk 9:43.†

strong.derivation: from (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 κῦμα, -τος, τό (< κύω, to be pregnant, to swell), [in LXX chiefly for גַּל;]
a wave: pl., Mt 8:24 14:24, Mk 4:37; κ. θαλάσσης, fig., Ju 13.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2965 (κύων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * κυνάριον, -ου, τό (in Att. also κυνίδιον, dim. of κύων),
a little dog: Mt 15:26, 27, Mk 7:27, 28.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G2949 (κῦμα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κύπτω, [in LXX chiefly for קדד;]
to bow the head, stoop down: Mk 1:7; seq. κάτω, Jo 8:[6, 8] (cf. ἀνα-, παρα-, συν-κύπτω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κωμόπολις, -εως, ἡ,
a country town: Mk 1:38 (v. Swete, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 λαλία, -ᾶς, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, דִּבְרָה;]
1. loquacity.
2. talk, speech, conversation: Mt 26:73 (cf. Ca 4:3), Jo 4:42 8:43.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (H04100 with prepositional prefix);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λαμά (Heb. לָמָה, v.l. λεμά = Aram. לְמָא),
why: Mt 27:46 (WH, mg., λεμά TTr., WH, txt., λεμά L), Mk 15:34 (λεμά LT, λαμμᾶ, Rec.).†

strong.derivation: from the same as the first part of G2991 (λαξευτός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † λατομέω, -ῶ (< λατόμος, a stonecutter, IV Ki 12:12, al.; < λᾶς, τέμνω; cf. λαξευτός), [in LXX: I Ch 22:2, al. (חצב); Ex 21:33, Num_21:18 (כּרה);]
to hew, hew out stones: Mt 27:60, Mk 15:46.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λευκαίνω (< λευκός), [in LXX: Ps 50 (51):7, Is 1:18 (לבן hi.), etc.;]
to whiten, make white: c. acc. rei, Mk 9:3, Re 7:14.†

strong.derivation: neuter singular of the same as G3062 (λοιποί);
strong.kjv: besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
55 λοιπός, -ή, -όν (< λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יֶתֶר, also for שְׁאָר, etc.;]
the remaining, the rest,
1. pl., οἱ λ.: c. subst., Mt 25:11, Ac 2:37, Ro 1:13, al.; absol., Mt 22:6, Mk 16:[13], Lk 24:10, al.; οἱ λ. οἱ (Bl., § 47, 8), Ac 28:9, I Th 4:13, Re 2:24; οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων (LS, s.v., ad. init.), Re 9:20; τὰ λ., Mk 4:19, Re 3:2, al.
2. Neut. sing. (acc. ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.;
(a). for the future, henceforth: Mk 14:41, I Co 7:29 (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), He 10:13; anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), Ac 27:20, II Ti 4:8; τοῦ λ. (sc. χρόνου; LS, s.v.; M, Pr., 73; Bl., § 36, 13), Ga 6:17, Eph 6:10;
(b). besides, moreover, for the rest: Phl 3:1 4:8; anarth., I Co 1:16 4:2, I Th 4:1 (M, Th., in l; Lft., Notes, 51).

strong.def: to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad
strong.kjv: cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
26 λυπέω, -ῶ (< λύπη), [in LXX for חרה, etc.;]
to distress, grieve, cause pain or grief: c. acc. pers., II Co 2:2, 5 7:8; pass., Mt 14:9 17:23 18:31 19:22 26:22, Mk 10:22 14:19, Jo 16:20 21:17, Ro 14:15, II Co 2:4, I Th 4:13, I Pe 1:6; λ. καὶ ἀδημονεῖν, Mt 26:37; opp. to χαίρειν, II Co 6:10; κατὰ θεόν, II Co 7:9, 11; τ. πνεῦμα τ. ἅγιον, Eph 4:30 (cf. συν-λνπέω).†

strong.def: something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λύτρον, -ον, τό (< λύω), [in LXX (Pent.15, Pr2, Isa1) for פִּדְיוֹם and cogn. forms, גְּאֻלָּה, כֹּפֶר, מְחִיר;]
a ransom (as for a life, Ex 21:30; for slaves, Le 19:20; for captives, Is 45:13): ἀντὶ πολλῶν, Mt 20:28, Mk 10:45 (v. Swete, in l., and for discussion of λ. and its cognates, Westc., He., 295 f.; Deiss., LAE, 331 f.; cf. also ἀντί-λύτρον).†

strong.derivation: prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, , is used as an alternate in certain tenses;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 μανθάνω, [in LXX chiefly for למד;]
1. to learn, esp. by inquiry: absol., I Co 14:31, I Ti 2:11, II Ti 3:7; c. acc. rei, Jo 7:15 (sc. αὐτά), Ro 16:17, I Co 14:35, Phl 4:9, II Ti 3:14, Re 14:3; seq. quaes. indir., Mt 9:13; Χριστόν, Eph 4:20 (ICC, in l.); seq. ἀπό, c. gen. rei, Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28; ἀπό, c. gen. pers., Mt 11:29, Col 1:7; παρά, c. gen. pers., II Ti 3:14; ἐν, c. dat. pers., I Co 4:6; "point" aorist (M, Pr., 117), to ascertain, seq. ὅτι, Ac 23:27; c. acc. seq. ἀπό, Ga3:2.
2. to learn by use and practice, acquire the habit of, be accustomed to: c. inf. (Bl., § 69, 4), I Ti 5:4, Tit 3:14; id. c. nom, in pred. (Bl., § 72, 1), Phl 4:11; c. acc. rei seq. ἀπό, He 5:8; ἀργαὶ μανθάνουσιν (EV, they learn to be idle; Bl., § 73, 5; Field, Notes, 210), I Ti 5:13.†

strong.derivation: accusative case of a derivative of the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι) (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μάτην (prop. acc. of μάτη, a fault, folly), adv., [in LXX for הֶבֶל, שָׁוְא, etc.;]
in vain, to no purpose: Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † μεγιστάν, -ᾶνος, ὁ (< μέγιστος), [in LXX chiefly for שַׂר, Je 24:8, al.; רַבְרְבָן, Da LXX TH 5:23, al.; freq. in Sir (sing., Si 4:7);] usually pl., οἱ μ.,
the chief men, nobles (Manetho, FlJ, al.): Mk 6:21, Re 6:15 18:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 **† μεθερμηνεύω, [in LXX: Si prol. 23*;]
to translate, interpret: Mt 1:23, Mk 5:41 15:22, 34, Jo 1:38, 42, Ac 4:36 13:8 (cf. ἑρμηνεύω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μέλι, -τος, τό, [in LXX freq. (Ge 43:11, al.) for דְּבַשׁ; for נֹפֶת, Pr 5:3;]
honey: Re 10:9, 10; ἄγριον (q.v.), Mt 3:4, Mk 1:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† μετα-μορφόω, -ῶ [in Sm.: Ps 33 (34):1*;]
to transform, transfigure: pass., of Christ's transfiguration, Mt 17:2, Mk 9:2 (cf. Lk 9:29); of Christians, Ro 12:2, II Co 3:18.†

strong.def: to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μηκύνω (< μῆκος), [in LXX: Is 44:14 (גּדל pi.), Ez 12:25, 28 (משׁךְ ni.)*;]
to lengthen, extend: of causing plants to grow, Is 44:14; pass. (mid., Swete, in l.), to grow: Mk 4:27.†

strong.derivation: masculine or neuter singular of G3398 (μικρός) (as noun);
strong.def: a small space of time or degree

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μισθωτός, -ή, όν, (< μισθόω), [in LXX for שָׂכִיר, Ex 12:45, al.;]
hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant, hireling: Mk 1:20, Jo 10:12, 13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μνημόσυνον, -ου, τό (< μνήμων, mindful), [in LXX freq. for זֵכֶר, זִכָּרוֹן and cogn. forms;]
a memorial: Mt 26:13, Mk 14:9, Ac 10:4 (where cf. Le 2:9, 16 5:12, Nu 5:28, Si 45:16, al.).†

strong.kjv: having an impediment in his speech

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † μογι-λάλος, -ον (< μόγις, λάλος), [in LXX: Is 35:6 (אִלֵּם)*;]
speaking with difficulty: Mk 7:32 (Tr., txt., μογγιλάλος, thick-voiced, v. Swete, in l.).†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of the feminine of G3432 (μοιχός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μοιχάω, -ῶ (= cl. μοιχεύω), [in LXX (mid., absol. and c. acc., with party of either sex as subj.): Je 3:8 5:7 7:9 9:2 (1) 23:14 36 (29):23, Ez 16:32 23:37, 43 (נאף)*;]
to commit adultery with: c. acc., fem. In NT always mid. in same sense; of the man: absol., Mt 5:32 19:9 (WH, txt., R, mg., om.); seq. ἐπ’ αὐτήν, Mk 10:11; of the woman: Mk 10:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μοιχεία, -ας, ἡ (< μοιχύω), [in LXX: Ho 2:2 (4) (נַאֲפוּפִים), 4:2 (נָאֹף), Je 13:27 (נִאֻפִים), Wi 14:26*;]
adultery: Jo 8:[3]; pl. (v. WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), Mt 15:19, Mk 7:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * μον-όφθαλμος, -ον (< μόνος), Ionic and κοινή,
one-eyed, having one eye: Mt 18:9, Mk 9:47.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the base of G3313 (μέρος) (through the idea of adjustment of parts);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μορφή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Jg 8:18 A (תֹּאַר), Jb 4:16 (תְּמוּנָה), Is 44:13 (תַּבְנִית), Da LXX 3:19 (צְלֵם), Da TH 4:33 5:6, 9, 10 7:28 (זִיו), To 1:13, Wi 18:1, IV Mac 15:4*;]
form, shape, appearance (Hom., Eur., Æsch., al.); in philos. lang. the specific character or essential form (Arist., v. Gifford, Inc., 26 ff.): Mk 16:[12], Phl 2:6, 7.†

strong.derivation: probably ultimately from the base of G3433 (μόλις) (through the idea of hardship);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † μύλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for רֵחַים, Nu 11:8, De 24:6, al.;]
1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX): Mt 24:41, Re 18:22.
2. a mill-stone (Anth.): Re 18:21 (T); μ. ὀνικός, Mt 18:6, Mk 9:42 (v. Swete, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μυρίζω (< μύρον),
Ionic and poët. (comic), to anoint: Mk 14:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νάρδος, -ου, ἡ (Heb. נֵרְדְּ, both from Sanscrit narda, v. Boisacq, s.v.), [in LXX: Ca 1:12 4:13, 14 (נֵרְדְּ)*;]
nard;
(a). an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment;
(b). ointment of nard: Mk 14:3, Jo 12:3.†

strong.derivation: from the inseparable negative particle (not) and G2068 (ἐσθίω);
strong.def: not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ (< νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω),in cl., chiefly poët., [in LXX: Da LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)*;]
not eating, fasting: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:3.†

strong.def: to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 νίπτω, late form of νίζω, [in LXX chiefly for רחץ;]
to wash, usually of a part of the body: c. acc. pers., Jo 13:8; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:5, 6, 8, 12, 14, I Ti 5:10; mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: Jo 9:7, 11, 15; τ. χεῖρας, Mt 15:2, Mk 7:3; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mt 6:17 (in cl. Att. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).†

strong.def: to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 νοέω -ῶ (< νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בּין, also for שׂכל hi., etc;]
1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, v. MM, xvii): absol., Mt 16:9, Mk 8:17; c. acc., Eph 3:4, I Ti 1:7; c. dat. instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jo 12:40; pass., Ro 1:20; seq. ὅτι, Mt 15:17 16:11, Mk 7:18; c. acc. et inf., He 11:8.
2. to think, consider: absol., Mt 24:15, Mk 13:14, Eph 3:20; c. acc. rei, II Ti 2:7. (cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†

strong.derivation: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 (νοῦς) and G2192 (ἔχω);
strong.def: in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * νουνεχῶς, adv. (< νοῦς, ἔχω),
sensibly, discreetly: Mk 12:34.†

strong.def: by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ξέστης, -ου, ὁ (a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al.: Le 14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)*;]
1. a sextarius (about a pint).
2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone: Mk 7:4.†

strong.derivation: feminine (abstract) of a compound of G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G1430 (δῶμα);
strong.def: architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 † οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ (< οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: I Ch 29:1 A (בִּירָה), Ez 17:17 40:2 (בּנה, מִבְנֶה), Si 22:16 40:19, al.;] = cl. οἰκοδομία (q.v.), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.),
1. the act of building; in NT always metaph., building up, edifying: Ro 14:19 15:2, I Co 14:26, II Co 10:8 13:10, Eph 4:29; c. gen. obj., I Co 14:12, II Co 12:19, Eph 4:12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., I Co 14:3.
2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Mt 24:1, Mk 13:1, 2; metaph., I Co 3:9, II Co 5:1, Eph 2:21.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G3588 (ὁ), G3739 (ὅς), and G3745 (ὅσος);
strong.def: such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so
strong.kjv: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 οἷος, -α, -ον, relat. pron.,
qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος: Mt 24:21, Mk 9:3, II Co 12:20, I Th 1:5, II Ti 3:11, Re 16:18; seq. τοιοῦτος, I Co 15:48, II Co 10:11; id. redundant, Mk 13:19; τ. αὐτὸν . . . σἷον, Phl 1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Ro 9:6.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of G3650 (ὅλος) and a derivative of G2545 (καίω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ὁλοκαύτωμα, -τος, τό (< ὅλος, καίω), [in LXX chiefly for עֹלָה;]
a whole burnt offering: Mk 12:33, He 10:6, 8(LXX) (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 113 f.).†

strong.def: a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὄμμα, -τος, τό, in cl. chiefly poët.; [in LXX for עַיִן (Pr5, Wi2, IV Mac3)*;]
an eye: pl., Mt 20:34, Mk 8:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὁμοιάζω (< ὅμοιος),
to be like: Mt 23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Mt 26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. Cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.)†

strong.def: belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ὀνικός, -ή, -όν (< ὄνος),
of or for an ass: μύλος ὀ., Mt 18:6, Mk 9:42 (elsewhere only in π.; v. MM, xviii).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary (a bound or limit);
strong.def: a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region)
