classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Ἀθῆναι, -ῶν, αἱ (plural because consisting of several parts),
Athens: Ac 17:15, 16 18:1, I Th 3:1.†

strong.def: an Athenæan or inhabitant of Athenæ

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀθηναῖος, -α, -ον,
Athenian: Ac 17:21, 22.†

strong.derivation: from (a contest in the public lists);
strong.def: to contend in the competitive games

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀθλέω, -ῶ (in cl. also ἀθλεύω, < ἆθλος, a contest, in war or in sport),
to contend in games, wrestle, combat: II Ti 2:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἄθλησις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀθλέω),
a contest, combat, esp. of athletes; fig., a struggle: He 10:32 (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2372 (θυμός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀθυμέω, -ῶ (ἄ-θυμος, without heart), [in LXX for חרה, etc.;]
to be disheartened: Col 3:21.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι) (meaning a penalty);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀθῷος (Rec. wrongly, -ῶος; LS, s.v.; Mayser, 131), -ον (< θωή, a penalty), [in LXX chiefly for נקה ni., pi., נָקִי;]
1. unpunished (MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. innocent: Mt 27:4 (WH, R, mg., δίκαιον) 27:24.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἴγειος (WH, -γιος), -α, -ον (< αἶξ, a goat), [in LXX for עֵז;]
of a goat: He 11:37 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from (to rush) and G251 (ἅλς) (in the sense of the sea;
strong.def: a beach (on which the waves dash)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 αἰγιαλός, -οῦ, ὁ (on the derivation, v. Boisacq, s.v.), [in LXX: Jg 5:17 (חוֹף), Si 24:14*;]
the sea-shore, beach (cf. Field, Notes, 146; DCG, i, 175 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 13:2, 48, Jo 21:4, Ac 21:5 27:39, 40.†

strong.def: an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Αἰγύπτιος, -α, ον,
Egyptian: Ac 7:22, 24, 28 21:38, He 11:29.†

strong.def: Ægyptus, the land of the Nile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 Αἴγυπτος, ου, ἡ,
Egypt: Mt 2:13-15, 19, Ac 2:10 7:9-39, He 3:16 11:26, 27; γῆ Αἴ., Ac 7:40 13:17, He 8:9, Ju 5 (cf. Ex 5:12, al.); ἡ Αἴ., Ac 7:11; fig., of Jerusalem as hostile to God, Re 11:8.†

strong.def: everduring (forward and backward, or forward only)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀΐδιος, -ον (< ἀεί), [in LXX: Wi 7:26, IV Mac 10:15*;]
everlasting (freq. in Inscr.; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ro 1:20, Ju 6.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1492 (εἴδω) (through the idea of downcast eyes);
strong.def: bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards God) awe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** αἰδώς (-όος), -οῦς, ἡ, [in LXX: III Mac 1:19 4:5*;]
a sense of shame, modesty: I Ti 2:9 (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from (to scorch) and (the face, from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Αἰθίοψ, -οπος, ὁ (< αἴθω, to burn, ὤψ, face; i.e. swarthy), [in LXX for כּוּשׁ;]
Ethiopian: Ac 8:27.†

strong.derivation: from G129 (αἷμα) and a derivative of G1632 (ἐκχέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† αἱματεκχυσία, -ας, ἡ (< αἷμα, ἐκ, χέω),
shedding of blood (Eccl.; Cremer, 71): He 9:22.†

strong.def: to flow blood, i.e. have a hæmorrhage
strong.kjv: diseased with an issue of blood

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἱμορροέω, (< αἷμα, ῥέω), [in LXX: Le 15:33 (דָּוֶה)*;]
to lose blood, suffer from a flow of blood (Hipp.): Mt 9:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Αἰνέας, -οῦ, ὁ,
Æneas: Ac 9:33, 34.†

strong.def: a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a thank(-offering)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † αἴνεσις, -εως, ἡ (< αἰνέω), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹדָה, תְּהִלָּה;]
praise (Eccl.): θυσία αἰνέσεως (Le 7:12, זֶבַח תּוֹדָה), He 13:15.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G136 (αἶνος) (in its primary sense);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἴνιγμα, -ατος, τό (< αἰνίσσομαι, to speak in riddles; < αἰνός = δεινός, dread, strange), [in LXX for חִידָה, Nu 12:8 and always exc. De 28:37 (שַׁמָּה);]
a dark saying, riddle: I Co 13:12 (cf. Nu 12:8).†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of G5869, place of springs);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Αἰνών, ἡ, indecl. (cf. Heb. עַיִן, a spring),
Aenon: Jo 3:23.†

strong.def: to take for oneself, i.e. to prefer

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 αἱρέω, [in LXX for אמר hi., בּחר, etc.;]
to take; Mid., -ομαι (M, Pr., 158 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.), to choose: Phl 1:22, II Th 2:13, He 11:25. (Cf. ἀν-, ἀφ-, δι-, ἐξ-, καθ-, περι-, προ-αιρέω.)†

strong.def: properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion
strong.kjv: heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 αἵρεσις, -εως, ἡ (< αἱρέω, -ομαι), [in LXX for נְדָבָה,]
1. capture.
2. choosing, choice (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).
3. that which is chosen, hence, opinion; esp. a peculiar opinion, heresy: I Co 11:19, Ga 5:20, II Pe 2:1, R, txt.
4. In late writers (MM, VGT), of a set of persons professing particular principles or opinions, a school, sect, party, faction: Ac 5:17 15:5 24:5, 14 26:5 28:22, I Co 11:19, Ga 5:20, II Pe 2:1, R, mg. (Cremer, 614).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἱρετίζω, [in LXX chiefly for בּחר (v. Cremer, 615);] = αἱρέομαι (Hipp., Inscr.),
to choose: Mt 12:18 (LXX, ἀντιλήμψομαι).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * αἱρετικός, -ή, όν (< αἱρέομαι),
1. capable of choosing (Plat.).
2. causing division, heretical, factious (Cremer, 614): as subst., Tit 3:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἴσθησις, -εως, ἡ (< αἰσθάνομαι), [in LXX chiefly for דַּעַת ;]
perception (MM, VGT, s.v.): Phl 1:9.†

strong.def: properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἰσθητήριον, -ου, τό (< αἰσθάνομαι), [in LXX: Je 4:19 (קִיר), IV Mac 2:22*;]
sense, organ of perception: He 5:14 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * αἰσχροκερδής, -ες (< αἰσχρός, κέρδος),
greedy of base gains: I Ti 3:8, Tit 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† αἰσχροκερδῶς, adv.,
from eagerness for base gain: I Pe 5:2 (here only).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * αἰσχρολογία, -ας, ἡ (< αἰσχρός, λέγω),
abusive language, abuse (Lft., ICC, in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.): Col 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 αἰσχρός, -ά, όν (< αἶσχος, shame, disgrace), [in LXX: Ge 41:3 ff. (רַע, רֹעַ), Jth 12:12, al.;]
base, shameful: I Co 11:6 14:35, Eph 5:12, Tit 1:11 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * αἰσχρότης, -τητος, ἡ (< αἰσχρός),
baseness: Eph 5:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† αἰτίωμα (Rec. αἰτίαμα, the usual form; v. MM, VGT, s.v.), -τος, τό (< αἰτιάομαι, αἰτία),
a charge, accusation: Ac 25:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 αἴτιος, -α, ὁ (< αἰτία), [in LXX: I Ki 22:22 (סבב) Da LXX Bel 41, TH Da Bel 42, Su 53, II Mac 4:47 13:4, IV Mac 1:11*;]
1. causative of, responsible for; as subst., ὁ αἰ., the cause, author: He 5:9; τὸ αἰ., the cause, Ac 19:40.
2. blameworthy, culpable; as subst., ὁ αἰ., the culprit, the accused (Lat. reus); τὸ αἰ. (= αἰτία, 3), the crime, Lk 23:4, 14, 22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † αἰχμαλωσία, -ας, ἡ (< αἰχμάλωτος), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁבִי, גּוֹלָה;]
captivity (Diod., al.): Re 13:10; pl., abstr. for concr., = αἰχμάλωτοι, Eph 4:8(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † αἰχμαλωτεύω (< αἰχμάλωτος), [in LXX chiefly for שׁבה;] = αἰχμαλωτίζω, q.v.,
to lead captive: Eph 4:8(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἀκαθαρσία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀκάθαρτος), [in LXX chiefly for טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא;]
uncleanness, impurity,
(a). physical (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 23:27;
(b). moral: Ro 1:24 6:19, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19, Eph 4:19 5:3, Col 3:5, I Th 2:3 4:7.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2540 (καιρός) (meaning unseasonable);
strong.def: to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀκαιρέομαι, -οῦμαι (< ἄκαιρος, unseasonable),
to have no opportunity (opp. to εὐκαιρέω): Phl 4:10.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G170 (ἀκαιρέομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀκαίρως, adv. (< ἄκαιρος, unseasonable), [in LXX: Si 35 (32):4*;]
out of season, unseasonably: opp. to εὐκαίρως (q.v.), II Ti 4:2 (cf. Cremer, 740; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2556 (κακός);
strong.def: not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἄ-κακος, -ον, [in LXX for פְּתִי, תָּם, etc.;]
(a). as in cl. (Æsch., Plat., al.), of persons, simple, guileless: Ro 16:18, He 7:26 (cf. Cremer, 327);
(b). of things, undamaged (? MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2607 (καταγινώσκω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀ-κατά-γνωστος, -ον (< καταγινώσκω), [in LXX: II Mac 4:47 ;]
not open to just rebuke, irreprehensible: Tit 2:8 (v. Cremer, 676; and for other exx., MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G2572 (καλύπτω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀ-κατα-κάλυπτος, -ον (< κατακαλύπτω), [in LXX: Le 13:45 A (פָּרוּע)*;]
uncovered, unveiled: I Co 11:5, 13.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2632 (κατακρίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀ-κατά-κριτος, -ον (< κατακρίνω),
1. uncondemned (EV): Ac 16:37, 22:25.
2. = cl. ἄκριτος, without trial, not yet tried (MM, VGT, s.v.) Ac 16:37, 22:25†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2647 (καταλύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀ-κατά-λυτος, -ον (< καταλύω), [in LXX: IV Mac 10:11*;]
indissoluble: He 7:16.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2664 (καταπαύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀκατάπαυστος, -ον (< καταπαύω),
that cannot cease, not to be restrained: c. gen. rei, II Pe 2:14, T, Tr. txt.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2525 (καθίστημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀ-κατά-στατος, -ον (< καθίστημι), [in LXX: Is 54:11 (סֹעֲרָה);]
unsettled, unstable: Ja 1:8, 3:8.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood;
strong.def: corresponding to H02506 and H01818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 Ακελδαμά, -δαμάχ, v.s. Αχελδαμάχ.

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ἀκέραιος, -ον (< κεράννυμι), [in LXX: Es 8:13*;]
unmixed, pure, hence, metaph. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), guileless, simple: Mt 10:16, Ro 16:19, Phl 2:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2827 (κλίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀκλινής, -ές (< κλίνω), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:7 17:3*;]
unbending, firm: metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.). He 10:23.†

strong.def: to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀκμάζω (< ἀκμήν), [in LXX: IV Mac 2:3*;]
to be at the prime; of produce of the ground, to be ripe (Thuc.): Re 14:18 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to (a point) and meaning the same;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀκμήν, acc. of ἀκμή,
a point, used as adv., at the present point of time, even now, even yet: Mt 15:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀκρασία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀκρατής, q.v.), [in LXX: I Mac 6:26*;]
in Arist. and later writers = ἀκράτεια (Lft., Notes, 222 f.), want of power, hence want of self-control, incontinence: Mt 23:25, I Co 7:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2904 (κράτος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀκρατής, -ές (< κράτος), [in LXX: Pr 27:20*;]
(a). powerless, impotent;
(b). in moral sense, lacking self-control, incontinent: II Ti 3:3.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄκρατος, -ον (< κεράννυμι), [in LXX: Ps 75:8 (חֲמַר), Je 25:15 (חֵמָה), III Mac 5:2*;]
unmixed, pure: οἶνος, Re 14:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀκρίβεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀκριβής), [in LXX: Da LXX TH 7:16 (יַצִּיב), Wi 12:21, Si 16:25 42:4*;]
exactness, precision (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 22:3.†

strong.derivation: superlative of (a derivative of the same as G206 (ἄκρον));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀκριβής, -ές [in LXX: Da LXX 2:45 6:12 (יַצִּיב) Da 4:25, Es 4:5, Si 18:29 19:25 31:24 32:3*;]
exact, precise, careful, of things and persons: superl., Ac 26:5.†

strong.derivation: neuter of the comparative of the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἀκριβῶς adv. (< ἀκριβής), [in LXX: De 19:18 (יָטַב), Da TH 7:19 (יְצֵב), Ez 39:14, Wi 19:18, Si 18:29;]
with exactness, carefully: Mt 2:8, Lk 1:3, Ac 18:25, Eph 5:15, I Th 5:2 (M, Th., in l.). Compar., ἀκριβέστερον (Milligan, NTD, 111; MM, VGT, s.v.), Ac 18:26 23:15, 20 24:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀκριβόω, -ῶ (< ἀκριβής), [in Aq.: Is 30:8 49:16*;]
to enquire with exactness, learn carefully: Mt 2:7, 16 (for similar ex., v. MM, VGT, sv.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀκροατήριον, -ου, τό (< ἀκροάομαι, to listen)
a place of audience: Ac 25:23 (Plut.).†

strong.def: apparently an intensive of G191 (ἀκούω)); a hearer (merely)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀκροατής, οῦ, ὁ (v. supr.) [in LXX: Is 3:3 (לַחַשׁ), Si 3:29 ;]
a hearer: Ro 2:13, Ja 1:22, 23, 25.†

strong.derivation: from G206 (ἄκρον) and probably a modified form of (the penis or male sexual organ);
strong.def: the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 † ἀκροβυστία, -ας, ή (perh. an Alexandrian form of cl. ἀκροποσθία; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.) [in LXX for עׇרְלָה;]
the prepuce, foreskin (LXX), hence abstr., uncircumcision: Ac 11:3, Ro 2:25-27 3:30 4:10-12, I Co 7:18-19, Ga 5:6 6:15, Col 2:13 3:11. By meton., the uncircumcised: Ro 4:9, Ga 2:7, Eph 2:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀκρο-γωνιαῖος, -αία, -αῖον (< ἄκροι, γωνία, an angle) [in LXX: Is 28:16 (פִּנָּה)*;] = Attic γωνιαῖος (freq. in Inscr.; MM, VGT, s.v. ἀ.),
at the extreme angle: ὁ ἀ., the corner foundation stone, Eph 2:20, I Pe 2:6.†

strong.def: properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀκροθίνιον, -ου, τό (< ἄκρος, θίς, a heap),
prop., the top of a heap, hence, in pl.,
1. first-fruits (Xen.; MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. In war, the choicest spoils (cf. Hdt., viii, 121 f.): He 7:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Ἀκύλας, -ου (and -α; MM, VGT, s.v.), ὁ (Lat.),
Aquila: Ac 18:2, 18 18:26, Ro 16:3, I Co 16:19, II Ti 4:19.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2967 (κωλύω);
strong.def: in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀκωλύτως adv. (< κωλύω), [in Sm.: Jb 34:31*;]
without hindrance (so freq. in legal documents; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 28:31.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1635 (ἑκών);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄκων (Attic contr. for ἀέκων), -ουσα, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ἕκων, willing), [in LXX: Jb 14:17, II Mac 11:12*;]
unwilling: I Co 9:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀλαζονία (Rec. -εία, the earlier form), -ας, ἡ (< ἀλαζών), [in LXX: Wi 5:8 17:7, 2; IV Mac 5:1-38*;]
the character of an ἀλαζών, boastfulness, vainglory, vaunting: Ja 4:16 (Mayor, in l.), I Jo 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀλαζών, -όνος, ὁ, ἡ (< ἄλη, wandering), [in LXX: Jb 28:8 (שַׁחַץ) Hb 2:5 (יָהִיר), Pr 21:24 (לוּץ)*;]
prop, a vagabond, hence, an impostor, a boaster: Ro 1:30, II Ti 3:2.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2980 (λαλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀ-λάλητος, -ον (< λαλέω),
inexpressible, not to be uttered: Ro 8:26.†

strong.def: an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀλεξανδρεύς, -έως, ὁ
an Alexandrian: Ac 6:9 18:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀλεξανδρινός (Rec. -δρῖνο; v. Kühner3, II, 296), -ή, -όν,
Alexandrian: Ac 27:6 28:11.†

strong.def: to be true (in doctrine and profession)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀληθεύω (< ἀληθής), [in LXX: Ge 20:16 (יָכַח) Ge 42:16 (אֶמֶת), Pr 21:3 (מִשְׁפָּט), Is 44:26 (שָׁלַם), Si 34:4*;]
to speak the truth (R, mg., deal truly; Field, Notes, 192): Ga 4:16, Eph 4:15.†

strong.def: to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἁλιεύω (< ἁλιεύς), [in LXX: Je 16:16 (דִּיג)*;]
to fish: Jo 21:3 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀλίσγημα, -τος, τό (< late ἀλισγέω, to pollute),
pollution: Ac 15:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀλλάσσω (< ἄλλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלף, מוּר hi., etc.;]
1. to change: Ac 6:14, Ga 4:20.
2. to transform: I Co 15:51, 52, He 1:12.
3. to exchange: c. acc., seq. ἐν (= בְּ, Ps 106:20) instead of simple gen. (Bl., § 36, 8), Ro 1:23

strong.kjv: be an allegory (the Greek word itself)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀλληγορέω, -ῶ (< ἄλλος, ἀγορεύω),
to speak allegorically (Cremer, 96 ff.): Ga 4:24.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (imperative of H01984 and H03050);
strong.def: praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ἁλληλουιά (Rec. ἀλληλούϊα; Heb. הַלְלוּיָהּ, praise the Lord), [in LXX in the titles of certain Pss (104 (105), al.), and at the end of Ps 150; also To 13:18, III Mac 7:13;]
hallelujah, alleluia: Re 19:1, 3, 4 19:6.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of apparently a primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἅλλομαι [in LXX for צָלַח, דָּלַג pi., etc.;]
to leap: Ac 3:8 14:10; of water, to spring up, Jo 4:14 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler (specially, in Gentile customs)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀλλοτρι-επίσκοπος (Rec. ἀλλοτριοεπ-), -ου, ὁ
one who meddles in things alien to his calling: I Pe 4:15 (v. ICC, in l.; Deiss., BS, 224-4; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀλλόφυλος, -ον (ἄλλος, φῦλον, a tribe), [in LXX chiefly for פְּלֶשֶׁת;]
foreign, of another race (MM, VGT, s.v.); as opp. to a Jew, a Gentile: Ac 10:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄλλως adv. (< ἄλλος),
otherwise: I Ti 5:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀλοάω, -ῶ (< ἅλως, v.s. ἅλων; and cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in LXX chiefly for דּוּשׁ;]
to thresh: I Co 9:9 9:10; I Ti 5:18.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3056 (λόγος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄ-λογος, -ον [in LXX: Ex 6:12 (שָׂפָה עָרֵל), Nu 6:12 (נָפַל), Jb 11:12, Wi 11:15, 16, IV Mac3*;]
1. without reason, irrational: ζῷα, II Pe 2:12, Ju 10.
2. contrary to reason: Ac 25:27 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀλόη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Ca 4:14 א (אֲהָלִים)*;]
the aloe, aloes (the powder of a fragrant wood): Jo 19:39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἁλυκός, -ή, -όν (< ἅλς), [in LXX for מֵלַח, שִׂדִּים;]
salt: Ja 3:12.†

strong.derivation: comparative of a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3077 (λύπη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄλυπος, -ον (< λύπη),
free from grief: Phl 2:28.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G3081 (λυσιτελεῖ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀ-λυσιτελής, -ές, >(cf. λυσιτελέω),
unprofitable: He 13:17.†

strong.derivation: from a collateral form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἅλωσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἁλίσκομαι), [in LXX: Je 50:46 (תּפשׂ ni.)*;]
a taking, capture: II Pe 2:12.†

strong.def: properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a preposition or adverb denoting close association

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἅμα adv.,
at once (Lat. simul): Ac 24:26 27:40, Ro 3:12 (one and all = יַחַד, Ps 14:3), Col 4:3, I Ti 5:13, Phm 22; seq. σύν, I Th 4:17 5:10; as prep. c. dat., together with: Mt 13:29 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.); also, c. adv., ἅ. πρωΐ (cl., ἅ. ἕω, etc.), early in the morning: Mt 20:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.entry:
1 ** ἀμαθής, -ές (< μανθάνω), [in Sm.: Ps 49:11*;]
unlearned, ignorant: II Pe 3:16 (on the rareness of this word, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀμαράντινος, -ον (< ἀμάραντος),
of amaranth (Inscr.); hence unfading: I Pe 5:4.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3133 (μαραίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀμάραντος, -ον (< μαραίνομαι), [in LXX: Wi 6:12 (σοφία)*;]
unfading (whence ὁ ἀ., the amaranth, an unfading flower): I Pe 1:4 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a form of G3144 (μάρτυς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀμάρτυρος, -ον (< μάρτυς),
without witness: Ac 14:17.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3163 (μάχη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἄμαχος, -ον (< μάχη);
1. invincible (freq. in cl.).
2. abstaining from fighting, non-combatant (Xen.). Metaph. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), not contentious: I Ti 3:3, Tit 3:2.†

strong.def: properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀμάω, -ῶ (in cl. chiefly poët.),
to reap: Ja 5:4.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3184 (μεθύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀμέθυστος, -ου, ἡ (acc. to Plut., < ἀ- μεθύω, being regarded as an antidote against drunkenness), [in LXX: Ex 28:19 36:19 39:12 Ez 28:13*;]
amethyst, a purple quartz: Re 21:20.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3199 (μέλω);
strong.kjv: make light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀμελέω, -ῶ (< μέλει), [in LXX: Je 4:17 (מרה) Je 31:32 (בּעל), Wi 3:10, II Mac 4:14*;]
(a). absol., to be careless, not to care: Mt 22:5;
(b). c. gen., to be careless of, to neglect: I Ti 4:14, He 2:3 8:9 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀ-μέμπτως, adv. (< ἄμεμπτος), [in LXX: Es 3:13*;]
blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, s.v. -ος): I Th 2:10 3:13 WH mg., 5:23.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3308 (μέριμνα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀμέριμνος, -ον (< μέριμνα), [in LXX: Wi 6:15 7:23*;]
free from anxiety or care: Mt 28:14, I Co 7:32 (for exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3346 (μετατίθημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀ-μετάθετος, -ον (< μετατίθημι), [in LXX: III Mac 5:1,12*;]
immutable: He 6:18; as subst., τὸ ἀ., immutability, He 6:17 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3334 (μετακινέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀ-μετα-κίνητος, -ον (< μετακινέω),
immovable, firm: I Co 15:58.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3338 (μεταμέλλομαι);
strong.kjv: without repentance, not to be repented of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀ-μεταμέλητος, -ον (< μεταμέλομαι),
not repented of, unregretted: Ro 11:29, II Co 7:10.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3340 (μετανοέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀμετανόητος, -ον (< μετανοέω),
1. impenitent: Ro 2:5
2. = ἀμεταμέλητος (π., Philo, al.; v. Deiss., BS, 257; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3358 (μέτρον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἄμετρος, -ον (< μέτρον),
without measure: adverbially, εἰς τὰ ἄ., excessively, II Co 10:13 10:15†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3384 (μήτηρ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀμήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ, ἡ (< μήτηρ),
without a mother (freq. in Gk. writers of the gods): ἀπάτωρ ἀ. of one without recorded genealogy, He 7:3 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3392 (μιαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** ἀ-μίαντος, -ον (< μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wi 3:13 4:2 8:20, II Mac 14:36 15:34*;]
undefiled, free from contamination (in π., of αἰθήρ; MM, VGT, s.v.): He 7:26 13:4, I Pe 1:4, Ja 1:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἄμμος, -ου, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for חוֹל;]
sand, sandy ground: Mt 7:26, Ro 9:27, He 11:12, Re 18:1, Re 20:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀμνός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for כֶּבֶשׂ;]
a lamb: fig., of Christ (DCG, ii, 620b), Jo 1:29, 36, Ac 8:32(LXX), I Pe 1:19 (cf. ἀρνίον; Cremer, 102, 635).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀμοιβή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἀμείβομαι, to repay); [in Aq., Sm.: Pr 12:14, al.;]
requital, recompense: I Ti 5:4 (for illustration from π. v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀμπλιᾶτος (T, -ίατος; Rec. Ἀμπλιᾶς; v. MM, VGT, 5.v.), -ου, ὁ,
Ampliatus: Ro 16:8.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a primary verb;
strong.def: to ward off (for oneself), i.e. protect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀμύνω, [in LXX (mid.): Jos 10:13 (נקם), נָקַם), Ps 118:10-12 מוּל hi.), Is 59:16 (ישׁע hi.), Wi 11:3, al.;]
to ward off, etc. Mid.
(a). to defend oneself against;
(b). to requite;
(c). = act., to defend, assist (Is 59:16): c. acc. pers., Ac 7:24 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G906 (βάλλω);
strong.def: a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀμφίβληστρον, -ου, τό (< ἀμφιβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם;]
something thrown around, as a garment; spec., a casting-net: Mt 4:18.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G4172 (πόλις);
strong.def: a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀμφίπολις, -εως, ἡ
Amphipolis, in Macedonia, so called because the river Strymon flowed around it: Ac 17:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3469 (μωμάομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀ-μώμητος, -ου (< μωμάομαι),
blameless: II Pe 3:14.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3470 (μῶμος);
strong.kjv: without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἄ-μωμος, -ον (< μῶμος, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for תָּמִים];
of sacrificial victims, without blemish: of Christ, He 9:14, I Pe 1:19; ethically, unblemished, faultless: Eph 1:4 5:27, Phl 2:15, Col 1:22, Ju 24, Re 14:5 (Cremer, 425, 788; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָמוֹן),
Amon, King of Judah: Mt 1:10 (Rec.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀνα-βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἀναβαίνω), [in LXX for מַעֲלָה: III Ki 10:19, 20, IV Ki 9:13 20:9 ff, II Ch 9:18, 19, Is 38:8, Ez 40:6, 49; ᾠδὴ τῶν ἀ., tit. 119(120)-133(134)*;]
1. a going up, an ascent (Pss, tit. 119(120)-133(134) ?).
