strong.derivation: middle voice from G303 (ἀνά) and G906 (βάλλω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-βάλλω, [in LXX: Ps 78:21 89:38 (עבר), I Ki 28:14, Ps 104:2 (עטה);]
to defer, put off (MM, VGT, s.v.): mid., Ac 24:22.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις);
strong.def: to cause to go up, i.e. haul (a net)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-βιβάζω (causal of ἀναβαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for עלה hi., also for רכב hi., etc.;]
to make go up, draw up, as a ship (Xen.): σαγήνην, Mt 13:48 (metaph., MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-βοάω, -ῶ [in LXX for צעק, זעק, קרא, etc.;]
to cry out: Mt 27:46 (WH, ἐβόησεν; v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀναβολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ά αβάλλω), [in LXX for כּנף, etc.;]
delay: Ac 25:17 (for exx. of other meanings, v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
strong.kjv: declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἀν-αγγέλλω, [in LXX chiefly for נגד hi.;]
1. to bring back word, report (Æsch., Thuc., al.): Jo 5:15 (WH, εἶπεν), Ac 14:27 15:4, II Co 7:7
2. Later, = ἀπαγγέλλω (MM, VGT, s.v.), to announce, declare (LXX; Cremer, 24): Mt 28:11 (WH, ἀπ-), Jo 4:25 16:13-15, Ac 19:18 20:20, 27 Ro 15:21, I Pe 1:12, I Jo 1:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ἀνα-γεννάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Sir prol. 17 א* (ΑΒאc παρα-)*;]
to beget again: metaph., of spiritual birth, I Pe 1:3 1:23 (cf. Cremer, 147; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ἀναγκαῖος, -αῖα, -αῖον (< ἀνάγκη), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 16:3, Sir prol. 22, II Mac 4:23 9:21, IV Mac 1:2*;]
1. necessary: Ac 13:46, I Co 12:22, II Co 9:5, Phl 2:25, Tit 3:14, He 8:3; comp. -αιότερον, Phl 1:24.
2. Of persons connected by bonds of nature or friendship, near, intimate (Field, Notes, 118; ΜΜ, VGT, s.v.): ἀ. φίλοι, Ac 10:24.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G315 (ἀναγκάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀναγκαστῶς adv.,
necessarily or by constraint: opp. to ἑκουσίως, I Pe 5:2 (rare).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G303 (ἀνά) and G1107 (γνωρίζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-γνωρίζω [in LXX: Ge 45:1 (ידע hith.)*;]
to recognize: Ac 7:13 (WH, txt., ἐγνωρίσθη).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀνά-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX: Ne 8:8 (מִקְרָא), I Es 9:48, Sir prol. 9, 13*;]
1. recognition (Hdt.).
2. reading (Plat., al.): of the public reading of Scripture (Milligan, NTD, 173, 210 f.): Ac 13:15, II Co 3:14, I Ti 4:13 (Cremer, 158; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀνα-δέχομαι [in LXX: II Mac 6:19 8:36*;]
1. to assume, undertake (in π. freq. as legal term: MM, VGT, s.v.): ἐπαγγελίας, He 11:17.
2. = cl. ὑποδέχομαι, to receive: of guests, Ac 28:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνα-δίδωμι [in LXX: Si 1:22, II Mac 13:15*;]
1. to give forth, send up, as of plants (Hdt., al.).
2. to give up, yield, hand over (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 23:33.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀνα-ζώννυμι, [in LXX: Jg 18:16, Pr 31:17 (חגר)*;]
to gird up: fig., τ. ὀσφύας τ. διανοίας, I Pe 1:13.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and a compound of the base of G2226 (ζῶον) and G4442 (πῦρ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνα-ζωπυργέω, -ῶ (< ζωός, πῦρ), [in LXX: I Mac 13:7*;]
to kindle afresh: metaph., II Ti 1:6 (for vernac. exx., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-θάλλω (< θάλλω, to flourish), [in LXX: Ps 28:7 (עלז), Ez 17:24 (פּרח hi.), Ho 8:9, Wi 4:4, Si 5:1-15*;]
to revive: Phl 4:10 (of MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: a (religious) ban or (concretely) excommunicated (thing or person)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † ἀνάθεμα, -τος, τό (< ἀνατίθημι), Hellenistic for Attic ἀνάθημα (Bl., § 27, 2);
1. prop. = τὸ ἀνατιθέμένον, that which is laid by to be kept, a votive offering (as ἀνάθημα in II Mac 2:13, Lk 21:5—where LT read -θεμα, v. M, Pr., 46).
2. [As equiv. in LXX for חֵרֶם,] devoted, a thing devoted to God (v. Driver, De., 98 f., and cf. Le 27:28-29), hence;
(a). of the sentence pronounced (De 13:15), a curse: Ac 23:14;
(b). of the object on which the curse is laid, accursed (De 7:26): Ro 9:3, I Co 12:3 16:22, Ga 1:8, 9 (v. ICC on Ro.; Lft., Ga., 1:8, 9; Cremer, 547; Tr., Syn., § v; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: to look again (i.e. attentively) at (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀνα-θεωρέω, -ῶ
to observe carefully, consider well: Ac 17:23, He 13:7 (Diod., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀν-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀναιρέω), [in LXX: Nu 11:15 (הָרַג), Jg 15:17 (רָמָה), Jth 15:4, II Mac 5:13*;]
1. a taking up or away (Thuc.).
2. a destroying, slaying, murder (Field, Notes, 116; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 8:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G159 (αἴτιος) (in the sense of G156 (αἰτία));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀν-αίτιος, -ον (< αἰτία), [in LXX: De 19:10, 13 21:8, 9 (נָקִי), Da LXX TH Sus 62, always of αἷμα (of. MM, VGT, s.v.)*;]
guiltless, innocent: Mt 12:5, 7.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G2537 (καινός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-καινίζω (< καινός), [in LXX: II Ch 15:8, Ps 102 (103):5 103 (104):30, La 5:21 (חדשׁ pi., hith.)., Ps 38 (39):2 (עכר ni.), I Mac 6:9*;]
to renew: He 6:6 (Isocr., Plut.).†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G2537 (καινός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀνα-καινόω, -ῶ = ἀνακαινίζω (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.),
to make new: II Co 4:16, Col 3:10 (v. Cremer, 323).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀνακαίνωσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀνακαινόω),
renewal: Ro 12:2, Tit 3:5 (Cremer, 324; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and G2572 (καλύπτω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀνα-καλύπτω [in LXX chiefly for גָּלָה ni., pi.;]
to unveil: metaph. of removing hindrance to perception of spiritual things, II Co 3:14 3:18.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2775 (κεφαλαιόω) (in its original sense);
strong.kjv: briefly comprehend, gather together in one

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) ** ἀνα-κεφαλαιόω, ῶ (v.s. κεφαλαιόω), [in Th., Al.: Ps 71 (72):20*;]
to sum up, gather up, present as a whole: mid., Ro 13:9, Eph 1:10 (on WH. v. Lft., Notes, 321 L; AR, in l.; Cremer, 354, 748).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX: III Mac 7:5*;]
an examination: spec. of legal preliminary investigation, Ac 25:26 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3056 (λόγος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀναλογία, -ας, ἡ (< λόγος), [in Al.: Le 27:18*;]
proportion (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ro 12:6 (cf. Cremer, 397).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνα-λογίζομαι [in LXX: Wi 17:13 א, II Mac 12:43 A, III Mac 7:7*;]
to consider: He 12:3 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνά-λυσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀναλύω),
a loosing, e.g. of a vessel from its moorings, hence, departure: from life, II Ti 4:6.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G264 (ἁμαρτάνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀναμάρτητος, -ον (< ἁμαρτεῖν), [in LXX: De 29:19 (18) II Mac 8:4 12:42*;]
1. without missing, unerring (Xen.).
2. In moral sense, faultless (Plat.), without sin: Jo 8:7 (v. Cremer, 102, 634; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-μένω [in LXX for קוה pi.;]
to await "one whose coming is expected, perhaps with the added idea of patience and confidence" c. acc., I Th 1:10 (v. M, Th., in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G3501 (νέος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-νεόω, -ῶ (< νέος), [in LXX: Jb 33:24, Es 3:13, I, IV Mac8*;]
to renew: pass., Eph 4:23 (v. Cremer, 428; MM, VGT, s.v.)†

strong.def: to become sober again, i.e. (figuratively) regain (one's) senses

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνα-νήφω
to return to soberness: metaph., II Ti 2:26 (cf. ἐκνήφω).†

strong.def: Ananias, the name of three Israelites

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 Ἀνανίας (WH, Ἁναν-), -α, ὁ (Heb. חֲנַנְיָה),
Ananias;
1. of Jerusalem: Ac 5:1, 3 5:5.
2. Of Damascus: Ac 9:10-13, 17 22:12.
3. High Priest: Ac 23:2 24:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G4483 (ῥέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀν-αντί-ρητος (T, -ρρητος), -ον (< ῥητός, spoken), [in Sm.: Jb 11:2 33:13*;]
not to be contradicted, undeniable: Ac 19:36 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀν-αντι-ρήτως (T, -ρρήτως), adv.,
without contradiction: Ac 10:29.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G514 (ἄξιος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀν-άξιος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ἄξιος), [in LXX: Je 15:19 א2 (זלל), Es 8:13, Si 25:8*;]
unworthy: c. gen., I Co 6:2 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀναξίως (v. supr.), adv., [in LXX: II Mac 14:42*;]
in an unworthy manner: I Co 11:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-πείθω, [in LXX: Je 29:8 (נשׂא hi.), I Mac 1:11*;]
to persuade, incite: Ac 18:13 (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: to complete; by implication, to occupy, supply; figuratively, to accomplish (by coincidence ot obedience)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀνα-πληρόω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for מלא, Le 12:6, al.; also שׁלם (Ge 15:16, III Ki 7:51, Is 60:20), etc.;]
1. to fill up, make full (in π. of completing contracts and making up rent; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.): τόπον, take one's place (cf. Heb. מָקוֹם מִלֵּא), I Co 14:16; άμαρτίας, complete the number, I Th 2:16; τ. νόμον, observe perfectly, Ga 6:2; pass., προφητεία, fulfilled, Mt 13:14.
2. to supply: τὸ ὑστέρημα, I Co 16:17, Phl 2:30 (Cremer, 838).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G626 (ἀπολογέομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀναπολόγητος, -ον (< ἀπολογεόμαι),
without excuse, inexcusable (in Polyb., al., as a forensic term; v. Lft., Notes, 252): Ro 1:20 2:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G705 (ἀριθμέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀν-αρίθμητος, -ον, (< ἀριθμέω), [Jb 31:25, al.],
innumerable: He 11:12.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος);
strong.def: properly, to pack up (baggage), i.e. (by implication, and figuratively) to upset

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνα-σκευάζω (< σκεῦος, a vessel),
prop. to pack up baggage, hence, to dismantle, ravage, destroy; metaph., to unsettle, subvert (MM, VGT, s.v.): ψυχάς, Ac 15:24.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G450 (ἀνίστημι) (in the sense of removal);
strong.def: properly, to drive out of home, i.e. (by implication) to disturb (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: trouble, turn upside down, make an uproar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἀνα-στατόω, ῶ (< ἀνάστατος, driven from home; < ἀνίστημι), [in LXX: Da 7:23 (דּוּשׁ;* also in Aq., and in π. (v. Deiss., LAE, 80 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.),]
to stir up, excite, unsettle: c. acc.;
(a). to tumult and sedition: Ac 17:6 21:38;
(b). by false teaching: Ga 5:12 (v. Milligan, NTD, 73 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνα-σταυρόω;
1. to impale (Hdt.).
2. to raise on a cross, crucify (Polyb., al.).
3. to crucify again: He 6:6 (v. Westc., in l.).†

strong.def: to overturn; also to return; by implication, to busy oneself, i.e. remain, live
strong.kjv: abide, behave self, have conversation, live, overthrow, pass, return, be used

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἀνα-στρέφω, [in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב;]
1. to overturn: Jo 2:15.
2. to turn back, return: Ac 5:22 15:16.
3. to turn hither and thither; pass., to turn oneself about, sojourn, dwell: Mt 17:22 Rec.; metaph. (like Heb. הלךְ, in κοινή writers and in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 315; BS, 88, 194; MM, VGT, s.v.), to conduct oneself, behave, live: II Co 1:12, Eph 2:3, I Ti 3:15, He 10:33 13:18, I Pe 1:17, II Pe 2:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 ** ἀνα-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ, (< ἀναστρέφομαι), [in LXX: To 4:14, II Mac 5:8 6:23*;]
1. a turning down or back, a wheeling about (Soph., Thuc., al.).
2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; v.s. ἀναστρέφω, and cf. Hort on Ja 3:13; MM, VGT, s.v.), manner of life, behaviour, conduct: Ga 1:13, Eph 4:22, I Ti 4:12, He 13:7, Ja 3:13, I Pe 1:15, 18 2:12 3:1, 2, 16, II Pe 2:7 3:11.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and the middle voice of G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: to set forth (for oneself), i.e propound

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀνα-τίθημι, [in LXX chiefly for חרם (Cremer, 546);]
to lay upon, set up, etc. Mid. -εμαι, in late writers (Plut., al.; v. also MM, VGT, s.v.), to set forth, declare: Ac 25:14, Ga 2:2.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀνα-τρέπω, [in LXX for דּחה, הדף, etc.;]
to overturn, destroy: Jo 2:15 WH, txt.; metaph., to subvert (MM, VGT, s.v.): II Ti 2:18, Tit 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ἀνα-τρέφω, [in LXX: Wi 7:4 B, IV Mac 10:2 11:15 א*;]
to nurse up, nourish, educate, bring up: Lk 4:16, WΗ, mg., Ac 7:20, 21 22:3.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G303 (ἀνά) and (to pour);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀνά-χυσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀναχέω, to pour out),
a pouring out, overflowing, excess: metaph., I Pe 4:4 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: properly, a recovery of breath, i.e. (figuratively) revival

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνά-ψυξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀναψύχω), [in LXX: Ex 8:15 (11 (רְוָחָה)*;]
a refreshing: Ac 3:19.†

strong.def: properly, to cool off, i.e. (figuratively) relieve

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-ψύχω, [in LXX for נפשׁ ni., חיה, etc. (freq. in sense of revive, refresh oneself);]
to refresh: c. acc. pers., II Ti 1:16 (MM, VGT, s.v.; Cremer, 588).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of G435 (ἀνήρ) and G4228 (πούς);
strong.def: an enslaver (as bringing men to his feet)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνδραποδιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἀνδράποδον, a slave, captured in war),
a slave-dealer, kidnapper: I Ti 1:10 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνδρίζω, [in LXX for חזק, אמץ (Jos 1:6 ff., I Ch 22:19, al.; in II Ki 10:12, Ps 27:14 31:25 combined with κρατιοῦσθαι, as in I Co 16:13);]
to make a man of. Mid., to play the man (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.): I Co 16:13.†

strong.def: man of victory; Andronicos, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀνδρόνικος, -ου, ὁ,
Andronicus: Ro 16:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνδρο-φόνος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: II Mac 9:28*;]
a man-slayer: I Ti 1:9 (cf. φονεύς, and v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1458 (ἐγκαλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** ἀν-έγκλητος, -ον (< ἀ-, ἐγκαλέω), [in LXX: III Mac 5:31*;]
not to be called to account, unreprovable: I Co 1:8, Col 1:22, I Ti 3:10, Tit 1:6, 7.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1555 (ἐκδιηγέομαι);
strong.def: not expounded in full, i.e. indescribable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀν-εκδιήγητος, -ον (< ἀ-, ἐκδιηγέομαι),
inexpressible: II Co 9:15 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1583 (ἐκλαλέω);
strong.def: not spoken out, i.e. (by implication) unutterable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀν-εκ-λάλητος, -ον (< ἀ-, ἐκλαλέω),
unspeakable: I Pe 1:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1655 (ἐλεήμων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀν-ελεήμων, -ον (< -ἀ, ἐλεήμων), [in LXX for אַכְזָר;]
without mercy: Ro 1:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀνεμίζω = Attic ἀνεμόω (< ἄνεμος);
pass., to be driven by the wind: Ja 1:6.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1830 (ἐξερευνάω);
strong.def: not searched out, i.e. (by implication) inscrutable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀνεξεραύνητος (Rec. -εύνητος, as in Attic; M, Pr., 46), -ον (< ἐξ-ερευνάω), [in Sm. (-ευ-): Pr., 25:3*;]
unsearchable: Ro 11:33.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀνεξί-κακος, -ον (< fut., ἀνέξομαι, κακός),
patiently forbearing (cf. ἀνεξικακία, Wi 2:19; and v. MM, VGT, s.v.): II Ti 2:24.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G2487 (ἴχνος);
strong.def: not tracked out, i.e. (by implication) untraceable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀνεξιχνίαστος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ἐξιχνιάζω, to track out; < ἴχνος), [in LXX: Jb 5:9 9:10 34:24 (חֵקֶר אֵין)*;]
that cannot be traced out: Ro 11:33, Eph 3:8 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G153 (αἰσχύνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀν-επ-αίσχυντος, -ον (< ἐπαισχύνομαι),
not to be put to shame: II Ti 2:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1949 (ἐπιλαμβάνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἀν-επί-λημπτος (Rec. -λμπτος; Bl., § 6, 8), -ον (< ἀ-, ἐπιλαμβάνω),
without reproach: I Ti 3:2 5:7 6:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀν-έρχομαι, [in LXX: III Ki 13:12 (הָלַךְ)*;]
to go up: Jo 6:3, Ga 1:17, 18 (cf. ἐπανέρχ-; and on its use of "going up" to the capital, MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἄνεσις, -εως, ἡ, (< ἀνίημι), [in LXX: II Es 4:22 (שָׁלוּ), II Ch 23:15, I Es 4:62, Wi 13:13, Si 15:20 26:10*;]
a loosening, relaxation: Ac 24:23 (RV, indulgence; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.); by St. Paul, opp. to θλίψις, expressed or understood, relief: II Co 2:12 7:5 8:13, II Th 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀν-ετάζω (< ἀνά, ἐτάζω, to examine; v. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in LXX: Jg 6:29 (דָּרַשׁ), Es 2:23 (בָּקַשׁ), Da TH Su 14*;]
to examine judicially: Ac 22:24, 29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄνευ, prep. c. gen. (rarer than χωρίς, q.v.; cf. Ellic. on Eph 2:12; MM, VGT, 42),
without: Mt 10:29, I Pe 3:1 4:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2111 (εὔθετος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀν-εύ-θετος, -ον (v. MM, VGT, s.v.),
not well placed, not fit: Ac 27:12.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and an obsolete (a brood);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνεψιός, -οῦ, ὁ (cf. Lat. nepos), [in LXX: Nu 36:11 (דּוֹד בֶּן), To 7:2 9:6 א*;]
a cousin: Col 4:10 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄνηθον, -ου, τό,
anise: Mt 23:23.†

strong.def: to attain to, i.e. (figuratively) be proper

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀν-ήκω (ἀνά, ἥκω), [in LXX: Jos 23:14 (בּוֹא), I Ki 27:8, Si. prol. 10, I, II Mac6*;]
prop., to have come up to; in later writers, impers. it is due, it is befitting: in ethical sense (MM, VGT, s.v.), Eph 5:4, Col 3:18; τὸ ἀνῆκον, Phm 8.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (lame);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀν-ήμερος, -ον (ἀ-, ἥμερο),
not tame, savage (MM, VGT, s.v.): II Ti 3:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄνθος, -εος, τό, [in LXX for צִיץ, etc.;]
a flower: Ja 1:10, 11, I Pe 1:24(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀνθρακιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< ἄνθραξ), [in LXX: Si 11:32, IV Mac 9:20*;]
a heap of burning coals: Jo 18:18 21:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄνθραξ, -ακος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for גַּחֶלֶת;]
coal, charcoal: . ἄ. πυρός, a burning coal, Ro 12:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἀνθρωπ-άρεσκος, -ον (ἄνθρωπος, ἄρεσκος, pleasing), [in LXX: Ps 52 (53):5*;]
studying to please men: Eph 6:6, Col 3:22 (Cremer, 642; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.kjv: human, common to man, man(-kind), (man-)kind, men's, after the manner of men

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἀνθρώπινος, -η, ον (< ἄνθρωπος), [in LXX for אָדָם, אֱנוֹשׁ;]
human, belonging to man: χεῖρες, Ac 17:25; σοφία, I Co 2:13; φύσις, Ja 3:7; κτίσις, I Pe 2:13 (MM, VGT, s.v.); ἀ. ἡμέρα, opp. to ἡ ἡμ. (3:13, God's Judgment-Day), human judgment, I Co 4:3 (v. Lft., Notes, 198); πειρασμὸς ἀ., temptation such as man can bear (AV, such as is common to man, v. Field, Notes, 175), I Co 10:13; ἀνθρώπινον λέγω, I speak in human fashion, with words not properly weighed, Ro 6:19 (v. Field, Notes, 156).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἀνθρωποκτόνος, -ον (< κτείνω, to kill),
a murderer, manslayer (Eur.; v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Jo 8:44, I Jo 3:15.†

strong.derivation: from G473 (ἀντί) and a superlative of G5228 (ὑπέρ);
strong.def: instead of the highest officer, i.e. (specially) a Roman proconsul

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * ἀνθ-ύπατος, -ου, ὁ (ἀντί, ὕπατος, altern. for ὑπέρτατος),
supreme, a consul, one acting in place of a consul, a proconsul, the administrator of a senatorial province (cf. ἡγεμών, and v. MM, VGT, 44): Ac 13:7, 8, 12 18:12 19:38.†

strong.def: to let up, i.e. (literally) slacken or (figuratively) desert, desist from

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀν-ίημι (ἀνά, ἵημι), [in LXX for רפה, נשׂא, etc.;]
1. to send up, produce, to send back.
2. to let go, leave without support: He 13:5 (cf. De 31:6; Hom., Il., ii, 71).
3. to relax, loosen (v. Field, Notes, 124 f.): Ac 16:26 27:40; hence, metaph., to give up, desist from: Eph 6:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2436 (ἵλεως);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) *† ἀν-έλεος, -ον (Attic ἀνηλεής, ἀνελεήμων; MM, VGT, s.v.),
merciless: Ja 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀν-οικο-δομέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for בּנה, גּדר;]
to build again, rebuild (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 15:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄνοιξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀνοίγω),
an opening (in MGr., springtime): ἐν ἀ., as often as I open, Eph 6:19.†

strong.def: illegality, i.e. violation of law or (genitive case) wickedness
strong.kjv: iniquity, X transgress(-ion of) the law, unrighteousness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ἀνομία, -ας, ἡ (< ἄνομος), [in LXX for עָוֺן, פֶּשַׁע, תּוֹעֵבָה, רֶשַׁע, etc.;]
lawlessness, iniquity: Mt 7:23 13:41 23:28 24:12, Ro 6:19, II Co 6:14, II Th 2:3, 7, Tit 2:14, He 1:9, I Jo 3:4; in pl. (as LXX, Ps 31:1, al.; v. Bl., § 32, 6; Swete, Mk., 153), of acts or manifestations of lawlessness: Ro 4:7(LXX), He 10:17.†

strong.def: lawlessly, i.e. (specially) not amenable to (the Jewish) law

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀνόμως, adv. [in LXX: II Mac 8:17*;]
1. lawlessly (II Mac 8:17).
2. = χωρὶς νόμου, without law: Ro 2:12.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3741 (ὅσιος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀν-όσιος, -ον (ἀ- neg., ὅσιος), [in LXX: Ez 22:9 (זִמָּה, Wi 12:4, II Mac 7:34 8:32, III Mac 2:2 5:7, IV Mac 12:11*;]
unholy, profane (Cremer, 464): I Ti 1:9, II Ti 3:2 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀνοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἀνέχω, -ομαι), [in LXX: I Mac 12:25 (RV, respite)*;]
1. in cl., a holding back, delaying (MM, VGT, s.v.).
2. forbearance, delay of punishment: Ro 2:4 3:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀντ-αγωνίζομαι, depon., [in LXX: IV Mac 17:14*;]
to struggle against: seq. πρός, c. acc., He 12:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀντ-ανα-πληρόω, -ῶ (ἀντί, ἀναπληρόω),
to fill up in turn: Col 1:24 (v. Lft., in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀντ-από-δοσις, -εως, ἡ (v. supr.), [in LXX chiefly for גְּמוּל, שִׁלּוּם;]
recompense: Col 3:24 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: to set oneself opposite, i.e. be disputatious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀντι-δια-τίθημι,
in mid, to place oneself in opposition, oppose: II Ti 2:25 (EV; but v. Field, Notes, 215 f.; cf. MM, VGT, s.v.).

strong.derivation: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G5087 (τίθημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀντί-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (< τίθημι),
opposition: I Ti 6:20.†

strong.def: to set down (troops) against, i.e. withstand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀντι-καθ-ίστημι, [in LXX: De 31:21 (ענה), Jos 5:7, Mi 2:8 (קוּם)*;]
1. causal in pres. impf. fut. and 1 aor.; to replace, oppose.
2. Intrans. in pass. and 2 aor. act.;
(a). to supersede;
(b). to resist: He 12:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄντικρυς (Tr. -ύς, Rec. ἀντικρύ), adv. (< ἀντί), [in LXX: Ne 12:8 (לְנֶגֶד), III Mac 5:16*;]
in cl., outright; in κοινή (= cl. καταντικρύ), over against: Ac 20:15 (v. Bl., § 5, 4; 40, 7; Rutherford, NPhr., 500 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀντί-λημψις, (Rec. -ληψις; v. MM, VGT s.v.; M, Pr., 56), -εως, ἡ (< ἀντιλαμβάνομαι), [in LXX for עֹז, זְרוֹעַ, etc., freq. in Pss and II, III Mac.; freq. also in π. in petitions to the Ptolemies in sense of βοήθεια (v. Deiss., LAE, 107; BS, 92, 223);]
1. cl. a laying hold of, an exchange.
2. Hellenistic (LXX, π.) help: pl. of ministrations of deacons; I Co 12:28 (DB, ii, 347 f.; Cremer, 386).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀντιλογία, -ας ἡ (< ἀντιλέγω), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב;]
gain-saying, strife (the latter sense being found in π.; v. MM, VGT, s.v.; cf. Field, Notes, 106): He 6:16 7:7 12:3, Ju 11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀντι-λοιδορέω, -ῶ,
to revile in turn: I Pe 2:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀντί-λυτρον, -ου, τό, [in Al.: Ps 48 (49):9*;]
a ransom: I Ti 2:6 (v. CGT, in l.; and cf. λύτρον).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G3408 (μισθός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀντιμισθία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀντίμισθος, for a reward),
a reward, requital: in good sense, II Co 6:13; in bad sense, Ro 1:27 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 Ἀντιόχεια, -ας, ἡ,
Antioch;
1. in Syria: Ac 11:19, 20, 22, 26, 27 13:1 14:26 15:22, 23, 30, 35 18:22, Ga 2:11.
2. In Pisidia: Ac 13:14 14:19, 21, II Ti 3:11.†

strong.def: an Antiochian or inhabitant of Antiochia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀντιοχεύς, -έως, ὁ,
a citizen of Antioch, an Antiochian: Ac 6:5.†

strong.derivation: contracted for a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀντίπας (T, Ἀντείπας), -α (in some MSS. it appears to be indecl.; but v. M, Pr., 12; it is abbrev. from Ἀντίπατρος), ὁ,
Antipas: Re 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀντιπατρίς, -ίδος, ἡ,
Antipatris, bet. Joppa and Caesarea: Ac 23:31.†

strong.derivation: from G473 (ἀντί) and G4098 (πίπτω) (including its alternate);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀντι-πίπτω, [in LXX: Ex 26:5 (קבל), Ex 26:17 (שׁלב), Nu 27:14 (מְרִיבָה), Jb 23:13 (שׁוּב hi.)*;]
1. to fall against or upon (Arist., Polyb.).
2. to strive against, resist (Arist.): c. dat., Ac 7:51.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀντι-στρατεύομαι,
to make war against: c. dat., Ro 7:23.†

strong.derivation: from G473 (ἀντί) and the middle voice of G5021 (τάσσω);
strong.def: to range oneself against, i.e. oppose

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀντι-τάσσω (Att., -ττω), [in LXX for לוּץ hi., נשׂא, etc.;]
to range on battle against; mid., to set oneself against, resist: absol., Ac 18:6; c. dat., Ro 13:2, Ja 4:6 5:6, I Pe 5:5 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G5179 (τύπος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀντί-τυπος, -ον (v.s. τύπος), [in LXX: Es 3:13 A*;]
1. act. striking back; metaph., resisting, adverse.
2. Pass. struck back; metaph., corresponding to (MM, VGT, s.v.);
(a). as impression of a seal or copy of an archetype (τύπος) (RV, like in pattern), He 9:24;
(b). as the reality (of which τύπος is the copy or adumbration) (RV, after a true likeness), I Pe 3:21 (Cremer, 357).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 *† ἀντί-χριστος, -ον, ὁ,
Antichrist, "one who assuming the guise of Christ opposes Christ" (Westc., Epp. Jo., 70): I Jo 2:18, 22 4:3, II Jo 7; pl. I Jo 2:18 (cf. ψευδόχριστος, and v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: to bale up (properly, bilge water), i.e. dip water (with a bucket, pitcher, etc.)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀντλέω, -ῶ (< ἄντλος, bilge-water in a hold), [in LXX for שׁאב, etc.;]
1. prop., to bale out.
2. Generally, to draw water: absol., Jo 2:8 4:15; ὕδωρ, Jo 2:9 4:7 (on its use of the water made wine, v. DCG, ii, 815a; MM, VGT, s.v.; Field, Notes, 84 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἄντλημα, -τος, τό (< ἀντλέω),
(a). prop., what is drawn (Diosc.);
(b). a vessel to draw with, a bucket (Plut.; v. Abbott, Essays, 88): Jo 4:11.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G3788 (ὀφθαλμός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀντοφθαλμέω, -ῶ (ἀντί, ὀφθαλμός), [in LXX: Wi 12:14*;]
to look in the face, look straight at (Polyb.). Metaph., to face, withstand (Wi 12:14, Polyb.): c. dat., ἀ. τ. ἀνέμῳ, as nautical term, to beat up against the wind (v. DB, ext., 366 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.): Ac 27:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5271 (ὑποκρίνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** ἀν-υπόκριτος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ὑποκρίνομαι), [in LXX: Wi 5:18 18:16*;]
unfeigned: Ro 12:9, II Co 6:6, I Ti 1:5, II Ti 1:5, Ja 3:17, I Pe 1:22 (Cremer, 380; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5293 (ὑποτάσσω);
strong.def: unsubdued, i.e. insubordinate (in fact or temper)
strong.kjv: disobedient, that is not put under, unruly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† ἀνυπότακτος, -ον (< ά- neg., ὑποτάσσω), [in Sm.: I Ki 2:12 10:27 (for LXX, λοιμός, בּני בליעל)*;]
of things, not subject to rule: He 2:8; of persons, unruly: I Ti 1:9, Tit 1:6, 10 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἄνω, adv. (< ἀνά),
(a). up, upwards: Jo 11:41, He 12:15;
(b). above (opp. to κάτω): Ac 2:19; with art. ἡ, Ga 4:26, Phl 3:14; τά, Jo 8:23, Col 3:1, 2; ἕως ἄ. (up to the brim), Jo 2:7 (Cremer, 106; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀνωτερικός, -ή, όν (< ἀνώτερος),
upper: Ac 19:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5624 (ὠφέλιμος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀν-ωφελής, -ές (ἀ- neg., ὄφελος), [in LXX: Is 44:10 (הוֹעִיל בִּלְתִּי), Je 2:8 (הוֹעִיל לֹא), Pr 28:3, Wi 1:11*;]
unprofitable: Tit 3:9; neut. as subst., unprofitableness: He 7:18.†

strong.kjv: as becometh, after a godly sort, worthily(-thy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** ἀξίως, adv. [in LXX: Wi 7:15 16:1, Si 14:11*;]
worthily: Ro 16:2, Eph 4:1, Phl 1:27; c. gen. (freq. in Inscr.; Deiss., BS, 248; MM, VGT, 51), ἀ. τ. Κυρίου, Col 1:10; τ. θεοῦ I Th 2:12, III Jo 6.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3707 (ὁρατός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀόρατος, -ον (< ὁράω), [in LXX: Ge 1:2 (תֹּהוּ), Is 45:3 (מִסְתָּר), II Mac 9:5*;]
unseen, invisible: Ro 1:20, Col 1:15, 16, I Ti 1:17, He 11:27.†

strong.def: akin to the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); to strangle oneself off (i.e. to death)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀπ-άγχω (< ἄγχω, to press, strangle), [in LXX: II Ki 17:23 (חנק), To 3:10*;]
to strangle; mid., to hang oneself (or, to choke; v. M, Pr., 155): Mt 27:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3811 (παιδεύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀ-παίδευτος, -ον (< παιδεύω), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, etc., chiefly in Wi. lit.;]
uninstructed, ignorant: II Ti 2:23.†

strong.def: to grieve out, i.e. become apathetic

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπ-αλγέω, -ῶ,
1. prop., to cease to feel pain for (Thuc., ii, 61).
2. In late Gk.
(a). to despair (Polyb., i, 35, 5);
(b). to become callous, reckless (Polyb., xvi, 12, 7; MM, VGT, s.v.): Eph 4:19.†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G245 (ἀλλότριος);
strong.def: to estrange away, i.e. (passively and figuratively) to be non-participant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀπ-αλλοτριόω, -ῶ, [in LXX for זוּר, נזר, etc.;]
to alienate, estrange; pass.: Eph 2:12 4:18, Col 1:21 (MM, VGT, s.v.; Cremer, 95, 633).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀπάντησις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀπαντάω), [in LXX chiefly for לִקְרַאת;]
usually with v.l., ὑπ-; a meeting; εἰς ἀ., c. gen. or dat., to meet: Mt 25:6 27:32 (WH, txt., omits), Ac 28:15, I Th 4:17 (v. M, Th., in l.; M, Pr., 14, 242; MM, VGT, s.v.; Lft., Notes, 69).†

strong.def: one (or a single) time (numerically or conclusively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἅπαξ, adv., [in LXX for אֶחָד, פַּעַם;]
(a). once: II Co 11:25, He 9:26, 27; ἔτι ἅ., He 12:26, 27; ἅ. τ. ἐνιαυτοῦ, He 9:7; καί ἅ. κ. δίς, twice: Phl 4:16, I Th 2:18;
(b). once for all: He 6:4 9:28 10:2, I Pe 3:18, Ju 3, 5 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3845 (παραβαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀ-παρά-βατος, -ον (< παραβαίνω),
inviolable, and so unchangeable: He 7:24 (v. Westc., in l.; Cremer, 653; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3903 (παρασκευάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀ-παρα-σκεύαστος, -ον (< παρασκευάζω),
unprepared: II Co 9:4.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G756 (ἄρχομαι);
strong.def: a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἀπ-αρχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἀπάρχομαι, to make a beginning in sacrifice, offer first fruits), [in LXX chiefly for תְּרוּמָה, רֵאשִׁית;]
1. the beginning of a sacrifice.
2. first fruits: τοῦ φυράματος (cf. Nu 15:20), Ro 11:16. Metaph., ἀ. τοῦ πνεύματος: Ro 8:23; of Christians: Ro 16:5, I Co 16:15, II Th 2:13 (WH, mg., R, mg., txt., ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς; v. Lft., Notes, 119 f.), Ja 1:18, Re 14:4; of Christ: I Co 15:20, 23 (Cremer, 117; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀπατάω, -ῶ (< ἀπάτη), [in LXX for פּתה, נשׁא hi., etc.;]
to deceive: c. acc., Ja 1:26; c. acc. pers., dat. rei, Eph 5:6; pass., I Ti 2:14 (on its infrequency in late writers, v. MM, VGT, s.v.; cf. ἐξαπατάω).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3962 (πατήρ);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπάτωρ, -ορος, ὁ, ὴ (< ἀ- neg., πατήρ);
1. fatherless.
2. without father (MM, VGT, s.v.), i.e., with no recorded genealogy: He 7:3.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G826 (αὐγάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀπ-αύγασμα, -τος, τό (< αὐγή, brightness, whence ἀπαυγάζω, to radiate or reflect), [in LXX: Wi 7:26*;]
of light beaming from a luminous body, radiance, effulgence: He 1:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ** ἀπείθεια (WH, -θία, exc. He 4:6, 11), -ας, ἡ (< ἀπειθής), [in LXX IV Mac 8:9, 18 12:4*;]
disobedience (MM, VGT, s.v.): Ro 11:30, 32, He 4:6, 11; υἱοὶ τῆς ἀ. (gen. of definition, v. M, Pr., 73 f.), Eph 2:2 5:6, Col 3:6 (T, WH, R, mg., omit).†

strong.kjv: not believe, disobedient, obey not, unbelieving

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἀπειθέω, -ῶ (< ἀπειθής), [in LXX for מרה, סרר, etc.;]
as in cl. (MM, VGT, s.v.); to disobey, be disobedient: absol., Ac 14:2 19:9, Ro 10:21 11:31 15:31, He 3:18 11:31, I Pe 3:20; c. dat., Jo 3:36, Ro 2:8 11:30, I Pe 2:8 3:1 4:17 (Cremer, 475).†

strong.def: to menace; by implication, to forbid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀπειλέω, -ῶ (ἀπειλή), [in LXX: Na 1:4 (גּער), Is 66:14 (זעם), Si 19:17, al.;]
to threaten: I Pe 2:23; mid., Ac 4:17 (v. MM, VGT, s.v., and cf. προσαπειλέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀπειλή, -ῆ, ἡ, [in LXX for גְּעָרָה, etc.;]
threatening, threat: Ac 4:29 9:1, Eph 6:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἄπ-ειμι (εἰμί, sum), [in LXX for כּחד ni., נדח ni.;]
to be absent: I Co 5:3, II Co 10:1, 11 13:2, 10, Phl 1:27, Col 2:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 * ἄπ-ειμι (εἶμι, ibo),
to depart: Ac 17:10.†

strong.derivation: reflexive past of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G2036 (ἔπω);
strong.def: to say off for oneself, i.e. disown

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀπ-εῖπον, 2 aor. without present in use [in LXX for מָאַס, אָמַר, etc.;]
1. to tell out.
2. to forbid (III Ki 11:2).
3. to renounce: 1 aor. mid. (WH, App., 164; MM, VGT, s.v.), II Co 4:2.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3987 (πειράω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀπείραστος, -ον (< πειράζω; for cl. ἀπείρητος, < πειράω),
untempted, untried, without experience: Ja 1:13 (v. Hort, in l.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3984 (πεῖρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄπειρος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., πεῖρα, trial), [in LXX: Nu 14:23, Za 11:15 (אֱוִילִי), Je 2:6 (עֲרָבָה)*;]
without experience of: c. gen. rei, He 5:13 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 *† ἀπ-εκ-δέχομαι, depon.,
to await or expect eagerly (Lft., Notes, 149; MM, VGT, s.v.): absol., I Pe 3:20; c. acc. rei, Ro 8:19, 23, 25, I Co 1:7, Ga 5:5; c. acc. pers., Phl 3:20, He 9:28.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G1562 (ἐκδύω);
strong.def: to divest wholly oneself, or (for oneself) despoil

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀπ-εκ-δύω,
to strip off clothes or arms; mid., to strip off from oneself: Col 3:9; to strip, despoil (mid, for act., ICC, in l.; but cf. Lft., Ellic.), Col 2:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀπ-έκ-δυσις, -εως, ἡ (ἀπεκδύω),
a putting or stripping off: Col 2:11 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀπ-ελαύνω, [in LXX for נצל, שׁלח;]
to drive away: Ac 18:16 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀπ-ελεγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἀπελέγχω, to convict, refute),
refutation, disrepute: ἐλθεῖν εἰς ἀ., Ac 19:27 (not elsewhere; v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: one freed away, i.e. a freedman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπ-ελεύθερος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a freedman: τ. κυρίου (MM, s.v.), I Co 7:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀπελλῆς, -οῦ, acc. -ῆν (MM, s.v.), ὁ,
Apelles: Ro 16:10.†

strong.def: from in front, i.e. opposite, before or against
strong.kjv: before, contrary, over against, in the presence of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † ἀπ-έναντι, adv. c. gen. (Hellenistic, common in LXX);
1. over against (MM, s.v.): Mt 27:61, Mk 12:41, WH, mg.
2. before, in the presence of: Mt 27:24 (WH, mg.), Ac 3:16, Ro 3:18.
3. against: Ac 17:7.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of G4008 (πέραν);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀπέραντος, -ον (< περαίνω, to complete, finish), [in LXX: Jb 36:26 (חֵקֶר אֵין), III Mac 2:9*;]
endless, interminable: I Ti 1:4.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of G4049 (περισπάω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀπερισπάστως, adv. (< περισπάω; the adj. occurs in Wi 16:11 Si 41:1);
without distraction: I Co 7:35.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4059 (περιτέμνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀ-περί-τμητος, -ον (< περιτέμνω), [in LXX chiefly for עָרֵל;]
uncircumcised; metaph. (τ.) καρδίαις (cf. Je 9:26, al.): Ac 7:51. (ἄσημος, found in π., appears to have been the word used by Greek-speaking Egyptians: v. Deiss., BS, 153; cf. also Cremer, 885; MM, s.v.)†

strong.def: to hold oneself off, i.e. refrain
singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἀπλότης, -ητος, ή (< ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: II Ki 15:11 (תֹּם), I Ch 29:17 (לֵבָב ישֶׁר, ἁ. τῆς καρδίας, cf. Col 3:22, where v. Lft.), Wi 1:1, al.;]
simplicity, sincerity: Ro 12:8, II Co 11:3, Eph 6:5, Col 3:22; as manifested in generous, unselfish giving, liberality, graciousness: II Co 8:2 9:11, 13 (v. ICC, Ro., 12:8; Hort, Ja., 1:5, and v.s. ἁπλῶς).†

strong.derivation: adverb from G573 (ἁπλοῦς) (in the objective sense of G572 (ἁπλότης));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἁπλῶς, adv. (< ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: Pr 10:9 (בַּתֹּם), Wi 16:27, II Mac 6:6*;]
simply, sincerely, graciously: Ja 1:5. ("Later writers comprehend under the one word the whole magnanimous and honourable type of character in which ... singleness of mind is the central feature"—Hort, Ja., 1:5)†

strong.def: to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀπο-βλέπω, [in LXX for פּנה, etc.;]
to look away from all else at one object; hence, to look steadfastly: He 11:26 (cf. ἀφοράω).†

strong.def: cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀπό-βλητος, -ον (< ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Le 7:18, al.; Sm.: Ho 9:3 (טמא);]
to be thrown away, rejected: I Ti 4:4 (Hom., Plut.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀπο-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἀποβάλλω);
1. a throwing away, rejection: opp. to πρόσλημψις, Ro 11:15.
2. a losing, loss: Ac 27:22.†

strong.derivation: past participle of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1096 (γίνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** ἀπο-γίνομαι (cl. -γίγν-) [in LXX: Da TH 2:1*;]
1. to be away, removed from.
2. to depart life, to die (MM, s.v.): τ. ἁμαρτίαις, i.e. with ref. to sins, I Pe 2:24 (Cremer, 149, 668).†

strong.def: to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀπο-δείκνυμι, [in LXX: Es 2:9 (ראה), al.;]
1. to bring out, show forth, exhibit (Lft., Notes, 200; ICC, in l.): I Co 4:9.
2. to declare, show: Ac 2:22.
3. to prove: Ac 25:7.
4. As freq. in late Gk., to proclaim to an office: seq. ὅτι, II Th 2:4 (Milligan, in l.; MM, s.v.; Lft., Notes. 113.)†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀπό-δειξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀποδείκνυμι), [in LXX: III Mac 4:20, IV Mac 3:19 13:10*;]
1. a showing off.
2. As used by Gk. philosophers, demonstration, certain proof: I Co 2:4 (v. ICC, in l.; MM, s.v.; Lft., Notes, 173).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀπό-δεκτος, -ον (< άποδέχομαι),
acceptable: I Ti 2:3 5:4.†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of G223 (Ἀλέξανδρος) and G3724 (ὁρίζω);
strong.def: to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπο-δι-ορίζω (< διορίζω, < ἅρος, a limit),
to mark off, hence metaph. to make separations: Ju 19 (Cremer, 806).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἀποδέχομαι),
acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): I Ti 1:15 4:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀπό-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀποτίθημι),
a putting away: I Pe 3:21, II Pe 1:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀπο-θησαυρίζω, [in LXX: Si 3:4*;]
to treasure up, store away: I Ti 6:19.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of (the head) and G1380 (δοκέω) (in the sense of watching);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀπο-καραδοκία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀποκαραδοκέω, used by Aq. in Ps 36 (37):7 for התהוֹלל; < ἀπό, κάρα the head, δοκέω, in Ion., to watch),
to watch with outstretched head, watch anxiously (Polyb., π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 3745, 377 f.), Ro 8:19, Phl 1:20 (Lft., in l.; Cremer, 177).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ἀπο-κατ-αλλάσσω (cf. καταλλάσσω: ἀπό here signifies completely, v. Lft., Col., 1:20, 21; Ellic., Eph., 2:16; but also Mey., Eph., 2:16),
to reconcile completely: Eph 2:16, Col 1:20, 21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπο-κατά-στασις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀποκαθίστημι),
restoration: Ac 3:21 (in π. of repairs and restorations of temples, v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι) (in its original sense of judging);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό (< ἀποκρίνω);
1. prop., a judicial sentence: II Co 1:9, R, mg.
2. an answer (v. Thayer, s.v.): II Co 1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, s.v.: cf. also Cremer, 375).†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2949 (κῦμα);
strong.def: to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀπο-κυέω (Rec. -κύω), -ῶ (< ἀπό, κυέω or κύω, to be pregnant), [in LXX: IV Mac 15:17*;]
prop., "the medical word for birth as the close of pregnancy" (Hort, Ja., 26 f.). In κοινή, "an ordinary syn. of τίκτω, but definitely 'perfectivised' (M, Pr., 111 ff.; MM, s.v.) by the ἀπό, and so implying safe delivery," to bring forth, give birth to: Ja 1:15, 18.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to enjoy);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀπόλαυσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀπολαύω, to take of, enjoy a thing), [in LXX: III Mac 7:16*;]
enjoyment: I Ti 6:17, He 11:25 (for late exx., v. MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀπολλύων, -οντος, ὁ (pres. ptcp. of ἀπολλύω),
Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Re 9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.)†

strong.derivation: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun;
strong.def: from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀπολλωνία, -ας, ἡ,
Apollonia, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:1.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G624 (Ἀπολλωνία);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 Ἀπολλώς, -ώ, ὁ (perh. contr. from Ἀπολλώνιος, Ac 18:24 D),
Apollos: Ac 18:24 19:1, I Co 1:12 3:4-6, 22 4:6 16:12, Tit 3:13.†

strong.kjv: answer (for self), clearing of self, defence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ἀπολογία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀπολογέομαι), [in LXX: Wi 6:10*;]
a speech in defence: Ac 25:16, II Co 7:11, Phl 1:7, 16, II Ti 4:16; c. dat. pers., I Co 9:3, I Pe 3:15; seq. πρός, Ac 22:1.†

strong.def: to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀπο-λούω, [in LXX: Jb 9:30 (רחץ)*;]
to wash off, wash away; mid., metaph., c. acc. rei, to wash off oneself: ἁμαρτίας, Ac 22:16; absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean (cf. Cremer, 406), I Co 6:11.†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament

1. In cl., a sending away (MM, s.v.), as, an expedition (Hdt.).
2. In LXX
(a). discharge, dismissal (Ec 8:8);
(b). a gift (III Ki 9:16, I Mac 2:13).
3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: Ac 1:25, Ro 1:5, I Co 9:2, Ga 2:8 (Cremer, 530).†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.entry:

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ,

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX, in sing.: Hb 3:3, Za 6:13 (הוֹד), in pl.: Is 42:8, 12 43:21 63:7 (תְּהִלָּה), Es 14:10, Wi 4:1 5:13 8:7, II-IV Mac22*;]
prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence—moral goodness, virtue;
(a). of God: II Pe 1:3;
(b). of men: Phl 4:8, II Pe 1:5; pl. (Is 42:8, 12 43:21 63:7, Es 14:10), excellencies: I Pe 2:9 (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; v. Hort, I Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95 f., thinks it means manifestations of divine power, as in current Gk. speech; cf. also MM, s.v.)†

strong.derivation: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G757 (ἄρχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament

5 Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ (< ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling),

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ἄρκος (Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a bear: Re 13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, s.v.)†

strong.derivation: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (perhaps with G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) prefixed);
strong.def: a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719 (ἁρμός)))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἅρμα, -τος, τό (< ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רכב ;]
a chariot: Ac 8:28, 29, 38, Re 9:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹ), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, II Ch 35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jg 1:27;
Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Re 16:16 (v. Swete, in l., but also Thayer, s.v.).†

strong.def: to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἁρμόζω (< ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc.;]
1. to fit, join.
2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid.,
(a). to join to oneself, marry, take to wife;
(b). to give in marriage: II Co 11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But v. M, Pr., 160; MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Si 27:2, IV Mac 10:5*;]
a joining, joint: He 4:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
30 ἀρνίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ἀρήν; v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Ps 113 (114):4, 6 (pl., עאֹן בְּנֵן), Je 11:19 (כֶּבֶשׁ), 27 (50):45 (צָעִיר)*;]
a little lamb, a lamb: Jo 21:15, Re27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ (< ἁρπάζω);
1. prop., acc., to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., de Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Phl 2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l.; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, s.v.).
2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Ez 22:25, of a lion's prey, טֶרֶף), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phl 2:6, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l.; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have accepted the latter as seeming to suit the logic of the passage better. The lexical difficulty, however, remains (MM, s.v., esp. the last ref.). As to the usage of St. Paul, he seems inclined to adopt the -μα form where it is appropriate (e.g. Ro 11:9, where cf. LXX; I Co 13:9, II Co 1:9), and there is certainly a presumption in favour of the active meaning here from the fact that he does not use the LXX ἅρπαγμα. Suggestions looking to a fresh exegesis are given in JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911.†

strong.kjv: catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament

an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: II Co 1:22 5:5, Eph 1:14. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phœnicians (AR, Eph., 1:14). It is found in π. with both spellings (v. Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; v. MM, s.v.)†

strong.def: unsewed, i.e. of a single piece

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) * ἄραφος, -ον (Rec. ἄρραφος, < ῥάπτω, to sew)
without seam: Jo 19:23.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G4490 (ῥητῶς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄρρητος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Le 18:23*;]
1. unspoken (Hom., al.).
2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; freq. in Inscr.; MM, s.v.): II Co 12:4.†

strong.kjv: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀρσενοκοίτης, -ου, ὁ (< ἄρσην, κοιτή),
a sodomite: I Co 6:9, I Ti 1:10.†

strong.derivation: contracted from a compound of G735 (Ἄρτεμις) and G1435 (δῶρον);
strong.def: gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀρτεμᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ,
Artemas: Tit 3:12.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G736 (ἀρτέμων);
strong.def: prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ,
Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: Ac 19:24, 27, 28, 34, 35.†

strong.def: properly, something ready (or else more remotely from G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ (< ἀρτάω, to fasten to),
a fore-sail or top-sail: Ac 27:40 (v. DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)) through the idea of suspension;
strong.kjv: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
36 ἄρτι, adv., [in LXX: Da LXX 9:22 10:11 (עַתָּה), al.;] adv., of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future,
just, just now, this moment: Mt 3:15 9:18 26:53, Jo 13:7, Ga 4:20, I Th 3:6 (v. Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l.), Re 12:10; opp. to past time, Jo 9:19, 25 13:33, I Co 16:7, Ga 1:9, 10; to future, Jo 13:37 16:12, 31, I Co 13:12, II Th 2:7, I Pe 1:6, 8; ἄχρι τῆς ἄ. ὥρας, I Co 4:11; ἕως ἄ., Mt 11:12, Jo 2:10 5:17 16:24, I Co 4:13 8:7 15:6, I Jo 2:9; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., v.s. ἀπάρτι (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀρτι-γέννητος, -ον (< ἄρτι, γεννάω),
new-born: I Pe 2:2 (Luc.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄρτιος, -α, -ον,
fitted, complete: II Ti 3:17 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ (< ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος),
archangel, a chief angel: I Th 4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ,
Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judæa, Samaria and Idumæa: Mt 2:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀρχηγός, -όν, [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, נָשִׂיא etc.;]
beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.;
1. founder, author (Lat. auchor; so sometimes in π., v. MM, s.v.; Milligan, NTD, 75): Ac 3:15 (R, mg.), He 2:10 (R, txt.; but v. Westc., in l., and Page, Ac 3:15).
2. prince, leader (so in MGr., v. Kennedy, Sources, 153): Ac 3:15 (R, txt.) 5:31, He 2:10 (cf. R, mg.) 12:2 (Cremer, 117).†

strong.derivation: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a derivative of G2413 (ἱερός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀρχ-ιερατικός, -ή, -όν (< ἀρχιερύς),
high-priestly: Ac 4:6 (MM, s.v.).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ, [in Sm.: IV Ki 3:4*;]
found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, s.v.); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, I Pe 5:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἄρχιππος, -ου, ὁ,
Archippus: Col 4:17, Phm 2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ (< τέκτων), [in LXX: Is 3:3 (חָרָשׁ) Si 38:27, II Mac 2:29*;]
a master-builder, architect: I Co 3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2827 (κλίνω) (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ (< τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches)
the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): Jo 2:8, 9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף),
Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: Mt 1:7, 8.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531 (σαλεύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον (< σαλεύω), [in LXX: Ex 13:16, De 6:8 11:18 (טוֹטָפָוֹת)*;]
unmoved, immovable: Ac 27:41; metaph., He 12:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc.;]
ungodliness, impiety: Ro 1:18 11:26, II Ti 2:16, Tit 2:12; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to be (by implied act) impious or wicked
strong.kjv: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀσεβέω, -ῶ (< ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פּשׁע, רשׁע;]
to be ungodly, act profanely: II Pe 2:6; c. cogn. acc. (MM, s.v.), Ju 15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι);
strong.def: irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἀσεβής, -ές (σέβω, to reverence), [in LXX chiefly for רשׁע;]
ungodly, impious: Ro 4:5 5:6, I Ti 1:9, I Pe 4:18, II Pe 2:5, 6 3:7, Ju 4, 15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄσημος, -ον (< σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: Ge 30:42 (עטף), Jb 42:11, III Mac 1:3*;]
without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, s.v.). Metaph. (MM, s.v.), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, Ac 21:39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀσθένημα, -τος, τό (< ἀσθενής),
an infirmity (MM, s.v.): Ro 15:1.†

strong.def: Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 Ἀσία, -ας, ἡ,
Asia, the Roman province: Ac 2:9 6:9 16:6 19:1, 10, 22, 26 (M, Pr., 73), Ac 19:27 Ac 20:4, 16, 18 21:27 24:18 27:2, Ro 16:5, I Co 16:19, II Co 1:8, II Ti 1:15, I Pe 1:1, Re 1:4.†

strong.def: an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀσιανός, -ή, -όν,
Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: Ac 20:4.†

strong.def: an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† Ἀσιάρχης, -ου, ὁ,
an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: Ac 19:31 (Strab., Inscr.; DB, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4621 (σῖτος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄσιτος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., σῖτος),
fasting, without eating (cf. MM, s.v.): Ac 27:33.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G4632 (σκεῦος);
strong.def: to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀσκέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Mac 15:4*;]
1. to adorn (poët.).
2. to practise, exercise (Hdt., Xen.).
3. to endeavour (Xen., al.): c. inf., Ac 24:16.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀσμένως, adv. (< ἥδομαι, to be glad), [in LXX: II Mac 4:12 10:33, III Mac 3:15 5:21*;]
gladly: Ac 21:17.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4680 (σοφός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄ-σοφος, -ον, [in LXX: Pr 9:8 א2 A*;]
unwise, foolish: Eph 5:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4695 (σπιλόω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† ἄ-σπιλος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., σπῖλος), [in Sm.: Jb 15:15 (LXX, καθαρός)*;]
spotless, unstained: I Pe 1:19; metaph., I Ti 6:14, Ja 1:27, II Pe 3:14 (for exx., v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀσπίς, -ίδος, ἡ, [in LXX for פֶּתֶן, etc.;]
an asp: Ro 3:13.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689 (σπένδω);
strong.def: literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἄσπονδος, -ον (< σπονδή, a libation);
1. without truce (Thuc.).
2. admitting of no truce, implacable (Dem., al.): II Ti 3:3.†

strong.derivation: neuter comparative of the base of G1451 (ἐγγύς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἆσσον (Rec., after Vg., Ἄσσον), adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near),
nearer: Ac 27:13 (RV, close in shore; v. Bl., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).†

strong.def: Assus, a city of Asia MInor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἄσσος, -ου (also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ἡ,
Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: Ac 20:13, 14 (v.s. ἆσσον).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀστατέω, -ῶ (< ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Is 58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)*;]
to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, s.v.): I Co 4:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀστεῖος, -ον (< ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: Ex 2:2 (טוֹב), Nu 22:32 (οὐκ ἀ. ירט), Jg 3:17 (בָּרִיא), Jth 11:23, Da LXX, Sus 7, II Mac 6:23*;]
1. of the town.
2. (Like Lat. urbanus),
(a). courteous,
(b). elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, s.v.), comely, fair (as in Ex 2:2), He 11:23, Ac 7:20.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4741 (στηρίζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀ-στήρικτος, -ον (< στηρίζω),
unstable, unsettled: II Pe 2:14 3:16.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of (to cherish affectionately);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἄστοργος, -ον (< στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, v.s. ἀγάπη),
without natural affection: Ro 1:31, II Ti 3:3 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (an aim);
strong.def: to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† ἀστοχέω, -ῶ (στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Si 7:19 8:9*;]
to miss the mark, fail: c. gen., I Ti 1:6 (so in π., MM, s.v.); seq. περί, I Ti 6:21, II Ti 2:18.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793 (συγκρίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀσύνκριτος (Rec. Ἀσύγκρ.), -ου, ὁ,
Asyncritus: Ro 16:14.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4859 (σύμφωνος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀ-σύμφωνος, -ον, [in LXX: Wi 18:10, Da, LXX, Bel 15*;]
dissonant, discordant; metaph., at variance: πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Ac 28:25.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934 (συντίθεμαι);
strong.def: properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀ-σύν-θετος, -ον (< συντίθεμαι; v. M, Pr., 222; MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Je 3:7, 8, 10, 11 (בּגד)*;]
false to engagements, not keeping covenant, faithless (MM, s.v.): Ro 1:31.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀσφαλής, -ές (< ἀ- neg., σφάλλω, to trip up), [in LXX for אשׁר pu., etc.;]
certain, secure, safe: Ac 21:34 22:30 25:26, Phl 3:1, He 6:19 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ἀσφαλίζω (< ἀσφαλής), [in LXX: Ne 3:15 (חזק hi.), Is 41:10 (תּמךְ), Wi 4:17 10:12 13:15*;]
to make firm, secure: mid., Mt 27:65, 66, Ac 16:24; pass., Mt 27:64 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀσχημονέω, -ῶ (< ἀσχήμαων), [in LXX: Ez 16:7, 22, 39 23:29 (עֶרְיָה); De 25:3 (קלה ni.)*;]
to act unbecomingly, behave dishonourably: I Co 13:5; seq. ἐπί, I Co 7:36 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: an indecency; by implication, the pudenda

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀσχημοσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ἀσχήμων), [in LXX chiefly for עֶרְוָה;]
unseemliness: Ro 1:27 (MM, s.v.); euphemism for ἡ αἰσχύνη, as freq. in LXX, shame, nakedness: Re 16:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of its congener G4976 (σχῆμα));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀσχήμων, -ον (< ἀ- neg., σχῆμα), [in LXX: Ge 34:7 (נְבָלָה), De 24:1 (עֶרְוָה), Wi 2:20, Da TH Sus 63, II Mac 9:2*;]
1. shapeless.
2. uncomely, unseemly: I Co 12:23.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4982 (σώζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀσωτία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀ- neg., σώζω), [in LXX: Pr 28:7 (זלל), II Mac 6:4*;]
prodigality, wastefulness, profligacy: Eph 5:18, Tit 1:6, I Pe 4:4 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀτακτέω, -ῶ (< ἄτακτος),
primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaph., to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): II Th 3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, v. M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021 (τάσσω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
