1 ** ἄ-τακτος, -ον (< τάσσω), [in LXX: III Mac 1:19*;]
out of order, out of place (Lat. inordinatus), freq. of soldiers not keeping the ranks, or an army in disarray (cf. III Mac 1:19); hence, metaph., irregular, disorderly (v. previous word): I Th 5:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἀ-τάκτως, adv., [in Sm.: IV Ki 9:20*;]
disorderly, irregularly: II Th 3:6, 11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἀτιμία, -ας, ἡ (ἄτιμος), [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן, etc.;]
dishonour, disgrace: I Co 11:14, II Co 6:8; εἰς ἀ., Ro 9:21, II Ti 2:20; ἐν ἀ., I Co 15:43; κατ᾽ ἀ., II Co 11:21; πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions, Ro 1:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀτμίς, -ίδος, ἡ, [in LXX for עָנָן, תִּימָרָה, etc.;]
vapour: Ja 4:14; ἀ. καπνοῦ, Ac 2:19(LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);
strong.def: uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄ-τομος, -ον (< τέμνω), [in Sm.: Is 54:8 (MM, s.v.)*;]
indivisible; of time, ἄτομον, a moment: ἐν ἄ., I Co 15:52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀτταλία (Rec. -άλεια), -υς, ἡ,
Attalia, a city of Pamphylia: Ac 14:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αὐγάζω (< αὐγή), [in LXX: Le 13:24-26, 28, 38 14:56 (בַּהֶרֶת) 13:39 (כֵּהֶה)*;]
1. Trans. (cl.), to irradiate.
2. Intrans.
(a). (poët.), to see clearly (so perh. II Co 4:4; MM, s.v.);
(b). as in LXX, to shine forth: II Co 4:4 (cf. δι-, κατ-αυγάζω).†

strong.def: a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αὐγή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Is 59:9 (נְגֹהָה), II Mac 12:9*;]
1. brightness
2. Later (as in MGr.; MM, s.v.), daylight, dawn: Ac 20:11 (Cremer, 118).†

strong.derivation: from G846 (αὐτός) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 αὐθάδης, -ες (< αὐτός, ἥδομαι), [in LXX: Ge 49:3, 7 (עַז), Pr 21:24 (יָהִיר)*;]
self-pleasing, arrogant: Tit 1:7, II Pe 2:10 (Cremer, 654).†

strong.derivation: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G140 (αἱρετίζω);
strong.kjv: of own accord, willing of self

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** αὐθαίρετος, -ον (< αὐτός, αἱρέομαι), [in Sm.: Ex 35:5, 22*;]
1. self-chosen.
2. of one's own accord: II Co 8:3, 17.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G846 (αὐτός) and an obsolete (a worker);
strong.def: to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† αὐθεντέω, -ῶ (< αὐθέντης, i.e. αὐτο- ἕντης, one who acts on his own authority, in π., an autocrat; cf. Wi 12:6; cf. -ία, III Mac 2:29; -ικος is freq. in vernacular, MM, s.v.),
to govern, exercise authority over: I Ti 2:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * αὐλητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< αὐλέω),
a flute-player: Mt 9:23, Re 18:22 (MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αὐλός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἄω, to blow), [in LXX chiefly for חָלִיל;]
a pipe: I Co 14:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** αὔξησις, -εως, ἡ (< αὔξω), [in LXX: II Mac 5:16*;]
increase, growth: Eph 4:16, Col 2:19.†

strong.def: self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * αὐτάρκεια, -ας, ἡ (< αὐτάρκης, q.v.),
(a). sufficiency (MM, s.v.): in subjective sense (v. Milligan, NTD, 57), II Co 9:8;
(b). contentment: I Ti 6:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αὐτάρκης, -ες (< αὐτός, ἀρκέω), [in LXX: Pr 24:31 (30:8) (חֹק), Si 5:1 11:24 34 (31):28 40:18, IV Mac 9:9*;]
as in cl., in philosophical sense, self-sufficient, independent; subjectively, contented: Phl 4:11 (in non-lit. π., the word means simply enough, sufficient; MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G846 (αὐτός) and a derivative or G2632 (κατακρίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† αὐτο-κατά-κριτος, -ον (< αὐτός, κατακρίνω),
self-condemned: Tit 3:11 (Eccl., Cremer, 377; MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * αὐτό-χειρ, -ρος, ὁ, ἡ (< αὐτός, χείρ),
with one's own hand: Ac 27:19.†

strong.derivation: from (probably from a base akin to that of G109 (ἀήρ)) (dust, as dried by wind);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * αὐχμηρός, -ά, -όν (< αὐχμός, drought);
1. dry.
2. squalid, dismal: II Pe 1:19 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5316 (φαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀφανής, -ές (< φαίνω), [in LXX: Ne 4:8 (2), Jb 24:20, Si 20:30 41:14, II Mac 3:34*;]
unseen, hidden: He 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀφανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἀφανίζω), [in LXX chiefly for שַׁמָּה, שְׁמָמָה;]
vanishing: He 8:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5339 (φείδομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀφειδία (L, -εία), -ας, ἡ (< ἀφειδής, unsparing);
1. extravagance.
2. unsparing treatment, severity: Col 2:23.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀφελότης, -ητος, ἡ = cl. ἀφέλεια (v. MM, s.v.),
simplicity: Ac 2:46.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἁφή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἅπτω, to fasten, fit), [in LXX for נֶגַע, freq. in Le;]
a joint (MM, s.v.): Eph 4:16, Col 2:19 (Lft., in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 **† ἀφθαρσία, -ας, ἡ (< ἄφθαρτος), [in LXX: Wi 2:23 6:19, IV Mac 9:22 17:12*;]
incorruptibility, immortality: Ro 2:7, I Co 15:42, 50, 53, 54, II Ti 1:10; ἀγαπώντων . . . ἐν ἀ., Eph 6:24 (v. AR, in l.).†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι, [in LXX for בּוֹא, etc.;] perfective of ἱκνέομαι,
to come (M, Pr., 247), to arrive at, come to, reach: metaph. (MM, s.v.), Ro 16:19.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5358 (φιλάγαθος);
strong.kjv: despiser of those that are good

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀ-φιλ-άγαθος, -ον,
without love of good: II Ti 3:3 (not elsewhere in Gk. lit., but v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5366 (φιλάργυρος);
strong.kjv: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀ-φιλ-άργυρος, -ον,
without love of money, not avaricious; I Ti 3:3, He 13:5. (For other instances, v. MM, s.v.)†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄφ-ιξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἀφικνέομαι), [in LXX: III Mac 7:18*;]
in cl. usually, arrival; rarely, departure: Ac 20:29 (so in π., cf. MM, s.v.; M, Pr., 26, n.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄφνω, adv., [in LXX for פִּתְאֹם;]
suddenly: Ac 2:2 16:26 28:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀφ-οράω, -ῶ, [in LXX: IV Mac 17:10 (είς θεόν)*;]
(a). to look away from all else at, fix one's gaze upon: metaph. (MM, s.v.), He 12:2;
(b). simply, to see: ἀφίδω (v.s. ἀπεῖδον, and Lft., Phl., in l.; MM, s.v.), Phl 2:23 (v. Ellic., in l.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3729 (ὁρμάω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἀφ-ορμή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Ez 5:7 (הָמַן), Pr 9:9, III Mac 3:2*;]
prop., a starting point; in war, a base of operations; metaph., an occasion, incentive, opportunity (MM, s.v.): II Co 11:12, Ga 5:13; ἀφ. λαμβάνειν, Lk 11:24, WH, mg., Ro 7:8, 11; ἀφ. διδόναι, II Co 5:12, I Ti 5:14.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5456 (φωνή);
strong.def: voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄφωνος, -ον (φωνή), [in LXX: Is 53:7 (אלם ni.), Wi 4:19, II Mac 3:29*;]
dumb, speechless: Ac 8:32(LXX); of idols (MM, s.v.), I Co 12:2; of beasts, II Pe 2:19; τοσαῦτα γένη φωνῶν καὶ οὐδὲν ἄ.—so many kinds of voices and none voiceless, i.e. without signification, unintelligible: I Co 14:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἄχαζ (WH, Ἄχας), ὁ (Heb. אָחָז),
Ahaz: Mt 1:9.†

strong.def: Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 Ἀχαία (T, Ἀχαΐα), -ας, ἡ (Bl., § 46, 11),
Achaia, the Roman province: Ac 18:12, 27 19:21, Ro 15:26, I Co 16:15, II Co 1:1 9:2 11:10, I Th 1:7, 8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀχαϊκός, -οῦ, ὁ,
Achaicus: I Co 16:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἀχείμ, ὁ,
Achim: Mt 1:14.†

strong.def: dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀχλύς, -ύος, ἡ, [in Aq.: Ez 12:7; Sm.: Jb 3:5*;]
a mist, esp. a dimness of the eyes: Ac 13:11 (v. Tr., Syn., § c).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀχρεόω (Rec. -ειόω, Polyb., LXX), -ῶ (< ἄχρεος = ἀχρεῖος), [in LXX (-ειόω) for אלח ni., etc.;]
to make useless, unprofitable: pass., Ro 3:12(LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5543 (χρηστός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄ-χρηστος, -ον, [in LXX: Ho 8:8 (חֵפֶץ אַיִן), Wi 2:11, Si 16:1, al.;]
useless, unserviceable: opp. to εὔχρηστος, Phm 11.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5579 (ψεῦδος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀ-ψευδής, -ές (< ψεῦδος), [in LXX: Wi 7:17*;]
free from falsehood, truthful: Tit 1:2.†

strong.def: wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἄψινθος, -ου, ἡ (also ἀψίνθιον, τό; ἀψινθία, ἡ),
wormwood: as a proper name, Re 8:11.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5590 (ψυχή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄψυχος, -ον (< ψυχή), [in LXX: Wi 13:17 14:29*;]
inanimate, lifeless: I Co 14:7.†

strong.def: Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βάαλ (Rec. βαάλ), ὁ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord),
Baal: Ro 11:4(LXX). The fem. art. here agrees with the usage of LXX, where, following a similar Hebrew practice (בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל), αἰσχύνη appears to have been substituted in reading for the written Βάαλ (cf. III Ki 18:19), and to account for the freq. use of the fem. art. bef. Β. The usage, however, is not general, and in the passage cited in Ro (III Ki 19:18), LXX reads τῷ Β.†

strong.def: Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 Βαβυλών, -ῶνος, ἡ (בָּבֶל, Heb. form of Assyr. Bab-ili, Gate of God),
Babylon: Mt 1:11, 12, 17, Ac 7:43(LXX); symbolically, of Rome: Re 14:8 16:19 17:5 18:2, 10, 21, and prob. also I Pe 5:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός (< βαίνω, to step), [in LXX I Ki 5:5 (מִפְתָּן), IV Ki 20:9, 10, 11 (מַעֲלָה), Si 6:36*;]
a step (IV Ki 20:9, 10, 11, of degrees of a dial); metaph., a degree, standing: I Ti 3:13.†

strong.derivation: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939 (βάσις);
strong.def: a palm twig (as going out far)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† βαΐον, ου, τό (also βὰϊον, another form of βὰϊς, from the Egyptian), [in LXX: I Mac 13:51*;], (freq. in Egyptian π., v. MM, Exp., x);
a palm-branch: Jo 12:13 (DB, i, 314).†

strong.def: Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Βαλαάμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בִּלְעָם), as in LXX (FlJ has ὁ βάλαμος);
Balaam (Nu 22-24): II Pe 2:15, Ju 11, Re 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαλάκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּלָק),
Balak; (Nu 22:2): Re 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαράκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּרָק),
Barak (Jg 4:6): He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαραχίας, -ου, ὁ (Heb. בֶּרֶכְיָה),
Barachiah: Mt 23:35, v.s. Ζαχαρίας.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 βάρβαρος, -ον (prob. onomatop., descriptive of unintelligible sounds), [in LXX: Ps 113 (114):1 (לעז), Ez 21:31 (36) (בּער), II Mac 2:21 4:25 10:4, III Mac 3:24*;]
barbarous, barbarian, strange to Greek language and culture (and also, after the Persian war, with the added sense of brutal, rude): Ac 28:2, 4, Ro 1:14, I Co 14:11, Col 3:11 (v. Lft., in l., and Notes, 249).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βαρέως, adv. (< βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, Ge 31:35 (בעיני חרה); β. ἀκούειν, Is 6:10 (כּבד hi.)*;]
heavily, with difficulty: Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (LXX).†

strong.def: son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαρ-ιησοῦς, -οῦ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יֵשׁוּעַ, son of Joshua),
Bar-Jesus: Ac 13:6 (v.s. Ἐλύμας).†

strong.def: son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαριωνᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יוֹנָה, son of Jonah),
Bar-Jonah, a surname of Peter: Mt 16:17.†

strong.def: son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 Βαρ-ναβᾶς, -α, ὁ (Aram. בַּר, son, as prefix to another word interpreted in Ac 4:36, τῆς παρακλήσεως, perh. נְבוּאָה, wh., however, should be rendered by προφητεία as in II Es 6:14, LXX. Deiss., BS, 309 f., thinks Β. may be a variant of the name Βαρνεβοῦς, son of Nebo, found in a Syrian Inscr., altered with a view to disguising its origin; v. also Milligan, NTD, iii; Dalman, Gr., 142),
Barnabas: Ac 4:36 9:27 11:22, 30 12:25 13-15, I Co 9:6, Ga 2:1, 9, 13, Col 4:10.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going down;
strong.def: compare G899 (βάθος)); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 βάρος, -εος, τό, [in LXX: Jg 18:21 (כּבד), Jth 7:4, Si 13:2, II Mac 9:10, III Mac 5:47*;]
weight;
(a). a weight, burden, lit. and metaph.: Mt 20:12, Ac 15:28, II Co 4:17, Re 2:24; ἀλλήλων τὰ β., one another's faults, Ga 6:2; ἐν β., burdensome: I Th 2:6, R, txt., but v. infr.;
(b). in late Gk. (Soph., Lex., s.v.), dignity, authority: ἐν βάρει, I Th 2:6 (R, mg.; v. Milligan, ICG, in l.).†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (H01247 and probably H06634);
strong.def: son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba),
Barsabbas:
1. the surname of one Joseph: Ac 1:23.
2. The surname of one Judas: Ac 15:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ, [in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד;]
heavy: Mt 23:4. Metaph., burdensome: ἐντολή, I Jo 5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, II Co 10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mt 23:23; αἰτιώματα, Ac 25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Ac 20:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * βαρύτιμος, -ον (< βαρύς, τιμή),
of great value, very costly: Mt 26:7 (T, πολυτίμου).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** βασανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< βασανίζω), [in LXX: IV Mac 9:6 11:2*;]
torture, torment: Re 9:5 14:11 18:7, 10, 15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< βασανίζω),
prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mt 18:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; < βασιλεύς), [in LXX; Ex 19:6, De 3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Ex 23:22, Wi 18:15, III Mac 3:28, IV Mac 3:8*;]
royal: I Pe 2:9(LXX) (v. Hort, in l.).†

strong.def: regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 βασιλικός, -ή, -όν (< βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates;]
royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Ac 12:20; ἐσθής, Ac 12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king (LAE, p. 3673), Ja 2:8; τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, Jo 4:46, 49 (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).†

strong.def: a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βάσις, -εως, ἡ (< βαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for אֶדֶן;]
1. a step (Æsch., al.).
2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wi 13:18): Ac 3:7.†

strong.def: to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βασκαίνω, [in LXX: De 28:54, 56 (רעע), Si 14:6, 8*;]
1. to slander (Dem.).
2. to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Ga 3:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βάτραχος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Ex 8, Ps 77 (78):45 104 (105):30 (צְכַרִדֵּעַ), Wi 19:10*;]
a frog: Re 16:13.†

strong.def: to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; v. MM, s.v.; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a);
to stammer, repeat idly: Mt 6:7 (Cremer, 765).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † βδελυκτός, ή, -όν (< βδελύσσω), [in LXX: Pr 17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Si 41:5, II Mac 1:27*;]
abominable, detestable: Tit 1:16 (Cremer, 137).†

strong.def: to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βδελύσσω (< βδέω, to stink), [in LXX chiefly for תּעב, שׁקץ;] >in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι);
to make foul; pass., Re 21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Ro 2:22 (Cremer, 137).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of basality);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; < βαίνω), [in LXX: Es 3:13, Wi 7:23, III Mac 5:31 7:7, IV Mac 17:4*;]
firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, He 6:19; metaph., sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109; cf . two foll. words): ἐπαγγελία, Ro 4:16; ἐλπίς, II Co 1:6; λόγος, He 2:2; παρρησία, He 3:6; ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), He 3:14; διαθήκη, He 9:17; κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, II Pe 1:10; comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος, II Pe 1:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (< βεβαιόω, q.v.), [in LXX: Le 25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wi 6:19*;]
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Phl 1:7; εἰς β., He 6:16, a phrase freq. in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104 ff.; Cremer, 140).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G939 (βάσις) and (a threshold);
strong.def: accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 βέβηλος, -ον (< βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל;]
1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (v. DCG, ii, 422b); hence,
2. (opp. to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, I Ti 4:7 6:20, II Ti 2:16; of men, I Ti 1:9, He 12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † βεβηλόω, -ῶ (< βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל;]
to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mt 12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Ac 24:6 (Cremer, 141).†

strong.def: worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else < Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest),
Beliar, a name of Satan: II Co 6:15 (v. DB, i, 269).†

strong.def: a missile, i.e. spear or arrow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βέλος, -εος, τό (< βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ;]
a missile, a dart: Eph 6:16.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (βάλλω) (used for the comparative of G18 (ἀγαθός));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βελτίων, -ον (gen. -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
neut. as adv., better, very well: II Ti 1:18 (also Ac 10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, v. M, Pr., 78, 236.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין),
Benjamin: Ac 13:21, Ro 11:1, Phl 3:5, Re 7:8.†

strong.derivation: from a provincial form of G5342 (φέρω) and G3529 (νίκη);
strong.def: victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη, Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ,
Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Ac 25:13, 23 26:30.†

strong.derivation: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (πέραν) (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Βέροια, -ας, ἡ,
Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:10, 13.†

strong.def: a Berœoean or native of Berœa

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βεροιαῖος, -α, -ον,
Berœan: Ac 20:4.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H02617);
strong.def: house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, v. Westc. on Jo 5:2, and DB, i, 279),
Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jo 5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).†

strong.def: a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 βῆμα, -τος, τό (< βαίνω), [in LXX: De 2:5 (מִדְרָךְ), Ne 8:4 (מִגְדָּל), I Es 9:42, Si 19:30 45:9, II Mac 13:26*;]
1. a step, stride, pace: Ac 7:5.
2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; freq. of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: Mt 27:19, Jo 19:13, Ac 12:21, 18:12, 16, 17 25:6, 10, 17; β. τοῦ θεοῦ, Ro 14:10; τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 5:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: To 13:17 (-ύλλιον in Ex 28:20, שֹׁהַם)*;]
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Re 21:20.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G979 (βίος) (through the idea of vital activity);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 βία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ, etc.;]
strength, force, violence: Ac 5:26 21:35 24:7 27:41.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βίαιος, -α, -ον (< βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר, etc.;]
violent: Ac 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< βιάζω), late form of βιατάς;
1. strong, forceful.
2. violent (Philo): Mt 11:12 (v.s. βιάζω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (dim. of βιβλάριον, dim. of βίβλος),
a little book: Re 10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.†

strong.derivation: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of G1006 (βόσκω));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose, [in LXX for אכל;]
to eat: Jo 6:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Βιθυνία, -ας,
Bithynia, a province in Asia Minor: Ac 16:7, I Pe 1:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βιόω, -ῶ (< βίος), [in LXX: Pr 7:2 9:6 (חיה), Jb 29:18, Wi 4:4 א1, 12:23, Si 40:28, IV Mac 5:22 17:18 * ;]
to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more freq. 2 aor., -ναι), I Pe 4:2 (cf. Jb, l.c.).†

strong.def: living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† βίωσις, -εως, ἡ (< βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;]
manner of life: Ac 26:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βλαβερός, -ά, -όν (< βλάπτω), [in LXX: Pr 10:26* ;]
hurtful: I Ti 6:9.†

strong.derivation: perhaps the same as the base of G985 (βλαστάνω);
strong.def: Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ,
Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Ac 12:20.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G984 (βλάπτω) and G5345 (φήμη);
strong.def: scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 βλάσφημος, -ον (< βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., v. Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Is 66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wi 1:6, Si 3:16, II Mac 9:28 10:4, 36 * ;]
(a). evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Ac 6:11, II Ti 3:2, II Pe 2:11 (cf. Ju 9);
(b). as subst. a blasphemer: I Ti 1:13 (Cremer, 570).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * βλέμμα, -τος, τό (< βλέπω),
a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, II Pe 2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)†

strong.def: a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βοή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX for זְעָקָה, etc. ;]
a cry: Ja 5:4.†

strong.def: aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (v.s. βοηθέω), [in LXX for עֵזֶר, etc. ;]
help: He 4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Ac 27:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βοηθός, -ον (v.s. βοηθέω), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.).
2. helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: He 13:6 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * βολίζω (< βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead),
to heave the lead, take soundings: Ac 27:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βόρβορος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Je 45(38):6 (טִיט)* ;]
mud, filth: II Pe 2:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 Βοσόρ v. Βεώρ.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ (< βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב,דֶשֶׁא,חָצִיר;]
1. grass, fodder.
2. green herb: He 6:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for אֶשְׁכֹּל;]
a cluster of grapes: Re 14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 βούλημα, -τος, τό (< βούλομαι), [in LXX: Pr 9:10 (דַּעַת), II Mac 15:5, IV Mac 8:18*;]
purpose, will: Ac 27:43, Ro 9:19, I Pe 4:3.†

strong.def: an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * βραβεῖον, -ου, τό (< βραβεύς, an umpire),
a prize in the games: I Co 9:24; metaph., of the Christian's reward, Phl 3:14.†

strong.def: to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** βραβεύω (< βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wi 10:12 * ;]
(a). prop., to act as umpire; hence,
(b). generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.c.; MM, s.v.): Col 3:15;
(c). in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.c., acc. to Thayer, s.v., Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βραδύνω (< βραδύς), [in LXX: Ge 43:10 (מההּ hith.), De 7:10, Is 46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;]
1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.c.).
2. More freq. intrans., to be slow, to tarry: I Ti 3:15, II Pe 3:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1021 (βραδύς) and a prolonged form of G4126 (πλέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† βραδυπλοέω, -ῶ (< βραδύς, πλοῦς),
to sail slowly: Ac 27:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * βραδύτης, -ῆτος, ἡ,
slowness: II Pe 3:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< βρέχω), [in LXX: Ps 67 (68):9, 104 (105):32 (גֶּשֶׁם)* ;]
1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77).
2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Mt 7:25, 27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βρόχος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Pr 6:5 (יָד) 7:21 (חֵלֶק) 22:25 (מֹוקֵשׁ), III Mac 4:8 * ;]
a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaph., a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): I Co 7:35.†

strong.def: to grate the teeth (in pain or rage)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω), [in LXX: Jb 16:10(9), Ps 34 (35):16 36 (37):12 111 (112):10, La 2:16 (חרק)* ;]
1. to bite or eat greedily.
2. to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Ac 7:54.†

strong.def: to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac.,
to be full to bursting;
1. of the earth producing vegetation.
2. Of plants putting forth buds.
3. Of springs, to gush with water: Ja 3:11.†

strong.def: (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל ;]
1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Ro 14:17, Col 2:16 (v. Lft., ICC, in l.); c. gen. obj., I Co 8:4; metaph., corrosion, rust: Mt 6:19, 20.
2. As also in cl. (Hom., al.) = βρῶμα, food: Jo 6:27a, II Co 9:10, Col 2:16 (EV, but v. supr.). He 12:16; metaph., of spiritual nourishment, Jo 4:32 6:27b, 55.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Ex 15:5, Ne 9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Ps 67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;]
1. the bottom.
2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: II Co 11:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (< βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης,
a tanner: Ac 9:43 10:6, 32.†

strong.def: made of linen (neuter a linen cloth)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 βύσσινος, -η, -ον (< βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;]
made of βύσσος, fine linen: Re 18:12, 16 19:8, 14.†

strong.def: properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה ;]
1. any raised place, a platform.
2. an altar: Ac 17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and v. DB, i, 75).†

strong.def: the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γαββαθα (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl.,
Gabbatha, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (DB, s.v.; Dalman, Words, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, stone pavement: Jo 19:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† γάγγραινα, -ης, ἡ,
a gangrene, an eating sore, which leads to mortification: II Ti 2:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γάδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גָּד),
Gad (Ge 30:11 49:13, al.): Re 7:5.†

strong.derivation: from (a town east of the Jordan);
strong.def: a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γαδαρηνός, -ή, -όν (< Γαδαρά, Gadara, the capital of Peræa),
Gadarene, of Gadara: Mt 8:28 (Rec. Γεργεσηνῶν), Mk 5:1, Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν), Lk 8:26, 37 Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † γάζα, -ης, ἡ (a Persian word), [in LXX for גִּנְזִין, II Es 5:17 6:1 7:20, 21, Es 4:7; גִּזְבָּר, II Es 7:21; Is 39:2 * ;]
treasure: Ac 8:27.†

strong.def: Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γάζα -ης, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה),
Gaza, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines: Ac 8:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.),
Gaius, the name of a Christian;
1. of Macedonia: Ac 19:29.
2. Of Derbe: Ac 20:4.
3. Of Corinth: Ro 16:23, I Co 1:14.
4. The one to whom III Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 γάλα, -ακτος, τό [in LXX for חלב ;]
milk: I Co 9:7. Metaph., of elementary Christian teaching: I Co 3:2, He 5:12, 13; τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γ., the rational (spiritual) genuine milk (v. Hort, in l.), I Pe 2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γαλάτης, -ου, ὁ (originally syn. with cl. Κέλτης; cf. I Mac 8:2, and v. next word),
a Galatian: Ga 3:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ,
Galatia;
1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C).
2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): I Co 16:1, Ga 1:2, II Ti 4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), I Pe 1:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γαλατικός, -ή, -όν (v. previous word),
Galatian, belonging to Galatia: Ac 16:6 18:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Γαλλίων, -ωνος, ὁ,
Gallio, proconsul of Achaia: Ac 18:12, 14, 17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γαμαλιήλ, ὁ (Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל),
Gamaliel the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law: Ac 5:34 22:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γεδεών, ὁ, indecl. in LXX and NT, in FlJ, Ant., v. 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן),
Gideon (Jg 6-8): He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γέλως, -ωτος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for שְׂחוֹק ;]
laughter: Ja 4:9.†

strong.def: to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γενεαλογέω, -ῶ (< γενεά, λέγω), [in LXX: I Ch 5:1 (יחשׁ)* ;]
to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., seq. ἐκ: He 7:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (v. previous word);
1. the making of a pedigree.
2. a genealogy: pl., I Ti 1:4, Tit 3:9 (v. CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141).†

strong.derivation: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G1074 (γενεά);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γενετή, -ῆς, ἡ = γενεή, Ion. for γενεά, [in LXX: Le 25:47 (עֵקֶר מִשְׁפָּחָו), Es 4:17 * ;]
birth: ἐκ γ., Jo 9:1.†

strong.def: the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γερουσία, -ας, ἡ (< γέρων), [in LXX (Hex. only in OT) for זָקֵן;]
a council of elders, senate; in NT, of the Sanhedrin (Cl. Rev., i, 43 f.; DB, ext., 99): Ac 5:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γέρων, -οντος, ὁ, [in LXX for זָקֵן;]
an old man: Jo 3:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γεωργέω, -ῶ (< γεωργός), [in LXX: I Ch 27:26 (מְלֶאכֶת הַשָּׂדֶה עָשָׂה), I Es 4:6, I Mac 14:8*;]
to till the ground: pass., He 6:7.

strong.derivation: neuter of a (presumed) derivative of G1092 (γεωργός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γεώργιον, -ου, τό (< γεωργός), [in LXX, freq. in Pr., for שָׂדֶה, etc. ;]
1. a field (Pr 24:5, 30, Strabo).
2. cultivation, husbandry, tillage (Pr 6:7 9:12, Je 28:23, Si 27:6): I Co 3:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 γηράσκω (also γηράω; < γῆρας), [in LXX chiefly for זקן;]
to grow old: Jo 21:18, He 8:13.†

strong.def: sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό, [in LXX for יַיִן, Jb 32:19 * ;]
must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Ac 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 γλυκύς, -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX chiefly for מָתֹוק ;]
Ja 3:11, 12; opp. to πικρόν, ἁλυκόν, Re 10:9, 10.†

strong.derivation: from G1100 (γλῶσσα) and the base of G2889 (κόσμος);
strong.def: properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον (< γλῶσσα, κομέω), [in LXX for אָרוֹן, II Ki 6:11, II Ch 24:8, 10, 11 * ;]
1. = cl. -εῖον (v. supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments.
2. As in LXX, π. (MM, s.v.), a box, chest: Jo 12:6 13:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** γνήσιος, -α, -ον (< γίγνομαι), [in LXX: Si 7:18, III Mac 3:19 * ;]
1. prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, s.v.).
2. true, genuine, sincere: Phl 4:3, I Ti 1:2, Tit 1:4; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, II Co 8:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** γνησίως, adv., [in LXX: II Mac 14:8, III Mac 3:23 * ;]
sincerely, honourably: Phi 2:20 (for a parallel in π., v. MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γνόφος (later form of δν-), [in LXX for אָפֵל, עֲרָפֶל, etc. ;]
darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §c): He 12:18.†

strong.def: cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.)
strong.kjv: advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 γνώμη, -ης, ἡ (< γιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Da TH 2:15 (דָּת), Ps 82(83):3 (סוֹד), elsewhere, chiefly II Es, for טְעֵם ;]
1. a means of knowing, a token (Theogn.).
2. In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (v. Edwards, Lex., App., A); †
(a). mind, understanding;
(b). purpose, intention: Ac 20:3;
(c). judgment, opinion: I Co 1:10, Re 17:13;
(d). counsel, advice: I Co 7:25, 40 II Co 8:10, Phm 14;
(e). royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): Re 17:17 (Cremer, 671).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γνώστης, -ου, ὁ (< γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for יִדְּעֹנִי ;]
one who knows, an expert: Ac 26:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † γογγυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Is 58:9 (אָוֶן), Ex 16:7-9, Nu 17:5, 10 (תְּלוּנָה), Wi 1:10, 11 Si 46:7 * ;]
a murmuring, muttering: Jo 7:12, Ac 6:1; ἄνευ γ., I Pe 4:9; pl., χωρὶς γ., Phl 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† γογγυστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< γογγύζω); [in Sm.: Pr 26:22, Is 29:24; Th.: Pr 26:20 * ;]
a murmurer: Ju 16.†

strong.def: properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * γόης, -ητος, ὁ (γοάω, to wail),
1. a wailer.
2. a wizard.
3. an impostor (cf. γοητεία, trickery, II Mac 12:24): II Ti 3:13.†

strong.def: Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Γόμορρα, -ας, ἡ, and -ων, τά (Heb. עֲמֹרָה),
Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain (Ge 19): Mt 10:15, Ro 9:29 (LXX), II Pe 2:6, Ju 7.†

strong.def: a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 γόμος, -ου, ὁ (< γέμω), [in LXX: Ex 23:5, IV Ki 5:17 (מַשָּׂא) * ;]
a ship's freight, cargo: Ac 21:3, Re 18:11, 12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γραπτός, -ή, -όν (< γράφω), [in LXX for מִכְתָּב ;]
1. painted.
2. written: Ro 2:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος),
anile, old-womanish: I Ti 4:7.†

strong.def: to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** γυμνάζω (< γυμνός), [in LXX: II Mac 10:15 * ;]
1. properly, to exercise naked.
2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: I Ti 4:7, He 5:14 12:11, II Pe 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** γυμνασία, -ας, ἡ (< γυμνάζω), [in LXX: IV Mac 11:20 * ;]
exercise: I Ti 4:8.†

strong.def: to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81),
to be naked or scantily clad: I Co 4:11 (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι, II Co 11:27; γυμνοί, Ja 2:15. In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 γυμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (< γυμνός), [in LXX for עֵירֹם, De 28:48 * ;]
nakedness: Ro 8:35, II Co 11:27, Re 3:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * γυναικάριον, -ου, τό (dim. of γυνή),
a little woman; contemptuously, a silly woman (EV): II Ti 3:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γυναικεῖος, -α, -ον (< γυνή), [in LXX chiefly for אִשָּׁה ;]
female: I Pe 3:7.†

strong.def: Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Γώγ, ὁ (Heb. גּוֹג), indecl.,
Gog, assoc. with Magog (q.v): Re 20:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† δαιμονιώδης, -ες (< δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;]
demon-like: Ja 3:15 (Cremer, 171).†

strong.def: a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δαίμων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for גַּד, Is 65:11 (א; δαιμονίῳ, AB) * ;]
in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: Mt 8:31.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of a primary root;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δάκνω [in LXX for נשׁךְ, Ge 49:17, al., exc. De 8:15 (שׂרף) ;]
to bite: metaph., Ga 5:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δακρύω [in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;]
to weep, shed tears: Jo 11:35.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ
Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: II Ti 4:10.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δάμαλις, -εως, ἡ (fem. of δαμάλης, a bullock), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה, עֶגְלָה ;]
a heifer, He 9:13.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω);
strong.def: perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δάμαρις, -ιδος, ἡ (< δάμαρ, poët., a wife),
Damaris: Ac 17:34.†

strong.def: a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δαμασκηνός, -ή, -όν
of Damascus, Damascene: II Co 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 Δαμασκός, -οῦ, ἡ (Heb. דַּמֶּשֶׂק),
Damascus: Ac 9:2ff. 22:5ff. 26:12, 20, II Co 11:32, Ga 1:17.†

strong.def: probably akin to the base of G1325 (δίδωμι); a loan

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δάνιον, -ου, τό (late form of δάνειον, Rec.; v.s. δανίζω), [in LXX: De 24:11 (נָשָׁה) 15:8, 10 (עָבַט hi.), IV Mac 2:8 * ;]
a loan: Mt 18:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δανιήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּנִיֵּאל, God is my Judge),
Daniel, the prophet: Mt 24:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δεῖγμα, -τος, τό (< δείκνυμι);
1. (cl.) a thing shown, a specimen.
2. = cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, II Pe 2:6), an example (a warning): Ju 7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† δειγματίζω (< δεῖγμα),
a rare word (ICC, ll. c.), to make a show of, to expose: Mt 1:19 (Rec. παραδ-, q.v.), Col 2:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δειλία, -ας, ἡ (< δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;]
cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): II Ti 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † δειλιάω, -ῶ (< δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד, etc. ;]
= the more freq. ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: Jo 14:27.†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G1171 (δεινῶς) (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange);
strong.def: so and so (when the person is not specified)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** δεῖνα, ὁ, ἡ, τό (gen. -νος, dat. -νι, acc. -να), [in Aq.: Ru 4:1, I Ki 21:2 (3) (Sm. also), IV Ki 6:8 * ;]
such an one, a certain one, whom one cannot or will not name: Mt 26:18.†

strong.derivation: the compound of a derivative of the base of G1169 (δειλός) and G1142 (δαίμων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δεισι-δαίμων, -ον (< δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity)
reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): Ac 17:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δεισιδαιμονία, -ας, ἡ (< δεισιδαίμων, q.v.);
1. fear of the gods;
(a). piety, religion;
(b). superstition.
2. Objectively, a religion: Ac 25:19 (Cremer, 72, 682).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † δεκα-πέντε [in LXX: Ex 27:15, I Mac 10:40, al. ;]
late form of πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen: Jo 11:18, Ac 27:5, WH, mg., ib. 28, Ga 1:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † δεκατέσσαρες, -ων, oἱ, αἱ, -α, τά, [in LXX: Ge 31:41, To 8:19, al. ;]
= cl. τεσσαρεσκαίδεκα, more freq. in later Gk. than the older form and in MGr. (for thirteen and upwards) universal, fourteen: Mt 1:17, II Co 12:2, Ga 2:1 (cf. τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος).†

strong.def: a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δεκάτη, -ης, ἡ prop. fem. (sc. μέρος) of δέκατος, -η, -ον, [in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר: Ge 14:20, Ne 12:44, et al. ;]
a tenth part, a tithe: He 7:2, 4, 8, 9 (for a curious inversion of the Biblical use, v. MM, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δέκατος, -η, -ον (< δέκα), [in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר and cognate forms ;]
tenth: Jo 1:40, Ac 19:9 (WH, txt., RV omit), Re 11:13; 21:20.†

strong.def: to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † δεκατόω, -ῶ, = cl. -τεύω (< δεκάτη), [in LXX: Ne 10:37 (38) (עשׂר pi.) * ;]
to take tithe of: c. acc. pers., He 7:6; pass. to pay tithe: He 7:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * δελεάζω (< δέλεαρ, a bait),
to allure by a bait: metaph., to allure, entice: c. acc, II Pe 2:14, 18; pass., Ja 1:14.†

strong.def: a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δεξιο-βόλος, -ου, ὁ (< δεξιός, βάλλω),
one who throws with the right hand: L for δεξιολάβος, Ac 23:23.†

strong.def: a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δερβαῖος, -α, -ον
of Derbe: Ac 20:4.†

strong.def: Derbe, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δέρβη, -ης, ἡ,
Derbe, a city of Lycaonia: Ac 14:6, 20 16:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δέρμα, -τος, τό (< δέρω), [in LXX for עוֹר ;]
the skin, hide of beasts: ἐν αἰγίοις δ., He 11:37.†

strong.def: to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δεσμεύω (< δεσμός), [in LXX for אָסַר (Jg 16:11, al.), אָלַם pi. (Ge 37:7, al.), etc. ;]
1. to put in chains: Lk 8:29, Ac 22:4.
2. to bind, tie together: φορτία, Mt 23:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δέσμη (Rec. δεσμή), -ης, ἡ (< δέω), [in LXX for אֲגֻדָּה, Ex 12:22 * ;]
a bundle: δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας (D, Orig., omit εἰς, and Blass thinks original reading, δέσμας δέσμας; v. Deiss., LAE, 1254), Mt 13:30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† δεσμο-φύλαξ, -κος, ὁ (δεσμός, φύλαξ),
a prison-keeper, gaoler: Ac 16:23, 27, 36 (cf. ἀρχιδ-, Ge 39:21).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G1199 (δεσμόν) (equivalent to G1196 (δεσμέω));
strong.def: a place of bondage, i.e. a dungeon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δεσμωτήριον, -ου, τό [in LXX for בֵּית הַסֹהַר (Ge), אָסִיר ;]
a prison: Mt 11:2, Ac 5:21, 23 16:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δεσμώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for אסר, מַסְגֵּר ;]
a prisoner: Ac 27:1, 42.†

strong.def: secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δευτεραῖος, -α, -ον (< δεύτερος), adj. with adverbial sense;
on the second day: δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν, Ac 28:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δῆλος, -η, -ον [in LXX for אוּר, etc. ;]
1. visible.
2. clear to the mind, evident: Mt 26:73; δ. (sc. ἐστίν), seq. ὅτι, I Co 15:27, Ga 3:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 δηλόω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for ידע ;]
to make plain, declare: c. acc., I Co 3:13, Col 1:8, He 9:8 12:27; c. dat. pers., II Pe 1:14; c. dat. pers., seq. περί (pass.), I Co 1:11; seq. εἰς, I Pe 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δημᾶς, ὁ (perh. contracted from Δημήτριος),
Demas, a companion of St. Paul: Col 4:14, Phm 24, II Ti 4:10.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1218 (δῆμος) and G58 (ἀγορά);
strong.def: to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to address a public assembly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δημηγορέω, -ῶ (< δῆμος, ἀγορεύω, to speak in the assembly), [in LXX: Pr 24:66 (30:31), IV Mac 5:15 * ;]
to deliver an oration: Ac 12:21.†

strong.def: Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δημήτριος, -ου, ὁ
Demetrius;
1. a silversmith, Ac 19:24, 38.
2. A Christian disciple, III Jo 12.†

strong.def: a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of the Creator)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** δημιουργός, -οῦ, ὑ (< δῆμος, ἔργον), [in LXX: II Mac 4:1 * ;]
1. one who works for the people.
2. Univ., an author, builder, maker; the maker of the world (Xen., Mem., I, 4, 9, al.), He 11:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δῆμος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
1. a district, country.
2. the common people, the people generally; esp. the people assembled: Ac 12:22 17:5 19:30, 33.†

strong.def: public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** δημόσιος, -α, -ον (< δῆμος), [in LXX: II Mac 6:10, III Mac 2:27 4:7 * ;]
belonging to the people, public: Ac 5:18; dat. fem. used adverbially (cl.);
(a). at the public expense, by public consent;
(b). publicly: Ac 16:37 18:28 20:20.†

strong.def: a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δή-που (WH, δή που), indef. adv.,
mostly in sense of surely, of course, we know: He 2:16 T (WH, δή που).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G950 (βεβαιόω);
strong.def: to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * δια-βεβαιόομαι, -οῦμαι
to affirm confidently: Tit 3:8; seq. περί, I Ti 1:7 (Cremer, 140).†

strong.def: to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain exactly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-γινώσκω (v. previous word), [in LXX chiefly for ידע, and cf. II Mac 9:15 ;]
1. to distinguish, ascertain exactly: Ac 23:15
2. As Athen. law-term, to determine: τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς, your case, Ac 24:22 (Cremer, 673).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** διά-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ (< διαγιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Wi 3:18 * ;]
1. a distinguishing, also as medical term.
2. As law-term (Lat. cognitio), determination, decision: Ac 25:21 (Cremer, 674).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δι-άγω [in LXX for עבר hi., etc. ;]
1. to carry over.
2. Of time, to pass: βίον, I Ti 2:2; absol., to live, seq. ἐν, Tit 3:3.†

strong.def: to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-δέχομαι [in LXX for מִשְׁנֶה (Deiss., BS, 115), פַּרְבָּר ;]
to receive through another, receive in turn: Ac 7:45 (RV, in their turn; v. Field, Notes, 116).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G1210 (δέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 διάδημα, -τος, τό (< διαδέω, to bind round), [in LXX for כֶּתֶר (as Es 1:11), etc. ;]
the band round the τιάρα of a Persian king; a diadem, the badge of royalty: Re 12:3 13:1 19:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 διά-δοχος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ (< διαδέχομαι), [in LXX: I Ch 18:17 (לְיַד), II Ch 26:11 (שַׂר) 28:7 (מִשְׁנֶה), Si 46:1 48:8, II Mac 4:29 14:26 * ;]
a successor: Ac 24:27 (for usage in LXX and π. in sense of court official, v. Deiss., BS, 115).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δια-ζώννυμι, (also -ννύω) [in LXX for חֲגוֹר, Ez 23:15 A * ;]
to gird round: ἑαυτόν, Jo 13:4; pass., ib. 13:5; mid., to gird oneself with: c. acc, Jo 21:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δι-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (< διαιρέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲלֹקֶת ;]
1. a distinction, diference.
2. a division, distribution: I Co 12:4-6 (cf. διαιρέω; Cremer, 616).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δια-κατ-ελέγχομαι
to confute completely: Ac 18:28.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G191 (ἀκούω);
strong.def: to hear throughout, i.e. patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) δι-ακούω [in LXX: De 1:16 (שׁמע), Jb 9:33 (יָד שִׁית hi.)* ;]
to hear through, hear fully; technically, to hear judicially (as De, l.c.; of. Deiss., BS, 230): Ac 23:35.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 διά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (< διακρίνω) [in LXX for מִפְלָשׂ, Jb 37:16 * ;]
the act of judgment, discernment: Ro 14:1, I Co 12:10, He 5:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 διά-λεκτος, -ου, ἡ (< διαλέγομαι), [in LXX: Da LXX 1:4 (לָשׁוֹן), Es 9:26 * ;]
1. conversation, discourse, speech (Plat., Dem., al.).
2. As in Polyb. and later writers, the language or dialect of a particular country or district: Ac 1:19 2:6, 8 21:40 22:2 26:14.†

strong.def: to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to conciliate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δι-αλλάσσω [in LXX: I Ki 29:4 (רָצָה hithp.), I Es 4:31, al. ;]
1. to change, exchange.
2. to change enmity for friendship, to reconcile: pass., c. dat. pers., Mt 5:24. "The word denotes mutual concession after mutual hostility, an idea absent from καταλλ-," q.v. (Lft., Notes, 288; cf. Deiss., LAE, 17815; Cremer, 91, 632).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-λύω [in LXX for אבה, חבל, etc. ;]
to part asunder, dissolve; of an assembly, pass., to disperse: Ac 5:36.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-μάχομαι [in LXX for לחם ni., Da LXX 10:20; Si 8:1, 3 38:28 51:19 * ;]
1. to struggle against.
2. In argument, to contend: Ac 23:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);
strong.def: to distribute, i.e. (of information) to disseminate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-νέμω [in LXX for חלק, De 29:26(25) * ;]
to distribute, divide: pass., to be spread about, Ac 4:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** δι-ανύω [in LXX: II Mac 12:17 * ;]
1. to accomplish fully, finish, complete: Ac 21:7 (EV).
2. In late writers (Xen., al., Clem., I ad Cor., xxv, 3), to continue: Ac, l.c. (Field, Notes, 134 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δια-πλέω, -ῶ
to sail across: Ac 27:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G4192 (πόνος);
strong.def: to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-πονέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ec 10:9 (עצב ni.), II Mac 2:28; in Aq.: Ge 6:6, I Ki 20:3 * ;]
to work out with labour. Pass., to be worn out, sore troubled: Mk 14:4 (WH, mg.), Ac 4:2 16:18.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G4249 (πρίζω);
strong.def: to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-πρίω [in LXX: I Ch 20:3 (שׂוּר) * ;]
to saw asunder. Pass., metaph. (vernacular?), EV, cut to the heart: Ac 5:33; seq. τ. καρδίαις αὐτῶν, Ac 7:54.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-σαφέω, -ῶ (< σαφής, clear), [in LXX: De 1:5 (בּאר pi.), Da LXX, 2:6 (חוה aph.), I-III Ma 9 * ;]
to make clear, explain fully: c. acc. rei, dat. pers., Mt 13:26 18:31.†

strong.def: to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δια-σπείρω [freq. in LXX for פּוּץ, etc. ;]
to scatter abroad, disperse: Ac 8:1, 4 11:19.†

strong.def: dispersion, i.e. (specially and concretely) the (converted) Israelite resident in Gentile countries

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δια-σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< διασπείρω), [in LXX of Israelites dispersed and exiled in foreign lands, as De 28:25 (זַעֲוָה) 30:4 (נדח ni.), Is 49:6 (נער); by meton., of the exiles themselves (as Ps 146 (147):2, II Mac 1:27) ;]
a dispersion: δ. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, Jo 7:35; metaph., of Christians (DB, iii, 782 f.), Ja 1:1, I Pe 1:1 (v. Hort, in ll.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 διάστημα, -τος, τό (< διίστημι), [in LXX for רֶוַח, etc.;]
an interval, space: of time (Si, prol.24), Ac 5:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δια-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< διαστέλλω), [in LXX for פְּדוּת: Ex 8:23(19), etc. ;]
1. a separation.
2. a distinction, difference: Ro 3:22 10:12, I Co 14:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † δια-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< διατάσσω), [in LXX: II Es 4:11 (פַּרְשֶׁגֶן)* ;]
in late writers (Deiss., LAE, 86 ff.) for cl. διάταξις (wh., however, is found in LXX, Ps 118 (119):91, al.);
(a). disposition (cf. διάταξις for צְבָא; Sm., IV Ki 23:4, Je 8:2 19:13); εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, AV, by the disposition of angels (Alf., in l., Field, Notes, 116; but v. infr.): Ac 7:53;
(b). ordinance (C. I. 3465): Ro 13:2, Ac 7:53, R, txt. (and v. mg.; Page and EGT, in l.; but also v. supr.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † διά-ταγμα, -τος, τό (< διατάσσω), [in LXX: II Es 7:11 (נִשְׁתְּוָן), Es 3:13, Wi 11:7 * ;]
an edict, mandate: He 11:23.†

strong.def: to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX: De 9:7 (היה), Je 20:7, 18 (כּלה), Es 8:13, II Mac 5:27 * ;]
prop. trans., to accomplish; used with ellipse of obj. as intrans. (Bl., § 81, 1), and joined to participles (in Ac, l.c., to adj.; v. Bl., § 73, 4) with adverbial sense (= continuously), to continue: Ac 27:33.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 δια-τρίβω [in LXX Le 14:8 (ישׁב), Je 42 (35):7 (גּוּר), To 11:8, 12, Jth 10:2, II Mac 14:23 * ;]
to rub hard, rub away, consume; δ. χρόνον, ἡμέρας, to spend time: Ac 14:3, 28 16:12 20:6 25:6, 14. Intransitively with ellipse of object (Bl., § 81, 1), to spend time, stay: Jo 3:22 11:54 15:35, Ac 12:19.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G5142 (τρέφω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** δια-τροφή, ῆς, ἡ (< διατρέφω, to support, sustain), [in LXX: I Mac 6:49 * ;]
food, nourishment: I Ti 6:8.†

strong.def: to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† δι-αυγάζω [in Aq.: Jb 25:5 * ;]
to shine through, to dawn: II Pe 1:19 (cf. ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα, Ca 2:17).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** διαυγής, -ές (< αὐγή), [in Aq.: Pr 16:2 * ;]
transparent: Re 21:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-φεύγω [in LXX: Jos 8:22 (פָּלִיט), ib. 10:28 (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;]
to flee through, escape: Ac 27:42.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 δια-φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שׁחת, and cogn. forms ;]
1. destruction.
2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, Ac 2:27 (LXX), Ac 2:31 13:34-37.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 διά-φορος, -ον (< διαφέρω), [in LXX for שְׁנָא (Da 7:7, 19); also as in Polyb., iv, 188, al., Τὸ δ., τὰ δ., money: Si 27:1 42:5, II Mac 3:6 ;]
1. different: Ro 12:6, He 9:10.
2. excellent: compar., -ώτερος, He 1:4 8:6.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ);
strong.def: to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay violent hands upon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * δια-χειρίζω (< χείρ),
to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid.
(a). = act.;
(b). in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: c. acc, Ac 5:30 26:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 διδακτικός, -ή, -όν (= cl. διδασκαλικός)
apt at teaching: I Ti 3:2, II Ti 2:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 διδακτός, -ή, -όν (< διδάσκω), [in LXX: Is 54:13 (לִמּוּד), I Mac 4:7 * ;]
1. that can be taught.
2. taught; c. gen., of source of teaching (in cl., poët. only);
(a). of persons: δ. θεοῦ, Jo 6:45 (LXX);
(b). of things, λόγοις δ. πνεύματος, I Co 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † δίδραχμος, -ον (< δίς, δραχμή), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶל (Ge 23:15, a1.), also for כֶּסֶף: Ge 20:16, De 22:29 ;]
worth two drachmae; τὸ δ. (sc. νόμισμα, coin),
a double drachma, nearly equal to the Jewish half-shekel, the amount of the Temple tax: Mt 17:24 (DB, iii, 428).†

strong.def: double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δίδυμος, -ου, ὁ (prop. name from δίδυμος, -η, -ον, double, sc. παῖς, twin)
Didymus, surname of the apostle Thomas: Jo 11:16 20:24 21:2.†

strong.def: an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square (from which roads diverge)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δι-έξ-οδος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹצָאָה, as Nu 34:4 ff., and freq. in Jos;]
in π. of the conclusion of a trial (MM, Exp., xi); a way out through, an outlet; pl., δ. τῶν ὁδῶν, RV, the partings of the highways: Mt 22:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δι-ερμηνευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (< διερμηνεύω),
an interpreter: I Co 14:28.†

strong.def: to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by interrogation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δι-ερωτάω, -ῶ
to find by inquiry: c. acc, Ac 10:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** διετής, -ές (< δίς, ἔτος), [in LXX: II Mac 10:3 * ;]
1. lasting two years.
2. two years old: ἀπὸ δ. (sc. παιδός, or neuter; cf. I Ch 27:23, ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς), Mt 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † διετία, -ας, ἡ (< διετής), [in LXX (Græc. Ven.): Ge 41:1 45:5 * ;]
the space of two years: Ac 24:27 28:30.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of an alternate of G5342 (φέρω);
strong.def: carried through, i.e. (adverbially with G1519 (εἰς) and G3588 (ὁ) prefixed) perpetually

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** δι-ηνεκής, -ές (< διήνεγκα, aor. of διαφέρω) [in Sm.: Ps 47 (48):15, 88 (89):30 ;]
unbroken, continuous: adverbially, εἰς τὸ δ., continually (for exx., v. Deiss., BS, 251), He 7:3 10:1, 12, 14.†

strong.def: having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double outlet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† διθάλασσος, -ον (δις, θύλασσα);
1. divided into two seas (as the Euxine, Strab., ii, 522).
2. dividing the sea: τόπον δ., a tongue of land, or reef, running out into the sea: Ac 27:41.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι, [in LXX for בּרח hi., Ex 26:28 * ;]
to go through, penetrate: He 4:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † δικαιοκρισία, -ας, ἡ
righteous judgment: Ro 2:5 (cf. τ. δικαίας κρίσεως, II Th 1:5; τὴν δ. κ., Jo 7:24. For use in π., v. Deiss., LAE, 89 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δικαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (< δικαιόω), [in LXX for מִשְׁפָּט, Le 24:22 * ;]
the act of pronouncing righteous, justification, acquittal: Ro 4:25 5:18 (Cremer, 199).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δικαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< δικάζω), [in LXX for שֹׁפֵט ;]
a judge: Ac 7:27, 35 (LXX).†

strong.def: right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δίκη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for נקם, ריב, etc. ;]
1. custom.
2. right.
3. a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, II Th 1:9; δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7.
4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: Ac 28:4.†

strong.def: equivocal, i.e. telling a different story

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δίλογος, -ον (< δίς, λέγω),
1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition.
2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Pr 11:13, Si 5:9) double-tongued: I Ti 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Διονύσιος, -ου, ὁ
Dionysius, an Athenian: Ac 17:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** διό-περ conjunct. (διό, q.v., strengthened by πέρ), [in LXX: Jth 8:17; II Mac 5 * ;]
for which very reason: I Co 8:13 10:14.†

strong.derivation: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές (< δῖος, πίπτω, v. Page on Ac, l.c.; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.),
fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), Ac 19:35.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός), meaning to straighten thoroughly;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * διόρθωμα, -τος, τό (< διορθόω, to make straight, set right),
a correction, reform: Ac 24:3.†

strong.derivation: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and a form of the base of G2877 (κοράσιον);
strong.def: sons of Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ (Ion. and κοινή form of Att., Διόσκοροι; < Διός, gen. of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son),
the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): Ac 28:11.†

strong.derivation: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and G5142 (τρέφω);
strong.def: Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες (< Διός, gen. of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus),
as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jo 9.†

strong.derivation: from G1364 (δίς) and (probably) the base of G4119 (πλείων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 διπλόος (poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) [in LXX for כָּפַל, מִשְׁנֶה, and cognates ;]
twofold, double: I Ti 5:17, Re 18:6; διπλότιρον, in twofold measure: Mt 23:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * διπλόω, -ῶ (< διπλόος),
to double: δ. τὰ διπλᾶ, Re 18:6.†

strong.def: properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in opinion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * διστάζω (< δίς),
to doubt, hesitate: Mt 14:31 28:17.†
