classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δίστομος, -ον (< δίς, στόμα), [in LXX: Jg 3:16, Ps 149:6, Pr 5:4 (פִּּיּוֹת), Si 21:3 * ;]
1. of rivers and roads, double-mouthed, double branching.
2. Of swords (Eur.; LXX, ll. c.), two-edged: He 4:12, Re 1:16 2:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δι-υλίζω (< δια, ὑλίζω, to strain) [in LXX: Am 6:6 * ;]
1. to strain thoroughly (Archytas; Am., l.c.).
2. Later, to strain out: fig., Mt 23:24.†

strong.def: to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively, alienate)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** διχάζω (δίχα, apart), [in Aq.: Le 1:17, De 14:6 * ;]
to cut apart, divide in two; metaph., to set at variance: Mt 10:35.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G1364 (δίς) and G4714 (στάσις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** διχοστασία, -ας, ἡ (< διχοστατέω, to stand apart), [in LXX: I Mac 3:29 * ;]
standing apart, dissension: Ro 16:17, Ga 5:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 διψάω,-ῶ (< δίψα, thirst), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא ;]
to thirst: absol., Mt 25:35, 37, 42, 44, Jo 4:13, 15 19:28, Ro 12:20 (LXX), I Co 4:11; fig., Jo 4:14 6:35 7:37, Re 7:16 21:6 22:17; c. acc (= cl. c. gen.), τ. δικαιοσύνην, Mt 5:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό (late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא and cognates ;]
thirst: II Co 11:27.†

strong.def: two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or purpose)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† δίψυχος, -ον (< δίς, ψυχή),
of two minds, wavering: Ja 1:8 4:8 (Cremer, 588; DB, iv, 528).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† διώκτης, -ου, ὁ (< διώκω),
a persecutor: I Ti 1:13.†

strong.def: to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † δογματίζω [in LXX: Es 3:9 (כָּתַב ni.), Da LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּתָא, דָּת), I Es 6:34, II Mac 10:3 15:36, III Mac 4:11 * ;]
to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Col 2:20.†

strong.def: test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 *† δοκιμή, -ῆς, ἡ (< δόκιμος), [in Sm.: Ps 67 (68):31 * ;]
1. the process of trial, proving, test: II Co 8:2 9:13.
2. The result of trial, approval, approvedness, proof : Ro 5:4, II Co 2:9 13:3, Phl 2:22 (Cremer, 212, 701).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1382 (δοκιμή);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δοκίμιον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Pr 17:3 27:21 (מַצְרֵף) * ;]
usually regarded as a variant form of δοκιμεῖον, a test, and so perh. Ja 1:3 (v. Mayor, in l.), but see next word (cf. Cremer, 212, 702).†

strong.def: properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. approved

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † δοκίμιος, -α, -ον (< δοκιμή), [in LXX: ἀργύριον δ. (עֲלִיל), Ps 11(12):6; and as v.l. for δόκιμος (B), ἀργυρίου δ. (זקק pu.), I Ch 29:4 (Bab); εἰ δ. ἐστιν (יְקָר), Za 11:13 א c a vid, Q *)* ;]
= δόκιμος,
tested, approved: τὸ δ. ὑμῶν τ. πίστεως, that which is approved in your faith, I Pe 1:7 (where Hort suggests the v.l. δόκιμος, found in some cursives), Ja 1:3 (but v. Mayor, in l. For full discussion of this word, not hitherto found in a Gk. Lexicon, and for exx. of its use in π., v. Deiss. (to whom is due the credit of its discovery), BS, 259 ff.; MM, Exp., xi; cf. also Milligan, NTD, 76).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δόλιος, -α, -ον (< δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Si—forמִרִמָהetc.;]
deceitful: II Co 11:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † δολιόω (< δόλιος), [in LXX: Nu 25:18, Ps 104 (105):25 (נָכַל), Ps 5:6 (חָלַק hi.) * ;]
to deceive: ἐδολιοῦσαν (-σαν, freq. in κοινή Gk. for impf. 3rd pers. pl.), Ro 3:13 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δολόω, -ῶ (δόλος) [in LXX: Ps 14 (15):3 (רגל), Ps 35 (36):2 (חלק hi.) * ;]
1. to ensnare.
2. As of wine, to adulterate, corrupt: τ. λόγον τ. θεοῦ, II Co 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Δορκάς, -άδος, ἡ (δορκάς, a gazelle),
Dorcas, also called Ταβειθά, q.v.: Ac 9:36, 39.†

strong.def: a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δόσις, -εως, ἡ (δίδωμι) [in LXX for חֹק (Ge 47:22), מַתָּך, מַתַּת (Pr 21:14 25:14), freq. in Si. ;]
1. properly, the act of giving: Phl 4:15.
2. Objectively, a gift: Ja 1:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † δότης, -ου, ὁ (< δίδωμι), [in LXX: Pr 22:8 * ;]
= δοτήρ,
a giver: II Co 9:7 (LXX) (not elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G1401 (δοῦλος) and G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: to be a slave-driver, i.e. to enslave (figuratively, subdue)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ (< δοῦλος, ἄγω),
to make a slave, bring into bondage: I Co 9:27 (Cremer, 703).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 δουλεία (T, -λία), -ας, ἡ (< δουλεύω), [in LXX, as Ex 13:3, for עֶבֶד and cognates ;]
slavery, bondage: Ro 8:15, 21, Ga 4:24 5:1, He 2:15.†

strong.kjv: bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 δουλόω, -ῶ (< δοῦλος), [in LXX for עבד ;]
to enslave, bring into bondage: Ac 7:6 (LXX), II Pe 2:19; metaph., I Co 9:19; pass., seq. ἐν, ib. 7:15; τ. θεῷ, Ro 6:22; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Ro 6:18; οἴνῳ, Tit 2:3; ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, Ga 4:3 (Cremer, 217).†

strong.derivation: probably from an alternate form of (to look);
strong.def: a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 δράκων, -οντος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for תַּנִּין ;]
a dragon, a mythical monster: fig., of Satan, Re 12:3-17 13:2, 4, 11 16:13 20:2.†

strong.derivation: perhaps akin to the base of G1404 (δράκων) (through the idea of capturing);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δράσσομαι [in LXX for נשׁק pi., Ps 2:12; elsewhere קמץ, as Le 2:2 ;]
to grasp with the hand, to lay hold of : metaph., c. acc (M, Pr., 65), I Co 3:19 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δρόμος, -ου, ὁ (< δραμεῖν, v.s. τρέχω) [in LXX chiefly for מְרוּצָה ;]
a course: fig., of life or ministry, Ac 13:25 20:24, II Ti 4:7.†

strong.derivation: a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name);
strong.def: Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δρούσιλλα (Rec. Δρουσίλλα), ης, ἡ,
Drusilla, wife of Felix: Ac 24:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † δυναμόω, -ῶ (< δύναμις), [in LXX for עזז, Ps 51 (52):7 67 (68):28; גּבר pi., hi., Ec 10:10, Da TH 9:27 * ;]
to make strong, strengthen: Eph 6:10 (WH, mg.; ἐνδυν-, WH, txt., RV), Col 1:11, He 11:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δυνατέω, -ῶ (< δυνατός),
to be able, be powerful, mighty: c. inf., Ro 14:4, II Co 9:8; absol., opp. to ἀσθενῶ II Co 13:3.†

strong.derivation: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a comparative of G1787 (ἐντός) (meaning a bowel);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δυσεντερία, -ας, ἡ,
Rec. for δυσεντέριον (q.v.), Ac 28:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a presumed derivative of G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δυσερμήνευτος, -ον (< ἑρμηνεύω),
hard of interpretation: He 5:11.†

strong.derivation: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a derivative of G3539 (νοιέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * δυσνόητος, -ον (< νοέω),
hard to understand: II Pe 3:16.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1418 (δυσ-) and G5345 (φήμη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** δυσφημέω, -ώ (< δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: I Mac 7:41 * ;]
1. intrans., to use evil words (Æsch.).
2. Trans., to speak ill of, defame (Soph.): pass., I Co 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δωδέκατος, -η, -ον
twelfth: Re 21:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† δωδεκά-φυλος, -ον (< δώδεκα, φυλή),
of twelve tribes: as subst. neut., τό δ. (cf. λαὸς ὁ δ., Sibyll. Orac.), the twelve tribes, Ac 26:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 δωρεά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< δίδωμι), [in LXX chiefly (-άν) for חִנָּם, as Ge 29:15 ;]
a gift: Ac 11:17, Ro 5:15, He 6:4; δ. τ. θεοῦ, Jo 4:10, Ac 8:20; τ. Χριστοῦ, Eph 4:7; τ. πνεύματος, Ac 2:38 10:45; τ. δικαιοσύνης, Ro 5:17; τ. χάριτος, Eph 3:7; ἀνεκδιηγήτὶῳ δ., II Co 9:15. Acc, δωρεάν, adverbially (as freq. in LXX),
(a). freely, as a gift: Mt 10:8, Ro 3:24, II Co 11:7, II Th 3:8, Re 21:6 22:17;
(b). in vain, uselessly: Jo 15:25(LXX) Ga 2:21.†

strong.derivation: accusative case of G1431 (δωρεά) as adverb;
strong.kjv: without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 9 δωρεάν, v.s. δωρεά.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** δώρημα, -τος, τό (< δωρέω), [in LXX: Si 31 (34):18* ;]
a gift, boon: Ro 5:16, Ja 1:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἑβδομηκοντάκις, adv., [in LXX for שִׁבְעִים, Ge 4:24 * ;]
seventy times: ἑ. ἑπτά, seventy times seven, Mt 18:22 (R, txt., ICC, in l.), or seventy-seven times (R, mg.; cf. M, Pr., 98; WM, 314; Meyer, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἕβδομος, -η, -ον (< ἑπτὰ), [in LXX chiefly for שְׁבִיעִי ;]
seventh: Jo 4:52, He 4:4 (LXX), Ju 14, Re 8:1 10:7 11:15 16:17 21:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † Ἑβραῖος (WH, Ἐβ-), -α, -ον (Aram, עִבְרַי), as subst., ὁ Ἑ., [in LXX for עֵבֶר, עִבְרִי ;]
a Hebrew.
1. In OT, of Israelites in contrast with those of another race (Ge 14:13, Ex 1:15, De 15:12, al.).
2. In NT as the correlative of Ἑλληνιστής, a Jew who had adopted, in greater or less degree, Greek culture and Greek language. The distinction was not merely linguistic (DB, ii, 325); as far as it was so, Συριστής would be a more correct Greek term for the Jew of Semitic speech (v.s. Ἑβραΐς, and cf. Dalman, Words, 7): Ac 6:1, II Co 11:22, Phl 3:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† Ἑβραΐς (WH, Ἐβ-), -ίδος (Aram. עִבְרַי), peculiar form of Ἑβραϊκός, [in LXX, ἡ Ἑ. φωνή, IV Mac 12:7 16:15 * ;]
in NT, ἡ Ἑ. διάλεκτος, Hebrew, i.e. the Aramaic vernacular of Palestine: Ac 21:40 22:2 26:14.†

strong.def: Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee) language

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 **† Ἑβραϊστί (WH, Ἐβ-), adv., [in LXX: Si prol. 13 * ;]
in Hebrew: Re 9:11; elsewhere, in Aramaic (v. supr.): Jo 5:2 19:13, 17, 20 20:16, Re 16:16.†

strong.def: pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. a bondsman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἔγγυος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: Si 29:15, 16, II Mac 10:28 * ;]
a surety: He 7:22 (exx. from π., v. MM, Exp., xi; cf. Cremer, 222).†

strong.derivation: neuter of the comparative of G1451 (ἐγγύς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἐγγύτερος, v.s. ἐγγύς.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἔγερσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐγείρω, -ομαι)), [in LXX: Jg 7:19, Ps 138 (139):2 (קוּם), I Es 5:62 * ;]
1. a rousing (Plat.).
2. a rising (Ps, l.c.): from death, Mt 27:53.†

strong.derivation: neuter plural of a presumed compound from G1722 (ἐν) and G2537 (καινός);
strong.def: innovatives, i.e. (specially) renewal (of religious services after the Antiochian interruption)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἐγκαίνια, v.s. ἐνκ-.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 ἐγκαινίζω, v.s. ἐνκ-.

strong.def: to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. bring to account (charge, criminate, etc.)
strong.kjv: accuse, call in question, implead, lay to the charge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἐγκαλέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for אמר, etc.; c. dat., Za 1:4 (קָרָא אֶל), Wi 12:12, Si 46:19 ;]
1. to call in, demand.
2. to bring a charge against, accuse: c. dat. pers. (as in cl.), Ac 19:38 23:28; seq. κατά, c. gen. pers., Ro 8:33. Pass., to be accused: c. gen. rei; στάσεως, Ac 19:40; ὦν (perh. by attraction = ἅ), Ac 26:2; seq. περί, c. gen. rei, Ac 23:29 26:7 (Cremer, 743).†

strong.def: to settle down in a place, i.e. reside

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἐγ-κατ-οικέω, v.s. ἐνκ-.

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G2759 (κέντρον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 6 ἐγ-κεντρίζω, v.s. ἐνκ-.

strong.kjv: crime laid against, laid to charge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἔγκλημα -τος, τό (< ἐγκαλέω),
an accusation, charge: Ac 23:29 25:16 (Cremer, 743).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1722 (ἐν) and (to gird);
strong.def: to engirdle oneself (for labor), i.e. figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to wear (in token of mutual deference)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐγ-κομβόομαι, -οῦμαι (< κόμβος, a knot, whence ἐγκόμβωμα, a garment tied on over others, used especially of a frock or apron worn by slaves),
to put on oneself, as a garment, gird on: ἀλλήλοις τ. ταπεινοφροσύνην (as for service, RV, cf. Thayer, s.v., but cf. also ICC, in l.), I Pe 5:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἐγ-κοπή, v.s. ἐνκ-.

strong.def: to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 5 ἐγ-κόπτω, v.s. ἐνκ-.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
507 εἰ, conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions.
I. Conditional, if;
1. c. indic., expressing a general assumption;
(a). pres.: seq. indic, pres., Mt 11:14, Ro 8:25, al.; seq. imperat., Mk 4:23 9:22, Jo 15:18, I Co 7:9, al.; seq. fut. indic., Lk 16:31, Ro 8:11, al.; seq. pf. or aor., with negation in apodosis, Mt 12:26, Ro 4:14, al.; similarly, seq. impf., Lk 17:6, Jo 8:39; seq. quæst., Mt 6:23, Jo 5:47 7:23 8:46, I Pe 2:20;
(b). fut.: Mt 26:33, I Pe 2:20;
(c). pf.: Jo 11:12, Ro 6:5, al.;
(d). aor.: Lk 16:11 19:8, Jo 13:32, 18:23, Re 20:15, al.
2. Where the assumption is certain = ἐπεί: Mt 12:28, Jo 7:4, Ro 5:17, al.
3. Of an unfulfilled condition, c. indic, impf., aor. or plpf., seq. ἄν, c. imp. or aor. (v.s. ἄν, I, i).
4. C. indic., after verbs denoting wonder, etc., sometimes, but not always, coupled with an element of doubt: Mk 15:44, I Jo 3:13, al.
5. C. indic., as in LXX (Nu 14:3o, I Ki 14:45, al. = Heb. אִם), in oaths, with the formula of imprecation understood in a suppressed apodosis (WM, 627; Burton, §272): Mk 8:12, He 3:11 (LXX) 4:3 (LXX).
6. Rarely (cl.) c. optat., to express a merely possible condition: Ac 24:19 27:39, I Co 14:10 15:37, I Pe3:14, 17.
II. Interrogative, if, whether.
1. As in cl., in indir. questions after verbs of seeing, asking, knowing, saying, etc.: c. indic. pres., Mt 26:63, Mk 15:36, Ac 19:2, II Co 13:5, al.; fut., Mk 3:2, Ac 8:22, al.; aor., Mk 15:44, I Co 1:16, al.; c. subjc. aor. (M, Pr., 194), Phl 3:12.
2. As in LXX (= Heb. אִם and interrog. הֲ, Ge 17:17, al.; v. WM, 639 f.; Viteau, i, 22), in direct questions: Mk 8:23 (Tr., WH, txt.), Lk 13:23, 22:49, Ac 19:2, al.
III. With other particles.
1. εἰ ἄρα, εἴγε, εἰ δὲ μήγε, v.s. ἄρα, γε.
2. εἰ δὲ καί, but if also: Lk 11:18; but even if, I Co 4:7, II Co 4:3 11:16.
3. εἰ δὲ μή, but if not, but if otherwise: Mk 2:21, 22, Jo 14:2, Re 2:5, al.
4. εἰ καί, if even, if also, although: Mk 14:29, Lk 11:8, I Co 7:21, II Co 4:16, Phl 2:17, al.
5. καὶ εἰ, even if, v.s. καί
6. εἰ μή, if not, unless, except, but only: Mt 24:22, Mk 2:26 6:5, Jo 9:33, I Co 7:17 (only), Ga 1:19 (cf. ἐὰν μή, 2:16; v. Hort., Ja., xvi); ἐκτὸς εἰ μή, pleonastic (Bl., §65, 6), I Co 14:5 15:2, I Ti 5:19.
7. εἰ μήν = cl. ἦ μήν (M, Pr., 46), in oaths, surely (Ez 33:27, al.): He 6:14.
8. εἴ πως, if haply: Ac 27:12, Ro 1:10.
9. εἴτε . . . εἴτε, whether . . . or: Ro 12:6-8, I Co 3:22 13:8, al.

classic.entry:
2 ἐκ-κλείω [in LXX: ἐ. κρίσιν, for נָטָה hi., Ex 23:2 (also as v.l., Jb 34:20, Ps 67:30 (Ps 68:30) * ;]
to shut out: Ga 4:17. Pass., Ro 3:27.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G2564 (καλέω);
strong.def: a calling out, i.e. (concretely) a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation (Jewish synagogue, or Christian community of members on earth or saints in heaven or both)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
114 ἐκκλησία, -ας, ἡ (< ἐκ-καλέω), [in LXX chiefly for קָהָל, otherwise for one of its cogn. forms ;]
1. prop., an assembly of citizens regularly convened (in Thuc., ii, 22, opp. to σύλλογος, a concourse): Ac 19:32, 39, 41.
2. In LXX of the assembly, congregation, community of Israel (De 4:10 23:2, al.): Ac 7:38, He 2:12 (LXX).
3. NT, esp. of an assembly or company of Christians, a (the) church;
(a). of gatherings for worship: I Co 11:18 14:19, 34, 35;
(b). of local communities: Ac 8:3, I Co 4:17; with name added, Ac 8:1, Ro 16:1, I Th 1:1, al.; pl., Ac 15:41, I Co 7:17; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ro 16:16; τ. Ἀσίας, I Co 16:19; τ. ἁγίων, I Co 14:33; εἰπὸν τ. ἐκκλησίᾳ, Mt 18:17 (but v. Hort, Ecclesia, 10); of a house-congregation (DB, i, 431a), Ro 16:5, I Co 16:19, Col 4:15, Phm 2;
(c). of the whole body of Christians: Mt 16:18, I Co 12:28, Eph 1:22, Phl 3:6, al.; τ. θεοῦ, Ac 20:28 (Κυρίου, T, R, mg.), I Co 15:9, Ga 1:13, I Ti 3:15; ἐ. προτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς, He 12:23.

strong.def: to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety)
strong.kjv: avoid, eschew, go out of the way

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐκ-κλίνω [in LXX for נָטָה, סוּר, etc. ;]
intrans., to turn aside, turn away: metaph., from the right path, absol., Ro 3:12 (LXX); from evil, absol., I Pe 3:11; seq. ἀπό, c. gen. pers., Ro 16:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐκ-κολυμβάω, -ῶ
to swim out of: Ac 27:42.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐκ-λαλέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Jth 11:9 * ;]
to speak out, divulge: Ac 23:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-λάμπω [in LXX for אוֹר hi., etc. ;]
to shine forth: Mt 13:43.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2990 (λανθάνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** ἐκ-λανθάνω [in Sm.: Ps 13:2 * ;]
to escape notice utterly; mid., to forget utterly: He 12:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ** ἐκλογή, ῆς ἡ (< ἐκλέγω), [in Aq.: Is 22:7; Sm., Th.: Is 37:24 * ;]
a choice, selection; in NT, always of the Divine choice (EV, election): σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς, gen. qual., a chosen vessel; κατ ἐ., Ro 9:11 11:5, 28; c. gen. pers., I Th 1:4, II Pe 1:10; by meton., ἡ ἐ. = οἱ ἐκλεκτοί, Ro 11:7.†

strong.def: (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. quietly withdraw

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-νεύω [in LXX: Jg 4:18 (סוּר) Jg 18:26, IV Ki 2:24 23:16 (פָּנָה), Mi 6:14 (סוּג hi.), III Mac 3:22 * ;]
1. to bend the head aside (Xen.).
2.
(a). to shun, avoid (Diod.);
(b). to withdraw: Jo 5:13†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐκ-νήφω [in LXX: Ge 9:24, Hb 2:7 (יָקַץ), Jl 1:5, Hb 2:19 (קַיץ hi.), I Ki 25:37 (יָצָא), Si 34 (31)2* ;]
to become sober after drunkenness: metaph., of sobriety of mind, I Co 15:34.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative from G1635 (ἑκών);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκούσιος, -ον (< έκών), [in LXX chiefly for נְדָבָה, as Nu 15:3 (κατ’ ἑ.);]
usually of actions, voluntary: κατὰ ἑ., of free will (Lft., in l), Phm 14.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G1595 (ἑκούσιον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἑκουσίως adv., [in LXX: Ps 54:6 (נְדָבָה) II Mac 14:3, al. ;]
voluntarily, willingly: He 10:26, I Pe 5:2.†

strong.def: long ago, for a long while
strong.kjv: of a long time, of old

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἔκ-παλαι adv. (of a class of compound adverbs common in late Gk.; v. Mayor on 2 Pe, l.c.),
for a long time, from of old: II Pe 2:3 3:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐκ-πέμπω [in LXX for שָׁלַח ;]
to send forth: Ac 13:4 17:10.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a form of G4072 (πέτομαι);
strong.def: to fly out, i.e. (by analogy) to extend

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-πετάννυμι [in LXX chiefly for פָּרַשׂ, as Is 65:2 (hithp.) ;]
to spread out (as a sail), stretch forth: Ro 10:21(LXX).†

strong.def: to drop away; specially, be driven out of one's course; figuratively, to lose, become inefficient
strong.kjv: be cast, fail, fall (away, off), take none effect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐκ-πίπτω [in LXX: Is 40:8 28:1, 4 (הֶבֶל), Jb 14:2 (מָלַל, v. RV. mg), Jb 15:30 (סוּר), Jb 15:33 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), etc. ;]
to fall out of, fall from, fall off: seq. ἐκ τ. χειρῶν, Ac 12:7; absol., Ac 27:32; of the withering of flowers (as LXX, ll c.), Ja 1:11, I Pe 1:24 (LXX); of navigators falling off from a straight course, Ac 27:17, 26, 29. Metaph., c. gen. rei: Ga 5:4, II Pe 3:17; absol., fall from its place, fail, perish: Ro 9:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἐκ-πλέω, -ῶ
to sail away: Ac 20:6; seq. εἰς, Ac 15:39 18:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐκ-πληρόω [in LXX: II Mac 8:10, III Mac 1:2, 22 * ;]
1. to fill full, make up a number.
2. to fulfil (MM, Exp., xii; Cremer, 839), Ac 13:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐκ-πλήρωσις, -εως, ἡ) [in LXX: II Mac 6:14 * ;]
a completion, fulfilment: Ac 21:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐκ-πορνεύω [in LXX chiefly for זָנָה, freq. of spiritual unfaithfulness ;]
strengthened form of πoρνεύω, implying excessive indulgence; mid, to give oneself up to fornication: Ju 7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐκ-πτύω
1. to spit out.
2. to spit at in disgust, to abominate, loathe (= cl. ἀποπτ-, καταπτ-): Ga 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-στρέφω [in LXX: De 32:20, Am 6:13 Ez 16:34 A (הָפַךְ), Za 11:16 (פָּרַק pi.), Ez 13:20 (צוּד pil.)* ;]
1. to turn out of (Hom.).
2. to turn inside out; metaph., to change entirely, pervert (Aristoph.): Tit 3:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-ταράσσω [in LXX: Ps 18:4 (בּﬠת pi.), Ps 88:16 (צמת), Wi 17:3, 4 18:17 * ;]
to throw into great trouble, agitate: Ac 16:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐκ-τένεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἐκτενής), [in LXX: Jth 4:9, II Mac 14:38, III Mac 6:41 * ;]
zeal, intentness, earnestness (cf. Deiss., BS, 262): Ac 26:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐκτενής, -ές (< ἐκτείνω), [in LXX: III Mac 3:10 5:29 * ;]
stretched, strained. Metaph., earnest, zealous: I Pe 4:8 .†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐκτενῶς adv., [in LXX: Jh.3.8 (חׇזְקָה), Jl 1:14, Jth 4:12, III Mac 5:9 * ;]
fervently, earnestly: Ac 12:5, I Pe 1:22; compar., Lk 22:44 (WH br., R, mg., omits).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐκ-τίθημι [in LXX for נָתַן ni., etc. ;]
to set out, expose: Ac 7:21, Metaph., to set forth, expound: Ac 11:4 28:23; c. acc rei, Ac 18:26.†

strong.def: the exterior; figuratively (as a preposition) aside from, besides
strong.kjv: but, except(-ed), other than, out of, outside, unless, without

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἕκτος, -η, -ον
the sixth: Mt 20:5, al

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);
strong.def: to deflect, i.e. turn away (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: avoid, turn (aside, out of the way)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐκ-τρέπω [in LXX for הָפַךְ, Am 5:8 * ;]
to turn out of the course, turn aside, c. acc Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: He 12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., v. Thayer, s.v. Westc., in l); fig., seq. εἰς, I Ti 1:6; ἐπί, II Ti 4:4; ὀπίσω, I Ti 5:15; c. acc, to shun, avoid: I Ti 6:20.†

strong.def: to rear up to maturity, i.e. (genitive case) to cherish or train

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐκ-τρέφω [in LXX for גָּדַל, etc. ;]
1. prop., of children, to nurture, bring up: Eph 6:4.
2. to nourish: Eph 5:29.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G1537 (ἐκ) and (to wound);
strong.def: a miscarriage (abortion), i.e. (by analogy) untimely birth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἔκ-τρωμα, -τος, τό (< ἐκτιτρώσκω, to miscarry), [in LXX: Jb 3:16, Ec 6:3 (נָפַל; also in Aq., Ps 58:9, Nu 12:12 (מוּת) * ;]
an abortion, an untimely birth (v. Field, Notes, 179): I Co 15:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi. ;]
to frighten away, terrify: c. acc pers., II Co 10:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐκ-ψύχω [in LXX: Jg 4:21 A (עוּף), Ez 21:7 (כָּהָה pi.)* ;]
to expire, breathe one's last: Ac 5:5, 10 12:23 (cf. ἐκπνέω; Cremer, 906).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἑκών, -οῦσα, -όν [in LXX: Ex 21:13, Jb 36:19 * ;]
willing, of one's own free will: Ro 8:20, I Co 9:17 (Cremer, 246).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἐλαμείτης (Rec. -αμίτης), -ου, ὁ (Heb. אֵילָם) [in LXX (cl.) Ἐλυμαίος, Ἔλαμος: Jth 1:6; Ἀιλαμείτης (vv.ll. Ἐλ-, -αμίτης; Bl., § 3, 7): Is 11:11 21:2 22:6) ;]
an Elamite: Ac 2:9.†

strong.derivation: comparative of the same as G1646 (ἐλάχιστος);
strong.def: smaller (in size, quantity, age or quality)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐλάσσων (-ττων, He 7:7, WH, 1 Ti 5:9), -ον (formed, with superl. ἐλάχιστος, from the epic ἐλαχύς, little, and serving as compar. of μικρός), [in LXX for מָעַט, etc. ;]
less, in age, rank or quality: Jo 2:19, Ro 9:12 (LXX), He 7:7; neut., -ον, adverbially: I Ti 5:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐλαττονέω, -ῶ (< ἔλαττον), [in LXX (with -όω) chiefly for חָסֵר ;]
to be less (RV, had no lack): II Co 8:15 (LXX) (a rare word; cf. MM, Exp., xii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐλαττόω, -ῶ (< ἐλάιττων), [in LXX (where also -σσῶ) chiefly for חָסֵר, and very freq. in Si;]
to make less: He 2:7 (LXX); pass., Jo 3:30, He 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐλαφρία, -ας, ἡ
lightness, levity: II Co 1:17.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to G1643 (ἐλαύνω) and the base of G1640 (ἐλάσσων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐλαφρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX chiefly for קַל, קָלָל ;]
light in weight easy to bear: Mt 11:30; θλίψρις (EV, our light affliction), II Co 4:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἐλεάζαρ(Heb. אֶלְעָזָר), ὁ, indecl.,
Eleazar: Mt 1:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἔλεγξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Jb 21:4 23:2 (שִׂיחַ) * ;]
rebuke: II Pe 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐλεγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἐλέγχω), [in LXX: Ps 38:14 39:11 (תּוֹכֵחָה), Si 20:29 21:6 41:4, al. ;]
reproof: II Ti 3:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐλεεινός, -ή, -όν (< ἔλεος in Re, l.c., WH have the Attic poëtic form, ἐλεινός),
pitiable, miserable: Re 3:17; comparat., I Co 15:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐλεήμων, -ον [in LXX chiefly for חַנּוּן ;]
merciful: Mt 5:7, He 2:17.†

strong.def: freedom (legitimate or licentious, chiefly moral or ceremonial)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ἐλευθερία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Le 19:20 (חֻפְשָׁה), I Es 4:49, 53, Si 7:21, 33:25, I Mac 14:27, III Mac 3:28 * ;]
liberty: with reference to the religious life, I Co 10:29, II Co 3:17, Ga 2:4 5:1, I Pe 2:16, II Pe 2:19; ὁ νόμος τῆς ἐ., Ja 1:25 2:12; ἡ ἐ. τῆς δόξης, Ro 8:21; ἐπ’ ἐ., Ga 5:13 (on which formula, cf. Deiss., LAE, 327 ff.; Cremer, 251).†

strong.derivation: probably from the alternate of G2064 (ἔρχομαι);
strong.def: unrestrained (to go at pleasure), i.e. (as a citizen) not a slave (whether freeborn or manumitted), or (genitive case) exempt (from obligation or liability)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
23 ἐλεύθερος, -α, -ον [in LXX chiefly for חׇפְשִׁי ;]
free;
(a). in civil sense, not a slave: Jo 8:33, I Co 7:21, 22 12:13, Ga 3:28, Eph 6:8, Col 3:11, Re 6:15 13:16 19:18; fem., Ga 4:22, 23, 30;
(b). as regards restraint and obligation in general: Mt 17:26, I Co 9:1; seq. ἐκ, I Co 9:19; ἀπό, Ro 7:3; c. inf., I Co 7:39; from the law, Ga 4:26, I Pe 2:16; from sin, Jo 8:36; τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ, as regards righteousness, Ro 6:20 (Cremer, 249).†

strong.def: to liberate, i.e. (figuratively) to exempt (from moral, ceremonial or mortal liability)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἐλευθερόω, -ῶ [in LXX: Pr 25:10. II Mac 1:27 2:22 * ;]
to make free: from sin, Jo 8:32, 36; seq. ἀπό, Ro 6:18, 22 8:2, 21; τ. ἐλευθερία (dat. commodi), Ga 5:1 (on the "punctiliar" force of this verb, v. M, Pr. 149; cf. also Cremer, 251).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἔλευσις, -εως, ἡ
a coming: Ac 7:52.†

strong.def: elephantine, i.e. (by implication) composed of ivory

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐλεφάντινος, -η, -ον (< ἐλέφας, ivory), [in LXX for שֵׁן ;]
of ivory: Re 18:12.†

strong.def: God of majesty; Eliud, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἐλιούδ, ὁ
indecl.,
Eliud, an ancestor of Jesus: Mt 1:14, 15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἑλίσσω [in LXX: Is 34:4 (גָּלַל ni.), Ps 102:26 (חָלַף hi.), etc. ;]
to roll, roll up: He 1:12 (LXX), Re 6:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἕλκω (Hellenistic form ἑλκύω in Jo, ll. c., Ac 16:19), [in LXX for מָשַׁךְ, etc. ;]
to draw: c. acc rei, Jo 18:10 21:6; c. acc pers., seq. ἔξω, Ac 21:30; εἰς, Ac 16:19, Ja 2:6. Metaph., to draw, lead, impel: Jo 6:44 12:32. (For discussion of ἕ. in Oxyrh. Log., v. Deiss., LAE, 437 ff.)†

strong.def: Hellas (or Greece), a country of Europe

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἑλλάς, -άδος, ἡ [in LXX: Is 66:19, Ez 27:13 (יָוָן), I Mac 1:1 8:9 * ;]
with varying usage as to geographical limits; in NT = 'Αχαία (cf. Ac 18:12),
Greece: Ac 20:2.†

strong.def: a Hellen (Grecian) or inhabitant of Hellas; by extension a Greek-speaking person, especially a non-Jew

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 Ἕλλην, -ηνος, ὁ [in LXX: Jl 3:6, Za 9:13 (יָוָן), etc.; I Mac 1:10, al. * ;]
a Greek; opp. to βάρβαρος, Ro 1:14; usually in ΝΤ of Greek Gentiles, opp. to Ἰουδαῖοι: Jo 7:35, Ac 11:20 14:1 16:1, 3 18:4 19:10, 17 20:21 21:28, Ro 1:16 2:9, 10 3:9 10:12, I Co 1:22, 24 10:32 12:13, Ga 2:3 3:28, Col 3:11; of proselytes, Jo 12:20, Ac 17:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἑλληνικκός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: Je 46:6 50:16 (יָנָה: aliter in Heb.), II Mac 4:10, 15 6:9 11:24 13:2, IV Mac 8:8 * ;]
Greek: τ. Ἑλληνικῇ (sc. γλωσσῇ), Re 9:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† Ἑλληνιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< Ἑλληνίζω, to Hellenize, affect Greek cus­toms),
a Hellenist (RV, Grecian Jew): Ac 6:1 9:29 11:20.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G1675 (Ἑλληνιστής);
strong.def: Hellenistically, i.e. in the Grecian language

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * Ἑλληνιστί adv.,
in Greek: Jo 19:20; Ἑ. (sc. λαλεῖν) γινώσκεις, Ac 21:37 (cf. Field, Notes, 135).†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3056 (λόγος) (in the sense of account);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐλλογάω, -ῶ (a κοινή word, elsewhere usually -έω; cf. Bl., § 22, 2),
to charge to one's account, impute: Phm 18 (on parallels, cf. Deiss., LAE, 79 f., 335 f.; Milligan, NTD, 73; MM, Exp., xii); of sin, Ro 5:13 (Cremer, 400).†

strong.derivation: from a primary (to anticipate, usually with pleasure);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
53 ἐλπίς (ἑλ-, Ro 8:20, WH, v. Bl., § 4, 3; M, Pr., 44), -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX for בָּטַח and its derivatives, תִּקְוָה (freq. in Jb), etc. ;]
expectation (in cl., rarely of evil, mostly of good, and so always in NT), hope;
1. of hope in general: II Co 1:6; c. gen. obj., Ac 16:19; art. inf., Ac 27:20, I Co 9:10; παρ’ ἐλπίδα, Ro 4:18; ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι, I Co 9:10.
2. Of religious hope: ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι, Ac 2:26 26:6, Ro 4:18 8:20, Tit 1:2; τῇ ἐ. ἐσώθημεν, Ro 8:24; κατ' ἐλπίδα ζωῆς αἰωνίου, Tit 3:7; of the Messianic hope of Israel, Ac 23:6 26:6, 7 28:20; of Christian hope, Ro 5:2, 4, 5 12:12 15:4, 13, I Co 13:13, II Th 2:16, He 3:6 6:11 7:19 10:23, I Pe 1:3, 21 3:15; c. gen. obj., Ro 5:2, Col 1:27, I Th 1:3 5:8, Tit 1:2; c. gen. of that on which the hope is based, Ac 26:6, Eph 1:18 4:4, Col 1:23; ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἐ., Ro 15:13; ἔχειν ἐ. (= cl. ἐλπίζειν), Ac 24:15, Ro 15:4, II Co 3:12 10:15, Eph 2:12, I Th 4:13; seq. ἐπί, c. dat., I Jo 3:3; εἰς, Ac 24:15; ὅτι, Ro 8:20, Phl 1:20, 21. Meton.,
(a). of the author or ground of hope (cl.): I Th 2:19, I Ti 1:1; c. gen. obj., Col 1:27;
(b). of the thing hoped for: Ga 5:5, Col 1:5, Tit 2:13, He 6:18 (Cremer, 252, 712).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἐλύμας, -α, ὁ (< Aram. or Arab., cf. DB, i, 246 b)
Elymas: Ac 13:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a presumed derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις);
strong.def: equivalent to G1684 (ἐμβαίνω); to intrude on (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμβατεύω [in LXX: c. acc, Jos 19:49 (נָחַל, Jos 19:51 (חָלַק pi.); seq. εἰς, I Mac 12:25 13:20 14:31 15:40; metaph., II Mac 2:30 * ;] (< ἐμβάτης < ἐμβαίνω)
1. to step in or on (Soph.), hence
(a). to frequent, haunt, dwell in (Æsch., Eur.); metaph., Col 2:18 (dwelling in, R, txt.; taking, R, mg.);
(b). to invade (1Mac, ll c.; metaph., Col, l.c.).
2. to enter on, come into possession of (Eur., Dem.; LXX, Jos, ll. c.); on the difficulties of reading and interpretation in this passage, v. Lft, Col., 194 f., 252; ICC, 268 ff.; Field, Notes, 197; Milligan, NTD, 177; and for exx. from π., MM, Exp., xii (cf. κενεμβ.).†

strong.def: causative of G1684 (ἐμβαίνω)); to place on, i.e. transfer (aboard a vessel)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμ-βιβάζω [in LXX: IV Ki 9:23 (רָכַב hi.), Pr 4:11 (דָּרַךְ hi.) * ;]
1. to set in, put in.
2. to put on board ship, embark: c. acc pers., seq. εἰς, Ac 27:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Is 19:14 (קֵא)* ;]
to vomit: fig., Re 3:16.†

strong.def: to rave on, i.e. rage at

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐμ-μαίνομαι depon.,
to rage against: c. dat., Ac 26:11.†

strong.def: God with us; Emmanuel, a name of Christ

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † Ἐμμανουήλ, ὁ (Heb. עִמָּנוּ אֵל, Is 7:14),
Immanuel: Mt 1:23 (LXX).†

strong.def: to stay in the same place, i.e. (figuratively) persevere

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐμμένω [in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;]
1. to abide in: Ac 28:30.
2. to abide by, be true to: seq. ἐν; τ. πίστει, Ac 14:22; τ. διαθήκῃ, He 8:9 (LXX); c. dat., τ. γεγραμμένοις (dat. ptcp. as in legal formula; cf. Deiss., BS, 248; MM, Exp., xii): Ga 3:10 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Ἑμμώρ (T, Ἐμμώρ, Rec. -όρ indecl. (Heb. חֲמוֹר),
Emmor (Ge 33:19): Ac 7:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐμ-παιγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἐμπαίζω, q.v.), [in LXX: Ez 22:4 (קַלָּסָה), Ps 38:7 B א1 קלה ni.), Wi 12:2, Si 27:28, II Mac 7:7, III Mac 5:22 * ;]
a mocking: He 11:36.†

strong.def: a derider, i.e. (by implication) a false teacher

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐμ-παίκτης, -ου, ὁ (< ἐμπαίζω, q.v.), [in LXX: Is 3:4 (ִתַּעֲלוּלִים) * ;]
a mocker: II Pe 3:3, Ju 18.†

strong.def: to perambulate on a place, i.e. (figuratively) to be occupied among persons

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐν-περι-πατέω, -ῶ (Rec. ἐμπ-, v.s. ἐν) [in LXX: Le 26:12 Jb 1:7, al. (הָלַךְ hithp.), Wi 19:21 ;]
to walk about in or among: seq. ἐν., dat. pers., II Co 6:16 (LXX),†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐμ-πλέκω [in LXX: Pr 28:18 (נָפַל), II Mac 15:17 * ;]
to weave in, entwine; pass., metaph., to be involved, entangled in: II Ti 2:4, II Pe 2:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐμ-πλοκή, ῆς, ἡ (< ἐμπλίκω),
a braiding: τριχῶν, I Pe 3:3.†

strong.def: to inhale, i.e. (figuratively) to be animated by (bent upon)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐν-πνέω, -ῶ (Rec. ἐμπ-, v.s. ἐν) [in LXX: De 20:16, Jos 10:28 ff. Jos 11:11, 14 (ptcp. neut., for נֶפֶשׁ, נְשָׁמָה), Wi 15:11 * ;]
1. to breathe on.
2. to breathe;
(a). absol.;
(b). c. gen. part.: fig., ἀπειλῆς κ. φόνου, Ac 9:1.†

strong.def: to travel in (a country as a pedlar), i.e. (by implication) to trade

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐμ-πορεύομαι depon. (< ἔμπορος), [in LXX chiefly for סָחַר ;]
1. to travel, esp. for business.
2. to traffic, trade: Ja 4:13.
3. C. acc rei
(a). to traffic in;
(b). to import: (Ho 12:1, for יָבַל hoph.).
4. C. acc pers., to make a gain of: II Pe 2:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμπορία, -ας, ἡ (< ἔμπορος), [in LXX for סָחַר, רָכַל etc. ;]
commerce, business, trade: Mt 22:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμπόριον, -ον, τό (ἔμπορος) [in LXX: De 33:19 (סָפַן), Ez 27:3 (רָכַל); ἐ. εἶναι, Is 23:17 (זָנָה)* ;]
a trading place, exchange: οἶκος ἐμπορίου, Jo 2:16.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G4198 (πορεύομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἔμ-πορος, -ου, ὁ (< πόρος, a journey), [in LXX chiefly for סָחַר, רָכַל ;]
1. a passenger on shipboard, one on a journey.
2. a merchant: Mt 13:45, Re 18:3, 11 ,15, 23.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to blow a flame);
strong.def: to enkindle, i.e. set on fire

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ἐμ-πίπρημι, ἐμπρήθω (for the form, v.s. ἐμπίπλημι, and cf. Veitch, s.v. πίμπρημι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂרַף ;]
to set on fire: πόλιν, Mt 22:7; pass., of the body, to become inflamed: Ac 28:6 (T; πίμπρημι WH, q.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G5316 (φαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐμφανής, -ές (< ἐμφαίνω, to show in, exhibit), [in LXX: Mi 4:1, Is 2:2 (כּוּן ni.), Wi 6:22 7:21 14:17; ἐ. γίνεσθαι, Ex 2:14 (יָדַע ni.), Is 65:1 (דָּרַשׁ ni.)* ;]
manifest: Ac 10:40; metaph., Ro 10:20 (LXX) (v.s. ἐπιφανής).†

strong.def: to exhibit (in person) or disclose (by words)
strong.kjv: appear, declare (plainly), inform, (will) manifest, shew, signify

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐμφανίζω [in LXX for יָדַע hi., etc. ;]
1. to manifest, exhibit: ἐαυτόν, c. dat pers., Jo 14:21, 22 (DCG, ii, 112b). Pass. and mid., to show oneself, appear: Mt 27:53, He 9:24 (cf. MM, Exp., xii).
2. to declare, make known: seq. ὅτι, He 11:14; c. dat. pers., Ac 23:15; c acc rei, seq. πρός, Ac 23:22; κατά, c. gen. pers., Ac 24:1 25:2; περί, Ac 25:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμ-φυσάω, -ῶ (< φυσάω, to blow), [in LXX for נָפַח, etc. ;]
to breathe into (cf. Ge 2:7, Wi 15:11, a1.), breathe upon: Jo 20:22.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἔμ-φυτος, -ον (< ἐμφύω, to implant), [in LXX: ἔ. ἡ κακία αὐτῶν, Wi 12:10 * ;]
1. innate (Wi 12:10).
2. rooted, implanted: Ja 1:21 (v. Mayor, in l).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐν-άλιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; < ἅλς, the sea),
of the sea: τὰ ἐ., marine creatures, Ja 3:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐν-άρχομαι [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל hi. ;]
to begin, make a beginning: Ga 3:3, Phl 1:6.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G1210 (δέω) (in the sense of lacking);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐνδεής, -ές (< ἐνδέω, to lack) [in LXX for חָסֵר, אֶבְיוֹן, etc. ;]
in want, needy: Ac 4:34,†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἔν-δειγμα, -τος (< ἐνδείκνυμι),
a plain token, proof: II Th 1:5 (cf. ἔνδειξις, which refers rather to the "act of proving"; ἔ., with the passive formation, to the thing proved, v. Lft., Notes, 100; M, Th., l.c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ἐν-δείκνυμι [in LXX for לָכַד, גָּמַל, רָאָה hi. ;]
to mark, point out. Mid„
1. to show forth, prove: c. acc rei, Ro 2:15 9:22, Eph 2:7, Tit 2:10 3:2, He 6:11; seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Ro 9:17 (LXX), I Ti 1:16; seq. εἰς, He 6:10 (c. cogn. acc), II Co 8:24.
2. to manifest (by act): c. acc rei et dat. pers., II Ti 4:14 (cf. Ge 50:15, 17, and v. MM, Exp., xiii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * ἔν-δειξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐνδείκνυμι),
a pointing out, showing forth, proof (v.s. ἔνδειγμα): Ro 3:25, 26, II Co 8:24, Phl 1:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἑν-δέκατος, -η, -ον
eleventh: Mt 20:6, 9, Re 21:20.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G1218 (δῆμος);
strong.def: to be in one's own country, i.e. home (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἐνδημέω, -ῶ (< ἔνδημος, living in a place),
to live in a place, be at home: ἐν τ. σώματι, II Co 5:6 5:9; πρὸς τ. Κύριον, II Co 5:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἔνδικος, -ον (< δίκη),
righteous, just: Ro 3:8, He 2:2 (Cremer, 204).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of the base of G1218 (δῆμος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) *† ἐν-δώμησις (Rec. -δόμησις), -εως, ἡ (< δωμάω, to build),
a build­ing in: ἡ ἐ. τ. τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις, its wall had jasper built into it, Re 21:18 (v. MM, Exp., xiii; Swete, Ap., l.c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐν-δοξάζω [in LXX for כָּבַד ni., Ex 14:4, 17, 18, Ez 28:22, etc.; for עָרַץ, Ps 89:7; Si 38:6, al. ;]
to glorify: pass., II Th 1:10, 12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † ἐν-δυναμόω, -ῶ [in LXX: Jg 6:34, I Ch 12:18 A (לָבַשׁ), Ps 52:7 (עָזַז)* ;]
to make strong, strengthen: c. acc, pers., Phl 4:13, I Ti 1:12, II Ti 4:17. Pass., Ac 9:22; c. dat., Ro 4:20; seq. ἐν, II Ti 2:1 (ἐν Κυρίῳ), Eph 6:10 (Cremer, 221).†

strong.def: to sink (by implication, wrap (compare G1746 (ἐνδύω)) on, i.e. (figuratively) sneak

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἐν-δύνω, v.s. ἐνδύω.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἔν-δυσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐνδύω), [in LXX: Jb 41:4 (לְבוּשׁ), Es 5:1 * ;]
a putting on: ίματίων, I Pe 3:3.†

strong.derivation: feminine from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐν-έδρα, -ας, ἡ (< ἕδρα, a seat), [in LXX: Jos 8:7, 9, Ps 10:8 (אָרַב)* ;]
a lying in wait, an ambush: Ac 23:16 (Rec. ἔνεδρον, a form freq. in LXX), Ac 25:3.†

strong.derivation: neuter of the same as G1747 (ἐνέδρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἔνεδρον, -ου, τό, v.s. ἐνέδρα.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ἐνέργεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἐνεργής), [in LXX: Wi 7:17, 26 13:4 18:22, II Mac 3:29, III Mac 4:21 5:12, 28 * ;]
operative power (as distinct from δύναμις, potential power), working: of God, Eph 1:19 3:7 4:16, Phl 3:21, Col 1:29 2:12; of Satan, II Th 2:9, 11 (cf. M, Th., l.c.; AR, Eph., 241 ff.; Cremer, 261).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐνέργημα, -τος, τό (< ἐνεργέω),
effect, operation (Polyb.): pl., I Co 12:6, 10 (Cremer, 262, 713).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἐνεργής, -ές (late form of ἐνεργός, on wh. cf. AR, Eph., 241),
at work, active, effective: I Co 16:9, Phm 6, He 4:12 (Cremer, 261).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐν-ευλογέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ ;]
to bless: pass., seq. ἐν, Ac 3:25 (LXX), Ga 3:8 (LXX) (Cremer, 770).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G2372 (θυμός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐνθυμέομαι, -οῦμαι (< θυμός), [in LXX for דָּמָה pi., etc. ;]
to reflect on, ponder: c. acc rei, Mt 1:20 9:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** ἐνθύμησις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐνθυμέομαι), [in Sm.: Jb 21:27, Ez 11:21 * ;]
consideration, pondering (EV, device): Ac 17:29; pl., thoughts, feel­ings: Mt 9:4 12:25, He 4:12.†

strong.derivation: contraction for the third person singular present indicative of G1751 (ἔνειμι);
strong.def: impersonally, there is in or among

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** ἔνι Ionic form of ἐν (ἐνί), with strengthened accent; [in LXX: Si 37:2, IV Mac 4:22 * ;]
= ἔνεστι,
is in, has place, can be: I Co 6:5, Ga 3:28 (tris) Col 3:11, Ja 1:17 (cf. Lft., Ga.; Hort and Mayor, Ja., ll. c.).†

strong.def: to place on hand, i.e. (reflexively) impend, (participle) be instant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἐν-ίστημι [in LXX: IV Ki 13:6 A (עמד), III Ki 12:24, I Es 5:47 9:6, Es 3:13, 1; I-IV Mac 9 * ;]
to place in; in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and in mid., intrans.;
(a). to be at hand, impend, threaten: II Ti 3:1;
(b). to be present: II Th 2:2 (but v. Thayer, s.v.); pf. ptcp., present: I Co 7:26, Ga 1:4, He 9:9; pl., Ro 8:38, I Co 3:22 (Cremer, 309).†

strong.def: dumb (as making signs), i.e. silent from astonishment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ἐνεός (Rec. ἐνν-), -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX: Is 56:10 (אִלֵּם), Ep. Je41; ἐ. ποιεῖν, Pr 17:28 * ;]
dumb, speechless: Ac 9:7.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3563 (νοῦς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἔννοια, -ας, ἡ (< νοῦς), [in LXX: Pr 1:4 2:11 3:21 4:1 5:2 8:12 16:22 18:15 19:7 23:4, 19 24:7 (מְזִמָּה, etc.), Wi 2:14, Da TH Su 28* ;]
1. thinking, consideration.
2. a thought, purpose, design: He 4:12, I Pe 4:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἔν-νομος, -ον [in LXX: Si, prol. 12* ;]
1. lawful, legal (MM, Exp., xiii): Ac 19:39.
2. Of persons,
(a). law-abiding;
(b). under law: ἔ. Χριστοῦ, in relation to Christ, I Co 9:21 (Cremer. 435).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐν-οικέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly (29/36) for יָשַׁב ;]
to dwell in; metaph., seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers: ὁ θεός, II Co 6:16; τ. πνεῦμα, Ro 8:11, II Ti 1:14; ὁ λόγος, Col 3:16; πίστις, II Ti 1:5; ἁμαρτία, Ro 7:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἑνότης, -ητος, ἡ (< εἷς),
unity, unanimity: Eph 4:3, 13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G5028 (τάφος);
strong.def: to inswathe with cerements for interment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐνταφιάζω [in LXX: Ge 50:2 (חָנַט; cf. ἐνταφιαστής, Ge 50:2 for רָפָא; v. Deiss., BS, 120 f.; MM, Exp., xiii)* ;]
a κοινή word (Deiss., LAE, 723),
to prepare for burial: Mt 26:12, Jo 19:40.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἔν-τευξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐντυγχάνω, q.v.), [in LXX: II Mac 4:8 * ;]
1. a lighting upon, meeting with.
2. conversation.
3. a petition (in this sense common in π.; cf. Deiss., BS, 121 f., 146; MM, Exp., xiii): I Ti 4:5; p1., I Ti 2:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐντόπιος, -ον (< τόπος),
of a place, resident: Ac 21:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐν-τρέφω
to train up, nurture; pass., metaph., τοῖς λόγοις τ. πίστεως, I Ti 4:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἔν-τρομος, -ον [in LXX: Da TH 10:11 (רָעַד hi.); ἔ. γίγνεσθαι, Ps 17 (18):7 76 (77):18 (רַעַשׁ), Wi 17:10, I Mac 13:2 * ;]
trembling with fear (Pint.): Ac 7:32 16:29, He 12:21 (ἔκτρ-, WH, mg.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐν-τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Jb 20:3, Ps 34 (35):26 43 (44):15 68 (69):7, 19 70 (71):13 108 (109):29 (כְּלִמָּה)* ;]
1. c. gen. pers., respect, reverence (Soph., Polyb., al.).
2. Absol., shame (Hipp.): I Co 6:5 15:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐν-τρυφάω, ῶ [in LXX: Is 55:2 57:4 (עָנַג hith.), Hb 1:10 (קָלַס hith.), IV Mac 8:8, etc. ;]
to revel in: ἐν-τ. ἀπάταις, II Pe 2:13 (v. Mayor, in l).†

strong.def: to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) confer with; by extension to entreat (in favor or against)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐν-τυγχάνω [in LXX: Da TH 6:12, [13] (קֶרֶב) Wi 8:20 16:28, II Mac 2:25 4:36 6:12 15:39, III Mac 6:37; seq. κατά, I Mac 8:32 10:61, 63, 64 11:25 * ;]
1. to fall in with.
2. to meet with in order to converse.
3. to petition, make petition: c. dat. pers., seq. ὑπέρ c. gen. pers., Ac 25:24 (cf. Field, Notes, 140), He 7:25, Ro 8:27, 34 (θεῷ, not expressed); seq. κατά, against: Ro 11:2 (cf. ἔντευξις, ὑπερ-εντυγχάνω).†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G5179 (τύπος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐν-τυπόω, -ῶ (< τύπος), [in LXX for פִּתּוּחַ, Ex 36:39 (39:30)) A * ;]
to imprint, engrave: pass. ptcp., c. dat., II Co 3:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐν-υβρίζω [in OT (Al.), Le 24:11 * ;]
to insult, mock at: He 10:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐνυπνιάζω (< ἐνύπνιον), [in LXX, as in NT, -ομαι, depon., chiefly for חָלַם ;]
to dream: ἐνυπνίοις ἐ., Ac 2:17 (LXX); pres. ptcp., Ju 8.†

strong.def: something seen in sleep, i.e. a dream (vision in a dream)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐνύπνιον, -ου, τό (< ὕπνος), [in LXX chiefly for חֲלוֹם ;]
a dream: pl., Ac 2:17.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3775 (οὖς);
strong.def: to take in one's ear, i.e. to listen

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐνωτίζομαι (< οὖς), depon. mid., [in LXX chiefly for אָזַן hi. ;]
to give ear to, hearken to: c. acc, Ac 2:14.†

strong.def: to buy up, i.e. ransom; figuratively, to rescue from loss (improve opportunity)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ἐξ-αγοράζω [in LXX: καιρόν ὑμεῖς ἐξαγοράζετε (זְבַן), Da LXX TH 2:8 * ;]
1. to redeem, ransom (esp. of slaves): metaph., Ga 3:13 4:5.
2. to buy up; mid., to buy up for oneself: τ. καιρόν, Eph 5:16, Col 4:5 (Cremer, 60).†

strong.def: actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἐξ-αιρέω -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi. ;]
to take out: c. acc, ὀφθαλμόν, Mt 5:29 18:9; mid.
(a). to take out for oneself, choose: Ac 26:17 (Thayer, s.v.; Page, Ac., l.c., but v. infr.);
(b). to deliver: Ac 7:10, 34 (LXX) 12:11 23:27 26:17 (EV, but v. supr.), Ga 1:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-αίρω [in LXX for נָסַע, יָרַשׁ hi., כָּרַת ni., מוּת, בָּעַר pi., etc. ;]
to lift up, lift off the earth, remove: I Co 5:13 (LXX)†

strong.def: to follow out, i.e. (figuratively) to imitate, obey, yield to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἐξ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX Am 2:4, Je 2:2 (אַחַר הָלַךְ), Is 56:11 (פָּנָה), Jb 31:9 (פָּתָה ni.), Si 5:2, Da LXX TH 3:(41)* ;]
to follow, follow up (in various senses): metaph., II Pe 1:16 2:2 ,15 †

strong.derivation: plural ordinal from G1803 (ἕξ) and G1540 (ἑκατόν);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξακόσιοι, -αι, -α.
six hundred: Re 13:18 14:20.†

strong.def: to smear out, i.e. obliterate (erase tears, figuratively, pardon sin)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐξ-αλείφω [in LXX for טוּחַ, Le 14:42, al.; metaph., מָחָה, שָׁחַת, etc. ;]
1. to plaster, wash over (LXX).
2. to wipe off, wipe out: δάκρυον, Re 7:17 21:4; metaph., χειρόγραφον, Col 2:14; τ. ὄνομα, seq. ἐκ, Re 3:5 (MM, Exp., xiii); pass., ἀμαρτίαι (ἐξαλιφθῆναι, WH), Ac 3:19 (cf. Ps 50(15):11 Ps 108(109):13, Is 43:25, Si 46:20 (ἁμ. ἀπαλ-), III Mac 2:19).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-άλλομαι [in LXX for קָלַל (Hb 1:8), etc. ;]
to leap up: Ac 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐξ-ανάστασις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐξανίστημι),
a rising again: ἐκ τ. νεκρῶν, Phl 3:11 (Cremer, 308).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐξ -απατάω, -ῶ strengthened form of ἀπατάω, [in LXX: Ex 8:29 (הָתַל hi.), Da TH Sus 56* ;]
to deceive: c. acc, Ro 7:11 Ro 16:18, I Co 3:18, II Co 11:3, II Th 2:3; pass., I Ti 2:14.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G639 (ἀπορέω);
strong.def: to be utterly at a loss, i.e. despond

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐξ-απορέω, -ῶ [in LXX, pass., for פּוּן, Ps 87(88):15 * ;]
so in NT, depon. pass., to be utterly at a loss, be in despair: absol. (as Ps, l.c.), II Co 4:8; τοῦ ζῆν, II Co 1:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G739 (ἄρτιος);
strong.def: to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐξ-αρτίζω (< ἄρτιος), [in LXX. Ex 28:7 (חָבַר pu.) * ;]
1. to com­plete, finish: τ. ἡμέρας, Ac 21:5.
2. to furnish, supply: pass., II Ti 3:17 (for exx., v. MM, Exp., xiii; Cremer, 651).†

strong.def: to rouse fully, i.e. (figuratively) to resuscitate (from death), release (from infliction)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-εγείρω [in LXX for עוּר ni., hi., etc. ;]
to raise up: Ro 9:17 (cf. ICC, in l); from the dead, I Co 6:14.†

strong.def: to issue, i.e. leave (a place), escape (to the shore)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἔξ-ειμι (< εἶμι),
to go forth: Ac 13:42 17:15 20:7; seq. ἐπί, c. acc, Ac 27:43.†

strong.def: to drag forth, i.e. (figuratively) to entice (to sin)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-έλκω [in LXX: Ge 37:28 (מָשַׁךְ), etc. ;]
to draw out or away: metaph., ὑπὸ τ. ἐπιθυμίας, Ja 1:14 (v. Mayor, in l).†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G1537 (ἐκ) and a presumed (to spue);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐξέραμα, -τος, τό (< ἐξεράω, to evacuate, disgorge)
a vomit: II Pe 2:22 (LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-εραυνάω (Rec. ἐξερευνάω), -ῶ, [in LXX for חָקַר, נָצַר, etc. ;]
to search out, search carefully: seq. περί, I Pe 1:10.†

strong.def: to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. ascertain or interrogate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐξ-ετάζω (< ἐτάζω (rare), to examine), [in LXX: De 13:14-15 De 19:18, I Ch 28:9 A (דּרשׁ), Ps 10 (11) 5, 6 (בּחן), Wi 6:3, Si 3:21, al. ;]
to examine closely, inquire carefully (of): seq. περί (c. ἀκριβῶς), Mt 2:8; seq. τίς, Mt 10:11; c. acc pers., Jo 21:12.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2278 (ἠχέω);
strong.def: to "echo" forth, i.e. resound (be generally reported)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξ-ηχέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Jl 3 (4):14 (הָמוֹן), Si 40:13, III Mac 3:2 * ;]
to sound forth (as a trumpet, or thunder; v. M, Th., l.c.): pass., I Th 1:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἕξις, -εως, ἡ (< ἔχω), [in LXX, cf. Si, prol. 9 ;]
habit, use, experience: He 5:14.†

strong.def: to have full strength, i.e. be entirely competent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐξ-ισχύω [in LXX: Si 7:6 * ;]
to have strength enough, to be quite able: c. inf., Eph 3:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξ-ολεθρεύω (so best MSS. and WH; also read -οθρεύω), [in LXX freq. (rare in Gk. writers) for כָּרַת ni., hi., etc. ;]
to destroy utterly: seq. ἐκ τ. λαοῦ, Ac 3:23 (LXX).†

strong.def: to exact an oath, i.e. conjure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-ορκίζω (later form of ἐξορκόω ), [in LXX: Jg 17:2 (אָלָה), Ge 24:3, III Ki 22:16 (שָׁבַע hi.)* ;]
1. to administer an oath to (Dem., Polyb., al.).
2. to adjure: c. acc pers., seq. κατά, c. gen. (as freq. in magic π.; MM, Exp., xiv), Mt 26:63.†

strong.def: one that binds by an oath (or spell), i.e. (by implication) an "exorcist" (conjurer)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐξ-ορκιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἐξορκίζω),
1. one who administers an oath.
2. an exorcist: Ac 19:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to stand out);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἐξέχω, to stand out), [in LXX for שֵׁן, Jb 39:28 * ;]
1. a projection (ἐ. πέτρας, Jb 39:28).
2. Metaph., eminence, excellence: οἱ κατ’ ἐ., the chief men, Ac 25:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐξ-υπνίζω [in LXX: Jg 16:14, 20, III Ki 3:13 (יָקַץ), Jb 14:12 (עוּר ni.)* ;]
to awaken out of sleep (= ἀφυπνίζω): c. acc pers., Jo 11:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἔξ-υπνος, -ον (< ὕπνος), [in LXX: I Es 3:3 * ;]
roused out of sleep: Ac 16:27.†

strong.def: to expel; by implication, to propel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-ωθέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נָדָה hi. ;]
1. to thrust out: Ac 7:45.
2. to drive out of the sea, drive on shore: Ac 27:39 (WH, txt., ἐκσῶσαι).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἐξώτερος, -α, -ον (compar., from ἔξω; opp. to ἐσώτερος) [in LXX chiefly for חִיצוֹן ;]
outer: σκότος, Mt 8:12 22:13 25:30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἑορτάζω (< ἑορτή), [in LXX for חָגַג ;]
to keep festival: I Co 5:8.†

strong.def: a self-committal (by assurance of conferring some good)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἐπ-άγγελμα, -τος, τό (< ἐπαγγέλλω),
a promise: II Pe 1:4 3:13.†

strong.def: to superinduce, i.e. inflict (an evil), charge (a crime)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐπ-άγω [in LXX for בּוֹא hi., etc. (29 words in all) ;]
to bring upon: c. dat. et acc, II Pe 2:5; ἑαυτοῖς ἐ. (for cl. mid., v. Mayor, in l), II Pe 2:1; ἐ. τὸ αἷμα (cf. Ge 20:9), Ac 5:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-αγωνίζομαι depon.;
1. to contend with (Plut.).
2. to contend for (C.I., 2335, 19): c. dat. rei, Ju 3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἐπαίνετος (Rec. -τός), -ου, ὁ
Epænetus, a Christian of Rome: Ro 16:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G134 (αἰνέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ἔπ-αινος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for תְּהִלָּה, etc. ;]
praise: Ro 2:29 Ro 13:3, I Co 4:5, II Co 8:18, Eph 1:6, 12, 14, Phl 1:11 4:8, I Pe 1:7 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-ακούω [in LXX for שָׁמַע, עָנָה, etc. ;]
1. to listen to.
2. to hearken to, hear with favour (one's prayer): c. gen. pers., II Co 6:2 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G202 (ἀκροατής);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπ-ακροάομαι, -ῶμαι
to listen attentively: Ac 16:25 (cf. Page, in l).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G318 (ἀνάγκη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπανάγκης, -ες (< ἀνάγκη), only in neut.;
1. ἐπάναγκες (sc. ἐστί), it is compulsory, necessary.
2. As adv., of necessity: Ac 15:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπ-ανα-μιμνήσκω
to remind again: c. acc pers., Ro 15:15.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G461 (ἀνορθόω);
strong.def: a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπ-αν-όρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐπανορθόω, to correct, restore; cf. II Mac 2:22) [in LXX: I Es 8:52, I Mac 14:34 * ;]
correction: of life, II Ti 3:16 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ἐπ-αρκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Mac 8:26 11:35 * ;]
1. to be strong enough for.
2. to ward off.
3. to aid, relieve: c. dat. pers., I Ti 5:10, 16 (mid., WH, mg.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G757 (ἄρχω) (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch");
strong.def: a special region of government, i.e. a Roman præfecture

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐπαρχεία (Rec. -χία, v. Bl., § 3, 5), -ας, ἡ (< ἔπαρχος, a prefect), [in LXX: Es 4:11 (מְדִינָה), Jth 3:6 A* ;]
the jurisdiction of a prefect, a province: Ac 23:34 25:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G846 (αὐτός) and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of (a thief);
strong.def: in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ** αὐτόφωρος, -ον (< αὐτός, φώρ, a thief), [in Sm.: Jb 34:11*;]
prop. with ref. to theft, then generally, in the very act: as freq., neut. dat. after ἐπί, Jo 8:4 (Rec., ἐπαυτοφώρῳ).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἐπαφρᾶς, -ᾶ (B1., § 7, 4), ὁ,
Epaphras: Col 1:7 4:12, Phm 23.*†

strong.def: to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-αφρίζω
to foam up: metaph., τ. αἰσχύνας, Ju 13.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) (in the sense of devoted to) and (Venus);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἐπαφρόδιτος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. charming);
Epaphroditus: Phl 2:5 4:18.†

strong.def: to rouse upon, i.e. (figuratively) to excite against

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπ-εγείρω [in LXX for עוּר hi., קוּם hi., etc. ;]
to rouse up, excite: c. acc rei, διωγμόν, Ac 13:50; ψυχάς, Ac 14:2.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1521 (εἰσάγω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπ-εισ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ
a bringing in besides or in addition (Hipp., FlJ, al.): He 7:19 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and (the accusative case plural neuter of) G1565 (ἐκεῖνος);
strong.def: upon those parts of, i.e. on the further side of

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-έκεινα adv. (= ἐπ’ ἐκεῖνα), [in LXX: Le 22:27, Nu 32:19, al. (הָלְאָה), etc. ;]
beyond; c. gen., Ac 7:43 (LXX) †

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1614 (ἐκτείνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπ-εκ-τείνω
to extend: mid., to stretch forward: c. dat., Phl 3:13.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1746 (ἐνδύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐπ-εν-δύω
= -δύνω (Hdt.),
to put on over; pass. (Plut., al.), to have on over, be clothed upon: II Co 5:2, 4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπενδύτης, -ου, ὁ (< ἐπενδύω), [in LXX for מְעִיל Le 8:7 A (Aq. ἐπένδυμα), I Ki 18:4 A, II Ki 13:18 * ;]
an outer tunic (RV, coat): Jo 21:7 .†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπ-ερώτημα, -τος, τό [in LXX: Da TH 4:14 (שְׁאֵלָא), Si 36(33):3 * ;]
1. a question, an inquiry (Hdt., Thuc.).
2. a demand: I Pe 3:21 (v. ICC, in l).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
strong.def: to walk upon, i.e. mount, ascend, embark, arrive
strong.kjv: come (into), enter into, go abroad, sit upon, take ship

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐπι-βαίνω [in LXX chiefly for רָכַב ;]
1. to get up on, mount: seq. ἐπί, c. acc, Mt 21:5 (LXX); to embark in (a boat), go aboard: c. dat., Ac 27:2; seq. εἰς, Ac 21:6 (Rec.); absol., Ac 21:2.
2. to go up to, go on to, enter: seq. εἰς, Ac 20:18 21:4; c. dat., Ac 25:1.†

strong.def: to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἐπι-βαρέω, -ῶ
to put a burden on, be burdensome: fig., absol., II Co 2:5; c. acc pers., I Th 2:9, II Th 3:8 (cf. M, Th., I, 2:9).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1014 (βούλομαι);
strong.def: a plan against someone, i.e. a plot

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐπι-βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Es 2:22, I Es 5:73, II Mac 5:7, al. ;]
a plan against, a plot: Ac 9:24 20:3, 19 23:30.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G1062 (γάμος);
strong.def: to form affinity with, i.e. (specially) in a levirate way

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐπι-γαμβρεύω (< γαμβρός, a connection by marriage) [in LXX: Ge 34:9, I Ki 18:21 ff., II Ch 18:1, Es 9:14 (חָתַן hithp.), Ge 38:8 R (יָבַם pi.), I Mac 10:54, 56 * ;]
1. to enter into affinity with: c. dat. (LXX, ll. c., exc. Ge 38:8).
2. to marry (as deceased husband's next of kin, cf. Ge 38:8): c. acc, Mt 22:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 * ἐπί-γειος, -ον (< ἐπί, γῆ),
of the earth, earthly: τὰ ἐ., Jo 3:12 Phl 2:10 3:19 (anarth.); σώματα, I Co 15:40; οἰκία, II Co 5:1; σοφία, Ja 3:15 (Cremer, 153).†

strong.def: to arrive upon, i.e. spring up (as a wind)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπι-γίνομαι (v.s. γίνομαι) [in LXX: Ep. Je 47, III Mac 2:6 * ;]
to arrive, arise, come on: Ac 28:13.†

strong.def: recognition, i.e. (by implication) full discernment, acknowledgement

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 † ἐπί-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐπιγινώσκω, q.v.), [in LXX: III Ki 7:14 (B. γν-), Pr 2:5, Ho 4:1, 6 6:7(6) (דַּעַת), Jth 9:14, II Mac 9:11 * ;]
acquaintance, discernment, recognition (Plut., al.): Phl 1:9, Col 3:10; c. gen. rei, Col 1:9 2:2, Phm 6; τ. ἀληθείας, I Ti 2:4, II Ti 2:25 3:7, Tit 1:1, He 10:26; τ. ἁμαρτίας, Ro 3:20; c. gen. pers., of God: Eph 1:17, Col 1:10, II Pe 1:2, 3; of Christ: Eph 4:13, II Pe 1:8 2:20; of God and Christ: II Pe 1:2; κατ ̓ ἐ., Ro 10:2; ἔχειν ἐν ἐ., Ro 1:28 (v. AR, Eph., 248 ff.; and for a somewhat different view, Thayer, s.v.; Lft. on Col, 1:9; Tr., Syn., lxxv; Cremer, 159 f.; cf. αἴσθησις).†

strong.def: to admit (as a guest or (figuratively) teacher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐπι-δέχομαι [in LXX: Jth 13:13 B2, I Mac 10:1 14:23, Si 51:26, al. ;]
1. in cl., of things, to allow of, admit of (Dem., Arist., al.). In late writers,
2. to accept besides (Polyb.), to accept; (in π. of the terms of a lease; v. ICC, on III Jo, l.c.): III Jo 9.
3. (a) to receive besides (Menand.);
(b). to receive hospitably (I Mac, Si, ll c.): III Jo 10†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1218 (δῆμος);
strong.def: to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἐπι-δημέω, -ῶ (< δῆμος);
1. to be at home (Thuc., Plat., al.),
2. to stay in a place, sojourn (Plat., Xen., al.; and v. MM, Exp., xiv): Ac 2:10 17:21; seq. ἐν, ib. 18:27 (WH, mg.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1299 (διατάσσω);
strong.def: to appoint besides, i.e. supplement (as a codicil)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐπι-δια-τάσσομαι
to add provisions to a document: Ga 3:15 (cf. ἐπιδιαθήκη, a second will, F1J, BJ, ii, 2, 3; the word is used of wills in π., cf. Deiss., LAE, 87).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός);
strong.def: to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐπι-δι-ορθόω
to set in order further: Tit 1:5 (Inscr.; Cremer, 808).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-δύω [in LXX: De 24:15, Jos 8:29, Je 15:9 (בּוֹא)* ;]
to go down, set (of the sun): Eph 4:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπιεικία (Rec. -είκεια), -ας, ἡ (< ἐπιεικής), [in LXX: Wi 2:19 12:18 Ba 2:27, Da LXX 3:(42), 4:24, TH (3:42), II Mac 2:22 10:4, III Mac 3:15 7:6 * ;]
fairness, moderation, gentleness ("sweet reasonableness," Matthew Arnold): Ac 24:4; c. πραΰτης, II Co 10:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐπιεικής, -ές (< εἰκός, likely), [in LXX: Ps 85(86):5 (סַלָּח), Es 8:13 * ;]
1. seemly, fitting (Hom.).
2. equitable, fair, moderate: I Ti 3:3, Tit 3:2, I Pe 2:18, Ja 3:17; τὸ ἐ. (Thuc., i, 76), Phl 4:5 (cf. Mayor, Ja, l.c., and v.s. ἐπιεικία).†
ἐπιείκεια v.s. ἐπιεικία

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπιθανάτιος, -ον [in LXX: Da Bel 31 ;]
condemned to death: I Co 4:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
