6 ἐπί-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐπιτίθημι), [in LXX: II Ch 25:27 (קֶשֶׁר), Ez 23:11 (עֲגָבָה) II Mac 4:41 5:5 14:15 * ;]
1. a laying on: χειρῶν, Ac 8:18, I Ti 4:14, II Ti 1:6, He 6:2 (cf. Westc., He., l.c.; CGT on 1Ti, l.c.).
2. an attack, assault (II Mac, ll.c.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιθυμητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἐπιθυμέω) [in LXX: Nu 11:34 (אָוָה hithp.); εἶναι ἐ., Pr 1:22 (חָמַד)* ;]
one longing for, lustful after: κακῶν, I Co 10:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-καθ-ίζω [in LXX for רָכַב, etc. ;]
to sit upon: Mt 21:7.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2564 (καλέω);
strong.def: to entitle; by implication, to invoke (for aid, worship, testimony, decision, etc.)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
32 (KJV) ἐπι-καλέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;]
1. to call, name, surname: c. acc (cl.), Mt 10:25; pass., Ac 1:23 4:36 10:5, 18, 32 11:13 12:12, 25, He 11:16; τ. ὄνομα, seq. ἐπί (denoting possession, as Heb. . עַל נִקְרָא שֵׁם .), Ac 15:17 (LXX), Ja 2:7 (see. CB on Am 9:12).
2. Mid. (so also act.; cl., LXX), to call upon, invoke, appeal to (θεόν, θεούς, Hdt., Xen., al.; cf. Deiss., LAE, 426): Καίσαρα (Σεβαστόν, Ac 25:25), Ac 25:11, 12, 21 26:32 28:19; sc. τ. Κύριον Ἰησοῦν, Ac 7:59; μάρτυρα (cl.) τ. θεόν, II Co 1:23; πατέρα, I Pe 1:17; τ. κύριον, Ro 10:12, II Ti 2:22; τ. ὄνομα κυρίου (μου, σου; like Heb. בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה קָרָא ), Ac 2:21 (LXX) Ac 9:14, 21 22:16, Ro 10:13, 14 (LXX) I Co 1:2 (Cremer, 335, 742).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-κάλυμμα, -τος, τό (< ἐπικαλύπτω), [in LXX: Ex 26:14 39:21(34), (מְכַסֶּה), IV Ki 17:19 (מָסָךְ), Jb 19:29 (aliter in Heb.)* ;]
a cover, veil: metaph., τ. κακίας, I Pe 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-καλύπτω [in LXX for כָּסָה, etc. ;]
to cover over, cover up: metaph., Ro 4:7 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G2672 (καταράομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐπι-κατ-άρατος, -ον (< ἐπικαταράομαι, to imprecate curses on), [in LXX for אָרוּר, also Wi 3:12 14:8, IV Mac 2:19 ;]
accursed: Ga 3:10 (LXX) 13 (LXX κεκαταραμένος) (Cremer, 109).†

strong.def: an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † Ἐπικούριος (Rec. -ειος), -ου, ὁ
an Epicurean, a follower of Epicurus: Ac 17:18.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and a (prolonged) form of the base of G2877 (κοράσιον) (in the sense of servant);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπικουρία, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπικουρέω to be an ἐπίκουρος, an ally) [in LXX: Wi 13:18 * ;]
aid, assistance: Ac 26:22.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3004 (λέγω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) ἐπι-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר ;]
1. to say in addition (Hdt.).
2. to call by name, to call: Jo 5:2.
3. to choose; mid., to choose for oneself: Ac 15:40.†

strong.def: to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-λείπω [in LXX: Ob 5 א1 R (שָׁאַר hi.) * ;]
to fail: c. acc pers., He 11:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐπι-λησμονή, -ῆς, ή (< επιλήθω), [in LXX: Si 11:27 * ;]
forgetful­ness: ἀκροατὴς ἐ. (gen. of qual.), Ja 1:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπί-λοιπος, -ον (< λοιπός), [in LXX for יָתַר, שָׁאַר ;]
still left, remaining: χρόνος, I Pe 4:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπί-λυσις -εως, ἡ (< ἐπιλύω), [in Aq.: Ge 40:8; Sm.: Ho 3:4 * ;]
1. release.
2. solution, interpretation: II Pe 1:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
to bear witness to: c. acc et. inf., I Pe 5:12,†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιμέλεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπιμελέομαι), [in LXX: Pr 3:8 (שִׁקּוּי), Wi 13:13, I Es 6:10, I Mac 16:14, al. ;]
attention, care: Ac 27:3 (v. Field, Notes, 143).†

strong.def: to stay over, i.e. remain (figuratively, persevere)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 ἐπι-μένω [in LXX: Ex 12:39 (מָהַהּ hith.)* ;]
to stay on, tarry or abide still: seq. έν, I Co 16:8; αὐτοῦ, there, Ac 15:34 (WH, txt., RV, txt., omit) 21:4; c. dat., τ. σαρκί, Phl 1:24; seq. παρά, c. dat. pers., Ac 28:14; πρός, c. acc pers., I Co 16:7, Ga 1:18; c. acc temp., Ac 10:48 21:4, 10 28:12, 14, I Co 16:7. Metaph., to continue in a pursuit or state: c. dat., τ. ἀμαρτίᾳ, Ro 6:1; τ. ὰπιστίᾳ, 11:23; τ. πίστει, Col 1:23; αὐτοῖς (v. CGT, in l), I Ti 4:16; τ. χρηστότητι, Ro 11:22; c. ptcp. (cf. Bl., § 73, 4; 76, 2), Jo 8:7, Ac 12:16.†

strong.def: to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-νεύω [in LXX: Pr 26:24 (נָכַר ni.), I Mac 6:57, II Mac 4:10 11:15 14:20 * ;]
to nod in command or approval, to nod approval, consent: Ac 18:20.†

strong.def: attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπίνοια, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπινοέω, to contrive) [in LXX: Je 20:10, Wi 6:16 9:14 14:12 15:4, Si 40:2, II Mac 12:45, IV Mac 17:2 * ;]
a thought, design: Ac 8:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπιορκέω, -ῶ (< ἐπίορκος), [in LXX: I Es 1:48, Wi 14:28 * ;]
to swear falsely, forswear oneself: Mt 5:33.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπί-ορκος, -ον [in LXX: Za 5:3 (שָׁבַע ni.) * ;]
1. of oaths, sworn falsely.
2. Of persons, perjured; as subst., a perjurer, false swearer: I Ti 1:10.†

strong.derivation: feminine singular participle of a comparative of G1909 (ἐπί) and (to go);
strong.def: supervening, i.e. (G2250 (ἡμέρα) or G3571 (νύξ) being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 (KJV) ἔπ-ειμι [in LXX: Ex 8:22(18) (עָמַד), Si 42:19, etc. ;]
1. to come upon, approach
2. Of time, to come on or after; mostly as ptcp., ἐπιών, -οῦσα, όν, next, following: τῇ- ἔ. (sc. ἡμέρᾳ, as freq. in late Gk.), Ac 16:11 20:15 21:18; ἡμέρᾳ (as usual in cl.), Ac 7:26; νυκτί, Ac 23:11.†

strong.def: to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπι-πλήσσω
1. to strike at, to punish.
2. to rebuke, reprove: I Ti 5:1.†

strong.def: to dote upon, i.e. intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἐπι-ποθέω, -ῶ [in LXX for יָאַב, אָרַג, כָּסַף hi., etc. ;]
to long for, desire: c. inf., Ro 1:11, II Co 5:2, I Th 3:6, II Ti 1:4, Phl 2:26 (WH, [txt.]); c. acc rei, I Pe 2:2; c. acc pers., II Co 9:14, Phl 1:8 2:26 (WH, mg); absol., Ja 4:5 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ἐπι-πόθησις, -εως, ἡ [in Aq.: Ez 23:11 * ;]
longing: II Co 7:7, 11.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of the latter part of G1971 (ἐπιποθέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐπι-πόθητος, -ον
greatly desired, longed for: Phl 4:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιποθία (WH, -πόθεια), -ας, ἡ = ἐπιπόθησις,
longing: Ro 15:23.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and some form of the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπίσημος, -ον (< σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: Ge 30:42 (קָשַׁר), Es 5:4 8:13, I Mac 11:37 14:48, II Mac 15:36, III Mac 6:1 * ;]
1. bearing a mark; of money, stamped, coined.
2. Metaph.,
(a). in good sense, notable, illustrious: Ro 16:7;
(b). in bad sense, notorious: Mt 27:16.†

strong.def: to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐπι-σκηνόω, -ῶ
to tent upon, spread a tabernacle over: metaph., seq. ἐπ’ ἐμέ (RV, rest upon, cover), II Co 12:9.†

strong.def: to oversee; by implication, to beware

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπι-σκοπέω, -ῶ [in LXX for פָּקַד ni., etc. ;]
1. to look upon, observe, examine: seq. μή, He 12:15.
2. As ἐπισκέπτομαι in LXX, NT, to visit, care for: I Pe 5:2 (R, txt.; WH om.; Cremer, 527).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4649 (σκοπός) (in the sense of G1983 (ἐπισκοπέω));
strong.def: a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐπί-σκοπος, -ου, ὁ (< σκοπός, a watcher), [in LXX for פָּקַד, its parts and derivatives, Nu 4:16 31:14, Jg 9:28, IV Ki 11:15, 18, II Ch 34:12, 17, Ne 11:9, 14, 22; אֵל, Jb 20:29; נוֹגַשׂ:, Is 60:17; Wi 1:6, I Mac 1:51 * ;]
a superintendent, guardian, overseer (cl.; for exx. v. LS, s.v.): Ac 20:28, I Pe 2:25 (ICC, in l.); as technical term for a religious office (Deiss., BS, 230 f.), in later Paul. epp. of the head of a church (Vg. episcopus), a bishop: Phl 1:1, I Ti 3:2, Tit 1:7 (v. reff. s.v. ἐπισκοπή).†

strong.def: to draw over, i.e. (with G203 (ἀκροβυστία) implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-σπάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Is 5:18 (מָשַׁךְ), etc. ;]
to draw on: mid., in peculiar sense of effacing signs of Judaism (cf. I Mac 1:15, FlJ, Ant., xii, 5, i; v. Thayer, s.v.), to become as uncircumcised: I Co 7:18.†

strong.def: to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐπι-στέλλω [in LXX: III Ki 5:8(22) Ne 6:19 (שָׁלַח), Jth 15:4, I Mac 10:25 12:7 13:18 (in each case with v.l. ἀποσ-) * ;]
1. to send to.
2. to send a message by letter, to write word (MM, Exp., xiv): c. dat. pers., Ac 21:25, He 13:22; seq. τοῦ, c. inf., Ac 15:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιστήμων, -ον, gen., -ονoς (ἐπίσταμαι) [in LXX: De 1:13 4:6, Is 5:21 (בִּין ni.), I Es 8:44, Si 10:25 21:15, etc. ;]
knowing, skilled: Ja 3:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐπι-στηρίζω [in LXX for סָמַךְ, etc. ;]
to make stronger, confirm: c. acc, Ac 14:22 15:32, 41.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 ἐπι-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἐπιατέλλω), [in LXX for אִגֶּרֶת, etc.; freq. in Mac ;]
1. a message.
2. a letter, an epistle: Ac 9:2, I Co 5:9, al.; pl., Ac 22:5, I Co 16:3, al.; ἐ. σνστατικαί, II Co 3:1 (cf. Milligan, NTD, 254 f.). (On the NT ἐπιστολαί, cf. Milligan, Th., 121 ff.; NTD, 85 ff.; Deiss., BS, 3 ff.; St. Paul, 8 ff.)

strong.def: to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπι-στομίζω (< στόμα),
to bridle; metaph., to stop the mouth, to silence: Tit 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπι-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἐπιστρέφω) [in LXX: Ez 47:7 (שׁוּב), Si 18:21 49:2, etc. ;]
a turning about; metaph., conversion (Field, Notes, 246): Ac 15:3.†

strong.def: a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ἐπι-συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἐπισυνάγω), [in LXX: II Mac 2:7 * ;]
a gathering together, assembly: He 10:25; seq. ἐπί, II Th 2:1 (cf. II Mac, l.c.).†

strong.derivation: from the middle voice of a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G4921 (συνιστάω);
strong.def: a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly)
strong.kjv: that which cometh upon, + raising up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † ἐπι-σύστασις, -εως, ἡ (< ἐπισυνίστημι) [in LXX: Nu 16:40 (עֵדָה) 26:9 (נָצָה hi.), I Es 5:73 A* ;]
a gathering, a riotous throng: Rec. (for ἐπίστασις, q.v.), Ac 24:12, II Co 11:28.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and (to trip);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπισφαλής, -ές (< σφάλλω, to cause to fall), [in LXX: Wi 9:14 (cf. -ῶς, ib. 4:4) * ;]
1. prone to fall (Plat.).
2. dangerous (Hipp., Plut., al.): Ac 27:9.†

strong.def: to accumulate further, i.e. (figuratively) seek additionally

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐπι-σωρεύω [in Sm.: Jb 14:17, Ca 2:4 * ;]
to heap together; metaph., διδασκάλους, II Ti 4:3.†

strong.def: an injunction or decree; by implication, authoritativeness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † ἐπι-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἐπιτάσσω), [in LXX: Da LXX 3:16 (פִּתְגָּם), I Es 1:18, Wi 14:16 18:16 19:6, III Mac 7:20 * ;]
= cl., ἐπίταγμα,
a command, Ro 16:26, I Co 7:6, 25, II Co 8:8, I Ti 1:1, Tit 1:3 (for use in Inscr. of divine commands, v. MM, Exp., xiv); μετὰ πάσης ἐ, with all authority: Tit 2:15.†

strong.def: to fulfill further (or completely), i.e. execute; by implication, to terminate, undergo

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐπι-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX for כָּלָה, עָשָׂה, etc. ;]
to complete, accomplish, execute: c. acc rei, Ro 15:28, II Co 7:1 8:6, 11, Phl 1:6, He 8:5; of religious services (cf. Hdt., ii, 37, al.), He 9:6; art. inf., II Co 8:11. Mid.,
(a). to complete for oneself, make an end (R, mg.; pass., R, txt; cf. Meyer, in l): Ga 3:3;
(b). to pay in full, pay the tax, be subject to: c. acc (cf. Xen., Mem., iv, 8, 8), I Pe 5:9 (pass., RV, etc.; cf. Thayer, s.v.; ICC, in 1).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιτήδειος, -α, -ον [in LXX: I Ch 28:2, Wi 4:5, I Mac 4:46, al. ;]
1. suitable, convenient,
2. useful, necessary: τὰ ἐ., necessaries, Ja 2:16,†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G5092 (τιμή);
strong.def: properly, esteem, i.e. citizenship; used (in the sense of G2008 (ἐπιτιμάω)) of a penalty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιτιμία, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπιτιμάω), [in LXX: Wis_3:10 * ;]
1. citizenship, franchise.
2. As in Inscr. (LS, s.v.), LXX, l.c. (= cl. τὸ ἐπιτίμιον), punishment, penalty: II Co 2:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπι-τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ἐπιτρέπω), [in LXX: II Mac 13:14 * ;]
power to decide, authority: Ac 26:12.†

strong.def: to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) to attain

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐπι-τυγχάνω [in LXX: Ge 39:2 (צָלַח hi.), Pr 12:27 (חָרַךְ)* ;]
1. to light upon.
2. to obtain, attain to: Ja 4:2, c. gen. rei (as in cl.), He 6:15 11:33; c. acc (late Gk.), Ro 11:7 (Rec. τούτου).†

strong.def: a manifestation, i.e. (specially) the advent of Christ (past or future)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐπιφάνεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπιφανής), [in LXX: II Ki 7:23 (נוֹרָא), Es 5:1, Am 5:22, II Mac 2:21 3:24 5:4 12:22 14:16 15:27, III Mac 2:9 5:8, 51,* ;] (in late Gk. and Inscr., freq. of deities, v. MM, Exp., xiv)
a manifestation, appear­ance: II Th 2:8, I Ti 6:14, II Ti 1:10 4:1, 8, Tit 2:13 (cf. M, Th., 148 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπιφανής, -ές (< ἐπιφαίνω), [in LXX (v. Thayer, s.v.) for יָרֵא, etc., Jg 13:6, Jl 2:11, 31 al.; II Mac 6:23, III Mac 5:35, al. ;]
renowned, illustrious, notable: Ac 2:20 (LXX) (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐπι-φαύσκω (variant form of ἐπιφώσκω, q.v.), [in LXX: Jb 25:5 (אהל hi.) 31:26 41:9(10) (הָלַל hi.) * ;]
to shine forth: fig., c. dat., Eph 5:14 (on v.l. -ψαύσει, v. ICC, Westc., AR, in l.).†

strong.def: to bear upon (or further), i.e. adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπι-φέρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַח ;]
1. to bring upon or against: κρίσιν, Ju 9.
2. to impose, inflict: Ro 3:5.†

strong.def: to furnish besides, i.e. fully supply, (figuratively) aid or contribute

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** ἐπι-χορηγέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Si 25:22, II Mac 4:9 A * ;]
to supply, provide: c. acc rei, II Pe 1:5; id. c. dat. pers., II Co 9:10, Ga 3:5; pass., Col 2:19, II Pe 1:11 (cf. χορηγέω, and v. MM, Exp., xiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐπι-χορηγία, -ας, ἡ (< ἐπιχορηγέω),
a supply: Eph 4:16, Phl 1:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐπι-χρίω [in Sm.: Ez 13:10 22:28 * ;]
to spread on, anoint: c. acc, Jo 9:11; id. seq. ἐπί, c. acc, Jo 9:6 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

strong.def: to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 * ἐπ-οικοδομέω, -ῶ
in NT, always metaph., of the spiritual life regarded as a building (Cremer, 449);
1. to build upon: I Co 3:10, 12, 14; pass., Eph 2:20.
2. to build up: Col 2:7, I Pe 2:5 (T, οἰκοδ- WH, Rec.), Ju 20.†

strong.def: to drive upon the shore, i.e. to beach a vessel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐπι-κέλλω
of a ship, to run ashore: c. acc, Ac 27:41.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐπ-ονομάζω [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;]
to name, call by a name, surname: pass., Ro 2:17.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐπ-οπτεύω [in Sm.: Ps 9:35 (10:14) 32 (33:13) * ;]
to watch (in Hom., as an overseer; cf Ps, ll. c.), look upon: I Pe 2:12 3:2.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἐπόπτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX (of God): Es 5:1, II Mac 3:39 7:35, III Mac 2:21 * ;]
1. an overseer (LXX, ll. c.).
2. a spectator: II Pe 1:16 (of ἐ. as applied to God, v. parallels in Inscr., MM, Exp., xiv; of the use of this term in the mysteries, v. Mayor on II Pe, l.c.; Thayer, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἔπος, -εος (-ους), τό [in LXX: Za 7:3, Si 44:5 * ;]
a word: ὡς ἔ. εἰπεῖν (cl.), so to speak: He 7:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 ἐπουράνιος, -ον (< οὐρανός), [in LXX: Ps 68:14 (שַׁדַּי), Da TH 4:23 A (שָׁמַיִם) II Mac 3:39, III Mac 6:28 7:6, IV Mac 4:11 AR, IV Mac 11:3 א* ;]
in or of heaven, heavenly (in Hom., of the Gods): οἱ ἐ., opp. to ἐπίγειοι and καταχθόνιοι, Phl 2:10; to χοϊκός, I Co 15:48, 49; σώματα (v. Lft., Col., 376), I Co 15:40; βασιλεία, II Ti 4:18; παπρίς, He 11:16; Ἱερουσαλήμ, He 12:22; κλῆσις (cf. Lft. on Phl 3:14), He 3:1; τὰ ἐ., He 8:5 9:23; opp. to ἐπίγειος, Jo 3:12; id., of the heavenly regions, Eph 1:3, 20 2:6 3:10 6:12; ἡ δωρεὰ ἡ ἐ., He 6:4 (Cremer, 468).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἑπτακισχίλιοι, -αι, -α
seven thousand: Ro 11:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἔραστος, -ου, ὁ
Erastus;
1. a companion of St. Paul, Ac 19:22, and prob. II Ti 4:20.
2. The treasurer of Corinth, Ro 16:23.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed prolonged form of G2054 (ἔρις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐρεθίζω [in LXX: Da LXX 11:10, 25 (גָּרָה hithp.), I Mac 15:40, II Mac 14:17, etc. ;]
1. to stir up, provoke (as in cl.): Col 3:21.
2. In good sense (cf. ἐρεθισμός, excitement in MGr.), to stir up, stimulate: II Co 9:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐρείδω (chiefly in poets and late prose for ἐρυγγάνω), [in LXX for תָּמַךְ (Pr 4:4 5:5 11:16, al.), etc. ;]
to prop, fix firmly: act., as mid., ἐρείσασα, of a ship driving ashore (RV, struck), Ac 27:41.†

strong.def: to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak out

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐρεύγομαι [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַג, Ho 11:10, Am 3:4, 8 al.; also for נָבַע, Ps 18 (19):2, etc. ;]
1. to spit or spue out.
2. Prop., of oxen (Hom.), to bellow, roar; whence, as in LXX, to speak aloud, utter: Mt 13:35 (LXX). (For other examples of softened force of words in late Gk., cf. σκύλλω, τρώγω, χορτάζω.) †

strong.derivation: apparently from G2046 (ἐρέω) (through the idea of inquiry);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐραυνάω, -ῶ late form of ἐρευνάω (Rec., ll. c.; cf. Bl., § 6, 1; M, Pr., 46), [in LXX, ἐρευν- (exc. I Ch 19:3 A), for חָפַשׂ pi., חָקַר, etc. ;]
to search, examine: Jo 7:52; c. acc rei, Jo 5:39, Ro 8:27, I Co 2:10, Re 2:23; seq. orat. obliq., I Pe 1:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἐρίζω (< ἔρις), [in LXX for מָרָה, etc. ;]
to wrangle, strive: Mt 12:19 (LXX, κεκράζεται).†

strong.derivation: perhaps as the same as G2042 (ἐρεθίζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ** ἐριθία (T, cl., -εία), -ας, ἡ, [in Sm.: Ez 23:11 * ;] (on the origin and history of the word, v. Hort, Ja., 81 ff.; Ellic. on Ga 5:20; Cremer, 262)
ambition, self-seeking, rivalry: Ja 3:14, 16; κατ’ ἐριθίαν, Phl 2:3; οἱ ἐξ ἐ., Ro 2:8, Phl 1:17; pl. (Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220; Swete, Mk., 153), II Co 12:20, Ga 5:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἔριον, -ου, τό [in LXX for צֶמֶר, Le 13:47, Is 1:18, al. ;]
wool: He 9:19, Re 1:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ἔρις, -ιδος acc, ἔριν (on the declension, v. B1., § 8, 3; WH, App., 157), ἡ, [in LXX: Ps 138 (139):20, Si 28:11 40:5, 9 * ;]
strife, wrangling, contention: Ro 1:29 13:13, I Co 3:3, II Co 12:20, Ga 5:20, Phl 1:15, I Ti 6:4, Tit 3:9; pl. (v.s. ἐριθία), Ro 13:13, WH, mg., I Co 1:11, Ga, l.c., WH, mg.†

strong.def: a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked person)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἐρίφιον, -ου, τό (dim, of ἔριφος, q.v.) [in LXX: To 2:13 * ;]
Mt 25:33, Lk 15:29 (ἔριφον, WH, txt.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἑρμᾶς, -ᾶ, acc, -ᾶν (Doric form of Ἑρμῆς),
Hermas, a Christian: Ro 16:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 ἑρμηνεία, v.s. ἑρμηνία.

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G2060 (Ἑρμῆς) (as the god of language);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἑρμηνεύω [in LXX: Es 4:7 (תִּרְגַּם), Es 10:3 Jb 42:18* ;]
1. to explain.
2. to interpret: Lk 24:27 (WH, mg.), Jo 1:39, 43 9:7, He 7:2.†

strong.def: Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek deities; also of a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Ἑρμῆς, -οῦ
acc, Ἑρμῆν, ὁ,
Hermes;
(a). the Greek god (Lat. Mercurius): Ac 14:12;
(b). a Christian: Ro 16:14.†

strong.def: born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἑρμογένης, -ους, ὁ
Hermogenes, a Christian: II Ti 1:15.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of (to creep);
strong.def: a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare H07431)) a small animal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἑρπετόν, -οῦ, τό (< ἕρπω, to crawl), [in LXX chiefly for רֶמֶשׂ, שֶׁרֶץ ;]
a creeping thing, reptile: Ac 10:12 11:6, Ro 1:23, Ja 3:7.†

strong.derivation: of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with G2281 (θάλασσα)) the Red Sea

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐρυθρός, -ά, -όν [in LXX for אֱדֹם, Is 63:2; ἐ. θάλασσα for סוּף -יָם Ex 10:19, al. ;]
red: ἡ ἐ. θάλασσα, the Red Sea, Ac 7:36, He 11:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἔσθησις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX: pl., II Mac 3:33, III Mac 1:16 * ;]
clothing: pl., Ac 1:10.†

strong.derivation: from G1519 (εἰς) and a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἔσ-οπτρον, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Wi 7:26, Si 12:11 * ;]
a mirror: I Co 13:12, Ja 1:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐσώτερος, -α, -ον (compar. of ἔσω), [in LXX chiefly for פְּנִימִי and cognate forms ;]
inner: Ac 16:24; τὸ ἐ., He 6:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἑταῖρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ and cognate forms, also Si 11:6 37:2ff., al. ;]
a companion, comrade: Mt 11:16 (WH, ἑτέροις); voc., as term of address, my friend: Mt 20:13 22:12 26:50.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἑτερό-γλωσσος (Att. -ττος), -ον, [in Aq.: Ps 113 (114):1, Is 33:19 * ;]
of alien speech, of another tongue (v. Cremer, 681): I Co 14:21 (aliter in LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω, -ῶ
to teach other or different doctrine: I Ti 1:3 6:3 (cf. CGT, in l.; Milligan, NTD, 102).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2087 (ἕτερος) and G2218 (ζυγός);
strong.def: to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἑτερο-ζυγέω, -ῶ [in LXX cf. ἑτερόζυγος, Le 19:19 (כִּלְאַיִם)* ;]
to be unequally yoked: metaph., c. dat. pers., II Co 6:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἑτέρως adv.,
differently, otherwise: Phl 3:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἑτοιμασία, -ας, ἡ (< ἑτοιμάζω, q.v.), [in LXX for כּוּן hi., כֵּן, מָכוֹן, and cognate forms, II Es 2:68 3:3, Ps 9:39 (10:17) 64 (65):9 88 (89):14, Na 2:3(4), Za 5:11, Ez 43:11, Da TH 11:7, 20, 21, Wi 13:12 * ;]
1. = ἑτοιμότης,
(a). readiness (Hipp.);
(b). preparation (LXX; e.g. ἑ. τ. καρδίας, Ps 9:39 (10:17)): Eph 6:15, EV.
2. foundation, firm footing (Ps 88 (89):14): Eph, l.c. (Hatch, Essays, 55; Exp Times., ix, 38; but v. also Abbott, Essays, 95).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἑτοίμως, adv. [in LXX: II Es 7:17ff., Da LXX TH 3:15 * ;]
readily: I Pe 4:5; ἑ. ἔχω, to be ready (Deiss., BS, 252; MM, Exp., xiv): c. inf., Ac 21:13, II Co 12:14.†

strong.def: Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Εὔα (WH, Εὕα, § 408; Rec. Εὖα; S (in I Ti), Εὕα), -ας, ἡ (Heb. חַוָּה, Ge 3:20),
Eve, wife of Adam: II Co 11:3, I Ti 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† εὐαγγελιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
an evangelist;
(a). in NT, a preacher of the gospel: Ac 21:8, Eph 4:11, II Ti 4:5;
(b). later, a writer of a gospel (eccl.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 εὐαρεστέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ hith., Ge 5:22, 24, Ps 25 (26):2 55 (56):13, al., Si 44:16 ;]
to be well pleasing: τ. θεῷ (LXX, ll. c.), He 11:5, 6. Pass., to be well pleased: c. dat., He 13:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 **† εὐ-άρεστος, -ον [in LXX: Wi 4:10 9:10 * ;]
well-pleasing, acceptable: Ro 12:2; c. dat. pers., Ro 12:1 14:18, II Co 5:9, Eph 5:10, Phl 4:18; id. seq. ἐν, Tit 2:9 (κυρίῳ), Col 3:20; ἐνώπιον, He 13:21 (for ex. in Inser., v. Deiss., BS, 215).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * εὐ-αρέοτως adv.,
acceptably: τ, θεῷ, He 12:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Εὔβουλος, -ου, ὁ.
Eubulus, a Christian: II Ti 4:21.†

strong.derivation: feminine from G2095 (εὖ) and the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) (as the god of the weather);
strong.def: a clear sky, i.e. fine weather

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** εὐδία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Si 3:15 * ;] (< εὔδιος, calm)
fair weather: Mt 16:2 (Rec., R, txt.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 εὐεργεσία, -ας, ἡ (< εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Ps 77 (78):11 (עֲלִילָה), Wi 16:11, 24, II Mac 6:13 9:26, IV Mac 8:17 * ;]
a good deed, kindness, benefit: I Ti 6:2; c. gen. pers. (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), Ac 4:9,†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐεργετέω, -ῶ (< εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Ps 12 (13):6 (גָּמַל), Wi 3:5, al. ;]
to do good, bestow benefit: Ac 10:38.†

strong.def: to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† εὐθυδρομέω, -ῶ
of ships, to run a straight course (Philo): Ac 16:11 21:1.†

strong.def: to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** εὐθυμέω, -ῶ (< ὔθυμος), [in Sm.: Ps 31 (32):11, Pr 15:15 * ;]
1. trans., to make cheerful (Æsch.).
2. Intrans. (Eur., Plut.; so mid. in Xen., Plat.), to be of good cheer: Ac 27:22, 25, Ja 5:13.†

strong.kjv: of good cheer, the more cheerfully

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** εὔ-θυμος, -ον [in LXX: II Mac 11:26 * ;]
1. kind (Hom.).
2. of good cheer (Æsch., al.): Ac 27:36.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 εὐθύνω (< εὐθύς), [in LXX: Nu 22:23, Jos 24:23 (נָטָה hi.), Jg 14:7, I Ki 18:20, 26 (יָשַׁר) Pr 20:24, Si 2:2, 6, al. ;]
1. to direct: Ja 3:4.
2. to make straight: Jo 1:23 (LXX, ἑτοιμάσατε).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐθύτης, -ητος, ἡ (< εὐθύς), [in LXX chiefly for יֹשֶׁר, מִישׁוֹר and cognate forms ;]
uprightness: He 1:8 (LXX).†

strong.def: properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 εὐλάβεια, -ας, ἡ (< εὐλαβής), [in LXX: Je 22:24 (דְּאָגָה), Pr 28:14, Wi 17:8 * ;]
1. caution, discretion (Soph., Plat., al.).
2. In later Gk. (Diod., Plut., al.), also reverence, godly fear: He 5:7 12:28.†

strong.def: to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐλαβέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX: Pr 24:28 (30:5), Na 1:7 (חָסָה), al., for 15 different Heb. words in all; also Si 7:29 41:3, al. ;]
1. to be cautious, to beware: Ac 23:10 (Rec.; φοβηθείς, WH, RV).
2. to reverence: He 11:7 (cf. Cremer, 388).†

strong.def: fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess
strong.kjv: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 εὐλογία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בְּרָכָה ;]
1. fair speaking, flattering speech: χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐ., Ro 16:18.
2. praise: of God (as in late Inscr.; LS, s.v.) and Christ, Re 5:12, 13 7:12
3. In LXX and NT: blessing, benediction;
(a). the act of blessing: I Co 10:16, He 12:17, Ja 3:10;
(b). concrete, a blessing: Ro 15:29, II Co 9:5, 6, Ga 3:14, Eph 1:3, He 6:7, I Pe 3:9 (cf. De 11:26, Si 7:32, al.).†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and a presumed derivative of G3330 (μεταδίδωμι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† εὐ-μετά-δοτος, -ον (< εὖ, μεταδιδωμι),
ready to impart: assoc. with κοινωνικός (for the distinction bet. the two, v. Field, Notes, 213; CGT, in l.), I Ti 6:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Εὐνίκη (Rec. -νείκη), -ης,
Eunice, Timothy's mother: II Ti 1:5.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3563 (νοῦς);
strong.def: to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐ-νοέω, -ῶ (< εὔνοος, friendly), [in LXX: Es 8:13 Bא1, Da LXX 2:43, III Mac 7:11 * ;]
to be favourable, kindly disposed: c. dat., Mt 5:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὔνοια, -ας, ἡ (< εὔνοος), [in LXX: Es 2:23, al. ;]
goodwill: Eph 6:7 (of slaves; cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† εὐνουχίζω (< εὐνοῦχος),
to make a eunuch of, castrate: pass., Mt 19:12; metaph., εὐ. έαυτόν, ib.†

strong.def: a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 εὐνοῦχος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. ὁ τὴν εὐνὴν (bed) ἔχων), [in LXX for סָרִיס (perhaps not of necessity an actual eunuch; DB, s.v.), Ge 39:1, al., Wi 3:14, Si 20:4 30:20 ;]
an emasculated man, a eunuch: Mt 19:12; one such holding, as was common, high office, as of chamberlain, at court, Ac 8:27, 34, 36, 38, 39; metaph., of one naturally incapacitated for or volun­tarily abstaining from wedlock, Mt 19:12.†

strong.def: fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Εὐοδία (Rec. -ωδία), -ας, ἡ
Euodia (not as AV, Euodias), a Christian woman: Phl 4:2.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3598 (ὁδός);
strong.def: to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 εὐ-οδόω, -ῶ (< ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for צָלַח hi. ;]
to help on one's way (Soph., al.). Pass., to have a prosperous journey; metaph. (Hdt., al.), to prosper, be prospered, be successful: III Jo 2, Ro 1:10, I Co 16:2 (on the tense, v. M, Pr., 54; ICC, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** εὐ-πειθής, ές, (< εὖ, πείθομαι), [in LXX: IV Mac 12:6 AR* ;]
ready to obey, compliant: Ja 3:17.†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G4012 (περί) and G2476 (ἵστημι);
strong.def: well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * εὐ-περί-στατος, -ον (< εὖ, περιΐστημι),
of sins, readily besetting: He 12:1 (on form and sense of the word, v. Westc., in l.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4160 (ποιέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† εὐ-ποιία (Rec. -ιΐα), -ας, ἡ
1. beneficence, doing good: He 13:16.
2. a benefit (FlJ, Ant., ii, 11, 2, al.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω) and the base of G4197 (πορεία);
strong.def: (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐ-πορέω, -ῶ (< εὔτορος, well provided for) [in LXX: Le 25:26, 49 נָשַׂג hi.), ib. 28 (v.l.), Wi 10:10 * ;]
to prosper, be well off: Ac 11:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐ-πορία, -ας, ἡ (< εὔπορος), [in LXX for חַיִל, IV Ki 25:10 A (freq. in Aq.)* ;]
1. facility.
2. plenty, wealth: Ac 19:25.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4241 (πρέπω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐ-πρέπεια, -ας, ἡ (< εὐπρεπής, comely), [in LXX for הָדָר, etc. ;]
goodly appearance, comeliness: Ja 1:11.†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G4327 (προσδέχομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † εὐ-πρόσ-δεκτος, -ον (< εὖ, προσδέχομαι)
more usual than δέκτος, q.v., acceptable: Ro 15:16, 31, II Co 6:2 8:12, I Pe 2:5.†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and the same as G4332 (προσεδρεύω);
strong.def: sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† εὐ-πρόσ-εδρος, -ον
Rec. for εὐπάρεδρος, q.v.: I Co 7:35.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4383 (πρόσωπον);
strong.def: to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† εὐ-προσωπέω, -ῶ (< εὐπρόσωπος, fair of face), [in Al.: Ps 140 (141):6, v.l. for -ίζω* ;]
to look well, make a fair show: metaph. (as in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 96), Ga 6:12.†

strong.def: a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, q.v.), -ωνος (< Εὖρος, the East wind, and Lat. Aquilo; Vg., Euroaquilo),
the Euraquilo, a N.E. wind (i.e. between Eurus and Aquilo): Ac 27:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐρύ-χωρος, -ον (< εὐρύς, broad + χώρα), [in LXX for רָחַב ni., and cognate forms (Is 30:23, al.), exc. II Ch 18:9 (גֹּרֶן ;]
spacious, broad: Mt 7:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 εὐ-σέβεια, -ας, ἡ (< εὐσεβής, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 1:7, Is 33:6 (יִרְאָה), Pr 13:11 (aliter in Heb.), Is 11:2 (יְהֹוָה יִרְאָה), I Es 1:23, Wi 10:12, Si 49:3, and very freq. in IV Mac ;]
1. piety, reverence (towards parents and others).
2. piety towards God, godliness: Ac 3:12, I Ti 2:2 4:7, 8 6:5, 6, 11, II Pe 1:3, 6, 7,; τὸ τῆς εὐ. μυστήριον, I Ti 3:16; ἡ κατ’ εὐ. διδασκαλία, I Ti 6:3; ἡ ἀλήθεια ἡ κατ' εὐ., Tit 1:1; μόρφωσις εὐσεβείας, II Ti 3:5; pl. (v. Bl., § 32, 6; Mayor on Ja 2:1), II Pe 3:11 (on the use of εὐ. and cognates in Past. Epp., v. CGT, on I Ti 2:2; cf. also Cremer, 524).†

strong.def: to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** εὐ-σεβέω, -ῶ (< εὐσεβής, q.v.), [in LXX: Da LXX Su 1:64, IV Mac 9:6 אR, IV Mac 11:5, 8, 23 18:2 * ;]
to reverence, show piety towards; c. acc (else­where more freq. seq. εἰς., περί, πρός): οἶκον, I Ti 5:4; θεόν, Ac 17:23 (Cremer, 525).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 εὐσεβής, -ές (< εὖ, σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pr 12:12, Is 24:16 26:7 (צַדִּיק), Mi 7:2 (חָסִיד), Is 32:8 (נָדִיב), and freq. in Si and IV Mac;]
pious, godly, devout: Ac 10:2, 7, II Pe 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** εὐσεβῶς adv., [in LXX: IV Mac 7:21 * ;]
piously, religiously: II Ti 3:12, Tit 2:12.†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὔσημος, -ον (< εὖ + οῆμα, a sign) [in LXX for כֶּסֶא, Ps 80 (81):3 (-ως, Da LXX 2:19)* ;]
1. conspicuous (cf. Ps, l.c.).
2. clear to the understanding, distinct: I Co 14:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** εὔσπλαγχνος, -ον (εὖ, σπλάγχνον, q.v.), [in Pr Ma 7 (Camb. Manual LXX, iii, 825) ;]
1. in Hippocr., as medical term (LS, s.v.).
2. Metaph. (cf. εὐσιλαγχνία, Eurip., Rhes., 192), in NT, tenderhearted, compassionate: Eph 4:32, I Pe 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * εὐσχημόνως adv. (< εὐσχήμων),
decorously, becomingly: I Co 14:40; περιπατεῖν, Ro 13:13, I Th 4:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** εὐσχημοσύνη (< εὐσχήμων), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:2 * ;]
seemliness, comeliness: I Co 12:23.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of the base of G5157 (τροπή) (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose);
strong.def: witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * εὐτραπελία, -ας, ἡ (< εὖ, τρέπω),
1. versatility, wit, facetiousness (Hippocr., Plat., al.).
2. = βωμολογία, coarse jesting, ribaldry (Abbott, Essays, 93): Eph 5:4.†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5177 (τυγχάνω);
strong.def: well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Εὔτυχος, -ου, ὁ (εὖ, τυχή),
Eutychus, a young man: Ac 20:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** εὐφημία, -ας, ἡ (< εὔφημος), [in Sm.: Ps 41 (42):5 46 (47):2 99 (100):2 125 (126):2 * ;]
good report, praise: opp. to δυσφημία, II Co 6:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὔφημος, -ον (εὖ, φήμη), [in Sm.: Ps 62 (63):6 ;]
primarily, utter­ing words or sounds of good omen, hence,
1. avoiding ill-omened words, religiously silent.
2. fair-sounding, auspicious (R, mg., gracious): Phl 4:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Εὐφράτης, -ου, ὁ
the river Euphrates: Re 9:14 16:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 εὐφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< εὔφρων, cheerful) [in LXX chiefly for שִׂמְחָה ;]
rejoicing, gladness: Ac 2:28 (LXX) 14:17.†

strong.def: gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ** εὐχαριστία, -ας, ἡ (< εὐχάριστος), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 16:28, Si 37:11, II Mac 2:27 * ;]
1. thankfulness, gratitude (Polyb.; Es, Si, II Mac, ll. c.): Ac 24:3.
2. giving of thanks, thanksgiving (so in π. and Inscr.; M, Th., 41 f.): I Co 14:16, II Co 4:15, Eph 5:4, Phl 4:6, Col 2:7 4:2, I Th 3:9, I Ti 4:3, 4, Re 4:9 7:12; c. dat. pers., II Co 9:11 (cf. τ. θεοῦ, Wis, l.c.); pl., II Co 9:12, I Ti 2:1 (Cremer, 904).†

strong.derivation: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5483 (χαρίζομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 εὐχάριστος, -ον (< εὖ, χαρίζομαι), [in LXX for חֵן, Pr 11:16 * ;]
1. = εὔχαρις, winning, gracious, agreeable (Pr, l.c.).
2. grateful, thankful: Col 3:15.†

strong.def: properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 εὐχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< εὔχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for נֵדֶר ;]
1. a prayer: Ja 5:15.
2. a vow: Ac 18:18 21:23.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a primary verb;
strong.def: to wish; by implication, to pray to God

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 εὔχομαι [in LXX chiefly for נָדַד, also for עָתַר hi., etc. ;]
to pray: c. acc rei, II Co 13:9; c. dat. pers., τ. θεῷ, Ac 26:29; seq. πρὸς τ. θεόν, II Co 13:7; c. acc et inf., Ac 27:29, III Jo 2; seq. ὑπέρ, Ja 5:16; ηὐχόμην εἶναι (on impf. here, v. ICC, in l., Lft., Phm 13), Ro 9:3 (Cremer, 718).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 εὔ-χρηστος, -ον (εὖ, χράομαι), [in LXX: Pr 31:13 (חֵפֶץ), Wi 13:13 * ;]
useful, serviceable: c. dat. pers., II Ti 2:21; id. seq. εἰς, c. dat. rei, II Ti 4:11; opp. to ἄχρηστος, Phm 11.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G5590 (ψυχή);
strong.def: to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† εὐψυχέω, -ῶ (< εὔψυχος, courageous),
to be of good courage: Phl 2:19.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G3605 (ὄζω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 εὐωδία, -ας, ἡ (< εὐώδης, fragrant; < ὄζω) [in LXX for נִיחֹחַ, Ge 8:21, al. (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας); Si 20:9 24:15, al. ;]
fragrance: metaph., Χριστοῦ εὐ,., II Co 2:15; ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας (a metaphor of sacrifice, most freq. in Pent. and Ez.), Eph 5:2, Phl 4:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐφάλλομαι [in LXX for צָלַח, I Ki 10:6 11:6 16:13 * ;]
to leap upon: seq. ἐπί c. acc pers. Ac 19:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * ἐφ-άπαξ, adv.
1. once for all (Eupol.): Ro 6:10 He 7:27 9:12 10:10.
2. at once: I Co 15:6.†

strong.def: an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Ἐφέσιος, -α, -ον
Ephesian: Ac 18:27 19:28, 34, 35 21:29.†

strong.def: Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 Ἔφεσος, -ου, ἡ
Ephesus, a city in Asia Minor Ac 18:19, 21, 24, 27 19:1, 17, 26 (on the gen., v. M, Pr., 73) Ac 20:16, 17, I Co 15:32 16:8, Eph 1:1, I Ti 1:3, II Ti 1:18 4:12, Re 1:11 2:1.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G2147 (εὑρίσκω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐφ-ευρετής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ἐφευρίσκω, to find out)
an inventor, contriver: κακῶν (cf. κακίας εὑρετής, II Mac 7:31), Ro 1:30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἐφ-ήμερος, -ον (ἐπί, ἡμέρα),
1. lasting for a day.
2. daily, for the day: Ja 2:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a cognate of G2240 (ἥκω);
strong.def: to arrive upon, i.e. extend to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX: Si 43:27, 30 R (ἀφικ- ABא)* ;]
to come to, to reach: seq. ἄχρι, II Co 10:13; εἰς, ib. 14.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (H0669 or better H06085);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἐφραίμ, (-ΐμ, Tr.)
Ephraim, a town near Jerusalem: Jo 11:54.†

strong.def: Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ζαβουλών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. זְבֻלוּן v. Ge 30:20)
Zebulun, Jacob's tenth son: the tribe of Z., Mt 4:13, 15, Re 7:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ζαρά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. זֶרַח, Ge 38:30),
Zerah, an ancestor of Jesus: Mt 1:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† ζεστός, -ή, -όν (ζέω), [in Aq.: Le 6:21 (14); in Al.: Le 7:12*;]
boiling hot (Strab., al.): metaph., Re 3:15, 16.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as G2218 (ζυγός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ζευκτήριος, -α -ον (< ζεύγνυμι),
fit for joining. As subst.,
(a). ζευκτήριον, τό = ζυγόν, a yoke;
(b). ζευκτηρία, -ας, ἡ = ζεύγλη, the crossbar of a double rudder: Ac 27:40 (found nowhere else).†

strong.def: in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name , which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ζεύς
gen., Διός, dat., Διΐ, acc., Δία (Δίαν, D, al.),
Zeus (Lat. Jupiter): Ac 14:12, 13.†

strong.def: to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ζέω [in LXX for רוּם, רתח, metaph., IV Mac 18:20;]
to boil, be hot; metaph., of anger, love, zeal: ptcp., fervent: τ. πνεύματι, Ac 18:25, Ro 12:11.†

strong.def: properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice)
strong.kjv: emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 ζῆλος, -ου, ὁ and in late Gk., also -εος, τό (II Co 9:2, Phl 3:6), [in LXX for קִנְאָה, Nu 25:11, al.;]
1. zeal: II Co 7:11 9:2; κατὰ ζῆλος, Phl 3:6; c. gen. obj., Jo 2:17(LXX), Ro 10:2; seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 7:7; c. gen. subj., θεοῦ, II Co 11:2; πυρός, He 10:27 (cf. Is 26:11, Wi 5:18, and cf. Westc., in l.).
2. jealousy: Ro 13:13, I Co 3:3, II Co 12:20, Ga 5:20 (WH, txt, RV), Ja 3:14, 16; πλησθῆναι ζήλου Ac 5:17 13:45; pl., ζῆλοι (v. B1., § 32, 6), Ga 5:20, WH, mg.†

strong.def: to have warmth of feeling for or against
strong.kjv: affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ζηλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for קנא pi.;]
1. to burn with envy or jealousy, to be jealous: absol., Ac 7:9 17:5, I Co 13:4, Ja 4:2 (R, mg., cf. Mayor, in l.).
2. to seek or desire eagerly: c. acc. rei, I Co 12:31 14:1, 39 (cf. Si 50:18, Wi 1:12); c. acc. pers., II Co 11:2, Ga 4:17; pass., Ga 4:18.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ζηλωτής, -οῦ, ὁ (< ζηλόω), [in LXX for קַנָּא (θεὸς ζ.), Ex 20:5 34:14, De 4:24 5:9 6:15; קַנּוֹא, Na 1:2 (θεός); pl., I Es 8:72; ζ. τῶν νόμων, II Mac 4:2;τὸν ζ. Φινεές, IV Mac 18:12 (cf. Nu 25:11)*;]
1. in cl. an emulator, zealous admirer (Plat., al.).
2. eagerly desirous, zealous;
(a). absol., as in OT, Ex 20:5 34:14, De 4:24 5:9 6:15, Na 1:2, I Es 8:72;
(b). c. gen. obj.: (zealous to acquire or to defend), I Co 14:12, Tit 2:14, I Pe 3:13; τ. νομου (II Mac 4:2), Ac 21:20; παραδόσεων, Ga 1:14; c. gen. pers., θεοῦ, Ac 22:3.
3. In FlJ, NT, a Zealot, member of the Jewish party so called: as surname of the Apostle Simon, Lk 6:15, Ac 1:13.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to the base of G1150 (δαμάζω) (through the idea of violence);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ζημία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX for ענשׁ ni. and cognate forms;]
damage, loss: Ac 27:10, 21, Phl 3:8; opp. to κέρδος, Phl 3:7.†

strong.derivation: probably contracted from a poetic form of G2203 (Ζεύς) and G1435 (δῶρον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ζηνᾶς, -ᾶ, acc. -ᾶν (contr. from Ζηνόδωρος),
Zenas: Tit 3:13.†

strong.def: a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ζήτημα, -τος, τό (< ζητέω), [in LXX: ζ. τίθεσθαι (דּרשׁ ni.), Ez 36:37 A*;]
an inquiry, question: Ac 15:2 18:15 23:29 25:19 26:3.†

strong.def: a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 * ζήτησις, -εως, ἡ (< ζητέω).
1. a seeking, search.
2. a questioning, inquiry, debate: Ac 15:2, 7, II Ti 2:23, Tit 3:9; seq. περί, Jo 3:25, Ac 25:20, I Ti 6:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 * ζιζάνιον, -ου, τό (in Talmud זוּנִין),
zizanium (EV, tares), a kind of darnel, resembling wheat: Mt 13:25-27, 29, 30, 36, 38, 40 (cf. DB, s.v. "Tares").†

strong.derivation: akin to the base of G3509 (νέφος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** ζόφος, -ου, ὁ (akin to γνόφος, q.v.), [in Sm.: Ex 10:22, Jb 28:3, Ps 10(11):2 90(91):6, Is 59:9*;]
in Hom. the gloom of the under-world; hence, darkness, deep gloom (poët. and late prose writers): He 12:18, II Pe 2:4, 17, Ju 6, 13.†

strong.derivation: from the root of (to join, especially by a "yoke");
strong.def: a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ζυγός (in cl. more freq. τὸ ζυγόν), -οῦ, ὁ (< ζεύγνυμι), [in LXX for עֹל, מֹאזְנַיִם, etc.;]
1. a yoke; metaph., of bondage or submission to authority: Mt 11:29, 30, Ac 15:10, Ga 5:1, I Ti 6:1.
2. a balance: Re 6:5 (cf. Is 40:12, al.).†

strong.def: to bind about (especially with a belt)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ζώννυμι and ζωννύω [in LXX chiefly for חגר;]
to gird: c. acc. pers., Jo 21:18. Mid., to gird oneself: Ac 12:8 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, περι-, ὑπο-ζώννυμι).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G2198 (ζάω);
strong.def: a live thing, i.e. an animal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
23 ζῷον (Rec. ζῶον, v. LS, s.v.), -ου, τό (< ζωός, alive), [in LXX for חַיָּה (chiefly) and cognate forms; freq. in Wi;]
a living creature, an animal: Re 4:6-9 5:6 ff. Re 6:1 ff. Re 7:11 14:3 15:7 19:4; ζῴων τ. αἷμα, He 13:11; ἄλογα ζ., II Pe 2:12, Ju 10.†

strong.derivation: from the same as G2226 (ζῶον) and G4160 (ποιέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ζωο-ποιέω, ῶ [in LXX for חיה pi., hi., Jg 21:14, IV Ki 5:7, Ne 9:6, Jb 36:6, Ps 70:20, Ec 7:13(12)*;]
1. in cl. (= ζωογονέω), to produce alive.
2. In LXX and NT, to make alive, cause to live, quicken (DCG, ii, 606a; Cremer, 275): Jo 5:21 6:53, Ro 4:17 8:11, I Co 15:45, II Co 3:6, Ga 3:21. Pass., I Co 15:22, 36, I Pe 3:18.†

strong.derivation: an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of G2228 (ἤ); used only (in the New Testament) before G3303 (μέν);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 5 ἦ (μήν), v.s. εἰ, iii, 7.

strong.derivation: neuter plural of the superlative of the same as G2234 (ἡδέως);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 ἥδιστα, v.s. ἡδέως.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἦθος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in LXX: Si, prol.:27 20:26(25), IV Mac 1:29 2:7, 21 5:24 13:27*;]
1. 1, a haunt, abode.
2. = ἔθος, custom, manner: pl., I Co 15:33.†

strong.derivation: of Hebrew origin (H0410 with pronominal suffix);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἡλεί (Rec. ἠλί, L, ἡλί; Heb. אֵלִי),
Eli, my God: Mt 27:46 (cf. ἐλωΐ).†

strong.derivation: from (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age);
strong.def: as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἡλίκος, -η, -ον,
1. prop., as big as, as old as.
2. As indirect interrog., what sized, what, how great, how small (the sense to be determined by the context): Col 2:1, Ja 3:5, Ga 6:11 (WH, mg.; πηλ-, WH, txt., RV).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἧλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Is 41:7 (מַסְמְרִים) etc.;]
a nail: Jo 20:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἡμέτερος, -α, -ον (ἡμεῖς), poss. pron. of first pers.,
our: Ac 2:11 24:6 26:5, Ro 15:4, II Ti 4:15, I Jo 1:3 2:2; τὸ ἡ., Lk 16:12, WH, txt., R, mg. (τὸ ὑμ., Rec., WH, mg., R, txt.); οἱ ἡ., our (people), Tit 3:14.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G2255 (ἥμισυ) and G5610 (ὥρα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἡμίωρον (Rec. -ιον), -ου, τό (ἥμι, half + ὥρα),
half an hour: Re 8:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἡνίκα, rel. adv. of time,
at which time, when; seq. ἂν, c. subjc., whensoever: II Co 3:15, 16.†

strong.def: than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἤπερ, v.s. ἤ.

strong.def: properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἤπιος, -α, -ον,
mild, gentle: I Th 2:7 (WH, R, mg., νήπιος); seq. πρός, II Ti 2:24.†

strong.derivation: perhaps by transposition from G2048 (ἔρημος) (through the idea of stillness);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἤρεμος, -ον, [in LXX: Es 3:13 A*;]
quiet, tranquil (Luc., al.): I Ti 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἡρῳδίων (Rec. Ἡρω-), -ωνος, ὁ,
Herodion: Ro 16:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἠσαῦ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. עֵשָׂו, Ge 25:25),
Esau: Ro 9:13(LXX), He 11:20 12:16.†

strong.def: (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἡσυχία, -ας, ἡ (< ἡσύχιος, q.v.), [in LXX for אִישׁוֹן, שָׁלֶו, etc.;]
1. quietness: II Th 3:12.
2. stillness, silence: Ac 22:2, I Ti 2:11, 12.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος) and perhaps G2192 (ἔχω);
strong.def: properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἡσύχιος, -α, -ον (= the more freq. ἥσυχος; cf. Wi 18:14, Si 25:20), [in LXX: Is 66:2 (נְכֵה־רוּחַ)*;]
quiet, tranquil: I Ti 2:2, I Pe 3:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἤτοι disjunct. part.,
whether: Ro 6:16.†

strong.def: to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἡττάω, -ῶ (ἡσσ-, II Co 12:13, v.s. ἥσσων), [in LXX for חתת, etc.;] pass.,
1. to be inferior: seq. ὑπέρ, II Co 12:13.
2. to be overcome: absol., II Pe 2:20; c. dat., II Pe 2:19.†

strong.def: a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἥττημα, -τος, τό, [in LXX for מַס, Is 31:9(8)*;]
defect, loss, defeat: Ro 11:12 (cf. Is 31:9(8), I Co 6:7 (cf. Field, Notes, 160 f., 171 f.; Lft., Notes, 212).†

strong.derivation: neuter of comparative of (slightly) used for that of G2556 (κακός);
strong.def: worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) ἥσσων (Rec. ἥττ-, the Attic literary form), ἧσσον,
inferior, less; neut., τὸ ἧ., adverbially, less: II Co 12:15; εἰς τὸ ἧ., for the worse (opp. to κρεῖττον): I Co 11:17.†

strong.derivation: third person singular imperative of G1510 (εἰμί);

strong.def: to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἠχέω, -ῶ (< ἦχος), [in LXX for המה, etc.;]
to sound: I Co 13:1 (cf. ἐξ-, κατ-ηχέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 θάλπω, [in LXX for סכן, etc.;]
to heat, warm; metaph.,
(a). to inflame (Trag.);
(b). to foster, cherish: Eph 5:29, I Th 2:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Θάμαρ (Tr., Θαμάρ), ἡ (Heb. תָּמָר, Ge 38:6),
Tamar: Mt 1:3.†

strong.derivation: from (the feminine form of) G2288 (θάνατος) and G5342 (φέρω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θανατη-φόρος, -ον (< θάνατος, φέρω), [in LXX: Nu 18:22 (מוּת), Jb 33:23, IV Mac 8:18, 26 15:26*;]
deadly, death-bringing: Ja 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θάρσος, -ους, τό,
courage: Ac 28:15.†

strong.derivation: apparently from a form of G2300 (θεάομαι);
strong.def: wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 θαῦμα, -τος, τό, [in LXX: Jb 17:8 18:20 20:8 21:5 (שַׂעַר, etc.)*;]
1. a wonder: II Co 11:14.
2. wonder: Re 17:6.†

strong.def: wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θαυμάσιος, -α, -ον (< θαῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for פּלא ni. (n. pl. = נִפְלָאוֹת);]
wonderful; n. pl., wonders: Mt 21:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * θεά, -ᾶς, ἡ (fem. of θεός, q.v.),
a goddess: Ac 19:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θεατρίζω (< θέατρον),
to make a spectacle of, expose to contempt (eccl.; ἐκθ-, Polyb.): pass., He 10:33.†

strong.def: a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * θέατρον, -ον, τό (< θεάομαι),
1. a theatre (used also as a place of assembly): Ac 19:29, 31.
2. Collective for οἱ θεαταί, the spectators.
3. = θέα, θέαμα, a spectacle, show: metaph., I Co 4:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 θεῖος, -εία, -εῖον (< θεός), [in LXX: Ex 31:3 35:31, Jb 27:3 33:4, Pr 2:17 (אֵל, אֱלוֹהַּ, אֱלֹהִים), Si 6:35, II Ma3, III Mac1, IV Mac25*;]
divine: δύναμις, II Pe 1:3; φύσις (for parallel in π., v. MM, Exp., xv), II Pe 1:4; τὸ θ., the Deity (so in cl.; of God, in Philo and FlJ), Ac 17:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† θειότης, -ητος, ἡ (< θεῖος) [in LXX: Wi 18:9*;]
divine nature, divinity: Ro 1:20 (for ex. from π., v. MM, Exp., xv).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θειώδης, -ες (< θεῖον),
of brimstone, sulphureous: Re 9:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † θέλησις, -εως, ἡ (θέλω), [in LXX: II Ch 15:15, Pr 8:35 (רָצוֹן), Ez 18:23 (חֵפֶץ), Da LXX 11:45 (צְבִי), To 12:18, Wi 16:25, II Mac 12:16, III Mac 2:26*;]
in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, will: He 2:4.†

strong.def: to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 θεμελιόω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for יסד;]
to lay the foundation of, to found: c. acc., τ. γῆν, He 1:10(LXX); pass., Mt 7:25, Lk 6:48; metaph., I Pe 5:10 (R, mg., settle); pass., Eph 3:18, Col 1:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θεο-δίδακτος, -ον,
taught of God (cf. διδακτοὶ θεοῦ, Jo 6:45): I Th 4:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† θεομάχος, -ον, [in Sm.: Jb 26:5, Pr 9:18 21:16*;]
fighting against God: Ac 5:39.†

strong.derivation: from G2316 (θεός) and a presumed derivative of G4154 (πνέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θεόπνευστος, -ον (< θεός, πνέω),
inspired by God: II Ti 3:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ (< θεοσεβής), [in LXX: Ge 20:11 (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאַה), Jb 28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Si 1:24, Ba 5:4, IV Mac 7:6, 22, א IV Mac 15:28 א IV Mac 17:15*;]
fear of God, godliness: I Ti 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θεοσεβής, -ές (< θεός, σέβομαι), [in LXX for אֱלֹהִים יְרֵא, Ex 18:21, al.;]
God-fearing, godly: Jo 9:31.†

strong.derivation: from G2316 (θεός) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * θεοστυγής, -ές (< θεός, στυγέω),
1. passive, as freq. in cl., hateful to God: Ro 1:30 (R, txt., cf. Lit., Notes, 256).
2. Active, hating God: Ro 1:30 (R, mg., cf. ICC, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † θεότης, -ητος, ἡ,
deity, Godhead: Col 2:9†

strong.derivation: apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of G2330 (θέρος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θεράπων, -οντος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד;]
an attendant, servant: He 3:5(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** θεριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (< θερίζω), [in LXX: Da LXX Bel32, TH Bel33*;]
a reaper: Mt 13:30, 39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θέρμη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Jb 6:17, Ps 18(19):6, Ec 4:11 (חמם and derivatives), Si 38:28*;]
heat: Ac 28:3.†

strong.def: a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 θεσσαλονικεύς, -έως, ὁ,
a Thessalonian: Ac 20:4 27:2, I Th 1:1, II Th 1:1.†

strong.def: Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 θεσσαλονίκη, -ης, ἡ,
Thessalonica, a city of Macedonia: Ac 17:1, 11, 13, Phl 4:16, II Ti 4:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Θευδᾶς (perh. contr. from Θεόδωρος, but v. MM, Exp., xv), -ᾶ, ὁ,
Theudas: Ac 5:36.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θήκη, -ης, ἡ (< τίθημι), [in LXX: Ex 25:26(27) (בַּיִת), Is 6:13 (מַצֶּבֶת) Is 3:26*;]
a receptacle, chest, case: of the sheath of a sword, Jo 18:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θήρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX for צַיִד, טֶרֶף, רֶשֶׁת, and cogn. forms;]
1. a hunting, chase (Hdt., Xen., al.).
2. prey, game (cl.).
3. As in Ps 34(35:8) = רֶשֶׁת, a net: Ro 11:9 (but v. Thayer, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2342 (θηρίον) and G3164 (μάχομαι);
strong.def: to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θηριομαχέω, -ῶ (< θηρίον, μάχομαι),
to fight with wild beasts (Diod., al.): I Co 15:32.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (to finger);
strong.def: to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 θιγγάνω, [in LXX for נגע, Ex 19:12*;]
1. to touch, handle: Col 2:21, He 12:20(LXX).
2. to injure (like Heb. נגע, and as in Eur., Iph. Aul., 1351): c. gen., He 11:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 θνητός, -ή, -όν (< θνήσκω), [in LXX: Pr 3:13 20:24 (אָדָם), Jb 30:23 (חַי), Is 51:12 (מוּת), Wi 9:14 15:17, II Mac 9:12, III Mac 3:29*;]
subject to death, mortal: Ro 6:12 8:11, I Co 15:53, 54, II Co 4:11 5:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * θρέμμα, -τος, τό (τρέφω);
1. a nurseling, esp. of animals (Eur., Plat., al.).
2. cattle: Jo 4:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† θρησκεία (-κία, T), -ας, ἡ (< θρῆσκος), [in LXX: Wi 14:18, 27, Si 22:5 A, IV Mac 5:6, 13*;]
religion in its external aspect (MM, Exp., xv), worship: Ac 26:5, Ja 1:26, 27; θ. τῶν ἀγγέλων, Col 2:18.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G2360 (θροέω);
strong.def: ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * θρῆσκος (-κός, WH), -ου, ὁ
religious, careful of the outward forms of divine service (see previous word): Ja 1:26.†

strong.derivation: from a prolonged compound of the base of G2360 (θροέω);
strong.def: and a derivative of G680 (ἅπτομαι) (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† θριαμβεύω (< θρίαμβος, 1. a festal hymn to Bacchus. 2. The Roman triumphus),
1. to triumph (and rarely, c. acc., to triumph over; so perh. Col 2:15, but v. infr.).
2. to lead in triumph: c. acc. pers., II Co 2:14; hence, generally, to make a spectacle or show of: Col 2:15 (but v. supr.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; and esp. Field, Notes, 181).†

strong.def: Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 Θυάτειρα, -ων, τά (-ας, ἡ, Re 1:11 L; cf. WH, App., 156),
Thyatira, a city of Lydia: Ac 16:14, Re 1:11 2:18, 24.†

strong.derivation: from G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing) a storm

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θύελλα, -ης, ἡ (< θύω), [in LXX De 4:11 5:22 (19) (עֲרָפֶל), Ex 10:22*;] (poët. in cl.),
a hurricane, cyclone, whirlwind: He 12:18.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing;
strong.def: denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† θύινος (usually θύϊνος, as Rec.), -η, -ον (< θυία, θύα, an African aromatic tree, with ornamentally veined wood of varying colour, = Lat. citrinus), [in Sm.: III Ki 10:11 (אַלְמֻגִּים)*;]
thyine: ξύλον, Re 18:12 (Diosc.).†

strong.def: a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θυμιατήριον, -ου, τό (< θυμιάω), [in LXX: II Ch 26:19, Ez 8:11 (מִקְטֶרֶת), IV Mac 7:11*;]
1. as in cl. (Hdt., iv, 162; Thuc., vi, 46) and LXX, a censer: He 9:4 (but v. infr., and cf. Westc., in l.).
2. As in Philo., rer. div., § 46, FlJ, Ant., iv, 2, 4, al., the altar of incense: He 9:4 (but v. supr. and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G2372 (θυμός) and G3164 (μάχομαι);
strong.def: to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† θυμομαχέω, -ῶ (θυμός, μάχομαι),
to fight desperately, have a hot quarrel: c. dat. pers., Ac 12:20.†

strong.def: to put in a passion, i.e. enrage

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θυμόω, -ῶ (θυμός), [in LXX (chiefly in pass.) for חרה, אף חרה, אָנֵף hith., etc.;] (no act. in Attic.);
to be wroth or very angry: Mt 2:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θυρεός, -οῦ, ὁ (< θύρα), [in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה;]
1. in Hom., a door-stone.
2. In late Gk. (Polyb., Plut.), the scutum, a large oblong shield: θ. τ. πίστεως, Eph 6:16 (cf. Wi 5:20, where ὁσιότης is likened to the ἀσπίς, the clypeus or small round shield of the light-armed soldier).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 θυρίς, -ίδος, ἡ (dim. of θύρα), [in LXX chiefly for חַלּוֹן;]
a window: Ac 20:9, II Co 11:33.†

strong.def: the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 θώραξ, -ακσς, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for שִׁרְיוֹן and cogn. forms;]
a breastplate: Re 9:9, 17; θ. τ. δικαιοσύνης, Eph 6:14 (cf. Is 59:17, Wi 5:18(19)); θ. πίστεως, I Th 5:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἴαμα, -τος, τό (< ἰάομαι), [in LXX for מַרְפֵּא (II Ch 36:16, Ec 10:4, Je 40 (33):6), etc.;]
1. most freq. in cl., a means of healing, remedy (Thuc., al.; Wi 11:4 10:9).
2. = ἴασις (q.v.), a healing (Plat.; Je 40 (33):6): pl., I Co 12:9, 28, 30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰαμβρῆς, ὁ,
Jambres (cf. Ex 7:11, 12): II Ti 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰαννῆς, ὁ,
Jannes (cf. Ἰαμβρῆς): II Ti 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἴασπις, -ιδος, ἡ, [in LXX: Ex 28:18 36:18 (39:11) (יַהֲלֹם), Is 54:12 (כַּדְכֹּד), Ez 28:13 (יָשְׁפֵה, v. BDB, Lex., s.v.)*;]
jasper, apparently not the modern stone of that name, but a translucent stone (DB, s.v.): Re 4:3 21:11, 18, 19.†

strong.derivation: future active participle masculine of G2390 (ἰάομαι);
strong.def: about to cure; Jason, a Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Ἰάσων, -ονος, ὁ,
Jason: Ac 17:5-7, 9; perhaps the same, Ro 16:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 ἰδέα, -ας, ἡ, v.s. εἰδέα.

strong.def: a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἰδιώτης, -ου, ὁ (< ἴδιος), [in LXX: Pr 6:8 (no Heb.)*;]
1. a private person, as opp. to the State or an official (βασιλεῖς κ. ἰδιῶται, Pr 6:8; and cf. MM, Exp., xv).
2. one without professional knowledge, unskilled, uneducated, unlearned: I Co 14:16, 23, 24 (R, mg., without gifts); ἀγράμματοι κ. ἰ., Ac 4:13; c. dat. (= cl. c. gen. rei), λόγῳ, II Co 11:6.†

strong.def: Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἰεζάβελ (L, Ἰεζ-; Tr. -βέλ; Rec. -βήλ) ἡ, indecl. (Heb. אִיזֶבֶל; LXX as txt.; FlJ, Ἰεζαβέλη),
Jezebel (III Ki 16:31, al.): symbolically, Re 2:20 (v. Swete, in l.).†

strong.def: holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἱεράπολις (WH, Ἱερὰ Πόλις), -εως, ἡ,
Hierapolis: a city in the Lycus valley in the Province of Asia: Col 4:13.†

strong.def: the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἱεράτευμα, -τος, τό (< ἱερατεύω), [in LXX: βασίλειον ἱ., Ex 19:6 (כֹּהֲנִים מַמְלֶכֶת) 23:22, II Mac 2:17*;]
a priesthood, body of priests: ἱ ἅγιον, I Pe 2:5; βασ. ἱ, I Pe 2:9 (LXX, Ex 19:6).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
