(b). as to excellence: He 1:4 6:9 7:7, 19, 22 8:6 9:23 10:34 11:16, 35; κ. ἐστι, seq. inf., I Pe 3:17.†

strong.def: a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Κρής, ὁ, pl., Κρῆτες,
a Cretan: Ac 2:11, Tit 1:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κρήσκης, -εντος (Bl., § 10, 4), ὁ (Lat.),
Crescens: II Ti 4:10.†

strong.def: Crete, an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Κρήτη, -ης, ἡ,
Crete: Ac 27:7, 12, 13, 31, Tit 1:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κριθή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX for שְׂעֹרָה;]
barley: pl. (as usually in cl.), Re 6:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κρίθινος, -η, -ον (< κριθή), [in LXX for שְׂעֹרָה;]
of barley: Jo 6:9, 13.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Κρίσπος, -ου, ὁ,
Crispus: Ac 18:8, I Co 1:14.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2923 (κριτής);
strong.def: a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κριτήριον, -ου, τό (< κριτής), [in LXX: III Ki 7:7 (מִשְׁפָּט), Da LXX TH 7:10, TH:26, (דִּין), Su 49, Ex 21:6, Jg 5:10*;]
1. a means of judging, test, criterion.
2. a tribunal: I Co 6:2, 4, Ja 2:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κριτικός, -ή, -όν (< κρίνω),
critical, able to discern or judge: c. gen. obj., He 4:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† κρυσταλλίζω (< κρύσταλλος),
to shine like crystal, be crystal-clear: Re 21:11 (ἅπ. λεγ.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κρύσταλλος, -ου, ὁ (< κρύος, frost), [in LXX: Jb 38:29, Ps 147:6, (17), Ez 1:22 (קֶרַח), etc.;]
crystal: Re 4:6 22:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κρυφῇ (prop. -ῆ, Rec.; later spelling is due to assimilation to dat.; cf. εἰκῆ), adv., [in LXX chiefly for סתר;]
secretly, in secret: Eph 5:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κτήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (κτάομαι), [in Sm.: Jl 1:11*;]
a possessor: Ac 4:34.†

strong.def: an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** κτίσμα, -τος, τό (< κτίζω), [in LXX: Wi 9:2 13:5 14:11, Si 36:20 (17), 38:34, III Mac 5:11*;]
1. (cl.) a colony.
2. a created thing, creature: I Ti 4:4, Ja 1:18, Re 5:13 8:9.†

strong.def: a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κτίστης, -ου, ὁ (< κτίζω), [in LXX: II Ki 22:32 (Heb., al.), Jth 9:12, Si 24:8, II, IV Mac5*;]
1. (cl.) a founder.
2. a creator: of God, I Pe 4:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κυβία (Att. -εία, and so Rec.), -ας, ἡ (< κύβος, a cube, a die),
dice-playing; metaph., trickery, sleight: Eph 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κυβέρνησις, -εως, ἡ (< κυβερνάω, Lat. gubernare, to guide), [in LXX: Pr 1:5 11:14 24:6 (תַּחְבֻּלוֹת)*;]
1. steering, pilotage (Plat.).
2. Metaph., government: pl., I Co 12:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κυβερνήτης, -ου, ὁ (v.s. κυβέρνησις), [in LXX for חֹבֵל, Ez 27:8, 27, 28, Pr 23:24, IV Mac 7:1*;]
1. a steersman, pilot: Ac 27:11, Re 18:17.
2. Metaph., a guide, governor (Eur., Plat.).†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G2945 (κύκλῳ);
strong.def: from the circle, i.e. all around

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 κυκλόθεν, adv., (< κύκλος), [in LXX chiefly for מִסָּבִיב, סָבִיב;]
from all sides, round about: Re 4:3, 4, 8.†

strong.def: a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† κύλισμα, -τος, τό (< κυλίω), [in Sm.: Ez 10:13*;]
1. a roll.
2. = κυλισμός (q.v.), a rolling, wallowing (or, as κυλίστρα, Xen., Eq., v. 3, a rolling place): II Pe 2:22 (Rec.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G2949 (κῦμα);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κύμβαλον, -ου, τό (< κύμβη, a cup), [in LXX chiefly for מְצֵלֶת;]
a cymbal: I Co 13:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κύμινον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: Is 28:25, 27 (כַּמֹּן)*;]
cummin: Mt 23:23.†

strong.def: a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Κύπριος, -α, -ον,
of Cyprus, Cyprian: Ac 4:36 11:20 21:16.†

strong.def: Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Κύπρος, -ου, ἡ,
Cyprus: Ac 11:19 13:4 15:39 21:3 27:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κυρήνη, -ης, ἡ,
Cyrene, a city in Libya: Ac 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κυρία (Κυρία, T, WH, mg.), -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for גְּבֶרֶת;]
a lady: II Jo 1, 5 (on the interpretation, v. ICC, 167 ff.).†

strong.def: belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† κυριακός, -ή, -όν (< κύριος), [in LXX: κ. φωνή (Συριακή φ., R), II Mac 15:36 A*;]
1. as freq. in Inscr. (LS, s.v.; Deiss., BS, 217 f.), of the lord or master, imperial.
2. of the Lord (i.e. Christ): δεῖπνον, I Co 11:20; ἡμέρα, Re 1:10. (Cf. λόγια κ., Papias, Eus., HE, iii, 39, 1; γραφαὶ κ., Clem. Alex., etc; for eccl. usage, cf. Soph., Lex., s.v.)†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† κυριότης, -ητος, ἡ (< κύριος),
lordship, dominion: Eph 1:21, II Pe 2:10, Ju 8; pl., Col 1:16 (cf. Lft., Col 1:16; Mayor, Ju 8; DB, i, 616 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 κυρόω, -ῶ (< κῦρος, 1. authority. 2. validity), [in LXX for קום;]
to confirm, ratify, make valid: II Co 2:8; pass., Ga 3:15 (cf. προ-κυρόω).†

strong.def: a limb of the body (as if lopped)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κῶλον, -ου, τό,
a limb, member of a body, [but in LXX (Le 26:30, Nu 14:29, 32, 33, I Ki 17:46, Is 66:24*) for פֶּגֶר;] hence, carcase: He 3:17(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** κῶμος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Wi 14:23, II Mac 6:4*;]
a revel, carousal: Ro 13:13, Ga 5:21, I Pe 4:3.†

strong.derivation: apparently a derivative of the base of G2759 (κέντρον) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * κώνωψ, -ωπος, ὁ,
a gnat: Mt 23:24.†

strong.def: Cos, an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) Κῶς, gen. Κῶ, ἡ,
Cos, an island in the Ægean Sea: acc. Κῶ, Ac 21:1 (Κῶν, Rec.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 λάθρᾳ (Att.; in Hom., -ρῃ, Rec. -ρα), adv., [in LXX chiefly for ‎בַּסֵּתֶר;]
secretly: Mt 1:19 2:7, Mk 5:33 (WH, mg.), Jo 11:28, Ac 16:37.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * λακτίζω (< λάξ, with the foot),
to kick: Ac 26:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 λαμπάς, -άδος, ἡ (< λάμπω), [in LXX for לַפִּיד;]
a torch (freq. fed, like a lamp, with oil): Mt 25:1 ff., Jo 18:3, Ac 20:8, Re 4:5 8:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λαμπρότης, -ητος, ἡ, [in LXX: Ps 109 (110):3 (הָדָר), al.;]
brightness, brilliancy: τ. ἡλίου, Ac 26:13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G2992 (λαός) and G1349 (δίκη);
strong.def: Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Λαοδικία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ,
Laodicea, a city on the Lycus in Phrygia: Col 2:1 4:13, 15, 16, Re 1:11 3:14.†

strong.def: a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λαοδικεύς, -έως, ὁ,
a Laodicean: Col 4:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λάρυγξ, -γγος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for חֵךְ, Jb 6:30, al; Ps 5:9 (גָּרוֹן);]
the larynx, throat: metaph., of speech (cf. Si 6:5), Ro 3:13(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λασέα (Rec. -αία), -ας, ἡ,
Lasea, a city of Crete, otherwise unknown: Ac 27:8.†

strong.derivation: a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) * λάσκω,
1. (in cl., poët.) to clang, crash, crack; in late prose, to crack or burst noisily: Ac 1:18 (ἐλάκησεν, perh., however, from λακέω, q.v.; Bl., in l.).
2. (in cl., prose) to scream, shout.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 λατρεία, -ας, ἡ (< λατρεύω, q.v.), [in LXX (always of divine service): Ex 12:25, 26 13:5, Jos 22:27, I Ch 28:13 (עֲבֹדָה), I Mac 1:43 2:19, 22, III Mac 4:14*;]
1. hired service, service.
2. (in cl. also) divine service, worship: Jo 16:2, Ro 9:4 12:1, He 9:1, 6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λεῖμμα (WH, λίμμα, v. their App., 154), -τος, τό (< λείπω), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:4 A (שְׁאֵרִית)*;]
a remnant: Ro 11:5.†

strong.def: to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 λειτουργέω, -ῶ (< λειτουργός), [in LXX chiefly for שׁרת pi., also for עבד, צבא, etc.;]
1. in cl., at Athens, to supply public offices at one's own cost, render public service to the State, hence, generally,
2. to serve the State, do a service, serve (of service to the Gods, Diod., i, 21): of the official service of priests and Levites (Ex 29:30, Nu 16:9, Si 4:14, I Mac 10:42, al.; cf. Deiss., BS, 140 f.), He 10:11; of Christians: c. dat. pers. seq. ἐν, Ro 15:27 (cf. Si 10:25); τ. κυρίῳ, Ac 13:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † λειτουργικός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX for עֲבֹדָה, שָׁרֵת; ἔργα, Nu 7:5; στολαί, Ex 31:9 (10) 39:13 (1); σκευή, Nu 4:12, 26, II Ch 24:14*;]
of or for service, ministering: πνεύματα, He 1:14.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G2992 (λαός) and G2041 (ἔργον);
strong.def: a public servant, i.e. a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 λειτουργός, -οῦ, ὁ (< λιός, ἔργον), [in LXX chiefly for מְשָׁרֵת, Jos 1:1 A, III Ki 10:5, Ps 102 (103):21, Si 7:30, al.;]
1. in cl., one who discharges a public office at his own expense, then, generally,
2. a public servant, a minister, servant: τ. ἁγίων λ., He 8:2 (cf. Ne 10:39, Si 7:30); Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Ro 15:16; pl., τ. θεοῦ, Ro 13:6, He 1:7(LXX); λ. ὑμῶν τ. χρείας μου, Phl 2:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† λέντιον, -ου, τό (Lat. linteum),
a linen cloth, towel: Jo 13:4, 5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λεπίς, -ίδος, ἡ (< λέπω, to peel) [in LXX chiefly for קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת;]
a scale: Ac 9:18.†

strong.def: Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λευειτικός (Rec. Λευϊτ-), -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Le, tit.*;]
Levitical: He 7:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 λέων, -οντος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for אֲרִי, אַרְיֵה, also for כְּפִיר, etc.;]
a lion: He 11:33, I Pe 5:8, Re 4:7 9:8, 17 10:3 13:2; metaph., II Ti 4:17, Re 5:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λήθη, -ης, ἡ (< λήθω = λανθάνω), [in LXX: Le 5:15 (מַעַל), Wi 16:11, Si 14:7, al.;]
forgetfulness: λ. λαβεῖν (on the phrase, v. Mayor, in l.): II Pe 1:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ληνός, -οῦ, ἡ (in some MSS., LXX and NT, ὁ), [in LXX chiefly for יֶקֶב, Nu 18:27, al.; also for רַהַט (Ge 30:38, 41), גַּת (Ne 13:15, al.), etc.;]
a trough or vat; esp. for the treading of grapes: Mt 21:33, Re 14:20 19:16; τὴν λ. . . . τὸν μέγαν (a solecism perhaps inadvertent), Re 14:19 (cf. ὑπολήνιον).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λῆμψις (Rec. λῆψις, so in cl.), -εως, ἡ (< λαμβάνω), [in LXX (λῆψ-): Pr 15:29 (16:8); λ. δώρων, Pr 15:27 (מַתָּנָה); λ. καὶ δόσις, Si 41:19 42:7*;]
receiving: δόσις καὶ λ., Phl 4:15.†

strong.def: the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λίβανος, -ου, ὁ (rarely ἡ), (from the Semitic; cf. the Heb. equiv.), [in LXX for לְבֹנָה Ex 30:34, Is 60:6, Si 24:15, al.;]
1. in cl., the frankincense-tree.
2. (Occas. in cl.) frankincense (so Le 2:1; cf. λιβανωτός): Mt 2:11, Re 18:13.†

strong.def: frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λιβανωτός, -οῦ, ὁ (< λίβανος), [in LXX: I Ch 9:29, (לְבֹנָה), III Mac 5:2*;]
1. in cl. (and LXX), frankincense, the gum of the libanus.
2. = Late Gk., λιβανωτρίς, a censer: Re 8:3, 5 (the same form appears in Inscr.; MM, xvi).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λιβερτῖνος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. libertinus),
a freedman: ἡ συναγωγὴ ἡ λεγομένη Λιβερτίνων, Ac 6:9 (Bl. thinks the original reading was Λιβυστίνων, Phil. Gosp., 69 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λιβύη, -ης, ἡ,
Libya: Ac 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 λιθάζω (< λίθος), [in LXX (seq. ἐν λίθοις): II Ki 16:6, 13 (סקל pi.)*;]
1. to throw stones (Arist., Polyb., al.).
2. = λιθοβολέω (LXX, NT), to pelt with stones, to stone: c. acc. pers., Jo 8:[5] 10:31-33 11:8, Ac 14:10; pass., Ac 5:26, II Co 11:25, He 11:37 (v. DB, Art., "Crimes and punishments," and cf. κατα-λιθάζω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 λίθινος, -η, -ον (λίθος), [in LXX for אֶבֶן;]
of stone: Jo 2:6, II Co 3:3, Re 9:20.†

strong.derivation: from G3037 (λίθος) and a derivative of G4766 (στρώννυμι);
strong.def: stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λιθό-στρωτος, -ον (< στρώννυμι), [in LXX: II Ch 7:3, Es 1:6, Ca 3:10 (רִצְפָּה, רָצַף)*;]
paved with stones, esp. of tessallated work (Ca 3:10); as subst., τὸ λ., a tessallated pavement: Jo 19:13 (cf. Γαββαθᾶ).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λιμήν, -ένος, ὁ, [in LXX: Ps 106 (107):30 (מָחוֹז), Ps 106 (107):35, I Es 5:55, I, II, IV Mac7*;]
a harbour, haven: Ac 27:8, 12 (cf. Καλοὶ Λιμένες).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λίνον (Tr. λῖνον), -ου, τό, [in LXX: Ex 9:31 (פִּשְׁתָּה), al.;]
1. flax: Mt 12:20(LXX).
2. linen: Re 15:6 (R, mg., v.s. λίθος).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λίνος (Rec. Λῖνος), ου, ὁ,
Linus: II Ti 4:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λιπαρός, -ά, -όν (< λίπος, fat), [in LXX: Jg 3:29, Ne 9:35, Is 30:23 (שָׁמֵן)*;]
oily, fatty; metaph., of living, rich, dainty: τὰ λ. καὶ τ. λαμπρά, Re 18:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† λίτρα, -ας, ἡ (cf. Lat. libra),
1. a Sicilian coin = Rom. libra or as.
2. In weight, a pound: Jo 12:3 19:39.†

strong.def: the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λίψ, λιβός, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for תֵּימָן, מַעֲרָבָה, etc., Ge 13:14, Nu 2:10, II Ch 32:30, al.;]
the SW. wind: βλέποντα κατὰ λ., Ac 27:12 (v. Page, in l.; Deiss., BS, 141).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 λογεία, v.s. λογία.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * λογικός, -ή, -όν (< λόγος, reason),
reasonable, rational: λατρεία, Ro 12:1; τὸ λ. (i.e. spiritual) γάλα (v. Hort, in l.; MM, xvi), I Pe 2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, v. ICC, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 λόγιον, -ου, τό (dimin. of λόγος, v. ICC, Ro., 70), [in LXX chiefly for אִמְרָה, אֵמֶר, Ps 17 (18):30 18 (19):14, al.; also for דָּבָר, Is 28:13, al.; (cf. λογεῖον (-ιον), for חֹשֶׁן, the oracular breastplate of the H.P., Ex 28:15, al.);]
an oracle: Ac 7:38, Ro 3:2, He 5:12, I Pe 4:11 (on the eccl., λόγια τ. Κυρίου, v. Lft., Essay on Sup. Rel., 172 ff.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * λόγιος, -ον (< λόγος),
1. in cl., learned (Ac 18:24, R, txt.).
2. In late Gk., eloquent: Ac 18:24 (v. Page, in l.; Field, Notes, 129).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λογισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< λογίζομαι), [in LXX: Ps 32 (33):10, 11, Pr 19:21, Is 66:18, al. (מַחֲשֶׁבֶת);]
a reasoning, thought: Ro 2:15, II Co 10:5.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3056 (λόγος) and G3164 (μάχομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† λογομαχέω, -ῶ (< λόγος, μάχομαι),
to strive with words: II Ti 2:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† λογομαχία, -ας, ἡ (< λογομαχέω),
a strife of words: pl., I Ti 6:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λόγχη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for רֹמַח, etc.;]
1. a spear-head.
2. a lance, spear: Mt 27:49 (|[WH]|, R, mg.), Jo 19:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 λοιδορέω, -ῶ (< λοίδορος), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב;]
to abuse, revile: c. acc. pers., Jo 9:28, Ac 23:4; pass., I Co 4:12, I Pe 2:23 (cf. ἀντι-λοιδορέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 λοιδορία, -ας, ἡ (< λοιδορέω), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב, מְרִיבָה;]
abuse, railing: I Ti 5:14, I Pe 3:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λοίδορος, -ον, [in LXX: Pr 25:24 26:21 27:15 (מִדְיָן) Si 23:8*;]
railing, abusive; as subst., ὁ λ., a railer: I Co 5:11 6:10.†

strong.derivation: genitive case singular of the same as G3062 (λοιποί);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
55 λοιπός, -ή, -όν (< λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יֶתֶר, also for שְׁאָר, etc.;]
the remaining, the rest,
1. pl., οἱ λ.: c. subst., Mt 25:11, Ac 2:37, Ro 1:13, al.; absol., Mt 22:6, Mk 16:[13], Lk 24:10, al.; οἱ λ. οἱ (Bl., § 47, 8), Ac 28:9, I Th 4:13, Re 2:24; οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων (LS, s.v., ad. init.), Re 9:20; τὰ λ., Mk 4:19, Re 3:2, al.
2. Neut. sing. (acc. ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.;
(a). for the future, henceforth: Mk 14:41, I Co 7:29 (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), He 10:13; anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), Ac 27:20, II Ti 4:8; τοῦ λ. (sc. χρόνου; LS, s.v.; M, Pr., 73; Bl., § 36, 13), Ga 6:17, Eph 6:10;
(b). besides, moreover, for the rest: Phl 3:1 4:8; anarth., I Co 1:16 4:2, I Th 4:1 (M, Th., in l; Lft., Notes, 51).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Λουκᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (prob. an abbreviation of Λουκανός; v. Lft., Col., 240; ICC, Lk., xviii; Bl., § 29; acc. to Ramsay, Exp., Dec., 1912, pp. 502 ff., a by-form of Λούκιος, from Lat. Lucius),
Luke: Lk, tit., Col 4:14, II Ti 4:11, Phm 24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λούκιος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Lucius),
Lucius: Ac 13:1, Ro 16:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 λουτρόν, -οῦ, τό (< λούω), [in LXX: Ca 4:2 6:5, (6) (רַחְצָה), Si 31 (34):25*;]
a washing, bath: τ. ὕδατος, Eph 5:26; τ. παλιγγενεσίας, Tit 3:5 (v. AR, Eph. 5:26).†

strong.def: to bathe (the whole person; whereas G3538 (νίπτω) means to wet a part only, and G4150 (πλύνω) to wash, cleanse garments exclusively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 λούω, [in LXX chiefly for רחץ (freq. of ceremonial washing; cf. Deiss., BS, 226 f.);]
to bathe, wash the body: c. acc. pers., Ac 9:37 (of a dead body); id. seq. ἀπό (Deiss., BS, 226 f.), Ac 16:33; pass. ptcp. pf., Jo 13:10, He 10:22; mid., to wash oneself (Mayor, in l.; M. Pr., 155 f., 238 f.), II Pe 2:22; metaph., Re 1:5, Rec., R, mg. (cf. ἀπο-λούω).†

strong.def: Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 λύδδα, -ας (Ac 9:38, -ης Rec.), ἡ and λύδδα, -ων, τά (Ac 9:32, 35; -αν, Rec.), (Heb. לֹד),
Lydda (modern Ludd): Ac 9:32, 35, 38.†

strong.derivation: properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Λυδία, -ας, ἡ,
Lydia, a woman of Thyatira: Ac 16:14, 40.†

strong.def: Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λυκαονία, -ας, ἡ,
Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor: Ac 14:6.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G3071 (Λυκαονία);
strong.def: Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λυκαονιστί, adv.,
in Lycaonian (speech): Ac 14:11.†

strong.def: Lycia, a province of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λυκία, -ας, ἡ,
Lydia, a region of Asia Minor; Ac 27:5.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a probably derivative of G3089 (λύω) (meaning filth);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λυμαίνομαι (< λύμη, outrage), [in LXX chiefly for שׁחת pi., hi., also for כִּרְסֵם, etc.;]
1. to outrage, maltreat: c. acc., Ac 8:3.
2. to corrupt, defile (Ez 16:25, Pr 23:8, IV Mac 18:8, al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Λυσίας, -ου, ὁ,
Lysias (Claudius L., Ac 23:26), Ac 24:[7], 22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λύσις, -εως, ἡ (< λύω), [in LXX: Ec 7:30 (8:1) (פֵּשֶׁר), Da LXX 12:8, Wi 8:8*;]
a loosing: of divorce, I Co 7:27.†

strong.def: Lystra, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 λύστρα, -ας, ἡ, and (in Ac 14:8 16:2, II Ti 3:11) -ων, τά (cf. Λύδδα),
Lystra, a city of Lycaonia: Ac 14:6, 8, 21 16:1, 2, II Ti 3:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 λυτρωτής, -οῦ, ὁ (< λυτρόω), [in LXX: of God, Ps 18 (19):14 77 (78):35 (גֹּאֵל)*;]
a redeemer, deliverer: Ac 7:35 (not found elsewhere).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Λωίς (Rec. Λωΐς), -ίδος, ἡ,
Lois: II Ti 1:5.†

strong.def: the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μαγδαλά (Aram. מַגְדְֺּלָא = Heb. מִגְדֹּל, which in Jos 15:37 B is rendered Μαγαδά),
Magdala: Mt 15:39 (Rec. for Μαγαδάν, q.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μαγία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (< μάγος),
1. the lore of the Magians (Plat.).
2. magic: pl., magic arts, sorceries: Ac 8:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μαγεύω (Eur., Plut., al.),
1. to be a Magus, or skilled in Magian lore.
2. to practise magic: Ac 8:9.†

strong.def: a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μάγος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for אַשָּׁף, Da LXX TH 2:2, 10, al. (cf. רַב־מָג chief magian, Je 39:3, 13);]
1. one of the Μάγοι, a Median tribe (Hdt).
2. a Magian, one of a sacred caste, originally Median, who seem to have conformed to the Persian religion, while retaining some of their old beliefs (v. DB, I vol., 565 f.; DB, iii, 203 ff.): Mt 2:1, 7, 16.
3. a wizard, sorcerer: Ac 13:6, 8 (cf. Wi 17:7, Ac 8:9, 11).†

strong.def: Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μαγώγ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מָגוֹג, Ge 10:2, Ex 38:2, al.),
Magog, associated with Gog: Re 20:8 (v. Swete, in l.).†

strong.def: Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μαδιάμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מִדְיָן),
Midian;
1. son of Abraham (Ge 25:2).
2. An Arabian tribe (Ge 36:35, Ps 82 (83):9, al).
3. γῆ Μ. (Heb. אֶרֶץ מִדְיָן), the land of Midian (Ex 2:15, al.): Ac 7:29.†

strong.def: intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† μαθητεύω (< μαθητής),
1. intrans. (as prop. vb. in -εύω, and so Plut., mor. 837 c. and elsew.), to be a disciple: c. dat., Mt 27:57 (Rec., WH, mg.).
2. Trans., to make a disciple: c. acc., Mt 28:19, Ac 14:21; pass., seq. dat., τ. Ἰησοῦ, Mt 27:57 (WH, R); τ. βασιλείᾳ, Mt 13:52.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μαθήτρια, -ας, ἡ (= μαθητρίς, fem, of μαθητής, q.v.),
a female disciple: Ac 9:36.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from a primary (to long for;
strong.def: through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 μαίνομαι, [in LXX: Je 32 (25):16 (הלל hith.) Je 36 (29):26 (שׁגע pu.), Wi 14:28, al.;]
1. to rage, be furious.
2. to rave, be mad: Jo 10:29, Ac 12:15 26:24, 25, I Co 14:23 (cf. ἐμ-μαίνομαι).†

strong.def: beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * μακαρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (μακαρίζω),
a declaration of blessedness, felicitation: Ro 4:6, 9, Ga 4:15 (Plat., Arist.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 Μακεδονία, -ας, ἡ,
Macedonia: Ac 16:9, 10, I Co 16:5, II Co 1:16, Phl 4:15, al.; M. καὶ Ἀχαία, Ac 19:21, Ro 15:26, I Th 1:7, 8.

strong.def: a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Μακεδών, -όνος, ὁ,
a Macedonian: Ac 16:9 19:29 27:2, II Co 9:2, 4.†

strong.def: a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μάκελλον, -ου, τό (Lat. macellum),
a meat-market: I Co 10:25 (v. Deiss., LAE, 274; MM, xvi).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 † μακροθυμία, -ας, ἡ (< μακρό-θυμος), [in LXX: Pr 25:15 (אַפַּיִם אֹרֶךְ), Je 15:15 (אַפַּיִם אֶרֶךְ) Is 57:15, Si 5:11, I Mac 8:4*;]
patience, longsuffering: of men, esp. in experiencing troubles and difficulties, Col 1:11, II Ti 3:10, He 6:12, Ja 5:10; of God's forbearance, Ro 2:4 9:22, II Co 6:6, Ga 5:22, Eph 4:2, Col 3:12, I Ti 1:16, II Ti 4:2, I Pe 3:20, II Pe 3:15.†

strong.derivation: adverb of a compound of G3117 (μακρός) and G2372 (θυμός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μακροθύμως, adv.,
with forbearance, patiently: Ac 26:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μακρο-χρόνιος, -ον (μακρός, χρόνος), [in LXX. μ. γίγνεσθαι, εἶναι (יָמִים הַאֲרִיךְ), Ex 20:12, De 4:40 5:16 17:20*;]
of long duration, longlived: Eph 6:3(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μαλακία -ας, ἡ (< μαλακός), [in LXX chiefly for חֳלִי, De 7:15 28:61, Is 38:9 53:3, al.;]
1. prop., softness, effeminacy (Hdt., Thuc., al.).
2. In NT, as in LXX, = ἀσθένεια, weakness, sickness: νόσος καὶ μ., Mt 4:23 9:35 10:1.†

strong.derivation: neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb (very);
strong.def: (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 12 μάλιστα, v.s. μάλα.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μάλχος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenistic form of Heb. מֶלֶךְ),
Malchus: Jo 18:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μάμμη, -ης, ἡ (onomatop.), [in LXX: IV Mac 16:9*;]
1. in cl., a child's name for mother.
2. In late Gk. (= cl., τήθη), a grandmother: (LXX, IV Mac 16:9), II Ti 1:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μαναήν, ὁ (Heb. מְנַחֵם),
Manaen: Ac 13:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Μανασσῆς, -ῆ, ὁ (Heb. מְנַשֶּׁה),
Manasseh;
1.
(a). the first-born son of Joseph;
(b). the tribe which bore his name: Re 7:6.
2. King of Judah: Mt 1:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μανία, -ας, ἡ (< μαίνομαι), [in LXX: Ho 9:7, 8 מַשְׂטֵמָה), Wi 5:4, al.;]
frenzy, madness: Ac 26:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μάννα, τό, (in FlJ, also ἡ), indecl. [in LXX: τὸ μάν, Ex 16:31 ff., elsewhere τ. μάννα, Nu 11:6 ff., al. (מָן, Aram. מַנָּא);]
manna: Jo 6:31, 49, He 9:4; symb., Re 2:17.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G3105 (μαίνομαι) (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration);
strong.def: to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μαντεύομαι (< μαντίς, a seer, diviner), [in LXX for קסם, De 18:10, al.;]
to divine, practise divination: Ac 16:16.†

strong.def: to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μαραίνω, [in LXX: Jb 15:30 (יָבֵשׁ pi.), 24:24, Wi 2:8 19:21*;]
1. prop., to quench fire; pass., of fire, to die away, go out.
2. In various relations, to quench, waste, wear out (cf. Wi 19:21); pass., to waste away; in later writers (Plut., Luc., al.), of the withering of flowers and herbage (act., Jb 15:30; pass., Jb 24:24, Wi 2:8): Ja 1:11 (cf. ἀμάραντον).†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come);
strong.def: maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μαρὰν ἀθά (Rec. μαραναθά; Aram.: on the original form v. Dalman, Gr., § 41, 1; 74, 3; Words, 328),
Maran atha, i.e. the Lord cometh (but v. Dalman, Gr., § 41, 1; 74, 3; Words, 328; Field, Notes, 180; ICC, in l.): I Co 16:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 * μαργαρίτης, -ου, ὁ,
a pearl: Mt 13:45, 46, I Ti 2:9, Re 17:4 18:12, 16 21:21 (-ῖται, WH); proverbially, Mt 7:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Μάρκος, -ου, ὁ,
Mark: Mk., tit., Ac 12:12, 25 15:37, 39, Col 4:10, II Ti 4:11, Phm 24, I Pe 5:13 (v. Swete, Mk., Intr., xiii ff.; DB, iii, 245 ff).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μάρμαρος, -ου, ὁ (< μαρμαίρω, to glisten), [in LXX: Ep. Je 72*;]
1. any crystalline stone (Hom., Eur., al.).
2. In later writers, marble: Re 18:12.†

strong.def: to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** μαρτύρομαι (< μάρτυρ), [in LXX: Jth 7:28, I Mac 2:56 א)*;]
to summon as witness (M, Th., 25 f.; Hort., 1Pe., 53 f.; Lft., Notes, 29; Ga 203), hence,
(a). to protest, affirm solemnly: seq. ὅτι, Ac 20:26, Ga 5:3;
(b). to adjure, beseech: c. dat. pers., Ac 26:22; c. acc. et inf., Eph 4:17; seq. εἰς, I Th 2:12 (cf. δια-, προ-μαρτύρομαι).†

strong.derivation: from a primary (to handle or squeeze);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μασάομαι (Rec. μασσ-), -ῶμαι (Aristoph. and late writers, but not in Trag. or in good Att. prose), [in LXX: Jb 30:4 (לֶחֶם), Si 19:9 A*;]
to bite, chew: Re 16:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μαστίζω (Ep. and late prose = Att. μαστιγόω), [in LXX: Nu 22:25 (נכה hi.), Wi 5:11, II Mac 2:21*;]
to whip, scourge: c. acc., Ac 22:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ματαιολογία, -ας, ἡ (< ματαιολόγος),
idle or foolish talk: I Ti 1:6.†

strong.def: an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ματαιολόγος, -ον (< μάταιος, λέγω),
talking idly: Tit 1:10.†

strong.def: empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μάταιος, -ον (as in Att., but -αία, -αιον, I Co 15:17, I Pe 1:18; < μάτην), [in LXX for שָׁוְא, הֶבֶל, כָּזָב, etc.;]
vain, useless: ἀνωφελὴς κ. μ., Tit 3:9; πίστις, I Co 15:17; θρησκεία, Ja 1:26; διαλογισμοί, I Co 3:20(LXX); ἀναστροφή, I Pe 1:18; of idols and heathen gods, τὰ μ. (Je 2:5, IV Ki 17:15, al.): Ac 14:15.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ματαιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< μάταιος), [in LXX for הֶבֶל, Ps 30 (31):6 38 (39):5 61 (62):9, al., and nearly 40 times in Ec; for שָׁוְא, Ps 25:4, al.; רִיק, etc.;]
vanity, emptiness, frailty, folly: Ro 8:20, II Pe 2:18; τ. νοός, Eph 4:17 (elsewhere only in Pollux, 6, 134, and Eccl.).†

strong.def: to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ματαιόω, -ῶ (< μάταιος), [in LXX: IV Ki 17:15, Je 2:5, al. הבל, etc.;]
to make vain, foolish: Ro 1:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Μαθθάν (Rec. Ματθ-, v.s. Μαθθαῖος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מַתָּן),
Matthan: Mt 1:15.†

strong.derivation: apparently a shortened form of G3161 (Ματταθίας);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 (KJV) Μαθθίας (Rec. Ματθ-, v.s. Μαθθαῖος), -α, ὁ (Heb. מַתִּיָה),
Matthias: Ac 1:23, 26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μάχη, -ης, ἡ (< μάχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב;]
1. a fight.
2. a strife, contention, quarrel: II Co 7:5, II Ti 2:23, Ja 4:1; pl., Tit 3:9.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;
strong.def: to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μάχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for ריב, also for נצה ni., etc.;]
1. to fight: Ac 7:26.
2. to quarrel, dispute: II Ti 2:24, Ja 4:2; πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Jo 6:52 (cf. δια-μάχομαι).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3173 (μέγας) and (to boast;
strong.def: akin to G837 (αὐξάνω) and G2744 (καυχάομαι)); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μεγαλ-αυχέω, -ῶ (= μεγάλα αὐχέω), [in LXX: Ez 16:50 (גּבהּ), al.;]
to boast great things: Ja 3:5 (Rec. for μεγάλα αὐχεῖ, WH).†

strong.def: magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μεγαλεῖος, -εία, -εῖον (< μέγας), [in LXX: Ps 70 (71):19 (גָּדוֹל), al., freq. in Sir;]
magnificent, splendid (Xen., Plut., al.): Ac 2:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μεγαλοπρεπής, ές (= μεγάλῳ πρέπων), [in LXX: De 33:26 (גַּאֲוָה), II Mac 8:15 15:13, III Mac 2:9*;]
befitting a great man, magnificent, majestic: II Pe 1:17 (cf. MM, xvi).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μεγάλως, adv., [in LXX for גָּדוֹל, etc.;]
greatly: Phl 4:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † μεγαλωσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< μέγας), [in LXX chiefly for גְּדוּלָה and cogn. forms, II Ki 7:23, Ps 144 (145):3, al.;]
greatness, majesty: He 1:3 8:1, Ju 25 (elsewhere Eccl. only).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μέγεθος, -ους, τό (< μέγας), [in LXX chiefly for קוֹמָה;]
greatness: Eph 1:19 (cf. MM, xvi, s.v. μέγας).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 μέγιστος, v.s. μέγας.

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3326 (μετά) and G3593 (ὁδεύω) (compare "method");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† μεθ-οδία (Rec. -εία; cf. Bl., § 3, 5), -ας, ἡ (< † μεθοδεύω, 1. to treat by rule. 2. to employ craft: IV Ki 19:27*)
craft, deceit: Eph 4:14 6:11 (not found elsewhere; v. AR, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μέθυσος, -α, -ον (also -ος, -ον; prop., only of women, but in late writers also = μεθυστικός, of men), [in LXX: Pr 23:21 (סבא) 26:9 (שִׁכּוֹר), Si 19:1 26:8, IV Mac 2:7*;]
drunken: I Co 5:11 6:10.†

strong.def: to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 μεθύω (< μέθυ, wine, cf. μέθη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁכר, רוה;]
to be drunken: Mt 24:49, Jo 2:10, Ac 2:15, I Co 11:21, I Th 5:7; metaph., Re 17:2, 6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 μειζότερος, v.s. μέγας.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 3 μέλαν, τό, v.s. μέλας.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μέλας, -αινα, -αν, gen., -ανος, -αίνης, -ανος, [in LXX: Ca 1:5, Za 6:2 (שָׁחֹר), etc.;]
black: Re 6:5, 12; opp. to λευκός, Mt 5:36; neut., τὸ μ., ink : II Co 3:3, II Jo 12, III Jo 13.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3199 (μέλω);
strong.def: to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μελετάω, -ῶ (< μελέτη, care), [in LXX chiefly for הגה;]
1. c. gen., to care for (Hes.).
2. C. acc. to attend to, practise: I Ti 4:15 (RV, be diligent in; cf. Souter in Exp., VIII, vi, 429, but v. infr.).
3. to study, ponder: Ac 4:25(LXX), I Ti 4:15 (AV, meditate on; cf. CGT, in l., but v. supr.; cf. προ-μελετάω).†

strong.def: Melita, an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μελίτη, (Rec., R, txt.), Μελιτήνη (WH, R, mg., v. WH, App., 160),
Melita, Melitene (mod. Malta): Ac 28:1.†

strong.def: a limb or part of the body

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
38 μέλος, -ους, τό, [in LXX chiefly for נֵתַח;]
a member, limb of the body: I Co 12:14, 19, 26, Eph 4:16 (WH, mg.), Ja 3:5; pl. (as always in cl.), τὰ μ.: Mt 5:29, 30, Ro 6:13, 19 7:5, 23 12:4, I Co 12:12 ff. Col 3:5, Ja 3:6 4:1. Metaph., πόρνης, I Co 6:15; of Christians, μ. ἀλλήλων, Ro 12:5, Eph 4:25; Χριστοῦ, I Co 6:15; σώματος Χριστοῦ, I Co 12:27, Eph 5:30.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 Μελχισεδέκ, indecl., ὁ (Heb. מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק),
Melchizedek: He 5:6, 10 6:20 7:1, 10, 11, 15, 17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μεμβράνα, -ας, ἡ (Lat. membrana),
parchment: II Ti 4:13.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** μέμφομαι, [in LXX: Si 11:7 41:7, II Mac 2:7*;]
to blame, find fault: absol., Ro 9:19; c. acc., αὐτούς (WH, txt.; αὐτοῖς, Rec., WH, mg.; on rendering with αὐτοῖς v. Westc., in l.), He 8:8.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3201 (μέμφομαι) and (fate;
strong.def: akin to the base of G3313 (μέρος)); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μεμψίμοιρος, -ον (< μέμφομαι, + μοῖρα, fate, lot),
complaining of one's fate, querulous: Ju 16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 μέν-τοι = μέν τοι,
yet, however: Jo 4:27, al.; εἰ μ., Ja 2:8 (if indeed).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μερισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< μερίζω), [in LXX for מַחֲלֹקֶת, מַחְלְקָה, Jos 11:23, Es 6:18*;]
1. a dividing, division: ψυχῆς κ. πνεύματος (i.e. between them or of the things themselves, v. Westc., in l.), He 4:12.
2. a distribution, bestowal (cf. μερίζω, 2); pl., He 2:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μεσημβρία, -ας, ἡ (μέσος, ἡμέρα), [in LXX chiefly for צֹהַר, Ge 3:16, al; also for נֶגֶב, Da LXX 8:4, 9, al.;]
1. noon: Ac 22:6.
2. the South: Ac 8:26.†

strong.def: to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μεσιτεύω (< μεσίτης),
to interpose, mediate: ὅρκῳ, He 6:17 (MM, ii, iii).†

strong.def: a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 † μεσίτης, -ου, ὁ (< μέσος), [in LXX: Jb 9:33 (בַּיִן)*;]
an arbitrator, mediator: Ga 3:19; c. dupl. gen. pers., θεοῦ κ. ἀνθρώπων, I Ti 2:5; c. gen. rei, διαθήκης, He 8:6 9:15 12:24; ὁ δε μ. ἑνὸς οὐκ ἔστιν, Ga 3:20 (v. Lft., in l.; and for exx. of this word in π., v. MM, xvi).†

strong.def: Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare 0763), a region of Asia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Μεσοποταμία, -ας, ἡ (sc. χώρα),
Mesopotamia: Ac 2:9 7:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μεσότοιχον, -ου, τό (< μέσος, τοῖχος),
a partition wall: Eph 2:14 (not elsewhere, but v. LS, s.v. μεσότοιχος).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G3319 (μέσος) and G3772 (οὐρανός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† μεσουράνημα, -τος, τό (< μεσουρανέω, to be in mid-heaven, of the sun at the meridian),
the zenith, mid-heaven: Re 8:13 14:6 19:17.†

strong.def: to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μεσόω, -ῶ (< μέσος), [in LXX: μεσούσης τ. νυκός, Ex 12:29 (חֲצִי), etc.;]
to be in the middle, esp. of time: τ. ἑορτῆς μεσούσης, in the middle of the feast, Jo 7:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Μεσσίας, -ου, ὁ (Aram. מְשִׁיחָא = Heb. מָשִׁיחַ = Χριστός, q.v.),
Messiah: Jo 1:42 4:25.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 μεστός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Na 1:10, Ez 37:1 (מָלֵא), Es 5:2, Pr 6:34*;]
full: c. gen. rei, Jo 19:29 21:11, Ja 3:8; metaph., of thoughts and feelings, Mt 23:28, Ro 1:29 15:14, II Pe 2:14, Ja 3:17 (cf. Pr 6:34).†

strong.def: to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μεστόω, -ῶ (< μεστός), [in LXX: III Mac 5:1. 10*;]
to fill: pass., c. gen. rei, Ac 2:13.†

strong.def: to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μετα-βάλλω, [in LXX chiefly for הפךְ;]
to turn about, change. Pass. and mid., to turn oneself about; metaph., to change one's mind: Ac 28:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μετ-άγω, [in LXX: III Ki 8:47, 48, II Ch 6:37 (שׁבה) 36:3 (סוּר hi.), I Es 1:45 2:10 5:69, Es 8:17, Si prol. 16 10:8, II Mac 1:33*;]
1. in Xen., Plut., and later writers, to transfer, transport (so LXX).
2. In sense otherwise unknown (v. Hort, in l.), to turn about, direct: Ja 3:3, 4.†

strong.def: transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** μετά-θεσις, -εως, ἡ (< μετατίθημι), [in LXX: II Mac 11:24*;]
1. change of position, removal: He 11:5.
2. change, as of that which has been established: He 7:12 12:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μετ-αίρω, [in LXX: IV Ki 16:17 25:11, Ps 79 (80):8, Pr 22:28 (סוּר hi., גּלה hi., etc.)*;]
1. trans., to remove (LXX, IV Ki 16:17 25:11, Ps 79 (80):8, Pr 22:28).
2. (not cl.) to depart: Mt 13:53 19:1 (cf. Aq.: Ge 12:9).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μετα-καλέω, -ῶ , [in LXX: Ho 11:1, 2 (קרא), I Es 1:50*;]
to call from one place to another. Mid., to send for: c. acc., Ac 7:14 10:32 20:17 24:25.†

strong.def: to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μετα-κινέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: De 19:14 (סוּג hi.), Is 54:10 (מוּט), etc ;]
trans., to move away, remove (ὅρια, De 19:14). Mid., to remove oneself, remove, shift: metaph., ἀπὸ τ. ἐλπίδος, Col 1:23.†

strong.def: to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use)
strong.kjv: eat, have, be partaker, receive, take

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ** μετα-λαμβάνω, [in LXX: Es 5:1, Wi 18:9, I-IV Mac12*;]
to have or get a share of, partake of: c. gen. rei, II Ti 2:6, He 6:7 12:10; τροφῆς, Ac 2:46 27:33, 34; c. acc. rei (of the whole), to get: καιρόν, Ac 24:25 (v. Bl., § 36, 1; MM, xvi).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μετά-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις), -εως, ἡ (< μεταλαμβάνω),
participation, taking, receiving: of food, I Ti 4:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μετ-αλλάσσω, [in LXX: Es 2:7 (מוּת), Es 2:20, I Es 1:31, II Mac9*;]
1. to exchange: τ. ἀλήθειαν . . . ἐν τ. ψεύδει, the truth for a lie (v. Bl., § 36, 8), Ro 1:25.
2. to change: c. acc. seq. εἰς, Ro 1:26 (ἀλλάσσω).†

strong.derivation: from G3326 (μετά) and the middle voice of G3199 (μέλω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μετα-μέλομαι, [in LXX chiefly for נחם: ni.;]
depon., pass., to regret, repent one: Mt 21:30, 32 27:3, II Co 7:8, He 7:21(LXX).†

strong.def: to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 μετα-πέμπω, [in LXX (mid.): Ge 27:45 (לקח), Nu 23:7 (נחה: hi.), II Mac 15:31, III Mac 5:18 R, IV Mac 12:3 6*;]
to send after or for: pass., Ac 10:29a. Chiefly in mid., to send for, summon Ac 10:5, 22, 29b 11:13 20:1 24:24, 26 25:3.†

strong.def: to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μετα-στρέφω, [in LXX chiefly for הפךְ;]
to turn about, turn, change: pass., Ac 2:20(LXX), Ja 4:9 (WH, txt., μετατρέπω, q.v.); in evil sense, to pervert, corrupt (cf. primary sense reverse): Ga 1:7.†

strong.derivation: from G3326 (μετά) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα);
strong.def: to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** μετα-σχηματίζω, [in LXX: IV Mac 9:22*;]
to change in fashion or appearance: c. acc. rei, τ. σῶμα, Phl 3:21; mid., seq. εἰς, II Co 11:13, 14; seq. ὡς, II Co 11:15; of a rhetorical device, to transfer by a fiction (Field, Notes, in l.), seq. εἰς, I Co 4:6.†

strong.def: to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert
strong.kjv: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μετα-τίθημι, [in LXX: Ge 5:24 (לקח), De 27:17, al. (סוּג hi.), Si 44:16, II Mac 7:24, al;]
1. to transfer to another place: c. acc., pass., He 11:5(LXX); seq. εἰς, Ac 7:16.
2. to change: c. acc., pass., He 7:12; seq. εἰς, fig., i.e. to make one thing a pretext for another, χάριν εἰς ἀσέλγειαν, Ju 4. Mid., to change oneself, pass over: seq. ἀπό et εἰς, Ga 1:6 (cf. II Mac 7:24).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μετ-έπειτα, adv. [in LXX: Jth 9:5, Es 3:13, III Mac 3:24*;]
afterwards: He 12:17.†

strong.def: to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink)
strong.kjv: be partaker, pertain, take part, use

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 μετ-έχω, [in LXX: Pr 5:17 (אֵת), 1:18, I Es 5:40 8:70, Si 51:28, al.;]
to partake of, share in: ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τοῦ μετέχειν, I Co 9:10; c. gen. rei, I Co 9:12 10:21, 30, He 2:14; in sacramental sense, ἑκ τ. ἐνὸς ἄρτου μ., I Co 10:17 (cf. MM, xvi); metaph., γάλακτος, He 5:13; of belonging to a tribe, He 7:13.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of a compound of G3326 (μετά) and G3624 (οἶκος);
strong.def: a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μετοικεσία, -ας, ἡ (= cl. μετοικία, -κησις; < μετοικέω, to change one's abode), [in LXX chiefly for גֹּלָה and cogn. forms, Ez 12:11, Ob 1:20, al.;]
change of abode, migration: of the Babylonian exile, μ. Βαβυλῶνος, Mt 1:11, 12, 17.†

strong.def: to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μετ-οικίζω (< μέτοικος, an emigrant), [in LXX chiefly for גּלה hi.;]
to remove to a new abode, cause to migrate: Ac 7:4, 43(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μετοχή, -ῆς, ἡ (< μετέχω), [in LXX: Ps 121 (122):3 א R (חבר pu.)*;]
sharing, fellowship: II Co 6:14.†

strong.def: a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μετρητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< μετρέω), [in LXX: III Ki 18:32 (סְאָה), II Ch 4:5, (בַּת), etc.;]
1. a measurer (Plat.).
2. = ἀμφορεύς, an Attic measure, = 1 1⁄2 Roman amphoræ or about 9 Eng. gallons: Jo 2:6.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of the base of G3357 (μετρίως) and G3806 (πάθος);
strong.def: to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μετριοπαθέω, -ῶ (< μετριοπαθής, moderating one's passions),
to hold one's passions or emotions in restraint; hence, to bear gently with, feel gently towards: He 5:2.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G3358 (μέτρον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μετρίως, adv. (μέτριος, moderate), [in LXX: II Mac 15:38*;]
moderately: litotes, οὐ μ., exceedingly, Ac 20:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 μέτωπον, -ου, τό (μετά + ὤψ, an eye), [in LXX for מֶצַח;]
the forehead: Re 7:3 9:4 13:16 14:1, 9 17:5 20:4 22:4.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of G3361 (μή) and (somebody);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μηδαμῶς (= μηδαμῆ, -δαμά, adv. fr. μηδαμός = μηδείς), [in LXX chiefly for הָלִלָה, הָלילָה;]
by no means, not at all. μ., Κύριε (sc. τοῦτο γένοιτο), Ac 10:14 11:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μηδέποτε (μηδέ, ποτέ), adv.,
never: II Ti 3:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μηδέπω (μηδέ, πώ), adv.,
not yet: He 11:7.†

strong.def: a Median, or inhabitant of Media

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μῆδος, -ου, ὁ,
a Mede, Median: pl., Ac 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μῆκος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in LXX chiefly for אֹרֶךְ;]
length: Eph 3:18, Re 21:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μηλωτή, -ῆς, ἡ (< μῆλον, a sheep or goat), [in LXX for אַדֶּרֶת, III Ki 19:13, 19, IV Ki 2:8, 13, 14*;]
a sheepskin: He 11:37.†

strong.def: a particle of affirmation (only with G2229 (ἦ)); assuredly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μήν, a particle of assurance,
verily, truly; εἰ (εἶ) μ. (= cl., ἦ μ. in LXX and π.), now verily, full surely: He 6:14(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * μήπω (μή πω, LTr., in Ro 9:11), adv.,
not yet: c. ptcp., Ro 9:11; c. acc. et inf., He 9:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μηρός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵךְ;]
the thigh: Re 19:16.†

strong.def: not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μή-τι-γε (μήτι γε, Rec., L; μή τι γε, Tr.), >strengthened form of μήτι,
let alone: i.e. according to context;
(a). much less;
(b). much more: I Co 6:3.†

strong.derivation: from G3384 (μήτηρ) and the base of G257 (ἅλων);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μητρολῴας (Rec. -αλῴας, in cl., -αλοίας, v. Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2), -ου, ὁ (< μήτρρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite);
(a). a matricide: I Ti 1:9 (AV, R, txt., but v. infr.);
(b). a smiter of his mother: I Ti 1:9 (R, mg., cf. Ex 21:15, and v. Ellic., CGT, in l.).†

strong.def: to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 μιαίνω, [in LXX chiefly for טָמֵא;]
1. to dye or stain.
2. to stain, defile, soil;
(a). in physical sense;
(b). in moral sense: Tit 1:15, He 12:15, Ju 8;
(c). in ritual sense (cf. Le 22:5, al.): Jo 18:28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μίασμα, -τος, τό (< μιαίνω), chiefly in trag. and late writers; [in LXX: Le 7:8 (18) (פִּגּוּל), Je 39 (32):34 (שִׁקּוּץ), Ez 33:31 (בֶּצַע), Jth 9:2, 4 13:16, I Mac 13:50*;]
a stain, defilement: pl., II Pe 2:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† μιασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< μιαίνω), [in LXX: Wi 14:26, I Mac 4:43*;]
1. prop., the act of defiling.
2. = μίασμα (q.v.): II Pe 2:10 (cf. Plut., Mor., 393c).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μίγμα (LT, cl., μῖγμα; on the orthogr., v. Bl., § 3, 5), -τος, τό (< μίγνυμι), [in LXX: Si 38:8*;]
a mixture: Jo 19:39 (ἕλιγμα, WH, R, mg.).†

strong.def: Miletus, a city of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Μίλητος, -ου, ἡ,
Miletus, a maritime city of Caria: Ac 20:15, 17, II Ti 4:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μίλιον, -ου, τό,
a Roman mile (1680 yds.): Mt 5:41.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (< μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Ps 30 (31):6, Wi 4:2 15:9, IV Mac 9:23 13:9*;]
to imitate: II Th 3:7, 9, He 13:7, III Jo 11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * μιμητής, -οῦ, ὁ (< μιμέομαι),
in NT always (like the verb) in good sense, an imitator: I Co 4:16 11:1, Eph 5:1, I Th 1:6 2:14, He 6:12.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of G3415 (μνάομαι) (from which some of the tenses are borrowed);
strong.def: to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
23 μιμνήσκω (Bl., -ῄ-, § 3, 3), [in LXX chiefly for זכר;]
to remind: mid. and pass.;
(a). reflexive, to remind oneself of, hence, to remember: c. gen. rei, Mt 26:75, Lk 1:54, 72 24:8, Ac 11:16, II Pe 3:2, Ju 17; c. neg., of sins, = to forgive, He 8:12 10:17(LXX); c. gen. pers., Lk 23:42; seq. ὅτι, Mt 5:23 27:63, Lk 16:25, Jo 2:17, 22 12:16; ὡς, Lk 24:6; pf., μέμνημι, in pres. sense (cl.), c. gen. pers. (rei), I Co 11:2, II Ti 1:4; pres., μιμνήσκομαι (only in late writers), c. gen. pers., in sense of caring for, He 2:6(LXX) 13:3;
(b). in passive sense, to be remembered, aor., ἐμνήσθην: seq. ἐνώπιον, c. gen. pers. (cf. Ez 18:22), Ac 10:31, Re 16:19 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐπ-ανα-, ὑπο-μιμνήσκω. The tenses of this verb are from the older μνάομαι).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† μισθαποδοσία, -ας, ἡ (< μισθός, ἀποδίδωμι; cl. μισθοδοσία),
payment of wages, recompense; meton.,
(a). of reward: He 10:35 11:26;
(b). of punishment: He 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μισθ-απο-δότης, -ου, ὁ, (v. supr.),
one who pays wages; meton., a rewarder: He 11:6.†

strong.def: to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μισθόω, -ῶ (< μισθός), [in LXX (mid.) chiefly for שׂכר;]
to let out for hire. Mid., to hire: c. acc., Mt 20:1, 7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μίσθωμα, -τος, τό (< μισθόω), [in LXX: De 23:18 (19), Mi 1:7, Ez 16:31, 34, 41 (אֶתְנַן), Ez 16:33, (נֵדֶה, נָדָן), Ez 16:32, Pr 19:13*;]
1. price, hire (cl, and LXX).
2. In sense not found elsewhere, a hired dwelling: Ac 28:30.†

strong.def: Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μιτυλήνη, -ης, ἡ (late form — Strab., Plut. — of cl. Μυτιλ-),
Mytilene, Mitylene, chief city of Lesbos: Ac 20:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Μιχαήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מִיכָאֵל, who like God?),
Michael, the Archangel (cf. Da 12:1): Ju 9, Re 12:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μνάσων, -ωνος, ὁ,
Mnason: Ac 21:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 μνεία, -ας, ἡ (< μιμνήσκω), [in LXX for זכר, its parts and derivatives;]
remembrance, mention (= μνήμη): Phl 1:3; μ. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen. pers., Ro 1:9, Eph 1:16, I Th 1:2, Phm 4 (cf. Ps 110 (111):4); μ. ἔχειν, c. gen. pers., I Th 3:6, II Ti 1:3 (on the v.l. in Ro 12:13, v. ICC, in l.; Field, Notes, 163).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μνήμη, -ης, ἡ (< μνάομαι), [in LXX for זֵכֶר, זִכָּרוֹן;]
memory, remembrance, mention: μ. ποιεῖσθαι, c. gen., to remember, II Pe 1:15 (but in cl., π., μ. π. more freq. = to make mention, and so perh. here, cf. Mayor, in l.; and for ex. from π., v. Zorell, s.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 μόλις, adv. (< μόλος, toil), [in LXX: Pr 11:31, Wi 9:16, al.;]
with difficulty, hardly, scarcely: Lk 9:39 (T, μόγις), Ac 14:8 27:7, 8, 16, Ro 5:7, I Pe 4:18(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μολόχ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. מֹלֶךְ, prop. מֶלֶךְ, King, but vocalized to read בֺּשֶׁת, shame, of. Βάαλ, and v. DB, iii, 415 f.),
Moloch, the god of the Ammonites: Ac 7:43(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μολύνω, [in LXX: Ge 37:31 (טבל), Is 59:3 (גּאל ni.), Za 14:2 (שׁכב ni.), Si 21:28, al.;]
to stain, soil, defile; in NT always symb. and fig.: I Co 8:7, Re 3:4 14:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † μολυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< μολύνω), [in LXX: Je 23:15 (חֲנֻפָה), I Es 8:83, II Mac 5:27*;]
defilement: c. gen. obj., II Co 7:1 (Plut., FlJ).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μομφή, ῆς, ἡ (< μέμφομαι), poët. form of μέμψις,
blame, complaint: Col 3:13.†

strong.def: a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** μονή, -ῆς, ἡ (< μένω), [in LXX: I Mac 7:38*;]
1. in cl.,
(a). a staying, abiding;
(b). continuance (LXX, I Mac 7:38).
2. In late Gk.,
(a). a statson (Paus.);
(b). an abode: Jo 14:2, 23;
(c). a monastery (cf. MM, iii, xvi; so in MGr.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 2 μόνον, v.s. μόνος.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μονόω, -ῶ (< μόνος), [in Aq.: Ge 49:6;]
to leave alone, forsake: of a childless widow, pf. ptcp. pass., I Ti 5:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† μορφόω, -ῶ (< μορφή), [in Aq.: Is 44:13*;]
to form: fig., Ga 4:19 (cf. μετα-, συμ-μορφόω).†

strong.def: formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† μόρφωσις, -εως, ἡ (< μορφόω),
1. a forming, shaping (Theophr.).
2. form, outline, semblance: Ro 2:20; opp. to δύναμις, II Ti 3:5.†

strong.def: to fabricate the image of a bullock

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μοσχο-ποιέω, -ῶ,
to make a calf (as an image): Ac 7:41 (LXX, ἐποίησε μόσχον).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μόχθος, -ου, ὁ (= Hom. μόγος), in cl. chiefly poët., [in LXX for תְּלָאָה, עָמָל, etc.;]
toil, labour, hardship, distress: II Co 11:27, I Th 2:9, II Th 3:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μουσικός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Ge 31:27, Ez 26:13 (שִׁיר), Da LXX TH 3:5 ff. (זְמָר), Si 22:6, al.;]
skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: Re 18:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μυελός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Ge 45:18 (חֵלֶב), Jb 21:24 (מֹחַ) Jb 33:24*;]
marrow: He 4:12.†

strong.def: to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μυέω, -ῶ (< μύω, to shut the mouth), [in LXX: III Mac 2:30*;]
to initiate into the mysteries (so chiefly in cl.; LXX, III Mac 2:30); hence, to instruct: pass., Phl 4:12 (RV, I have learned the secret).†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the same as G3453 (μυέω) (through the idea of tuition);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** μῦθος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Wi 17:4 A, Si 20:19*;]
1. speech, conversation.
2.
(a). a story, narrative (Hom.);
(b). later, opp. to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: I Ti 1:4 4:7, II Ti 4:4, Tit 1:14, II Pe 1:16.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of ( to "moo");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** μυκάομαι, -ῶμαι, in cl. chiefly poët., [in Sm.: Jb 6:5*;]
prop., of oxen (onomatop.), to low, bellow; of a lion, to roar: Re 10:3.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G3455 (μυκάομαι) (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds);
strong.def: to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μυκτηρίζω (< μυκτήρ, the nose), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:21, Jb 22:19, Ps 79 (80):6, al. (לעג), Pr 1:30 (נאץ) Pr 15:20 (בּזה), I Mac 7:34, al.;]
to turn up the nose or sneer at, mock: pass., Ga 6:7 (cf. ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω).†

strong.def: Myra, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Μύρα, Μύρρα (LT, Tr., WH), -ων, τά,
Myra, a city of Lycia: Ac 27:5.†

strong.derivation: plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many);
strong.def: ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 μυρίος, -α, -ον,
1. numberless, countless, infinite: I Co 4:15 14:19.
2. As a definite numeral, in pl., μύριοι, -αι, -α, ten thousand: Mt 18:24.†

strong.def: Mysia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Μυσία, -ας, ἡ,
Mysia, a province of Asia Minor: Ac 16:7, 8.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of the base of G3466 (μυστήριον) and (the face;
strong.def: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† μυ-ωπάζω (< μύωψ, closing the eyes, short-sighted; < μύω, ὤψ),
to be short-sighted: II Pe 1:9 (R, mg., closing his eyes; v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: probably akin to the base of G3433 (μόλις)) and probably (the face; from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μώλωψ, -ωπος, ὁ, [in LXX for חַבּוּרָה, Ex 21:25, al.;]
a bruise, wound from a stripe: I Pe 2:24(LXX) (Arist., Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 μωμάομαι, -ῶμαι (< μῶμος), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Pr 9:7 (מוּם), Wi 10:14, Si 31 (34):18*;]
to find fault with, blame: II Co 8:20; pass., II Co 6:3.†

strong.def: a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μῶμος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX, of physical blemishes: Le 21:17 ff., De 15:21, Ca 4:7, al. (מוּם); of mental defect, Si 20:24, al.;]
1. in cl. poets and late prose, blame, disgrace.
2. In LXX, perh. because of resemblance to מוּםpossible misspelling of מאוּם, a physical blemish (cf. ἄμωμος, I Pe 1:19, and v. Hort., in l.); metaph., of licentious persons, II Pe 2:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** μωρία, -ας, ἡ (< μωρός), [in LXX: Si 20:31*;]
foolishness: I Co 1:18, 21, 23 2:14 3:19.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3474 (μωρός) and G3004 (λέγω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * μωρολογία, -ας, ἡ,
foolish talking: Eph 5:4.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G3466 (μυστήριον);
strong.def: dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 μωρός, -ά, -όν, [in LXX for נָבָל, etc.; freq. in Si.;]
1. prop., of the nerves, dull, sluggish (Hipp., Arist.).
2. Of the mind, dull, stupid, foolish: Mt 5:22 (v. Field, Notes, 3 ff.) 7:26 23:17, 19 (T, WH, txt., R, om.) Mt 25:2, >3, 8, I Co 3:18 4:10; of things, παράδοσις, Mk 7:13 (T, WH, txt., R, om.): ζητήσεις, II Ti 2:23, Tit 3:9; τὸ μ. τ. θεοῦ, I Co 1:25; τὰ μ. τ. κόσμου, I Co 1:27.†

strong.def: Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Ναθαναήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל),
Nathanael, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (q.v.): Jo 1:45-49 21:2.†

strong.derivation: a flower of the same name, from (stupefaction, as a "narcotic");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νάρκισσος, -ου, ὁ,
Narcissus: Ro 16:11.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3491 (ναῦς) and G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ναυαγέω, -ῶ (< ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break),
to suffer shipwreck: II Co 11:25; metaph., seq. περὶ τ. πίστιν, I Ti 1:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ναύ-κληρος, -ου, ὁ (< ναῦς, κλῆρος),
a shipowner, shipmaster: Ac 27:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ναῦς, νεώς acc. ναῦν, ἡ, [in LXX for אֳנִי, אֲנִיָּה;]
a ship: Ac 27:41 (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; v. M, Pr., 25 f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ναύτης, -ου, ὁ (< ναῦς), [in Aq.: Ez 27:9; Sm.: Ez 27:29*;]
a seaman, sailor: Ac 27:27, 30, Re 18:17.†

strong.def: a youth (up to about forty years)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 νεανίας, -ου, ὁ (< νεάν = νέος), [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר;]
a young man: Ac 7:58 20:9 23:17, 18.†

strong.def: new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νεάπολις, -εως, ἡ, Rec. for Νέα Πόλις (WH), the more freq. form (LS, s.v.),
Neapolis, a maritime city of Macedonia: Ac 16:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† νεκρόω, ῶ (< νεκρός),
to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, He 11:12; σῶμα, Ro 4:19. Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, Col 3:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ (< νεκρόω),
1. a putting to death.
2. a state of death, death: Ro 4:19, II Co 4:10 (v. Deiss., LAE, 94).†

strong.derivation: from G3501 (νέος) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);
strong.def: newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νεό-φυτος, -ον (< νέος, φύω), [in LXX: Jb 14:9, Ps 143 (144):12, Is 5:7 (נֶטַע), Ps 127 (128):3 (שְׁתִיל)*;]
newly planted (LXX). Metaph., as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: I Ti 3:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νεύω, [in LXX: Pr 4:5 21:1*;]
to nod or beckon, as a sign : c. dat. pers. et inf., Jo 13:24, Ac 24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).†

strong.def: Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Νεφθαλείμ (-λίμ, WH in Re 7:6), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי),
Naphtali: Mt 4:13, 15(LXX), Re 7:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νέφος, -ους, τό, [in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנָן;]
a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaph. (as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: He 12:1.†

strong.def: a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for כִּלְיָה, Ex 29:13, al.; metaph., Ps 7:9 15 (16):7 25 (26):2, Wi 1:6, al.;]
a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaph., of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Re 2:23.†

strong.derivation: from a form of G3485 (ναός) and (to sweep);
strong.def: a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * νεω-κόρος, -ου,
a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (v. DB, i, 722 b): Ac 19:35.†

strong.def: appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν (< νεώτερος), [in LXX: III Mac 4:8*;]
= νεανικός, youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, II Ti 2:22 (Polyb.).†

strong.derivation: probably an intensive form of G3483 (ναί);
strong.def: a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νή, particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: ν. τ. ὑγίειαν, Ge 42:15, 16 (חֵי)*;]
by: c. acc., I Co 15:31.†

strong.def: to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * νηπιάζω (< νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.),
to be a babe: I Co 14:20.†

strong.derivation: apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (ναῦς) (meaning wet);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νηρεύς, -έως, ὁ,
Nereus: Ro 16:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† νησίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.),
a small island: Ac 27:16.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G3491 (ναῦς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 νῆσος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for אִי;]
an island: Ac 13:6 27:26 28:1, 7, 9, 11, Re 1:9 6:14 16:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in I Ti 3:2, 11), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον), (< νήφω),
1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine.
2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: I Ti 3:2, 11, Tit 2:2.†

strong.def: to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * νήφω,
