to be sober, abstain from wine; metaph., of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: I Th 5:6 8, II Ti 4:5 (v. Ellic., in l.), I Pe 1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐκ-νήφω, and v. MM, xvii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νίγερ, ὁ (Lat. niger)
Niger: Ac 13:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νικάνωρ, -ορος, ὁ,
Nicanor: Ac 6:5.†

strong.def: conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νίκη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: I Ch 29:11 (נֵצַח), freq. in I-IV Mac;]
victory: I Jo 5:4.†

strong.def: victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Νικόδημος, -ου, ὁ,
Nicodemus: Jo 3:1, 4, 9 7:50 19:39.†

strong.def: a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Νικολαΐτης, -αυ, ὁ,
a Nicolaitan: pl., Re 2:6, 15.†

strong.def: victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νικόλαος, -αυ, ὁ,
Nicolaus: Ac 6:5.†

strong.def: victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ,
Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l.): Tit 3:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † νῖκος, -ους, τό, late form of νίκη, [in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Es 3:9, II Mac 10:38, IV Mac 17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Jb 14:20), II Ki 2:26, Jb 36:7, Am 1:11 8:7, Je 3:5, La 5:20 (לָנֶצֵח, as נ׳ in Syr., = victory)*;]
victory: Mt 12:20 (Is 42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), I Co 15:54 (Is 25:8, Aq., Th.), I Co 15:55 (Ho 13:14, LXX δίκη), I Co 15:57.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† νιπτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (νίπτω),
a basin: Jo 13:5.†

strong.def: a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** νόημα, -τος, τό (νοέω), [in LXX: Si 21:11, Ba 2:8, III Mac 5:30*;]
a thought, purpose, design: II Co 2:11 10:5 11:3, Phl 4:7. Meton., of the mind, II Co 3:14 4:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** νόθος, -η, -ον, [in LXX: Wi 4:3*;]
a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: He 12:8.†

strong.derivation: feminine from the same as G3551 (νόμος);
strong.def: pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νομή, -ῆς, ἡ (< νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc.;]
1. a pasture, pasturage: fig., Jo 10:9.
2. a grazing, feeding; metaph., of a spreading sore, II Ti 2:17 (Polyb.).†

strong.derivation: adverb from a derivative of G3551 (νόμος);
strong.def: legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** νομίμως, adv. (< νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:18*;]
rightly, lawfully: I Ti 1:8, II Ti 2:5.†

strong.def: what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νόμισμα, -τος, τό (< νομίζω), [in LXX: Es 8:36 (דָּת), Ne 7:71 R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), I Mac 15:6*;]
1. that which is established by usage, a custom.
2. The current coin of a state: Mt 22:19.†

strong.def: legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** νομοθεσία, -ας, ἡ (< νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: II Mac 6:23, IV Mac 5:35 17:16*;]
legislation, lawgiving: Ro 9:4.†

strong.def: to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νομοθετέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for ירה hi.;]
1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: He 7:11.
2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., He 8:6.†

strong.derivation: from G3551 (νόμος) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ (< νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: Ps 9:20*;]
a lawgiver: Ja 4:12.†

strong.def: to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** νοσέω, -ῶ (< νόσος), [in LXX (metaph.): Wi 17:8*;]
to be sick: metaph., of mental ailment, seq. περί, I Ti 6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νοσσίον, -ου, τό, dimin. of νοσσός, q.v., [in LXX: Ps 83 (84):3 (אֶפְרֹחַ)*;]
a young bird: Mt 23:37.†

strong.def: to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 νοσφίζω (< νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: Jos 7:1 (לקח), II Mac 4:32*;]
1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon.
2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tit 2:10 (for ex. in π., v. MM, xvii); seq. ἀπό, Ac 5:2, 3.†

strong.derivation: from G3563 (νοῦς) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
strong.def: calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** νουθεσία, -ας ἡ (< νουθετέω), = cl. νουθέτησις; [in LXX: Wi 16:6*;]
admonition: I Co 10:11, Eph 6:4, Tit 3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).†

strong.def: to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 νουθετέω, -ῶ (< νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: I Ki 3:13 (כּהה pi.), Jb8 (יסר pi., בִּין), Wi 11:10 12:2, 26*;]
to admonish, exhort: c. acc. pers., Ac 20:31, Ro 15:14, I Co 4:14, Col 1:28 3:16, I Th 5:12, 14, II Th 3:15.†

strong.derivation: feminine of a compound of G3501 (νέος) and G3376 (μήν) (as noun by implication, of G2250 (ἡμέρα));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) νεομηνία (Att. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ (< νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ;]
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Col 2:16.†

strong.derivation: probably contracted for a compound of G3565 (νύμφη) and G1435 (δῶρον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, q.v.), -ης, ἡ,
Nympha (v. M, Pr., 48): Col 4:15, WH, R, mg.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of G3568 (νῦν) for emphasis;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 νυνί, an Attic strengthened form of νῦν (in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : Jb5, Pss2, II, IV Mac4, Ep. Je.*;]
now;
1. of time: c. praes., Ac 24:13, Ro 15:23, 25, I Co 13:13, II Co 8:11, 22, Phm 9, 11; c. pf., Ro 3:21; c. pret., Ro 6:22 11:30 (WH, mg.) 7:6, Eph 2:13, Col 1:21 3:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, Ac 22:1.
2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Ro 7:17, I Co 5:11 (νῦν, WH) 12:18 (νῦν, WH, txt.) 15:20, He 8:6 (νῦν, WH, txt.), He 9:26 (cf. WM, 24, 579n).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** νύσσω (Att. -ττω), [in LXX: Si 22:19, III Mac 5:14*;]
to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jo 19:34, [Mt 27:49], WH.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3506 (νεύω);
strong.def: to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νυστάζω (cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc;]
to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Mt 25:5. Metaph., of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Ps 120 (121):4, Is 5:27): II Pe 2:3.†

strong.def: a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον (< νύξ, ἡμέρα, v. B1., § 28, 4),
lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: II Co 11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 νωθρός, -ά, -όν, [in LXX: Pr 22:29 (חָשֹׁךְ), Si 4:29 11:12*;]
sluggish, slothful: He 5:11 6:12 (for similar usage in π., v. MM, xvii).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 νῶτος, -ου, ὁ, in Att. most freq. τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι, and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מָתְנַיִם;]
the back: Ro 11:10(LXX).†

strong.def: hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ξενία, -ας, ἡ (< ξένος), [in LXX: Si 29:27 B1*;]
hospitality, entertainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l., but v. infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: Ac 28:23, and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l., Phl., p. 9; but v. supr., and cf. MM, xvii).†

strong.def: to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ** ξενίζω (< ξένος), [in LXX: Es 3:13, Si 29:25, II Mac 9:6, III Mac 7:3*;]
1. to receive as a guest, entertain: c. acc. pers., Ac 10:23 28:7, He 13:2; pass., Ac 10:6, 18, 32 21:16.
2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; II Mac 9:6), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: Ac 17:20; pass., I Pe 4:4, 12.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3581 (ξένος) and G1209 (δέχομαι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω (< ξένος, δέχομαι),
to entertain strangers: I Ti 5:10.†

strong.def: foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ξένος, -η, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for נׇכְרִי;]
(a). foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, Ac 17:18; διδαχαί, He 13:9;
(b). c. gen. rei, strange to, estranged from, ignorant of : Eph 2:12;
(c). strange, unusual: I Pe 4:12.
As subst., ὁ ξ.,
(a). a foreigner, stranger: Mt 25:35, 38, 43, 44 27:7, Ac 17:21, III Jo 5; ξένοι κ. τάροικοι (opp. to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), Eph 2:19; ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι, He 11:13;
(b). one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality;
α. the guest;
β. the host ( = ξενοδόκος, Hom., Il., xv, 532): Ro 16:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ξύλινος, -η, -ον (ξύλον), [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ;]
wooden: II Ti 2:20, Re 9:20 (cf. Ep. Je 4 ff.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the same as G3586 (ξύλον) (meaning a razor);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ξυράω, -ῶ
late form of ξυρέω (q.v.) : I Co 11:6 (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but v.s. ξύρω).†

strong.derivation: probably from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη);
strong.def: a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ,
bulk, mass; metaph., an encumbrance: He 12:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 **† ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ὁδός, ἡγέομαι), [in LXX: Es 8:1, Wi 7:15 18:3, I Mac 4:2, II Mac 5:15*;]
a leader on the way, a guide: Ac 1:16. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, Ro 2:19; pl., Mt 15:14 23:16, 24.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3598 (ὁδός) and G4198 (πορεύομαι);
strong.def: to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ (< ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, Ge 37:25, al.),
to travel, journey: Ac 10:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ (v. supr.), [in LXX: Wi 13:18 18:3 19:5, I Mac 6:41*;]
a journey: Jo 4:6, II Co 11:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀδύνη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for יָגוֹן, מַר, etc. (26 words in all);]
pain, distress, of body or mind: Ro 9:2, I Ti 6:10.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G1416 (δύνω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀδυρμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ὀδύρομαι, to lament), [in LXX : Je 38 (31):15 (תַּמְרוּריִם), II Mac 11:6*;]
lamentation, mourning: Mt 2:18(LXX), II Co 7:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ὀζείας (Rec. Ὀζίας), -ου, ὁ (Heb. עֻזִּיָּה),
Uzziah: Mt 1:8, 9.†

strong.derivation: a primary verb (in a strengthened form);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὄζω, [in LXX: Ex 8:14 (10) (בּאשׁ)*;]
to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jo 11:39.†

strong.def: a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ὀθόνη, -ης, ἡ (of Semitic origin, cf. Heb. אֵטוּן, yarn);
1. fine linen (Hom., al.).
2. Later, a sheet or sail: Ac 10:11 11:5.†

strong.def: domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 οἰκεῖος, -α, -ον (< οἶκος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, שְׁאֵר, etc.; in Is 58:7, οἰ. τοῦ σπέρματος for בָּשָׂר;]
in or of the house (opp. to ξένος, ἀλλότριος);
(a). of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods;
(b). of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: I Ti 5:8; c. gen. pers., of the family of: metaph., τ. θεοῦ, Eph 2:19; τ. πίστεως (Lft., in l.), Ga 6:10.†

strong.def: to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 οἰκέω, -ῶ (< οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly for ישׁב;]
(a). trans., to inhabit: c. acc., I Ti 6:16;
(b). intrans., to dwell: seq. μετά (of married life), I Co 7:12, 13; metaph., seq. ἐν: ἀγαθόν, Ro 7:18; ἁμαρτία, Ro 7:20; πνεῦμα θεοῦ, Ro 8:9, 11, I Co 3:16 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-, ἒν-κατ-, παρ-, περι-, συν-οικέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 οἴκημα, -τος, τό (< οἰκέω), [in LXX: Ez 16:24 (גַּב), To 2:4, Wi 13:15*;]
a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms (e.g. brothel. Hdt., ii, 121; cf. Ez 16:24), a prison (Thuc., iv, 47 f.): Ac 12:7.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (οἰκέω) (equivalent to G3612 (οἴκημα));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό (< οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), [in LXX: II Mac 11:2, III Mac 2:15*;]
a habitation: Ju 6; trop., II Co 5:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν (< οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος,
belonging to the household, one's own: Mt 10:36; opp. to οἰκοδεσπότης, Mt 10:25.†

strong.def: to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 οἰκο-δεσποτέω, -ῶ (< οἰκοδεσπότης),
to rule a household: I Ti 5:14.†

strong.def: be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * οἰκ-ουρός, -ον (< οἶκος + οὖρος, a keeper);
1. watching or keeping the house; as subst., ἡ οἰ., a housekeeper (Soph., Eur.; v. LS, s.v.).
2. keeping at home: Tit 2:5, Rec. (v. Field, Notes, 220 ff.; CGT, in l., and cf. οἰκουργός).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 οἰκτείρω (< οἶκτος, pity), [in LXX for רחם pi., חנן, etc.;]
to pity, have compassion on. c. acc. pers., Ro 9:15(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 οἰκτιρμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< οἰκτείρω), [in LXX, usually in pl., chiefly for רַחַם;]
compassion, pity: σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, a heart of compassion, Col 3:12; in pl. (as LXX for Heb. רַחֲמִים), οἰ. τ. θεοῦ, Ro 12:1, He 10:28; ὁ πατὴρ τῶν οἰ, II Co 1:3; σπλάγχνα κ. οἰ., Phl 2:1.†

strong.derivation: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a form of the base of G5397 (φλύαρος);
strong.def: an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ (< φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, De 21:20;
drunkenness, debauchery: I Pe 4:3.†

strong.def: to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 οἴομαι, οἶμαι, [in LXX for הִנֵּה, Ge 37:7, al.;]
to suppose, expect, imagine; c. acc. et inf., Jo 21:25; c. inf., Phl 1:17; seq. ὅτι, Ja 1:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀκνέω, -ῶ (< ὄκνος, shrinking, hesitation), [in LXX: Nu 22:16 (מנע ni.), Jg 18:9 (עצל ni.), To 12:6, 13, Jth 12:13, Si 7:35, IV Mac 14:4*;]
to shrink from doing, hesitate to do (Hom., Thuc., al.); hence, to delay c. inf., Ac 9:38 (cf. Nu 22:16, and v. MM, xviii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὀκνηρός, -ά, -όν (< ὀκνέω), [in LXX for עָצֵל Pr 6:6, 9 al.;]
shrinking, hesitating, timid: c. dat. (Bl., § 38, 2), Ro 12:11; hence, slothful: Mt 25:26. Of things, that which causes shrinking, irksome: Phl 3:1.†

strong.def: an eight-day old person or act

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὀκταήμερος, -ον (< ὀκτώ, ἡμέρα),
of the eighth day, eight days old: c. dat. ref., περιτομῇ ὀ., Phl 3:5 (words of this class denote duration, cf. τεταρταῖος).†

strong.def: a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὀλέθριος, -ον (also -α, -ον, as in Wi 18:15), [in LXX : III Ki 21 (20):42 (חֵרָם), Wi 18:15*;]
destructive, deadly: δίκην, II Th 1:9, L, txt. (for ὄλεθρος, q.v.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὀλιγόψυχος, -ον [in LXX: Is 35:4 (מהר ni.), etc.;]
faint-hearted: I Th 5:14.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3641 (ὀλίγος) and ("care");
strong.def: to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀλιγωρέω, -ῶ (< ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), [in LXX: Pr 3:11 (מאס)*;]
to esteem lightly, think little of: c. gen., He 12:5(LXX).†

strong.def: a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὀλοθρευτής (Rec. ὁλ-), -οῦ, ὁ (< ὀλοθρεύω),
a destroyer: I Co 10:10 (not elsewhere).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὀλοθρεύω (< ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω), [in LXX for כּרת, שׁחת hi., etc.;]
to destroy: He 11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὀλοκληρία, -ας, ἡ (< ὁλόκληρος), [in LXX: Is 1:6 (מְתֹם)*;]
completeness, soundness: Ac 3:16.†

strong.def: complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὁλό-κληρος, -ον (< ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Le 23:15, Ez 15:5 (תָּמִים), De 27:6, Jos 9:2 (8:31) (שָׁלֵם), Za 11:16 (נצב ni.), Wi 15:3, I Mac 4:47, IV Mac 15:17*;]
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wi 15:3, IV Mac 15:17), I Th 5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Ja 1:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀλολύζω (onomatop.), [in LXX chiefly for ילל hi.;] (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving),
to cry aloud: Ja 5:1.†

strong.def: complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὁλοτελής, -ές (< ὅλος, τέλος),
complete, perfect: I Th 5:23.†

strong.derivation: probably a contraction from (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ὀλυμπᾶς (perh. contr. fr. Ὀλυμπιόδωρος, Bl., § 29), -ᾶ,
Olympas: Ro 16:15.†

strong.def: an unripe (because out of season) fig

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Ca 2:13 (פַּגָּה)*;]
an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring: Re 6:13.†

strong.def: completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὅλως, adv. (< ὅλος),
altogether, assuredly, actually (c. neg., at all): Mt 5:34, I Co 5:1 6:7 15:29.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὁμιλία, -ας, ἡ (< ὅμιλος), [in LXX: Ex 21:10 (עֹנָה), al.;]
company, association: I Co 15:33.†

strong.derivation: adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G2372 (θυμός);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ὁμοθυμαδόν (< ὁμός, θυμός), [in LXX for יַחַד (freq. in Jb), Wi 10:20 18:5, 12, al.;]
with one mind, with one accord: Ac 1:14 2:46 4:24 5:12 7:57 8:6 12:20 15:25 18:12 19:29, Ro 15:6 (Hatch, Essays, 63 f., argues that the un-cl. sense together, which is found in Jb 3:18 38:33, Nu 24:24, Wi 18:5, 12 (but not 10:20), al., should be attached to the NT instances, but v. Abbott, Essays, 96; MM, xviii).†

strong.derivation: from G3664 (ὅμοιος) and the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές (< ὅμοιος, πάσχω), [in LXX: Wi 7:3, IV Mac 12:13*;]
of like feelings or affections: c. dat., Ac 14:15, Ja 5:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὁμοιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< ὅμοιος), [in LXX: Ge 1:11, 12 (מִין), Wi 14:19, IV Mac 15:4*;]
likeness: καθ’ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, He 4:15; id. c. gen. (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of), He 7:15.†

strong.kjv: made like to, likeness, shape, similitude

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὁμοίωμα, -τος, τό (< ὁμοιόω), [in LXX for דְּמוּת, תַּבְנִית, תְּמוּנָה, etc.;]
that which is made like something;
(a). concrete, an image, likeness (Ps 105 (106):20, Ez 1:5, I Mac 3:48, al.): Re 9:7;
(b). abstract, likeness, resemblance: Ro 5:14 6:5 8:3, Phl 2:7; ἐν ὁ. εἰκόνος, Ro 1:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὁμοίωσις, -εως, ἡ (ὁμοιόω), [in LXX chiefly for דְּמוּת, Ps 57 (58):4, al.;]
1. a making like, becoming like (Plat.).
2. likeness: Ja 3:9(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ (< ὁμολογέω), [in LXX: De 12:6, 17, Am 4:5, Ez 46:12 (נְדָבָה), Le 22:18, Je 51 (44):25 (נֶדֶר), I Es 9:8*;]
1. in cl., an agreement, assent, compact (in π., of a contract; Deiss., BS, 249).
2. confession (prob. always in an objective sense): II Co 9:13, I Ti 6:12, 13, He 3:1 4:14 10:13.†

strong.derivation: adverb of present passive participle of G3670 (ὁμολογέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὁμολογουμένως, adv. (< ὁμολογέω), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:31 7:16 16:1*;]
1. as agreed, conformably with.
2. confessedly, by common consent: I Ti 3:16.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5078 (τέχνη);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὁμότεχνος, -ον (< ὁμός, τέχνη),
practising the same craft, of the same trade: Ac 18:3.†

strong.def: akin to G260 (ἅμα)) as adverb; at the same place or time

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὁμοῦ, adv. (< ὁμός),
together;
(a). prop., of place: Jo 21:2, Ac 2:1;
(b). without idea of place: Jo 4:36 20:4.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5424 (φρήν);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὁμόφρων, -ον (< ὁμός, φρήν), = ὁμόνοος,
agreeing, of one mind: I Pe 3:8.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ);
strong.def: at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὅμως, adv. (< ὁμίς),
yet: ὅ. μέντοι, but yet, nevertheless, Jo 12:42; by hyperbaton, out of its proper position, I Co 14:7, Ga 3:15 (but v. Bl., § 77, 14).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * ὄναρ, τό,
indecl., used only in nom, and acc. sing. (the other cases are supplied by ὄνειρος), a dream: κατ’ ὄ. (in later writers only), in a dream, Mt 1:20 2:12, 13, 19, 22 27:19.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3688 (ὄνος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὀνάριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὄνος),
a young ass: Jo 12:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 † ὀνειδισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (ὀνειδίζω), [in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה;]
a reproach: Ro 15:3, He 10:33; εἰς ὀ. ἐμπεσεῖν, I Ti 3:7; ὁ ὀ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ, He 11:26 13:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. profitable, < ὄνησις, profit),
Onesimus: Col 4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; v. MM, iii, xviii).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G3685 (ὀνίνημι) and G5411 (φόρος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ὀνησίφορος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. bringing advantage),
Onesiphorus: II Ti 1:16 4:19.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (, to slur);
strong.def: for which another prolonged form () is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 (ὄνομα) through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὀνίνημι, [in LXX: To 3:8, Si 30:2*;]
to profit, benefit, help; mid., to have profit, derive benefit: optat. (M, Pr., 195), c. gen., Phm 20.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν) ("acid");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 (KJV) ὀξύς, -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX: Ps 56 (57):4, al. (חַד), Am 2:15 (קַל), Is 5:28 (שׁנן), etc.;]
1. sharp: Re 1:16 2:12 14:14, 17, 18 19:15.
2. Of motion, swift: Ro 3:15 (LXX ταχινός).†

strong.def: to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὁπλίζω (< ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Je 52:25*;]
to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; fig., ἔννοιαν: I Pe 4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-οπλίζω).†

strong.derivation: probably from a primary (to be busy about);
strong.def: an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὅπλον, -ου, τό, [in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה, etc.;]
1. a tool, implement, instrument: ὅπλα ἀδικίας (opp. to ὅ. δικαιοσύνης), Ro 6:13.
2. Freq., in pl., arms, weapons: Jo 18:3, II Co 10:4; metaph., τ. φωτός, Ro 13:12; τ. δικαιοσύνης, II Co 6:7.†

strong.def: of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent G5108 (τοιοῦτος) of quality)
strong.kjv: what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ὁποῖος, -οία, -οῖον, [in LXX: Ca 5:10, II Mac 11:37*;]
of what sort: I Co 3:13, Ga 2:6, I Th 1:9, Ja 1:24; τοιοῦτος ὁ., such as, Ac 26:29.†

strong.derivation: a (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice) ; which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternate of G3708 (ὁράω);
strong.def: to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from G991 (βλέπω), which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from G1492 (εἴδω), which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while G2300 (θεάομαι), and still more emphatically its intensive G2334 (θεωρέω), signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and G4648 (σκοπέω) a watching from a distance)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὀπτάνω, [in LXX: III Ki 8:8 (ראה ni.), To 12:19*;]
late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. c. dat., Ac 1:3. (For exx. from π., v. Deiss., LAE, 79, 2525; MM, ii, xviii.).†

strong.derivation: apparently from the base of G3796 (ὀψέ) and G5610 (ὥρα);
strong.def: properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Je 31 (48):32 47 (40):10, 12 (קַיִץ)*;]
1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September).
2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Re 18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†

strong.def: something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 ὅραμα, -τος, τό (< ὁράω), [in LXX for חָזוֹן, מַרְאֶה, etc.;]
that which is seen;
(a). a sight, spectacle: Mt 17:9, Ac 7:31;
(b). an appearance, vision: Ac 9:10, 12(Rec.) 10:3, 17, 19 11:5 12:9 16:9, 10 18:9 (cf. ὀπτασία).†

strong.def: the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὅρασις, -εως, ἡ (ὁράω), [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה, חָזוֹן and cognate forms;]
1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes.
2. appearance (Nu 24:4, Ez 1:5, Si 41:20, al.): Re 4:3.
3. = ὅραμα, a vision: Ac 2:17(LXX), Re 9:17.†

strong.def: gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὁρατός, -ή, -όν (ὁράω),
visible: τὰ ὁ., Col 1:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀργίλος, -η, -ον (< ὀργή), [in LXX: Pr 22:24 29:22 (חֵמָה), etc.;]
inclined to anger, passionate: Tit 1:7.†

strong.def: a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ὀργυιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (< ὀρέγω),
the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: Ac 27:28.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735 (ὄρος));
strong.def: to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ὀρέγω, [in Sm.: Jb 8:20, Ez 16:49*;]
to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaph., to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: c. gen. rei, I Ti 3:1, He 11:16; φιλαργυρίας (v. Ellic. and CGT, in l.), I Ti 6:10.†

strong.def: excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὄρεξις, -εως, ἡ (< ὀρέγομαι), [in LXX Wi 14:2 15:5 16:2, 3, Si 18:30 23:6, IV Mac 1:33, 35*;]
the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, Ro 1:27.

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and G4228 (πούς);
strong.def: to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ (< ὀρθό-πους, going straight),
= cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaph., Ga 2:14 (not elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G3735 (ὄρος);
strong.def: right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀρθός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX chiefly for יָשָׁר;]
straight;
(a). in height, straight, upright: Ac 14:10;
(b). in line, straight, direct: fig., He 12:13(LXX).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος), to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ (< ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: Pr 3:6 11:6 (ישׁר pi.)*;]
to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, fig., Pr 3:6 11:6). Metaph., τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, II Ti 2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l.; not found elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3727 (ὅρκος) and a derivative of G3660 (ὀμνύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ (< ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; v. MM, xviii), [in LXX: Ez 17:18, 19 (אָלָה) I Es 9:93*;]
affirmation on oath, an oath: He 7:20, 21, 28.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὁρμή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX: Pr 3:25 (שֹׁאָה), etc.;]
1. a violent movement, impulse: Ja 3:4;
2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. Ac 14:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὅρμημα, -τος, τό (ὁρμάω), [in LXX: Ho 5:10, Am 1:11 (עֶבְרָה), etc.;]
a rush: Re 18:21.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3733 (ὄρνις);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὄρνεον, -ου, τό, = ὄρνις, [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר;]
a bird: Re 18:2 19:17, 21 (Hom., al.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of the base of G3725 (ὅριον) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὁροθεσία, -ας, ἡ (< ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι),
a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; Ac 17:26.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀρφανός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX for יָתוֹם;]
1. prop., orphan, fatherless: Mk 12:40, WH, mg, Ja 1:27.
2. In a general sense (as also in cl.; v. LS, s.v.; and cf. MM, xviii), bereft, friendless, desolate: Jo 14:18.†

strong.def: how (i.e. with G302 (ἄν), so) many times as

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὁσάκις (< ὅσος),
relat. adv., as often as: seq. ἐάν (q.v.), I Co 11:25, 26, Re 11:6.†

strong.derivation: of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from 1342, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from G2413 (ἱερός), which denotes formal consecration;
strong.def: and from G40 (ἅγιος), which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. hallowed (pious, sacred, sure)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ὅσιος, -ον (so sometimes in cl., but most freq. -α, -ον), [in LXX chiefly for חָסִיד, also for טָהוֹר, יָשָׁר, תָּמִים;]
religiously right, righteous, pious, Holy: of men, Tit 1:8, He 7:26; by meton., ὁ. χεῖρας, I Ti 2:8 (cf. De 32:4); of God, Re 15:4 16:5; as subst., ὁ ὅ., of the Messiah, Ac 2:27 13:35 (LXX); τὰ ὅ. Δανεὶδ τ. πιστά (Field, Notes, 121), Ac 13:34(LXX).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὁσίως (< ὅσιος), adv., [in LXX: III Ki 8:61, Wi 6:10*;]
piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, v. M, Th., 24 f.), I Th 2:10.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὀσμή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὄζω), [in LXX chiefly for רֵיחַ;]
a smell, odour: Jo 12:3; metaph. (EV, savour), II Co 2:14, 16; of the effect of sacrifice (cf. רֵיחַ הַגִּיחֹחַ, Ge 8:21, al., v.s. εὐωδία), ὀ. εὐωδίας, Eph 5:2, Phl 4:18.†

strong.def: earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀστράκινος -η, -ον (< ὄστρακον, an earthen vessel or potsherd), [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶשׂ;]
made of clay, earthen: II Co 4:7, II Ti 2:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ (ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell),
the sense of smell, smelling: I Co 12:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** οὐδαμῶς (< οὐδαμός, not even one), adv., [in LXX: II-IV Mac8*;]
in no wise, by no means: Mt 2:6 (OT).†

strong.kjv: as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 οὐδέπω, adv., [in LXX: Ex 9:30 (טֶרֶם)*;]
not yet: Lk 23:53, Jo 7:39 19:41 20:9, Ac 8:16.†

strong.def: is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 οὐκοῦν, adv. (< οὔκουν, not therefore),
with the negative element lost, therefore, so then: Jo 18:37.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 οὐρά, -ᾶς, ἡ, [in LXX for זָנָב;]
a tail: Re 9:10, 19 12:4.†

strong.derivation: from G3772 (οὐρανός) and the enclitic of source;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** οὐρανόθεν (< οὐρανός), adv., [in LXX: IV Mac 4:10*;]
from heaven: Ac 14:17 26:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Οὐρβανός, -οῦ, ὁ (Lat. Urbanus),
Urban: Ro 16:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Οὐρίας, -ου, ὁ (Heb. אוּרִיָּה),
Uriah: Mt 1:6.†

strong.def: indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ὀφειλή, -ῆς, ἡ (< ὀφείλω),
a debt: Mt 18:32; metaph., one's due: Ro 13:7, I Co 7:3 (found also in π.; v. Deiss., BS, 221; MM, xviii).†

strong.def: something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀφείλημα, -τος, τό (< ὀφείλω), [in LXX: De 24:10 (מַשָּׁאָה), I Es 3:20, I Mac 15:8*;]
that which is owed, a debt: Ro 4:4; metaph. (as Aram. חוֺבָא, חוֺב), of sin as a debt, Mt 6:12.†

strong.derivation: first person singular of a past tense of G3784 (ὀφείλω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὄφελον, 2 aor. of ὀφείλω, without the augment (v. M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish; [in LXX (with aor. indic.): Ex 16:3 (מִי־יִתֵּן), Nu 14:3 (2) 20:3 (לוּא), Ps 118 (119):5 (אַחֲלֵי), etc.;]
would that: with indic. aor., I Co 4:8; impf., II Co 11:1, Re 3:15; fut., Ga 5:12 (a practicable wish, v. Bl., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)†

strong.derivation: from (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὄφελος, -ους, τό (< ὀφέλλω, to increase), [in LXX: Jb 15:3 (יעל hi.)*;]
advantage, help: I Co 15:32, Ja 2:14, 16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ὀφθαλμο-δουλία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (< ὀφθαλμός, δοῦλος),
eye-service: Eph 6:6, Col 3:22 (not found elsewhere).†

strong.def: to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ὀχλέω, -ῶ (< ὄχλος), [in LXX: To 6:7, III Mac 5:41*;]
to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass., Ac 5:16 (act. absol., = pass., to be in a tumult, III Mac 5.41; cf. ἐν-, παρ-εν-οχλέω, and v. MM, xviii).†

strong.def: to make a crowd, i.e. raise a public disturbance

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ὀχλο-ποιέω, -ῶ,
to gather a crowd, make a riot: Ac 17:5 (not elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: from a remote derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀχύρωμα, -τος, τό (< ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm), [in LXX for מִבְצָר, etc.;]
a stronghold, fortress (Ps 88 (89):40, Na 3:12, 14 al.); in LXX and NT, also metaph. of that in which confidence is placed (Pr 10:29 21:22, al.): II Co 10:4.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G3702 (ὀπτός);
strong.def: a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** ὀψάριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὄψον, (1) cooked meat; (2) a relish or dainty, esp. fish, cf. MGr. τὸ ψάρι, fish; in comic poets and late prose writers only), [in LXX: To 2:2 א (B ὄψον)*;]
fish: Jo 6:9, 11 21:9, 10, 13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὄψιμος, -ον (< ὀψέ), [in LXX: De 11:14, Pr 16:15, Ho 6:4 (3), Jl 2:23, Za 10:1, Je 5:24 (מַלְקוֹשׁ), Ex 9:32 (אָפִיל)*;] poët. and late for ὄψιος,
late: ὑετὸς ὄ., the latter rain (v. DB, s.v. "rain"), with ellipsis of ὑετός (v. WM, 740), Ja 5:7.†

strong.def: properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὄψις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה;]
1. the act of seeing, the sense of sight.
2. face, countenance: Jo 11:44, Re 1:16.
3. appearance: κατ’ ὄ. κρίνειν (v. MM, xviii), Jo 7:24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † παγιδεύω (< παγίς), [in LXX: I Ki 28:9 (נקשׁ hith.), Ec 9:12 (יקשׁ pu.)*;]
to ensnare: metaph., c. acc., ἐν λόγῳ, Mt 22:15 (not elsewhere).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3806 (πάθος);
strong.def: something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 * πάθημα, -τος, τό (< πάσχω), like πάθος,
1. that which befalls one, a suffering, affliction: pl., Ro 8:18, II Co 1:6, 7, Col 1:24, II Ti 3:11, He 2:10 10:32, I Pe 5:9; of Christ's sufferings: τὰ εἰς Χ., I Pe 1:11; τ. Χριστσῦ, I Pe 5:1; id. as shared by Christians, II Co 1:5, Phl 3:10, I Pe 4:13.
2. a passive emotion, affection, passion: Ga 5:24; τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, Ro 7:5.
3. = τὸ πάσχειν, an enduring or suffering: c. gen. obj., He 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παθητός, -ή, -όν (< πάσχω),
1. one who has suffered.
2. subject to suffering (R, mg., v. M, Pr., 222) or destined to suffer (AV, R, txt.): Ac 26:23.†

strong.def: properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πάθος, -ους, τό (< πάσχω), [in LXX: Jb 30:31 (אֵבֶל), Pr 25:20, and very freq. in IV Mac (1:1 ff., al.)*;] like πάθημα;
1. that which befalls one, that which one suffers.
2. a passive emotion or affection (esp. of violent emotion), a passion, passionate desire; in NT always in bad sense: Col 3:5; π. ἀτιμίας, Ro 1:26; π. ἐπιθυμίας, I Th 4:5.†

strong.derivation: from G3816 (παῖς) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue"))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * παιδαγωγός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παῖς, ἄγω),
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opp. to πατήρ, I Co 4:15; fig., of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, Ga 3:24, 25.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3816 (παῖς);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παιδάριον, -ου, τό, dimin. of παῖς, [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר;]
a little boy, a lad (in late and colloq. Gk. the word seems to be used with greater latitude and even to lose its dimin. force entirely; cf. To 6:2, 3, and v. MM, xviii): Jo 6:9.†

strong.def: tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 παιδεία (-ία, T), -ας, ἡ (< παιδεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מוּסָר;]
1. the rearing of a child (Æsch.).
2. training, learning, instruction (Plat., al.): Eph 6:4, II Ti 3:16.
3. As in LXX (Pr 3:11 15:5, al.), chastening, discipline: He 12:5(LXX), 7, 8, 11.†

strong.def: a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παιδευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (< παιδεύω), [in LXX: Ho 5:2 (מוּסָר), Si 37:19, IV Mac 5:34 9:6*;]
1. prop., a teacher, instructor: Ro 2:20.
2. a corrector, one who disciplines (cf. Ho 5:2): He 12:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παίζω (< παῖς), [in LXX: Ge 21:9 26:8, Ex 32:6 (צחק pi.); and more freq. (Jg 16:25, al.) for (שׁחק pi.;]
prop., to play as a child, hence, generally, to play (as with singing and dancing): I Co 10:7(LXX) (cf. ἐμ-παίζω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παλαιότης, -ητος, ἡ (< παλαιός),
oldness: γράμματος, Ro 7:6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πάλη, -ης, ἡ (< πάλλω, to sway)
wrestling, hence, generally, fight, contest: fig., of the spiritual combat of Christians, Eph 6:12.†

strong.def: (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† παλινγενεσία (Rec. παλιγγ-), -ας, ἡ (< πάλιν, γένεσις),
new birth, renewal, restoration, regeneration;
(a). of persons (Plut., Phil., al.), of spiritual regeneration, διὰ λουτροῦ παλινγενεστίας (gen. attr., v. Ellic., in l.), Tit 3:5;
(b). of the world, as in Stoics, Jewish Apocal., al. (v. Dalman, Words, 177 ff.), Mt 19:28.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G4443 (πυρά);
strong.def: every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (G5561 (χώρα) being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 Παμφυλία, -ας, ἡ,
Pamphylia, a province of Asia Minor: Ac 2:10 13:13 14:24 15:38 27:5.†

strong.derivation: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πανήγυρις, -εως, ἡ (< πᾶς + ἄγυρας = ἀγορά), [in LXX: Ho 2:11 (13) 9:5, Ez 46:11 (מוֹעֵד), Am 5:21 (עֲצָרָה)*;]
prop., a national festal assembly in honour of a god; hence, generally, any festal assembly: He 12:23 (for exx. in π., v. MM, xviii).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πανοικεί (Rec., LTr., -κί), adv. (< πᾶς, οἶκος), a word rejected by strict Atticists, though found once in Plat. (Eryx., 392 c); [in LXX: Ex 1:1 (בַּיִת), III Mac 3:27 (where A in each case reads -κίᾳ, the Attic form, cf. Ge 50:8, al.)*;]
with all the household: Ac 16:34.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πανοῦργος, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for עָרוּם;]
ready to do anything;
(a). in cl., chiefly in bad sense, knavish, crafty: II Co 12:16;
(b). in good sense, skilful, clever (Pr 13:1 28:2).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** πάντῃ (Rec. -τη), adv. (< πᾶς), [in LXX: Si 50:22, III Mac 4:1*;]
every way, entirely: Ac 24:3.†

strong.def: the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 † παντοκράτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (< πᾶς, κρατέω), [in LXX: freq. in Jb 5:8, 17, al. (שַׁדַּי), and for צְבָאוֹת, in the phrase θεός (κυρίος) π., II Ki 5:10, al., and freq. in Am, Za, Ma; also in Wi 7:25, Si 42:17 50:14, 17, and freq. in Jth, II, III Mac;]
almighty: II Co 6:18, Re 1:8 4:8 11:17 15:3 16:7, 14 19:6, 15 21:22.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G939 (βάσις);
strong.def: to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 παρα-βαίνω, [in LXX for סוּר, עבר, פּרר hi., שׂטה, etc.;]
1. in Hom. (twice), to go by the side of, stand beside.
2. In Æsch., Herod., Thuc., al., to go past or pass over, chiefly metaph., to overstep, violate, transgress (Jos 7:11, Ez 16:59, Si 40:14, al.): τ. παράδοσιν, Mt 15:2; τ. ἐντολήν, Mt 15:3; seq. ἀπό (as סוּר מִן, De 17:20, al.), to turn aside, fall away (cf. π. τῆς ἀληθείας, Arist., Cael., i, 5, 2): Ac 1:25.†

strong.def: to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-βάλλω, [in LXX: Pr 2:2 4:20 5:1, 13 22:17 (נטה hi.), Ru 2:16 (שׁלל), II Mac 14:38 (elsewhere as v.l.4)*;]
1. to throw to or beside, as fodder to horses (Hom., al.).
2. to lay beside, compare (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mk 4:30, Rec.
3. Reflexive, to betake oneself, come near; of seamen, to cross over: εἰς Σάμον, Ac 20:15.
4. In mid. = παρα-βολεύομαι, q.v.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ (< παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Ps 100 (101):3 (סֵטִים), IV Ki 2:24 A, Wi 14:31, II Mac 15:10*;]
1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.).
2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaph., transgression (Plut., al.): Ro 4:15 5:14, He 2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Ro 2:23; ἐν π., I Ti 2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Ga 3:19.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** παρα-βάτης, -ου, ὁ (< παραβαίνω), [in Sm.: Ps 16 (17):4 138 (139):19, Je 6:28*;]
1. one who stands beside, the warrior who stands by the charioteer (cf. παραβαίνω, 1).
2. a transgressor (Æsch., παρβάτης): Ga 2:18, Ja 2:9; π. νόμου, Ro 2:25, 27, Ja 2:11.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G1011 (βουλεύω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρα-βολεύομαι
= cl. παραβάλλομαι (II Mac 14:38),
to expose oneself to danger, hazard one's life: c. dat. ref., τ. ψυχῇ (v. M, Pr., 64), Phl 2:30 (Rec. παραβουλ-). Cited by Deiss., LAE, 84, 120.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 * παρ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ (< παραγγέλλω),
an instruction, charge, command: Ac 5:28 16:24, I Th 4:2, I Ti 1:5, 18. (In Xen., Polyb., of a military order.)†

strong.def: to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy
strong.kjv: make a public example, put to an open shame

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † παρα-δειγματίζω (< δείκνυμι), [in LXX: Nu 25:4 (יקע hi.), Je 13:22 (חמס ni.), Ez 28:17 (רַאֲוָה), Es 4:17, Da LXX 2:5*;]
to set forth as an example; in bad sense, to put to open shame: He 6:6 (Polyb., Plut., al.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G1304 (διατρίβω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρα-δια-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ,
useless wrangling: v.l. in Rec. for διαπαρατριβή (q.v.), I Ti 6:5.†

strong.def: to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † παρα-ζηλόω, -ῶ, [in LXX: De 32:21, III Ki 14:22, Ps 77 (78):58 (קנא pi., hi.), Ps 36 (37):1, 7, 8 (חרה hith.), Si 30:3*;]
to provoke to jealousy: Ro 10:19(LXX) 11:11, 14, I Co 10:22.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-θαλάσσιος, -α, -ον (< παρά, θάλασσα), [in LXX: Je 29 (47):7 (היָּם חוֹף), etc.;]
by the sea: Mt 4:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρα-θεωρέω, -ῶ,
1. to examine side by side, compare.
2. to overlook, neglect: pass., Ac 6:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 παρα-θήκη, -ης, ἡ (< παρατίθημι), [in LXX: Le 6:2, 4 (5:21, 23) (פִּקָּדוֹן), and in To 10:13, II Mac 3:10, 15, v.l. for παρακαταθήκη (q.v.)*;]
a deposit or trust: I Ti 6:20, II Ti 1:12, 14 (for exx. of this form, v. MM, Exp., iii, xviii).†

strong.def: to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** παρ-αινέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: II Mac 7:25, 26, III Mac 5:17 7:12*;]
to exhort, advise: c. acc. pers. et inf. (v. Bl., § 72, 5; M, Pr., 205), Ac 27:22; absol., seq. λέγων, Ac 27:9.†

strong.def: to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** παρά-κειμαι, [in LXX: Jdt.3.2, 3, Si 30:18 34 (31):16, Da LXX Bel 1:14, II, III Mac5*;]
to lie beside, be near, be present: Ro 7:18, 21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ** παρά-κλητος, -ον (< παρακαλέω), [in Aq., Th.: Jb 16:2*;]
called to one's aid in a judicial cause (Dion. Cass.); hence, most freq. as subst., ὁ π., an advocate, pleader, intercessor (Dem., al.; so in Rabbinic lit., פְּרַקְלִיטָא), "a friend of the accused person, called to speak to his character, or otherwise enlist sympathy in his favour" (Field, Notes, 102). In NT, specif., ὁ π.,
(a). of Christ, I Jo 2:1 (v. ICC, Jo. Epp., 23 ff.);
(b). of the Holy Spirit (AV, comforter; but v. opp. c.), Jo 14:16, 26 15:26 16:7 (cf. also Abbott, Essays, 86, 97; Deiss., LAE, 339 f.; MM, xviii; Westc., Jo., ii, 188 ff.).

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * παρ-ακοή, -ῆς, ἡ,
1. a hearing amiss (Plat.).
2. Later, as following inattention, disobedience: Ro 5:19, II Co 10:6, He 2:2 (cf. παρακούω, and v. Tr., Syn., § lxvi).†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense);
strong.def: (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. sail past

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * παρα-λέγω,
to lay beside; mid.,
(a). to lie beside (Hom.);
(b). later, of sailors, to sail past: c. acc., Ac 27:8, 13.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω);
strong.def: transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρ-αλλαγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< παραλλάσσω), [in LXX: IV Ki 9:20 (שִׁגָּעוֹן)*;]
in various senses (LS, s.v.), change: Ja 1:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παρα-λογίζομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רמה pi.;]
1. to miscalculate.
2. to reason falsely, hence, to mislead: Col 2:4, Ja 1:22.†

strong.def: to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 παρα-μένω, [in LXX: Pr 12:7, Da TH 11:17 (עמד), etc.;]
to remain beside or near: He 7:23, Ja 1:25; of remaining alive, I Co 16:6 (WH, κατα-), Phl 1:25 (cf. συμ-παραμένω).†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of a derivative of G3454 (μῦθος);
strong.def: to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** παρα-μυθέομαι, -οῦμαι, [in LXX: II Mac 15:9 (Sm.8)*;]
1. to encourage, exhort.
2. to comfort, console: c. acc. pers., Jo 11:31, I Th 2:11 5:14; id. seq. περί, Jo 11:19.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** παραμυθία, -ας, ἡ (< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 19:12*;]
1. encouragement, exhortation.
2. comfort, consolation: I Co 14:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** παραμύθιον, -ου, τό (< παραμυθέομαι), [in LXX: Wi 3:18*;]
1. an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: Phl 2:1 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; v. Lft. and ICC, Phl 2:1).
2. assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wi 3:18, and freq. in cl.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3551 (νόμος);
strong.def: to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-νομέω, ῶ, [in LXX for חלל, etc., chiefly in Pss and II Mac;]
to be a παράνομος, to transgress the law: Ac 23:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρανομία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Ps 36 (37):7 (מְזִמָּה), etc.;]
law-breaking, transgression: II Pe 2:16.†

strong.def: to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † παρα-πικραίνω, [in LXX chiefly for מרה qal., hi., מְרִי, most freq. in Pss and Ez;]
to embitter, provoke: absol. (yet sc. τ. θεόν, cf. Ps 105 (106):7, Ez 2:5-8, al., and with τὸν θ. added, Ps 5:4, Ez 20:21, al.), He 3:16 (cf. παραπικρασμός).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παραπικραίνω), [in LXX: Ps 94 (95):8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Ex 17:7; ἀντιλογία, De 33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Nu 20:24)*;]
provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), He 3:8, 15(LXX).†

strong.def: to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-πίπτω, [in LXX: Ez 14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 (מעל), 22:4 (אשׁם), Es 6:10 (נפל hi.), Wi 6:9 12:2, II Mac 10:4 A*;]
1. most freq. (Hdt., Thuc., al.), to fall in one's way, befall.
2. to fall into or in (seq. εἰς, Polyb.; c. dat., II Mac 10:4).
3. to fall away (Ez 14:13 15:8 18:24 20:27 22:4, Wi 6:9 12:2; in Polyb., c. gen.): absol., He 6:6.
4. to fail (λόγος, Es 6:10; cf. I Ki 3:19).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρα-πλέω,
to sail by or past: c. acc., Ac 20:16.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4139 (πλησίον) (as adverb);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρα-πλήσιος, -α, -ον (Hdt., Plat., al.; also -ος, -ον, Thuc., Polyb.),
coming near, nearly resembling. Neut. -ον, adverbially, = ίως, in a way nearly resembling: c. dat., Phl 2:27.†

strong.derivation: adverb from the same as G3897 (παραπλήσιον);
strong.def: in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** παρα-πλησίως, adv. (< παραπλήσιος), [in Quint.: Ho 8:6*;]
in like manner: He 2:14.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the alternate of G4482 (ῥέω);
strong.def: to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-ρρέω, [in LXX: Is 44:4 (יבל), Pr 3:21*;]
to flow by, drift away, slip away: He 2:1.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);
strong.def: side-marked, i.e. labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** παράσημος, -ον (< σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: III Mac 2:29*;]
1. in cl., marked amiss, spurious, counterfeit. Later,
2. marked at the side, annotated (Plut.).
3. marked with a sign (LXX); as subst., a figurehead: Ac 28:11 (v. MM, xix).†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος);
strong.def: to furnish aside, i.e. get ready

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 παρα-σκευάζω, [in LXX: Je 27 (50):42 (ערךְ), etc.;]
to prepare, make ready: absol. (sc. τ. δεῖπνον, etc.; of. Hdt., ix, 82, II Mac 2:27), Ac 10:10; mid., to prepare, make preparations: I Co 14:8 (cf. Je 50:42); pass., II Co 9:2, 3.†

strong.def: to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-τείνω, [in LXX: Nu 23:28 (שׁקף ni.), etc.;]
to extend, prolong: τ. λόγον, Ac 20:7.†

strong.def: to chance near, i.e. fall in with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρα-τυγχάνω,
to happen to be near or present: Ac 17:17.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G846 (αὐτός);
strong.def: at the very instant, i.e. momentary

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρ-αυτίκα, adv. (< πάραυτα = παρ’ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα), [in LXX: Ps 69 (70):3, To 4:14*;]
1. immediately.
2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: II Co 4:17.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρα-φρονέω (< παρά, φρήν), [in LXX: Za 7:11 (סרר)*;]
to be beside oneself, be deranged: II Co 11:23.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρα-φρονία, -ας, ἡ, = cl. παραφροσύνη,
madness: II Pe 2:16.†

strong.def: to winter near, i.e. stay with over the rainy season

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * παρα-χειμάζω,
to winter at a place: seq. εἰς, Ac 27:12; ἐν, Ac 28:11; πρὸς ὑμᾶς, I Co 16:6; ἐκεῖ, Tit 3:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρα-χειμασία, -ας, ἡ (< παρα-χειμάζω),
a wintering: Ac 27:12 (Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πάρδαλις, -εως, ἡ, [in LXX for נָמֵר, Ca 4:8, Ho 13:7, Is 11:6, al.;]
a panther, leopard: Re 13:2.†

strong.def: to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-εισ-άγω,
1. to lead in by one's side, bring forward, introduce.
2. In late writers, to introduce or bring in secretly: II Pe 2:1.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρ-είσ-ακτος, -ον (< παρεισάγω),
brought in secretly (as spies or traitors): Ga 2:4.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and a compound of G1519 (εἰς) and G1416 (δύνω);
strong.def: to settle in alongside, i.e. lodge stealthily

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-εισ-δύω (also -δύνω),
to slip in secretly, steal in: παρεισεδύησαν (vulgar aor.; pass. for act., Bl., § 19, 2), Ju 4 (cf. also MM, xix).†

strong.def: to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * παρ-εισ-έρχομαι,
1. to come in beside or by the way: Ro 5:20.
2. to come in secretly, steal in: Ga 2:4.†

strong.def: to bear in alongside, i.e. introduce simultaneously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-εισ-φέρω,
to bring in or supply besides: σπουδὴν π. (late Gk. for cl. σ. ποιεῖσθαι; cf. Deiss., BS, 361), II Pe 1:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† παρ-εκτός, = cl. παρέκ, -έξ, [in Aq.: De 1:36; Al., Le 23:38*;]
1. as adv., besides, in addition: τὰ π. (sc. γινόμενα), II Co 11:28.
2. As prep. c. gen., except: Mt 5:32 19:9 (WH, mg., R, mg.), Ac 26:29.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G1685 (ἐμβάλλω);
strong.def: a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 παρ-εμ-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (< παρεμβάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲנֶה;]
1. an insertion, interpolation (Æschin.).
2. In the Macedonian dialect (Rutherford, NPhr., 473), as a military term;
(a). an army in battle array: He 11:34 (cf. Ex 14:19, 20, Jg 4:16, al.; freq. in Polyb.);
(b). a camp (Ex 29:14, al.): He 13:11, 13, Re 20:9;
(c). barracks, soldiers' quarters: Ac 21:34, 37 22:24 23:10, 16, 32 28:16 (WH, txt., R, om.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρ-εν-οχλέω, -ῶ (cf. ἐνοχλέω), [in LXX for לאה hi. (Mi 6:3), etc.;]
to annoy concerning a matter (παρά): c. dat. pers., Ac 15:19.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G1927 (ἐπιδημέω);
strong.def: an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † παρ-επί-δημος, -ον (v.s. ἐπιδημέω), [in LXX: Ge 23:4, Ps 38 (39):12 (תּוֹשָׁב)*;]
sojourning in a strange place; as subst., ὁ π., a sojourner: of Christians, I Pe 1:1; ξένοι καὶ π., He 11:13; πάροικοι καὶ π., I Pe 2:11 (v. Deiss., BS, 149).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πάρεσις, -εως, ἡ (< παρίημι),
1. a letting go, dismissal.
2. prætermission, passing by (of debt or sin): Ro 3:25.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (meaning to harangue an assembly);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** παρηγορία, -ας, ἡ (< παρηγορέω, to address, exhort, console), [in LXX: IV Mac 5:12 6:1*;]
1. an address, exhortation (LXX, IV Mac 5:12 6:1).
2. comfort, consolation: Col 4:11.†

strong.def: a Parthian, i.e. inhabitant of Parthia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πάρθος, -ου, ὁ,
a Parthian: Ac 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 παρ-ίημι, [in LXX: Je 4:31 (פּרשׂ pi.), etc.;]
1. to pass by or over, let alone, disregard: Lk 11:42.
2. to relax, loosen; pass., to be relaxed, weakened, exhausted: παρειμένας χεῖρας, He 12:12 (LXX ἀνειμ-).†

strong.derivation: probably by contraction for (a derivative of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3306 (μένω));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Παρμενᾶς, ᾶ, ὁ,
Parmenas: Ac 6:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πάρ-οδος, -ου, ἡ, [in LXX: Ge 38:14 (דֶּרֶךְ), etc.;]
a passing or passage: ἐν π., in passing, I Co 16:7.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † παρ-οικία, -ας, ἡ (< παροικέω, q.v.), [in LXX: II Es 8:35 (גּוֹלָה), Ps 33 (34):4 54 (55):15 118 (119):54 119 (120):5, La 2:22 (מגוֹר; and cogn. forms), Hb 3:16, I Es 5:7, Jth 5:9, Wi 19:10, Si prol. 26 16:8 41:5 44:6, III Mac 6:36 7:19*;]
a sojourning: Ac 13:17, I Pe 1:17.†

strong.def: having a home near, i.e. (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 πάρ-οικος, -ον, [in LXX chiefly for גֵּר, תּוֹשַׁב;]
1. in cl. Attic, dwelling near, neighbouring; as subst., a neighbour.
2. In late writers (LXX, Philo) and in Inscr. (Deiss., BS, 227 f.; Kennedy, Sources, 102), foreign, alien; as subst., an alien, a sojourner: Ac 7:6(LXX), 29; metaph., ξένοι καὶ π. (opp. to συμπολίτης), Eph 2:19; π. καὶ παρεπιδήμους (q.v.), I Pe 2:11 (v. Lft. on Clem. Rom., 1 Co., § 1).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and perhaps a derivative of G3633 (οἴομαι);
strong.def: apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 παροιμία, -ας, ἡ (< πάροιμος, by the way), [in LXX. Pr tit 1:1 25:1, (מָשָׁל) subscr., Si 6:35 8:8 18:29 39:3 47:17*;]
1. a wayside saying (Hesych.; v. LS, s.v.), a byword, maxim, proverb: II Pe 2:22.
2. In NT, of figurative discourse (as מָשָׁל, Is 14:4, al.), a parable, allegory: Jo 10:6 16:25, 29 (v. Abbott, Essays, 82 ff.).†

strong.def: staying near wine, i.e. tippling (a toper)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† πάρ-οινος, -ον, = cl., παροινικός (παρά, οἶνος),
given to wine, drunken: I Ti 3:3, Tit 1:7.†

strong.def: to escape along, i.e. be gone

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-οίχομαι,
to have passed by; of time, to be gone by: ἐν τ. παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς, Ac 14:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† παρ-ομοιάζω,
to be like: c. dat., Mt 23:27.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G3691 (ὀξύς);
strong.def: to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παρ-οξύνω, [in LXX for נאץ, קצף, רגז, etc.;]
1. primarily, but never so in cl., to sharpen (μάχαιραν, De 32:41, שׁנן).
2. Metaph., as always in cl.,
(a). to spur on, stimulate (Arist., Xen., al.);
(b). to provoke, rouse to anger (De 9:7, 18, Ps 105 (106):29, al.): pass., Ac 17:16, I Co 13:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παροξυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παροξύνω), [in LXX: De 29:(28) 27, Je 39 (32):37 (קֶצֶף)*;]
1. stimulation, provocation: π. ἀγάπης, He 10:14.
2. irritation: Ac 15:39.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παρ-οργίζω, [in LXX chiefly for כּעס hi.;]
(in cl., passive only), to provoke to anger: Ro 10:19(LXX), Eph 6:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † παρ-οργισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< παροργίζω), [in LXX: III Ki 15:30, IV Ki 23:26 (כַּעַס); IV Ki 19:3, Ne 9:18, 26 (נְאָצָה); Je 21:5 A (קֶצֶף)*;]
irritation ("distinguished from ὀργή as implying a less permanent state"; ICC, Eph., 140; and v. Tr., Syn., § xxxvii): Eph 4:26.†

strong.def: to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-οτρύνω,
to urge on, stir up: c. acc. pers., Ac 13:50 (Pind., Hipp., and late writers).†

strong.derivation: from the present participle of G3918 (πάρειμι);
strong.def: a being near, i.e. advent (often, return; specially, of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physically, aspect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 παρ-ουσία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX: Ne 2:6 A, Jth 10:18, II Mac 8:12 15:21, III Mac 3:17*;]
1. usually in cl., a being present, presence: I Co 16:17, II Co 10:10; opp. to ἀπουσία, Phl 2:12 (cf. II Mac 15:21).
2. a coming, arrival, advent (Soph., Eur., Thuc., al., v. LS, s.v.; so Jth 10:18, II Mac 8:12): II Co 7:6, 7, Phl 1:26, II Th 2:9; in late writers (v. M, Th., 145 ff.; MM, xix; LAE, 372 ff.) as technical term for the visit of a king; hence, in NT, specif. of the Advent or Parousia of Christ: Mt 24:3, 27, 37, 39, I Co 15:23, I Th 2:19 3:13 4:15 5:23, II Th 2:1, 8, Ja 5:7, 8, II Pe 1:16 3:4, 12, I Jo 2:28.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G3795 (ὀψάριον);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * παρ-οψίς, -ίδος, ἡ (< παρά, ὄψον; v.s. ὀψάριον),
1. a side-dish of dainties (Xen., al.).
2. In Comic poets and late prose, the dish itself on which the dainties are served: Mt 23:25, 26 (In this sense it is condemned by the Atticists; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 265 f.)†

strong.def: to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 παρρησιάζομαι (< παρρησία), [in LXX: Jb 22:26 (ענג hithp.), Ps 11 (12):5 93 (94):1, Pr 20:9, Ca 8:10, Si 6:11*;]
to speak freely or boldly, be bold in speech: Ac 9:27, 28 13:46 14:3 18:26 19:8 26:26, Eph 6:20, I Th 2:2.†

strong.def: Patara, a place in Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πάταρα, -ων, τὰ,
Patara, a maritime city of Lycia: Ac 21:1.†

strong.def: Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πάτμος, -ου, ἡ,
Patmos, an island in the Ægean Sea: Re 1:9.†

strong.derivation: from G3962 (πατήρ) and the same as the latter part of G3389 (μητραλῴας);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 1 * πατραλῴας, v.s. πατρολῴας.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † πατριάρχης, -ου, ὁ (< πατριά, ἄρχω), [in LXX: I Ch 24:31 (אָב), II Ch 19:8 26:12 (הָאָבוֹת רֹאשׁ), I Ch 27:12 (שַׂר), II Ch 23:20 (שַׂר־הַמֵּאוֹת), IV Mac 7:19 16:25*;]
a patriarch: Ac 2:29 7:8, 9, He 7:4.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 πατρικός, -ή, -όν (< πατήρ), [in LXX for אָב, Ge 50:8, al.;]
paternal, ancestral: Ga 1:14.†

strong.derivation: perhaps a contraction for (a compound of G3962 (πατήρ) and G979 (βίος));

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Πατρόβας, -ᾶ, ὁ,
Patrobas: Ro 16:14.†

strong.derivation: from G3962 (πατήρ) and a derivative of G3860 (παραδίδωμι) (in the sense of handing over or down);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† πατρο-παρά-δοτος, -ον (< πατήρ, παραδίδωμι),
handed down from one's fathers, inherited: I Pe 1:18 (Diod., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 πατρῷος, -α, -ον (< πατήρ), [in LXX: Pr 27:10 (אָב), II Es 7:5, II-IV Mac12*;]
of one's fathers, received from one's fathers: Ac 22:3 24:14 28:17.†

strong.def: (little; but remotely from a derivative of G3973 (παύω), meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
158 Παῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Paulus),
1. Sergius Paulus: Ac 13:7.
2. the Apostle Paul (cf. Σαῦλος): Ac 13:9, and freq. throughout Ac., Ro 1:1, I Co 1:1, al., II Pe 3:15.

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Πάφος, -ου, ἡ,
Paphos, a city in Cyprus: Ac 13:6, 13.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G4078 (πήγνυμι) (meaning thick);
strong.def: to thicken, i.e. (by implication) to fatten (figuratively, stupefy or render callous)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 παχύνω (< παχύς, thick), [in LXX: De 32:15, Is 6:10 (שָׁמֵן), al.;]
to thicken, fatten; pass., to grow fat. Metaph., to make dull or stupid (τ. ψυχάς, Plut.); pass., to wax gross: ἡ καρδία, Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (LXX).†

strong.def: to foot a journey, i.e. travel by land

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * πεζεύω (< πεζός),
