strong.derivation: probably akin to G5420 (φράσσω) through the idea of defining;
strong.def: to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φράζω [in LXX: Jb 6:24 (בִּין hi.) Jb 12:8 (יָרָה hi.), Da LXX 2:4 (חָוָה pa.) * ;]
to show forth, tell, declare, explain: Mt 13:36 (WH, RV, διασάφησον) 15:15.†

strong.derivation: apparently a strengthening form of the base of G5424 (φρήν);
strong.def: to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 φράσσω [in LXX: Jb 38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Ho 2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pr 21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;]
to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, He 11:33; στόμα, metaph., Ro 3:19; pass., καύχησις, II Co 11:10.†

strong.def: to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φρεν-απατάω, -ῶ (< φρεναπάτης),
to deceive one's mind (Lft., deceive by fancies, v. Ga., l.c.): c. acc. pers., Ga 6:3.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φρεναπάτης, -ου, ὁ (< φρήν, ἀπάτη),
a deceiver (B1., deceiver of his own mind, § 28, 52, where v. ref. to π.): Tit 1:10 (eccl.).†

strong.derivation: probably from an obsolete (to rein in or curb; compare G5420 (φράσσω));
strong.def: the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φρήν gen., φρενός, ἡ, [in LXX most freq. in Pr (6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also III Mac 4:16 5:47 ;]
chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.;
1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff.
2. heart, mind, thought: pl., I Co 14:20 (v. Edwards, Eng.-Gr. Lex., App., 1).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) φρίσσω (Att.. -ττω, and so IV Mac 14:9 17:7) [in LXX: Jb 4:15 (סמר pi.), etc. ;]
1. to be rough, bristle.
2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Ja 2:19 (v. Hort, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ** φρόνημα, -τος, τό (< φρονέω), [in LXX: II Mac 7:21 13:9 * ;]
that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 86), the thought: Ro 8:6, 7, 27.†

strong.def: to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φροντίζω (< φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: I Ki 9:5 (דָּאַג), Ps 39 (40):17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;]
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., c acc., c. gen.), c. inf., Tit 3:8 (v. Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G3708 (ὁράω);
strong.def: to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 φρουρέω, -ῶ (< φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Es 4:56, Jth 3:6, Wi 17:16, I Mac 11:3 * ;]
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: II Co 11:32; metaph., Ga 3:23, Phl 4:7, I Pe 1:5.†

strong.def: to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † φρυάσσω (so Ps, l.c., NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Ps 2:1 (רָגַשׁ), II Mac 7:34 R, III Mac 2:2 * ;]
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaph., to be wanton, insolent: Ac 4:25 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a presumed derivative of (to roast or parch;
strong.def: akin to the base of G5395 (φλόξ)); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φρύγανον, -ου, τό (< φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל, etc. ;]
a dry stick: pl., brushwood: Ac 28:3.†

strong.def: Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φρυγία, -ας, ἡ (prop., the adj., Φρυγίος, -α, -ον; sc. γῆ, χώρα),
Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor: Ac 2:10; Φ. καὶ Γαλατικὴ χώρα (Γ. χ. κ. Φ.), Ac 16:6 18:23 (on these phrases v. DB, i, 89 f.; CGT, Gal., xxii f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φύγελος (Rec. -λλος), -ου, ὁ
Phygelus: II Ti 1:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φυγή, -ῆς, ἡ (< φεύγω), [in LXX chiefly for מָנוֹס and cogn. forms ;]
flight: Mt 24:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† φυλακίζω [in LXX: Wi 18:4 * ;]
to imprison: Ac 22:19.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a derivative of G5442 (φυλάσσω);
strong.def: a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φυλακτήριον, -ου, τό
1. an outpost, fortification (Thuc., al.).
2. a safeguard (Plat.).
3. an amulet (Plut., al.); in NT for the Talmudic תְּפִלִּין, a prayer fillet, a phylactery, a small strip of parchment on which portions of the law were written and worn on the forehead and next the heart (cf. Ex 13:16): Mt 23:5.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 φύλαξ, -ακος, ὁ (< φυλάσσω), [in LXX for שָׁמַר, צוּר ;]
a guard, keeper: Ac 5:23 12:6, 19.†

strong.derivation: from a prolonged form of (to mix a liquid with a solid;
strong.def: perhaps akin to G5453 (φύω) through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 φύραμα, -τος, τό (< φυράω, to mix), [in LXX: Ex 8:3 (7:28) 12:34 (משארת), Nu 15:20, 21 (עריסה) * ;]
that which is mixed or kneaded, a lump: of dough, Ro 11:16, I Co 5:6, 7, Ga 5:9; of clay, Ro 9:21.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * φυσικός, -ή, -όν (< φύσις),
natural
(a). produced by nature, innate (Xen., Arist., al.);
(b). according to nature (Arist., Diod., al.): opp. to παρὰ φύσιν, Ro 1:26, 27;
(c). governed by mere natural instinct (cf. Plut., Mor., 706A): ζῷα γεγεννημένα φ. (RV, born mere animals; Mayor, born creatures of instinct; ICC, animals born of mere nature), II Pe 2:12,†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φυσικῶς adv.,
naturally, by nature: Ju 10.†

strong.derivation: from G5449 (φύσις) in the primary sense of blowing;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 *† φυσιόω, -ῶ (< φῦσα, bellows), = cl. φυσάω,
to puff or blow up, inflate. Metaph., to puff up, make proud: I Co 8:1. Pass., to be puffed up with pride: I Co 4:18, 19 5:2 13:4; seq. ὑπό, Col 2:18; seq. ὑπὲρ . . . κατά, I Co 4:6 (on the form of the subjc., v. M, Pr., 54; Bl., § 22, 3).†

strong.def: growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 (KJV) ** φύσις, -εως, ἡ (< φύω) [in LXX: Wi 7:20 13:1 19:20 אΑ, III Mac 3:29, IV Mac 1:20 5:7, 8, 25 13:27 15:13, 25 16:3 * ;]
nature, i.e.,
(a). the nature (natural powers or constitution) of a person or thing: Ja 3:7, II Pe 1:4;
τέκνα φυσει ὀργῆς, Eph 2:3;
(b). origin, birth (Soph., Xen., al.): Ro 2:27, Ga 2:15;
(c). nature, i.e. the regular order or law of nature: I Co 11:14; dat., φύσει adverbially, by nature, Ro 2:14, Ga 4:8; παρὰ φύσιν, against nature, Ro 1:26 11:24; καρὰ φ., according to nature, naturally, Ro 11:21, 24.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† φυσίωσις, -εως, ἡ (< φυσιόω),
a puffing up, swelling with pride: pl., II Co 12:20.†

strong.def: trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 φυτεία, -ας, ἡ (< φυτεύω), [in LXX: IV Ki 19:29 (נטע), Mi 1:6, Ez 17:7 (מַטָּע) * ;]
1. a planting (Xen., al.; LXX).
2. = φύτευμα, that which is planted, a plant (Inscr.): Mt 15:13.†

strong.def: an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φωστήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (< φῶς), [in LXX: Ge 1:14, 16 (מָאוֹר), Da LXX 12:3 (זֹהַר), I Es 8:79, Wi 13:2, Si 43:7 * ;]
a luminary, light: Phl 2:15, Re 21:11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * φωσ-φόρος, -ον (< φῶς, φέρω),
light-bringing; as subst., ὁ φ., the morning star (Plat., al.; cf. ἐωσφόρος, Is 14:12, Jb 3:9, Ps 110:3): metaph., II Pe 1:19 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (φωτίζω) [in LXX: Jb 3:9, Ps 26 (27):1 43 (44):3 77 (78):14 138 (139):11 (אוֹר), Ps 89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;]
illumination, light: metaph., I Co 4:4, 6.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 χάλαζα, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בָּרָד ;]
hail: Re 8:7 11:19 16:21.†

strong.def: a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ
a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Ac 7:4.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of reducing the strength;
strong.def: difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χαλεπός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: Is 18:2 (נוֺרָא), Wi 3:19, Si 3:21, al. ;]
hard;
(a). hard to do or deal with, difficult;
(b). hard to bear, painful, grievous: καιροί, II Ti 3:1;
(c). of persons, hard to deal with, harsh, fierce, savage: Mt 8:28.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5469 (χαλινός) and the reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† χαλιναγωγέω, -ῶ (< χαλινός, ἄγω),
to lead with a bridle; metaph., to bridle, restrain: c. acc., γλῶσσαν, Ja 1:26; σῶμα, 3:2.†

strong.def: a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;]
a bridle: Ja 3:3, Re 14:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) χάλκεος, -έα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν) (< χαλκός), [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;]
brazen (i.e. of copper): Re 9:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ (< χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;]
a worker in metal, esp. a copper-smith: II Ti 4:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ
chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Re 21:19.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G5475 (χαλκός) and G3030 (λίβανος) (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy);
strong.def: burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό
chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Re 1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).†

strong.derivation: adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of a fissure in the soil;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χαμαί adv.,
on or to the ground: Jo 9:6 18:6.†

strong.def: Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן),
Canaan: Ac 7:11; γῆ Χ., Ac 13:19.†

strong.def: a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Χαναναῖος, -α, -ον
Canaanite: γυνή, Mt 15:22.†

strong.def: a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 * χάραγμα, -τος, τό (< χαράσσω, to engrave),
(a). a stamp, impress, mark: Re 13:16, 17 14:9, 11 16:2 19:20 20:4 (v. Deiss., BS, 240 ff.);
(b). a thing graven: Ac 17:29.†

strong.def: a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (< χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Le 13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), II Mac 4:10, IV Mac 15:4 א R * ;]
1. a tool for graving.
2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaph., χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, He 1:3.†

strong.def: a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 † χάρισμα, -τος, τό (< χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Si 7:33א(AB, χάρις) 38:30 Bl(אAB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;]
a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including all spiritual graces and endowments (Lft., Notes, 148 f.): Ro 1:11 5:15, 16 6:23 11:29 12:6, I Co 1:7 7:7 12:4, 9, 28, 30, 31, II Co 1:11, I Ti 4:14, II Ti 1:6, I Pe 4:10.†

strong.def: Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Χαρράν
indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Ge 29:4 E, Ez 27:28 B, elsewhere -άν—Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Ac 7:2, 4.†

strong.def: a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χάρτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Is 8:1 A, Je 43 (36):2, 6, 23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;]
a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (v. Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jo 12 (Plat., Inscr.).†

strong.def: to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χειμάζω (< χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pr 26:10 (†) * ;]
1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters.
2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Ac 27:18.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G5494 (χειμών) and G4482 (ῥέω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον (< χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;]
winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: Jo 18:1.†

strong.def: to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χειραγωγέω, -ῶ (< χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Jg 16:26 A (בְּיָר מַחֲזׅיק), To 11:16 א * ;]
to lead by the hand: Ac 9:8 22:11.†

strong.derivation: from G5495 (χείρ) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person)
strong.kjv: some to lead by the hand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * χειρ-αγωγός, -όν (< χείρ, ἄγω)
leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Ac 13:11.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G5495 (χείρ) and G1125 (γράφω);
strong.def: something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† χειρόγραφος, -ον (< χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: To 5:3 9:2, 5 * ;]
written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaph., Col 2:14.†

strong.derivation: from a comparative of G5495 (χείρ) and (to stretch);
strong.def: to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ (< χείρ, τείνω)
1. to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.).
2. to appoint:
(a). by vote, II Co 8:19
(b). without vote, Ac 14:23 (v. Rackham, in l.) (cf. προχειροτονέω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) † Χερουβείν (Rec. -βίμ), τά (Heb. כְּרוּבׅים),
Cherubim: He 9:6 (cf. Ex 25:17 (18), al.; v. DB, i, 377 ff.).†

strong.def: "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 (KJV) ἐχθές (Rec. χθές), adv., [in LXX for תְּמוֹל, etc.;]
yesterday: Jo 4:52, Ac 7:28, He 13:8 (on the form, v. Rutherford, NPhr., 370 f.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 χίλιοι, -αι, -α
a thousand: II Pe 3:8 (LXX), Re 11:3 12:6 14:20 20:2-7.†

strong.def: Chios, an island in the Mediterranean

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Χίος, -ου, ἡ
Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Ac 20:15.†

strong.derivation: perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (G5465 (χαλάω)) or G5494 (χειμών) (as descending or empty);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χιών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;]
snow: Mt 28:3, Re 1:14.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ [in LXX: II Mac 12:35 * ;]
a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (q.v.): Mt 27:28, 31 (v. Tr., Syn., § 1).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative probably of G5491 (χεῖλος);
strong.def: to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * χλευάζω (< χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wi 11:14, II Mac 7:7, IV Mac 5:22 * ;]
to jest, mock, jeer: Ac 17:32.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * χλιαρός, -ά, -όν (< χλίω, to become warm),
warm, tepid; metaph., of persons, luke-warm: Re 3:16.†

strong.derivation: feminine of apparently a primary word;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Χλόη, -ης, ἡ (i.e. tender foliage),
Chloe: I Co 1:11.†

strong.def: dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 χοϊκός, -ή, -όν, (< χοῦς)
earthy, made of dust: I Co 15:47-49 (v. Field, Notes, 179 f.).†

strong.def: a chœnix or certain dry measure

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ [in LXX: Ez 45:10, 11 (בַּת) * ;]
a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Re 6:6 (EV, measure).†

strong.def: to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** χολάω, -ῶ (< χολή), [in LXX: III Mac 3:1 R * ;]
1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.).
2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: c. dat. pers., Jo 7:23.†

strong.derivation: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue);
strong.def: "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χολή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;]
gall: Mt 27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mk 15:23, v. Swete, in l.; DCG, i, 634a); metaph., Ac 8:23.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5525 (χορός) and G71 (ἄγω);
strong.def: to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χορηγέω, -ῶ (< χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;]
1. to lead a χορός (v. LS, s.v.).
2. to defray the cost of a χορός.
3. In late writers, metaph., c. acc. (v. M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: II Co 9:10, I Pe 4:11 (Polyb., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † χόρτασμα, -τος, τό (< χορτάζω), [in LXX: Ge 24:25, 32 42:27 43:24, Jg 19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), De 11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Si 30:33 (33:24)) Si 38:26 * ;]
fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Ac 7:11 (RV, sustenance).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from G5495 (χείρ), to handle);
strong.def: to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 χράομαι, χρῶμαι (< χρή), [in LXX for עשׂה, etc. ;]
to use, make use of: c. dat. (cf. M, Pr., 64, 158), Ac 27:17, I Co 9:12, 15, I Ti 1:8 5:23; μᾶλλον χρῆσαι (i.e. the opportunity; v. M, Pr., 247), I Co 7:21; as some­times in late writers (cf. M, Pr., 64; Lft., Notes, 233), c. acc., I Co 7:31; of feelings, etc., to exercise, shew: II Co 1:17 3:12; c. adv., ἀποτόμως, to deal sharply, II Co 13:10; c. dat. pers. (cl.), to treat, deal with, Ac 27:3.†

strong.derivation: third person singular of the same as G5530 (χράομαι) or G5531 (χράω) used impersonally;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * χρή impers. (< χράω, v. LS, s.v.),
it is necessary: Ja 3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ (< χρηματίζω, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 24:60 (31:1) (מַשָּׂא), II Mac 2:4 11:17 * ;]
a divine response, an oracle: Ro 11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) χρήσιμος, -η, -ον (< χράομαι), [in LXX: Ge 37:26 בֶּצַע etc. ;]
useful: II Ti 2:14.†

strong.def: employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χρῆσις, -εως, ἡ (< χράομαι), [in LXX: I Ki 1:28 (שׁאל), Si 18:8, al. ;]
use: in a sexual sense, Ro 1:26; c. gen. obj., θηλείας, ib. 27 (for exx., v. Thayer, s.v.).†

strong.def: to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χρηστεύομαι (< χρηστός),
to be kind: I Co 13:4 (eccl.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G5543 (χρηστός) and G3004 (λέγω);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ (χρηστός, λέγω),
fair speaking: in bad sense, Ro 16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†

strong.def: usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 χρηστότης, -ητος, ἡ (< χρηστός), [in LXX for מוֺב and cogn. forms ;]
1. goodness, excellence, uprightness: Ro 3:12 (LXX).
2. goodness of heart, kindness: Ro 2:4, II Co 6:6, Ga 5:22, Col 3:12, Tit 3:4; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Eph 2:7; id., opp. to ἀποτομία, Ro 11:22.

strong.def: an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 χρίσμα (T, χρῖσμα, as in cl.; v. Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το (< χρίω), [in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Ex 29:7, al.) ;]
later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.),
an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l.; but cf. Westc., in l, for the view that the oil, not the act, is meant): I Jo 2:20, 27.†

strong.def: a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Χριστιανός (D, Χρεισ-; on the form Χρησ-, v. Bl., § 3, 6; 27, 4 on the ending, -ανος, v. Bl., ll. c.; Deiss., LAE, 382), -οῦ ὁ,
a Christian, the name first given to the disciples by pagan gentiles at Antioch: Ac 11:26 26:28, I Pe 4:16 (v. reff. in Thayer, s.v.; also DB, i, 384).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed compound of G5550 (χρόνος) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος);
strong.def: to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * χρονοτριβέω, -ῶ (< χρόνος, τρίβω),
to spend time: Ac 20:16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χρύσεος, -εα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν; on acc sing. fem., -ᾶν, Re 1:13 and gen. pl. uncontr., -εων, Re 2:1, LTr., v. M, Pr., 48 and cf. Thackeray, Gr., x, 172 f.) (< χρυσός), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
golden, i.e. made or overlaid with gold: II Ti 2:20, He 9:4, Re 1:12, 13, 20 2:1 4:4 5:8 8:3 9:13, 20 14:14 15:6, 7 17:4 21:15.†

strong.def: a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 χρυσίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of χρυσός, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
a piece of gold, gold: I Co 3:12, He 9:4, I Pe 1:7, Re 3:18 21:18, 21; of golden ornaments, I Ti 2:9 (WH, txt., RV), I Pe 3:3, Re 17:4 18:16 (WH, txt., R); of gold coin, money, Ac 3:6 20:33, I Pe 1:18.†

strong.def: gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χρυσο-δακτύλιος, -ον
with a gold ring: Ja 2:2.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Ex 28:20 36:20 (39:13), Ez 28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;]
a chrysolite (on its identification, v. Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Re 21:20.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χρυσό-πρασος, -ου, ὁ
a chrysoprase (v. Swete, Ap., 289): Re 21:20.†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) (through the idea of the utility of the metal);
strong.def: gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 χρυσός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for זהב ;]
gold: Mt 2:11, Re 9:7; of golden ornaments, Mt 23:16, 17, I Ti 2:9 (Rec., WH, mg.), Ja 5:3, Re 17:4 (Rec., WH, mg.) Re 18:12, 16 (Rec., WH, mg.); of images, Ac 17:29; of gold coin, Mt 10:9.†

strong.def: to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 χρυσόω, -ῶ (< χρυσός) [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה pi. ;]
to gild, cover with gold: pass., c. dat., χρυσίῳ (pleonast., cf. Ex 26:37), Re 17:4 18:16.†

strong.derivation: probably akin to the base of G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of handling;
strong.def: the body (properly, its surface or skin)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 χρώς, gen., χρωτός, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]
in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin: Ac 19:12.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† χῶρος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat. corus), the N.W. wind: Ac 27:12.†

strong.derivation: probably strengthened from (to rub or touch the surface;
strong.def: compare G5597 (ψώχω)); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ψάλλω [in LXX chiefly for זמר pi. (Jg 5:3, Ps 7:17, al.), also for נגן pi. (I Ki 16:16ff., al.) ;]
1. to pull, twitch, twang (as a bowstring, etc.; Æsch., Eur., al.), hence,
2. absol.,
(a). to play a stringed instrument with the fingers (Hdt., Plat., al.);
(b). later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: Ja 5:13; c. dat. pers., Ro 15:9 (LXX), Eph 5:19; dat. instr., I Co 14:15.†

strong.def: a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ψευδ-άδελφος, -ου, ὁ
a false brother: of professing Christians, II Co 11:26, Ga 2:4.†

strong.def: a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ψευδ-απόστολος, -ου, ὁ
a false apostle: II Co 11:13.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ψευδής, -ές (< ψεύδομαι), [in LXX for שֶׁקֶר, שָׁוְא, כָּזָב; etc. ;]
lying, false, untrue (of persons and things): Re 2:2; μάρτυρες, Ac 6:13; as subst., ὁ ψ., a liar: Re 21:8.†

strong.def: a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ψευδο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ
a false teacher: II Pe 2:1.†

strong.def: mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ψευδο-λόγος, -ον (< ψευδής, λέγω),
speaking falsely, lying: I Ti 4:2 (Aristoph., Polyb., al.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;
strong.def: to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 ψεύδω to deceive by lies; more freq. in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT), [in LXX chiefly for כּחשׁ pi. ;]
1. absol., to lie: He 6:18, I Jo 1:6, Re 3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Ro 9:1, II Co 11:31, Ga 1:20, I Ti 2:7 c. dat. pers. (Ps 17 (18):45, Je 5:12, al.), Ac 5:4; seq. εἰς, Col 3:9; κατά, Ja 3:14 (Hort, in l.).
2. Like act., c. acc., to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Ac 5:3.†

strong.derivation: from G5571 (ψευδής) and a kindred form of G3144 (μάρτυς);
strong.def: a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† ψευδο-μάρτυς, -υρος, ὁ [in LXX: Da LXX Su 60, TH ib. 61 Bl * ;]
a false witness: Mt 26:60; c. gen. obj. (v. WM, § 30, 1a), I Co 15:15.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ψευδο-μαρτυρία, -ας, ἡ
false witness: Mt 15:19 26:59.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ψεῦδος, -εος (-ους), τό [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב ;]
a falsehood, untruth, lie: Re 14:15; opp. to ἡ ἀλήθεια, Jo 8:44, Ro 1:25, Eph 4:25, II Th 2:11, I Jo 2:21; to τὸ ἀληθές, ib. 27; ποιεῖν ψ., Re 21:27 22:15; ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους (gen. qual., v. M, Th., 104; and on the meaning and construction, v. also ICC, in l.), II Th 2:9.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ψευδώνυμος, -ον (< ψευδής, ὄνομα)
under a false name, falsely called: I Ti 6:20 (Æsch., Plut., al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ψεῦσμα, -τος, τό (< ψεύδω), [in Aq., Th.: Jb 34:6, Pr 23:3; in Sm.: Jb 13:4, al. ;]
a lie, falsehood: Ro 3:7 (Plat., Plut. al.).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ψεύστης, -ου, ὁ (< ψεύδω), [in LXX: Ps 115:2 ( 116:11) (כֹּזֵב), Pr 19:22 Aא2 (כָּזָב), Si 15:8 25:2 * ;]
a liar: Jo 8:44, 55, Ro 3:4, I Ti 1:10, Tit 1:12, I Jo 1:10 2:4, 22 4:20 5:10 .†

strong.def: a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ (< ψάω, to rub) [in LXX: Ex 4:25 (צֹר), La 3:16 (חָצָץ), Ec 7:26 (25) (חֶשְׁבּוֺך), IV Ki 12:4 (5) A, Si 18:10, IV Mac 15:26 * ;]
1. a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, v. Swete, in l.), Re 2:17.
2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Ac 26:10.†

strong.def: by implication, a slander; probably akin to G5574 (ψεύδομαι)); whispering, i.e. secret detraction

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ψιθυρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: Ec 10:11 (לַחַשׁ) * ;]
a whispering;
(a). of secret slander, II Co 12:20 (Plut.);
(b). of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.c.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ (v. supr.),
a whisperer (as epithet of Hermes, Dem., 1358, 6): in bad sense, Ro 1:30.†
Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v

strong.def: sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from G4152 (πνευματικός), which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from G5446 (φυσικός), which is the lower or bestial nature)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ** ψυχικός, -ή, -όν (< ψυχή) [in LXX: IV Mac 1:32 * ;]
of the ψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opp. to πνευματικός, I Co 2:14 15:44, 46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; v. infr.), Ju 19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opp. to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l.), Ja 3:15†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό (< ψύχω), [in LXX: Ge 8:22 (קֹר), Jb 37:9, Ps 147:6 (17) (קָרָה), Za 14:6, Da LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;]
cold: Jo 18:18, Ac 28:2, II Co 11:27.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ψυχρός, -ά, -όν (< ψύχω), [in LXX: Pr 25:25 (קַר), Si 43:20, IV Mac 11:26 * ;]
cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Mt 10:42; metaph., of indifferent persons, Re 3:15, 16 †

strong.def: to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from G4154 (πνέω), which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of G109 (ἀήρ), which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ψύχω [in LXX for קוּר, שׁטח ;]
to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaph., Mt 24:12.†

strong.def: to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ψωμίζω (< ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אכל hi. ;]
to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: c. acc. pers., Ro 12:20 (LXX); c. acc rei, to give out for food, I Co 13:3 (cf. WM, § 32, 4an; for dupl. acc., cf. Nu 11:4, Si 15:3, al.).†

strong.derivation: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5597 (ψώχω);
strong.def: a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ψωμίον, -ου, τό
dimin. of ψωμός, a fragment, morsel: Jo 13:26, 27, 30.†

strong.def: the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 (KJV) Ω, ω, ὦ μέγα (cf. ὂ μικρόν),
omega, ô, the twenty-fourth and last letter. As a numeral, ωʹ = 800, ω͵ = 800,000. As a symbol of the last (= τὸ τέλος), τὸ Ὦ (Rec. Ω, L, ὦ, T, ω), the Omega: Re 1:8 21:6 22:13 (cf. Ἄλφα).†

strong.def: a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while G5215 (ὕμνος) denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and G5568 (ψαλμός) still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ᾠδή, -ῆς, ή [in LXX chiefly for שִׁיר ;]
a song, ode, whether sad or joyful; in LXX and NT always in praise of God or Christ: Re 5:9 14:3 15:3; ᾠ πνευματικαί Eph 5:19, Col 3:16.†

strong.def: to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ὠδίνω [in LXX chiefly for חוּל, also for חבל pi., etc. ;]
to have birthpangs, to travail: Ga 4:27 (LXX), Re 12:2; metaph., Ga 4:19 (cf. συν-ωδίνω).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from an apparently primary (a sum or price);
strong.def: to purchase (synonymous with the earlier G4092 (πίμπρημι))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὠνέομαι, -οῦμαι
to buy: ὠνήσατο (= cl. ἐπρίατο; v. Rutherford, NPhr., 210 ff.; Veitch, s.v.), c. gen. pret., Ac 7:16.†

strong.def: belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively))

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ὡραῖος, -α, -ον (< ὥρα), [in LXX for נָאָה, טוֹב, יָפֶה, etc. ;]
seasonable, timely, esp. of ripe fruits; hence, blooming, beautiful (both of things and persons): Mt 23:27, Ac 3:2, 10, Ro 10:15 (LXX, ὥρα).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὠρύομαι depon., [in LXX for שׁאג ;]
of animals (also of men, Hdt., al.), to roar, howl: λέων, I Pe 5:8.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ὠσηέ (Tr., Ὁσ-), ὁ (Heb. הוֹשֵׁעַ),
Hosea: Ro 9:25.†

strong.def: just as if, i.e. as it were

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ὡσ-περ-εί adv.,
as, as it were: I Co 15:8.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of the base of G5624 (ὠφέλιμος);

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὠφέλεια (WH, -λία), -ας, ἡ [in LXX for יָעַל hi., בֶּצַע, etc. ;]
1. assistance, help (Thuc., Plat., al.).
2. profit, advantage, benefit (Hdt., Plat., al.): Ro 3:1, Ju 16.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 * ὠφέλιμος, -ον (< ὠφελέω),
useful, serviceable, profitable: c. dat. commod., Tit 3:8; seq. πρός, c. acc, I Ti 4:8, II Ti 3:16.†

strong.def: father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application
strong.kjv: chief, (fore-) father(-less), [idiom] patrimony, principal. Compare names in 'Abi-'.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
אָב 1101 n.m. father
1. father of individual
2. of God as father of his people
3. head of household, family or clan
4. ancestor
5. originator or patron of a class, profession, or art
6. fig. of producer, generator
7. fig. of benevolence & protection
8. term of respect & honor
9. specif., ruler, chief (late)

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry: [אַב, אַבָּא] n.m. father

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry: [אֵב] n.[m.] freshness, fresh green (Lag B N 207 inf. ibb; thence concr., cf. Ar. Arabic; above stem & mng. better than √ אנב (spring) cf. As. inbu, fruit, Aram. אִנְבֵּהּ (q.v.) Dl HA 65, Pr 114) עֹדֶנּוּ בְאִבּוֹ while in its freshness (i.e. אָחוּ, reed) Jb 8:12; concr., pl. green shoots בְּאִבֵּי הַנַּחַל Ct 6:11 (∥ הֲפָֽרְחָה הַגֶּפֶן הֵנֵצוּ הָרִמֹּנִֽים׃).

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry: [אֵב] n.m. fruit

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry: אֲבַגְתָא n.pr.m. (Pers. cf. בִּגְתָא) eunuch of Ahasuerus Est 1:10.

strong.def: properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)
strong.kjv: break, destroy(-uction), not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, [idiom] and surely, take, be undone, [idiom] utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
אָבַד vb. perish (M I אבד, As. abâtu Dl W 184 Aram אֲבַד, Syriac).—
Qal Pf. א׳ Nu 21:30 +; אָבְדוּ ψ 10:16 + (+ Ez 6:3 𝔊 Co) etc.; Impf. יֹאבַד Jb 3:3 Je 4:9; יֹאבֵ֑ד Jb 20:7 + 2t.; 3fs. תֹּאבַד Dt 22:3 + 4t.; תֹּאבֵ֑ד Jb 8:13 + 3t.; יֹאבְדוּ Ju 5:31 + 3t.; יֹאבֵ֑דוּ Jb 4:9 +; 3fpl. וַתֹּאבַדְנָה֙ I S 9:3; תֹּאבֵדוּן Dt 4:26 +; נֹאבֵ֑ד Jon 1:6, 3:9; נֹאבְדָה Jon 1:14 etc.; Inf. abs. אָבֹד Dt 4:26 + 2t.; cstr. אֲבֹד Dt 7:10 Pr 11:10; אֲבָדְךָ Dt 28:20; אָבְדֶ֑ךָ Dt 28:22; אֲבָדְכֶם Jos 23:13; אָבְדָם Ob 12 Pr 28:28; Pt. אֹבֵד Dt 26:5 + 7t.; cstr. אֹבַד Dt 32:28 (bef. ע? v. Di Bö § 378); etc.
1. perish, die, of individuals (mostly late) Nu 17:27 (∥ גוע & (v. 28) מות), (also Dt 26:5? cf. infr.) Jon 1:6, 14 Jb 31:19 cf. 29:13 Pr 31:6 Est 4:14, 16, 16 Mi 4:9 Je 40:15 cf. Is 57:1 Pr 11:10 28:28 Ec 7:15 ψ 119:92; emphasis on morality Jb 4:20 ψ 146:4 Ec 9:6; Saul & Jonath., under fig. of weapons 2 S 1:27; lion Jb 4:11; caravan Jb 6:18 (cf. Di); cf. אָ׳ חָסִיד מִן־הָאָרֶץ Mi 7:2, וְאָ׳ מֶלֶךְ מֵֽעַזָּה Zc 9:5; perish, be exterminated (judgment for sin), of Israel Lv 26:38 Dt 8:19, 19, 20 28:20, 22 30:18, 18 Je 27:10, 15 cf. 6:21, Ob 12 cf. ψ 80:17 Is 27:13; other nations Dt 7:20 Je 10:15 51:18 ψ 2:12 10:16 83:18 cf. 9:4 Am 1:8 Is 41:11 60:12 cf. Jon 3:9 v. also Ex 10:7 Nu 21:29, 30 (JE) Je 48:46; house of Ahab 2 K 9:8; wicked in general Ju 5:31 Jb 4:9 cf. v 7, ψ 37:20 49:11 68:3 (∥ sim. of melting wax), 73:27 92:10; also Pr 19:9 21:28; לָנֶצַח א׳ Jb 20:7; cf. דֶרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים א׳ ψ 1:6; sq. מֵעַל הָאָ֑רֶץ (of annihilation of Isr.) Dt 4:26, 26 11:17 Jos 23:13, 16 (D); sq. מִתּוֹךְ הַקָּהָל (of Korah’s company) Nu 16:33 (JE); perish, be ruined, destroyed, of inanimate things, e.g. land Je 9:11 (∥ נִצְּתָה כַמִּדְבָּר) cf. 48:8; harvest Jo 1:11; Jonah’s gourd Jon 4:10; riches Je 48:36 Ec 5:13; vessel ψ 31:13; houses Am 3:15 (so oft. As. Dl W); city Ez 26:17 (but del. 𝔊 Co); cf. bamôth Ez 6:3 𝔊 Co; heavens & earth ψ 102:27.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
אֶל (nearly always followed by Makkeph), prep. denoting motion to or direction towards (whether physical or mental).
1. of motion to or unto a person or place
2. Where the limit is actually entered, into
3. Of direction towards anything

5. Unto sometimes acquires from the context the sense of in addition to
6. Metaph. in regard to, concerning, on account of
7. Of rule or standard according to (rare)
8. Expressing presence at a spot, against, at, by, not merely after verbs implying motion
9. Prefixed to other preps. it combines with them the idea of motion or direction to

classic.name: BDB

הוּא m. הִיא f., pron. of the 3rd ps. sing. he, she, used also (in both genders) for the neuter it
1. an emph. he (she, it, they), sometimes equivalent to himself (herself, itself, themselves), or (esp. with the art.) that (those)
2. It resumes the subj. with emph.
3. Where, however, the pron. follows the pred., its position gives it the minimum of emphasis, and it expresses (or resumes) the subject as unobtrusively as possible
4. It anticipates (as it seems) the subject

6. In a neuter sense, that, it (of an action, occurrence, matte, etc.)
7. With the art.: so regularly when joined to a subst. defined itself by the art.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
הָיָה 3570 vb. fall out, come to pass, become, be

a.
(1). וַיְהִי and it came to pass that, most often (c. 292 t.)
(2). rarely also Pf. c. וְ conj. וְהָיָה
b. less oft. וְהָיָה Pf. consec. and it shall come to pass, or frequentat. came to pass (repeatedly, etc.)
II. Come into being, become
1.
a. abs., in lively narrative, arise, appear, come
b. sq. prep.
2. become
a. sq. pred. noun (to be viewed as implicit accus.)
b. sq. pred. adj.
c. become like

1. exist, be in existence
2. abide, remain, continue

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
הָלַךְ 1546 vb. go, come, walk
Qal Impf. usually (629 t.) as if from ילך
I. lit.
1. of persons
2. Also of animals, in similar meanings and combinations
3. in like manner of inanimate things
4. The inf. abs. is often used
a. as in other vbs., quite independently
b. to intensify meaning of finite form
c. most noteworthy is the joining of the Inf. abs.
(1). with a following Inf. abs. denoting a simutaneous action or process, and so emphasizing duration or continuance
(2). with a foll. vb. fin. c. ו consec. (rare)
(3). in cases where vb. fin. is foll. by Inf. abs. adj. denoting progress, advance
(4). twice, where vb. fin. is not הלך, but another vb. denoting motion
(5). quite by itself
(6). 13 t. the Inf. abs. = Imv. & is followed by Pf. consec.
d. akin to the use of Inf. abs. are some instances of Pt.
5. In combination with other verbal forms
II. Fig.; the most common uses follow; in most the origin in a literal meaning is evident:
1. pass away, die
2. live (‘walk’), in general
3. of moral and religious life
4. other fig. uses
Pi. (chiefly poet. and late)
1. walk in or with a throng
2. also of walking about = living
3. depart, go entirely away
4. fig. of mode of life, action, etc.
Hithp. walk, walk about, move to and fro
Hiph.
1. lead, bring
2. lead away
3. carry, bring
4. fig. of influence on character
5.
a. cause to walk, go
b. cause to flow, run
c. cause to depart, retire, go back

I. יהוה is not used by E in Gn, but is given Ex 3:12-15 as the name of the God who revealed Himself to Moses at Horeb

3. יהוה is also used with several predicates, to form sacred names of holy places of Yahweh

Qal Pf. 3 ms. sf. כְּלָאוֹ Je 32:3; 3 fs. כָּֽלְאָה Hg 1:10; 2 fs. sf. כְּלִתִ֫נִי I S 25:33; 1 s. כָּלִאתִי ψ 119:101; 3 pl. כָּֽלְאוּ Hg 1:10, כָּלוּ I S 6:10; Impf. 3 ms. יִכְלֶה Gn 23:6; 2 ms. תִכְלָא ψ 40:12; 2 fs. תִּכְלָ֑אִי Is 43:6; 1 s. אֶכְלָא ψ 40:10; Imv. sf. כְּלָאֵֽם Nu 11:28; Inf. cstr. לִכְלוֹא Ec 8:8; Pt. pass. כָלוּא Je 32:2, כָּלֻא ψ 88:9; (on the metapl. forms, as if fr. כלה, v. Ges § 76, 21 c Kö i. 611);—
1. shut up, c. acc. I S 6:10 (+ בְ loc.), Je 32:3; pt. pass. Je 32:2 (בְ loc.), fig. ψ 88:9 (opp. יצא).
2. restrain, c. acc. I S 25:33 (+ מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים), ψ 119:101 (+ מִכָּל־); כְּלָאֵם (sc. מֵהִתְנַבֵּא) Nu 11:28; כ׳ שְׂפָתַי ψ 40:10; כ׳ אֶת־הָרוּחַ Ec 8:8. On ψ 74:11 v. כלה Pi. 2.
3. withhold, כ׳ אֶת־קִבְרוֹ מִמְּךָ מִקְּבֹר מֵתֶֽךָ Gn 23:6 (P), כ׳ רַחֲמֶיךָ מִמֶּנִּי ψ 40:12, Hg 1:10 b, prob. also v a (rd. מָ֑ל for MT 𝔊 מִטָּ֑ל, We); abs. אַל־תִּכְלָאִי (sc. exiles) Is 43:6 (∥ תְּנִי).
Niph. Impf. וַיִּכָּלֵא הַגֶּשֶׁם מִן־הַשָּׁמָיִם Gn 8:2 (J), and the rain from heaven was restrained, cf. וַיִּכָּלְאוּ מַיִם רַבִּים Ez 31:15 (in fig.; ∥ מנע); וַיִּכָּלֵא הָעָם מֵהָבִיא Ex 36:6 (P).
Pi. [Pf. כִּלָּא and] Inf. cstr. לְכַלֵּא v. כלה Pi.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
מִן־, and מִ, before יְ, prep. expressing the idea of separation, hence out of, from, on account of, off, on the side of, since, above, than, so that not
1. with verbs expressing (or implying) separation or removal
a. from, against
b. מן also, without a verb of similar significance, sometimes expresses the idea of separation, away from, far from
c. of position, off, on the side of, on
2. Out of, Gk. ἐκ, Lat. ex
3. Partitively
4. Of time—
a. as marking the terminus a quo, the anterior limit of a continuous period from, since
b. as marking the period immediately succeeding the limit after
c. towards, to
5. (וְעַד) עַד … מִן from … even to
6. In comparisons, beyond, above
7. מן is prefixed to an infin.:
a. with causal force, from, on account of, through
b. after verbs implying restraint, prevention, cessation, etc.
c. with a temporal force, since, after
8. Once as a conj. before a finite verb. that
9. In compounds:

strong.kjv: according, after, because, before, by, for, from, [idiom] him, [idiom] more than, (out) of, part, since, [idiom] these, to, upon, when.

classic.name: BDB
classic.entry:
עַל, עָ֑ל
I. subst. height
II. As prep. upon, and hence on the ground of, according to, on account of, on behalf of, concerning, beside, in addition to, together with, beyond, above, over, by, on to, towards, to, against
1. Upon, of the substratum upon which an object in any way rests, or on which an action is performed
a. —
(a). of clothing, etc., which any one wears
(b). With verbs of covering or protecting, even though the cover or veil be not over or above the thing covered, but around or before it
b. Of what rests heavily upon a person, or is a burden to him
c. Of a duty, payment, care, etc., imposed upon a person, or devolving on him
d. על is used idiom. to give pathos to the expression of an emotion, by emphasizing the person who is its subject, and who, as it were, feels it acting upon him
e. חָיָה עַל to live upon (as upon a foundation or support)
f. Of the ground or basis, on which a thing is done
2. It expresses excess
3. It denotes elevation or pre-eminence
4. It expresses addition
5. It expresses the idea of being extended, or suspended over anything, without however being in contact with it, above, over
6. From the sense of inclining or impending over, על comes to denote contiguity or proximity, Engl. by (or sts. on)
7. In connection with verbs of motion (actual or fig.)
8. By writers of the silver age, על is sts. used with the force of a dative
9. With other particles:
III. As conj.
a. עַל אֲשֶׁר because that
b. עַל כִּי similar in meaning, but less frequent
c. עַל alone:
(a). because
(b). notwithstanding that, although
IV. Compounds:
1. with כְּ (rare and late)
a. as concerning, as upon
b. the like of their deeds is the like of (that which) he will repay
2. מֵעַל from upon, from over, from by

strong.derivation: properly, the same as H5920 (עַל) used as a preposition (in the singular or plural often with prefix, or as conjunction with a particle following);
strong.def: above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications
strong.kjv: above, according to(-ly), after, (as) against, among, and, [idiom] as, at, because of, beside (the rest of), between, beyond the time, [idiom] both and, by (reason of), [idiom] had the charge of, concerning for, in (that), (forth, out) of, (from) (off), (up-) on, over, than, through(-out), to, touching, [idiom] with.
